facts.key_finding: Full issue of the Journal of Cosmetic Dentistry (Summer 2011) combining case-based articles on all-ceramic and lithium disilicate esthetic restorations, AACD accreditation examiner observations and many advertisements.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: An issue-level compilation, not a single study; no single practice conclusion can be drawn from it.

facts.population: Patients with posterior single-tooth implant-supported restorations on CAD-CAM abutments
facts.intervention: CAD-CAM abutment emergence profile and profile angle at 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3 mm from the implant-abutment junction
facts.main_result: Convex emergence profile gave greater marginal bone loss than concave or straight; profile angle correlated with bone loss within 2 mm of the junction (cut-offs about 20-34 degrees).
facts.funding_coi: No competing interests declared

facts.population: Participants receiving single-unit implants in healed sites
facts.intervention: Definitive abutment connected at implant placement (one abutment-one time)
facts.comparison: Healing abutments disconnected and reconnected three times at 8, 10 and 12 weeks
facts.main_result: At 2 years cumulative bone loss was -0.61 mm (definitive abutment) vs -0.81 mm (healing abutment), no significant difference.
materials_brands: P-I Morse Taper M+N implant (Zimmer Biomet)
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Results relate to one implant model and no anterior sites were included.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 21 partially edentulous posterior patients each receiving two tissue-level implants
facts.intervention: Tissue-level implant with convergent transmucosal collar
facts.comparison: Tissue-level implant with divergent transmucosal collar
outcomes: peri-implant bone loss on periapical radiographs
facts.main_result: Convergent collar lost less bone (0.29 ± 0.34 mm) than divergent (0.60 ± 0.63 mm), P = .031.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: 22 patients with 40 single-tooth implants in posterior regions
facts.intervention: Customized zirconia abutments with cemented all-ceramic crowns
facts.comparison: Customized titanium abutments with cemented metal-ceramic crowns
facts.main_result: At 13 years technical survival of abutments and crowns was 100% in both groups, with similar biological and esthetic outcomes; implant survival was 90%.
facts.sample_size: 15 patients with 21 abutments examined (13 zirconia, 8 titanium)
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no conflict of interest; Nobel Biocare supplied abutments

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.main_result: A biologically driven protocol: 3.5-4 mm vertical distance from implant-abutment interface to mucosal margin, polished titanium/zirconia submucosal materials, slim vertical subcritical contour, one abutment/one time.

facts.population: 32 partially edentulous patients from five Italian clinics, two splinted implants each
facts.intervention: Implants placed with recorded insertion torque of 30-100 Ncm, early loaded at 2 months
outcomes: peri-implant marginal bone resorption at 2, 6 and 12 months
facts.main_result: No correlation between insertion torque (30-100 Ncm) and bone resorption; mean resorption 0.9 mm at 12 months.

facts.population: Patients treated with Nobel Biocare bone level implants by four surgeons
facts.intervention: Permanent abutment placed at implant surgery (one-abutment one-time)
facts.comparison: Conventional healing abutment (HA cohort)
outcomes: marginal bone loss at 3 months and longest follow-up
facts.main_result: One-abutment one-time did not affect presence of MBL but reduced its magnitude by 0.300 mm where bone loss occurred (p=0.023); mean MBL 0.52 mm.
facts.limitations: Cohort design limits conclusions.

facts.population: Patients needing a single-tooth implant crown in the anterior maxilla
facts.intervention: Zirconia abutment (Thommen SPI ART) with Lava zirconia crown
facts.comparison: Titanium abutment (Thommen SPI EASY, CPTi grade 4)
facts.main_result: Zirconia abutments showed a non-significant tendency to better aesthetics (ICAI 7.6 vs 11.3 at 1 year); two zirconia abutment fractures occurred.
facts.sample_size: 38 patients recruited, 25 of 30 randomized analysed at 1 year
facts.funding_coi: Partially supported by unrestricted grant from Thommen Medical; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Sample size not sufficient to contrast outcomes.

facts.population: 5 beagle dogs, 6 implants each (Branemark System)
facts.intervention: Abutments of c.p. titanium, ceramic (Al2O3), gold alloy and short titanium with porcelain-fused-to-gold, followed by 6 months of plaque control
facts.comparison: c.p. titanium control abutments
outcomes: mucosal attachment dimensions (junctional epithelium, connective tissue)
facts.main_result: Titanium and ceramic abutments allowed a mucosal attachment of ~2 mm epithelium and 1-1.5 mm connective tissue; gold alloy and porcelain abutments showed recession and bone resorption.
facts.follow_up: 6 months of plaque control after abutment connection

facts.population: 5 beagle dogs (mandibular implant sites, 3 months after premolar extraction)
facts.intervention: Installation of Astra Tech, Branemark (2-stage) and Bonefit-ITI (1-stage) implants, one of each per mandibular quadrant in random order
facts.comparison: 1-stage (non-submerged) versus 2-stage (submerged) implant systems
facts.main_result: No statistically significant differences among the three implant systems in any histometric variable; lamellar bone density was 85.4% (Astra), 87.4% (Branemark) and 88.4% (Bonefit).
facts.follow_up: 3 months healing plus 6 months plaque control

facts.population: Partially edentulous patients with missing single or multiple teeth (review question); only in vitro studies of implant-supported FDPs were found
facts.intervention: Additively manufactured (3D-printed, DLP/SLA) implant-supported fixed dental prostheses
facts.comparison: Subtractively manufactured (milled) implant-supported fixed dental prostheses
facts.main_result: No clinical study met the inclusion criteria and six in vitro studies gave inconclusive results on marginal/internal discrepancies and mechanical properties, so no meta-analysis was possible.
facts.sample_size: 2,184 records identified; 6 in vitro studies included
facts.funding_coi: Financially supported by the Clinic for Reconstructive Dentistry, University of Zurich
facts.limitations: No clinical studies found (only in vitro), no grey literature search, language restriction, and incomplete material and processing data

facts.key_finding: This book chapter defines peri-implant mucositis (reversible, mucosa only) and peri-implantitis (soft tissue inflammation with bone loss), notes there is no consensus classification, and compares tissues around teeth and implants. Implants have reduced vascularization and parallel collagen fibers, so peri-implant tissue breaks down more easily.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Probe gently at routine visits, control biofilm and periodontal disease early, and respect the biologic width around implants to avoid early bone loss.

facts.population: 16 healthy volunteers wearing intraoral splints carrying discs of five implant/abutment materials
facts.intervention: 24-hour intraoral biofilm formation on discs of gold-based and silver-based noble alloys, zirconia and PEKK
facts.comparison: Titanium zirconium alloy (TiZr) as reference material
facts.main_result: Silver-based (PA) and gold-based (EL) alloys formed least biofilm; versus PA, biofilm mass was 1.5x higher for EL, 1.7x PEKK, 2.2x TiZr and 2.4x zirconia.
facts.sample_size: 16 volunteers, two runs, 15 discs per splint
facts.funding_coi: Institut Straumann AG and Cendres+Métaux SA provided the test materials

facts.population: Literature on biologic width around dental implants (animal histology and human clinical studies)
facts.comparison: Biologic width around natural teeth
outcomes: biologic width dimensions (junctional epithelium, connective tissue, sulcus)
influence of surgical technique, loading, surface, abutment, implant position
facts.main_result: Most studies report larger peri-implant biologic width than around natural teeth, with contradictory data on influencing factors.

facts.population: Patients with posterior mandibular partial edentulism treated with at least two implants
facts.intervention: 2 mm (Group A) or 1 mm (Group B) abutment connected at implant surgery
facts.comparison: 2 mm abutment connected after 2 months in a second stage (Group C)
facts.main_result: Mean marginal bone change at 3 years was 0.35, 0.60 and 0.71 mm in groups A, B and C, with a significant difference between A and C (p=0.048).
facts.sample_size: 29 subjects and 59 implants at 3 years (33 subjects, 68 implants at start)
materials_brands: OsseoSpeed EV implants (Astra Tech, Dentsply Implants)
facts.funding_coi: Two authors are usual speakers for Dentsply; no financial interests declared in the products

facts.population: Subjects receiving posterior single implant-supported crowns (41 subjects, 56 implants)
facts.intervention: Screw-retained monolithic lithium-disilicate crowns luted to titanium bases
facts.comparison: Cemented monolithic lithium-disilicate crowns on individualized titanium abutments
outcomes: biological complications (mucositis by BOP, gingival and plaque index)
facts.main_result: Mucositis incidence at 12 months was 14.2% (screw-retained) vs 17.9% (cemented), marginal bone loss 0.03-0.15 mm; retention mode did not influence complication rate.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Ivoclar Vivadent; implants and metal components funded by the Oral Reconstruction Foundation; two authors received honoraria from funders
facts.limitations: Short 24-month follow-up, radiographs only up to 12 months, and a power analysis based on an estimated effect size

facts.population: Patients with single-tooth implants in the anterior maxilla or mandible
facts.intervention: Screw-retained crown on a directly veneered one-piece customized zirconia abutment (SCREW)
facts.comparison: Cemented lithium disilicate crown on a one-piece customized zirconia abutment (CEM)
facts.main_result: At 5 years implant survival was 100% and restoration survival 82.4% in both groups, with similar marginal bone change (median -0.23 mm CEM vs -0.15 mm SCREW) and 15.4% technical complications in each group.
facts.sample_size: 34 patients with 34 single-tooth implants; 26 re-examined at 5 years
facts.funding_coi: International Team for Implantology research grant 780_2011 and the University of Zurich clinic; authors report no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Small sample size, relatively high drop-out rate (8 of 34), no posterior implants, strict inclusion criteria

facts.journal: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.population: 115 consecutive patients with a single failing molar replaced by an immediate posterior implant
facts.intervention: Flapless molar extraction with immediate implant, bone graft and a custom chair-side healing abutment (Anatomic Harmony Abutment)
facts.main_result: Overall implant survival was 98.26% with 3 failures in 115 implants (100% maxilla, 96.08% mandible), with follow-up up to 8 years.
facts.funding_coi: No relevant financial relationship with a commercial interest declared

facts.population: 19 patients edentulous from severe periodontal disease with 160 implants supporting fixed full-arch screw-retained metal-ceramic restorations
facts.intervention: OsseoSpeed Astra Tech TX implants with fixed full-arch metal-ceramic restorations on uni-abutments
facts.comparison: Abutment heights of 1, 2, 4 and 6 mm compared with each other
facts.main_result: No implant failed in 5 years and only 14 of 160 implants (8.75%) lost more than 2 mm of bone; MBL was larger with 1 mm abutments (-0.987 mm) than 2, 4 or 6 mm.
materials_brands: OsseoSpeed Astra Tech TX implants (Dentsply Implants)
facts.funding_coi: Junta de Andalucía grants; authors declare no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Retrospective design with a not very large number of patients, and panoramic radiographs

facts.population: 122 subjects with a single screw-retained implant restoration in the anterior or premolar region
facts.intervention: Emergence angle, profile and mucosal tunnel depth of the crown measured on superimposed digital scans
facts.main_result: Site-specific platform-level emergence angle, profile and mucosal tunnel depth were significantly associated with detectable plaque (p<.01) and bleeding on probing (p<.02).
facts.sample_size: 122 subjects with single screw-retained implant crowns
facts.funding_coi: Periodontology Research Fund of HKU Faculty of Dentistry and European Research Group on Periodontology; authors declare no conflict
facts.limitations: Cross-sectional design unsuitable for chronological consistency, small sample, mixed bone- and tissue-level implants

facts.population: Adults needing single-tooth replacement in the anterior maxilla (first premolar to first premolar); 54 of 60 recruited completed
facts.intervention: Screw-retained CAD/CAM zirconia abutments (Atlantis) with concave transmucosal morphology, veneered with feldspathic porcelain
facts.comparison: Linear divergent transmucosal abutment morphology (control)
outcomes: probing depth and bleeding on probing
facts.main_result: No significant differences between concave and linear divergent abutments at 1 year; implant survival 100%, restoration survival 98.2%.
facts.sample_size: 54 subjects completed (29 concave, 25 linear divergent) of 60 recruited
facts.funding_coi: Partial funding from Dentsply Sirona (investigator-initiated study); two authors received lecture honoraria from Dentsply Sirona

facts.population: Patients with single implant prostheses restored with titanium base abutments (6 RCTs plus 23 prospective/retrospective studies; 857 prostheses)
facts.intervention: Titanium base abutments (TBA) for single-unit implant prostheses
facts.comparison: Other abutments (in the six RCTs)
facts.main_result: TBA restorations had an estimated 98.6% survival at 1 year (95% CI 97.9-99.4%); survival did not differ from other abutments in RCTs (OR 0.74)
facts.sample_size: 857 single implant-supported prostheses with TBA; 6 RCTs in meta-analysis
facts.funding_coi: Supported in part by the ITI Consensus Conference; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Short 1-year follow-up, heterogeneous TBA designs, and limited data on fit tolerance and geometry

facts.population: Partially or completely edentulous patients with implants in RCTs comparing connection designs
facts.intervention: External, internal flat-to-flat or conical implant abutment connection
facts.comparison: Other connection designs (positive control connection)
facts.main_result: Conical connections gave lower marginal bone loss (P=.011) and fewer prosthetic complications (P=.038) than external hexagon; no difference in survival or biologic complications
facts.funding_coi: No specific grant received

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Participants with posterior partial edentulism (Kennedy Class I or II)
facts.intervention: Internal conus design implants (Astra Tech Fixture ST)
facts.comparison: External hex design implants (Osseotite Standard)
facts.main_result: Mean bone change from placement to 3 years was -0.25 mm (ICI) vs -0.5 mm (EXI); EXI had more abutment complications (11 vs 1 participants)
facts.sample_size: 39 participants with 47 ICI and 46 EXI implants
facts.limitations: Neither participant nor investigator was blinded

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 26 subjects (aged 17-56) with two nonadjacent missing teeth in healed esthetic-zone sites
facts.intervention: Curved, grooved titanium abutment (Curvy, Nobel Biocare) with provisional then definitive crowns
facts.comparison: Conventional divergent straight titanium abutment (Esthetic, Nobel Biocare), split-mouth randomization
facts.main_result: Marginal bone loss T0-T12 was 0.00 +/- 0.37 mm (curved) vs 0.12 +/- 0.27 mm (straight), P = .25; PES 10 vs 9.7 (P = .46); no significant differences.
facts.funding_coi: Grant from Smile Care, Mumbai; Nobel Biocare supplied implants and abutments free; no conflicts of interest declared

facts.population: 22 patients with at least two adjacent missing teeth receiving bridges on bone level platform-switched implants
facts.intervention: 3 mm definitive abutments
facts.comparison: 1 mm definitive abutments
outcomes: interproximal implant bone loss at 3 and 6 months
association with patient and implant variables
facts.main_result: At 6 months 1-mm abutments had greater interproximal bone loss than 3-mm abutments (0.91 vs 0.11 mm)
facts.funding_coi: Sponsored by LASAK, Praha; authors declare no conflict of interest

facts.population: 90 sets of 4.5 x 10 mm bone level implants with conical hybrid connection mounted in acrylic blocks
facts.intervention: Abutment angulations of 15° and 25° and collar lengths of 2 and 4 mm, with dynamic cyclic loading
facts.comparison: 0° (straight) abutment and 2 mm collar
outcomes: percentage of removal torque loss before and after cyclic loading
facts.main_result: Screw loosening increased with abutment angulation and collar length after 100,000 loading cycles (post-load RTL 23.5% at 0°, 33.4% at 15°, 40.1% at 25°)
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no competing interests
facts.limitations: Results limited to this in vitro setting

facts.population: 11 edentulous patients with five implants each in the anterior mandible
facts.intervention: Subcrestal (1-3 mm) implant placement, immediately loaded
facts.comparison: Equicrestal implant placement
facts.main_result: Subcrestal placement had less crestal bone loss than equicrestal (-0.80 vs -0.99 mm at 5 years), not significant
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Wide range of subcrestal depth (1-3 mm) and small number of patients, so each depth could not be evaluated

facts.population: 44 Straumann bone-level implants (22 TorcFit, 22 CrossFit connection)
facts.intervention: Angled screw access channel titanium-base abutments with screw-retained crowns
facts.comparison: Straight screw channel abutments (hybrid zirconia abutments with cement-retained crowns); TorcFit vs CrossFit connection
outcomes: removal torque value after 24 h and after cyclic loading
facts.main_result: CrossFit connection gave higher removal torque and lower torque loss; no screw loosening during 2.4 million cycles and screw channel angle did not affect stability after loading
facts.funding_coi: Buser Implant Foundation Junior Investigator Grant; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Only one implant system and two connections tested; cyclic loading without liquid medium or enamel antagonists

facts.population: 120 sets of dental implants and abutments (Implacil De Bortoli), four platform/diameter groups of 30
facts.intervention: Switched-platform implants (regular 4.0 mm and wide 5.0 mm) at three simulated bone insertion levels (0, 3, 5 mm loss), fracture strength tested at 30 degrees
facts.comparison: Matched-platform implants of the same diameters
facts.main_result: Switched-platform implants had lower fracture strength at all insertion levels but less deformation than matched-platform implants
materials_brands: Implacil De Bortoli implants and abutments

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Two clinical cases (e.g. a 45-year-old woman needing replacement of a maxillary lateral incisor)
facts.intervention: Customized definitive zirconia abutment fabricated in the lab from registered soft tissue contours and inserted at stage-two surgery
facts.main_result: The pre-fabricated definitive abutment guides peri-implant soft tissue healing and replicates an optimal emergence profile (concept demonstrated in two cases, no controlled data)
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Further histologic and clinical research and long-term follow-up are needed

outcomes: clinical and histologic characteristics of healthy peri-implant tissues
facts.main_result: Healthy peri-implant mucosa is about 3-4 mm high with about 2 mm of epithelium, and roughly 60% of the intrabony implant is in contact with mineralized bone
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: 80 dental implants (8 groups of 10) with an inoculated internal lumen
facts.intervention: New internal conical connection with double taper principle (DAT, CSR-DAT implants)
facts.comparison: Seven other internal connections (groups 1-7)
facts.main_result: No contamination in the test connection in the first 6 h and none in 7 of 10 implants at 96 h, whereas all control connections were significantly contaminated (>100,000 CFU/ul) by 24 h (p<0.05).
outcomes: bacterial microleakage (E. coli CFU) from inside to outside the implant-abutment assembly over 96 h
materials_brands: DAT connection (Double Action Tight) on CSR-DAT implants

facts.journal: University of Michigan School of Dentistry (MS thesis, Graduate Periodontics)
facts.population: 192 bone-level implants in 119 patients
facts.intervention: Implants grouped by transmucosal abutment height (>2 mm vs <2 mm) combined with restorative emergence angle (<30 vs >30 degrees)
facts.comparison: Long-Gradual, Long-Abrupt, Short-Gradual and Short-Abrupt groups compared with each other
facts.main_result: Short-abrupt group had 0.48 mm more MBL than Long-Gradual and about 4x greater odds of peri-implantitis than Long-Abrupt (OR 4.19); each 1 mm of abutment height cut the odds of MBL by 51%.
facts.follow_up: at least 1 year between radiographs T0 (12-18 months after crown placement) and T1
facts.limitations: Retrospective design; level of initial crown emergence not documented; only bone-level implants evaluated
facts.key_finding: In bone-level implants, a transmucosal abutment shorter than 2 mm combined with an abrupt emergence angle gave the most marginal bone loss and about four times the peri-implantitis prevalence. Abutment height was the stronger factor; emergence angle mattered only when the abutment was short.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Choose an abutment taller than 2 mm on bone-level implants, especially when the restoration emergence angle is abrupt.

facts.population: 44 patients with single-tooth gaps in the esthetic zone (44 two-piece implants)
facts.intervention: Screw-retained all-ceramic single crown (veneered zirconia abutment as one piece)
facts.comparison: Cemented all-ceramic single crown (veneered lithium disilicate crown on zirconia abutment, resin cement)
facts.main_result: Cemented restorations had a higher biological complication rate (36.8% vs 0.0%) and overall complication rate (68.4% vs 22.7%) than screw-retained; marginal bone levels were equal (0.4 mm).
facts.funding_coi: Funded by University of Zurich; authors report no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Small sample (44 patients), 6.8% drop-out and implants mostly in premolar sites
materials_brands: IPS e.max / e.max Ceram lithium disilicate crowns

facts.population: 30 patients with titanium implants in the posterior mandible and maxilla (18 in per-protocol analysis)
facts.intervention: Hydrophilic modMA and modMA Ti-Zr healing abutments left transmucosal for 8 weeks, then biopsied
facts.comparison: Hydrophobic machined (M) healing abutments
facts.main_result: Per protocol (18 patients), epithelial contact was highest at modMA2 (53.45%) then modMA1 (32.25%) and machined (23.15%); connective tissue contact followed the same order.
facts.funding_coi: Unrestricted grant of Institut Straumann AG; authors declare no conflict of interest

facts.population: Fifteen edentulous sites treated with implants (posterior)
facts.intervention: Titanium, zirconia and gold alloy abutments with 8-week healing, then peri-implant tissue harvested for histology
facts.comparison: Titanium abutment as reference for zirconia and gold alloy
facts.main_result: Titanium and zirconia had similar histological attachment percentages while gold alloy was significantly lower (P=.004), with higher inflammation.
facts.funding_coi: Chulalongkorn University funding; authors declare no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Tissue conditions reported after only 2 months, i.e. early soft tissue maturation

facts.journal: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
facts.main_result: Gold alloys, ceramics and amino-alcohol contamination appear to promote epithelial downgrowth, whereas concave abutments, platform switching and microgrooved surfaces are believed to inhibit it.
facts.funding_coi: Authors report no financial interest in companies whose products were mentioned

facts.population: 16 of 24 originally recruited patients needing a single-tooth replacement in the esthetic area
facts.intervention: Immediate non-occluding provisional crown on hydrophilic bone-level implant (n=7)
facts.comparison: No provisional crown, definitive restoration at 16 weeks (n=9)
facts.main_result: At 60 months peri-implant bone loss was similar in test (-0.42 mm) and control (-0.37 mm) groups, with high survival and success in both.
facts.funding_coi: Sponsored by Institut Straumann AG
facts.limitations: Small sample size does not allow statistical inference at 60 months
materials_brands: Straumann Bone Level RC SLActive implant

facts.population: Partially edentulous patients treated with dental implants
facts.intervention: Concave/convergent implant transmucosal profiles
facts.comparison: Divergent/parallel implant transmucosal profiles
facts.main_result: Concave/convergent profiles had significantly less marginal bone loss (mean difference 0.772 mm, P<.001); no significant effects for soft tissue outcomes or platform-matching connections.
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no conflicts of interest declared

facts.population: 75 participants with 105 implants in molar or premolar sites
facts.intervention: Implants of identical design with conical connection
facts.comparison: External hexagon vs internal hexagon vs conical connection (35 implants each)
facts.main_result: Marginal bone level changed over time (P<.001) but did not differ between connection types (P=.152); 7 implant failures, no significant difference (P=.356).
facts.funding_coi: Agreement between University of Barcelona and Avinent SA; several authors declare Avinent and other industry support
outcomes: probing depth, plaque index, bleeding on probing

facts.main_result: Implant position, implant-abutment connection, restorative material, restoration design and cleansability all influence peri-implant tissue health; malpositioned implants produce emergence profiles that limit hygiene access.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: 13 included studies (in vitro, RCT, prospective and retrospective cohort) on implant-abutment connections
facts.intervention: Different implant-abutment connections: external hexagon, internal hexagon, conical
facts.comparison: Conical versus external and traditional internal hexagon connections
facts.main_result: All connections show some micro-gap and micro-leakage, but conical connections seem to behave better, with fewer mechanical complications and probably lower marginal bone loss.
facts.funding_coi: No funding, no competing interests
facts.limitations: Studies used different approaches and are hard to compare; more prospective in vivo studies needed.
facts.key_finding: This systematic review of 13 studies compared external, internal hexagon and conical implant-abutment connections. All showed micro-gap and bacterial leakage, but conical connections performed somewhat better mechanically and biologically.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Conical connections may be preferable for fewer mechanical complications and less bone loss, though the evidence is weak and connection type is not the only factor.

facts.journal: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
facts.population: Axisymmetric finite element model of an axially loaded mandibular titanium implant with retention elements on the neck
facts.intervention: Conical implant-abutment interface
facts.comparison: Flat top implant-abutment interface
facts.main_result: The conical interface lowered the peak bone-implant interfacial shear stress versus the flat top and moved it more apically, so it can theoretically resist a larger axial load.
facts.key_finding: In a finite element model, a conical implant-abutment interface produced lower peak bone-implant shear stress than a flat top interface, and the peak sat deeper in the bone rather than at the marginal bone.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Theoretically, a conical interface lets an implant tolerate a larger axial load before stress-triggered marginal bone resorption.

facts.population: Implants with their abutments from three systems (Nobel Replace Select, Straumann, Intra-lock), about 4.5 mm diameter
facts.intervention: Toluidine blue placed inside the implant screw, abutment connected per manufacturer torque, release into distilled water measured spectrophotometrically up to 144 h
facts.comparison: The three implant systems against each other
facts.main_result: All three systems leaked; after 144 h about 22% of the dye was released from Intra-lock, 55% from Straumann and 100% from Replace Select.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by NYU dental school research training program; implants supplied by manufacturers
facts.key_finding: Three internal-connection implant systems all leaked toluidine blue despite controlled torquing; leakage differed significantly, with Replace Select highest and Intra-lock lowest.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: No tested implant-abutment connection was fully sealed, so bacterial leakage cannot be excluded whichever of these systems is used.

facts.population: 30 patients with single posterior implants
facts.intervention: Convergent abutments (machined, or with ultrathin threaded micro-surface)
facts.comparison: Machined divergent abutment
outcomes: vertical width of connective and epithelial tissue (histology)
connective tissue vertical width by synchrotron microtomography
facts.main_result: Connective tissue was significantly taller next to convergent than divergent abutments, and the ultrathin threaded convergent surface had the greatest collagen bundle amount and density in 3D.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: The model does not reproduce cyclic masticatory loading, and synchrotron imaging cannot separate transverse from longitudinal fibers.
facts.key_finding: Healing abutments with a convergent profile were associated with a taller peri-implant connective tissue than divergent ones, and an ultrathin threaded surface gave denser collagen organization.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Convergent abutment profiles may favor connective tissue height; threaded micro-surface may improve the soft tissue seal.

facts.population: 18 histological animal studies (mostly dogs, also pigs and minipigs) of transmucosal implant components
facts.intervention: Different abutment or transmucosal collar materials and surface modifications
facts.comparison: Machined titanium transmucosal surface
facts.main_result: Only 4 of 18 studies could be meta-analyzed; attachment dimensions were comparable to machined titanium except a significantly higher ajE-CBI distance for chemically modified acid-etched surfaces (SMD 1.0, 95% CI 0.22 to 1.79).
facts.limitations: No study had low risk of bias in all domains; heterogeneity limited meta-analysis; animal data do not allow definitive conclusions.
facts.key_finding: In 18 animal histology studies, most abutment material or surface changes gave soft-tissue attachment comparable to machined titanium; only a chemically modified acid-etched surface differed, and evidence quality was low.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Animal data do not yet show that abutment material or surface modification clearly improves soft-tissue attachment.

facts.population: 64 implants in 25 partially edentulous patients (two adjacent implants in posterior jaw)
facts.intervention: 3-mm high cylindrical abutments
facts.comparison: 3-mm high wide abutments
facts.main_result: Cylindrical abutments gave significantly less marginal bone remodeling and loss than wide abutments over 12 months, and less bleeding on probing (p < .05).
facts.funding_coi: Not funded; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Results apply only to subcrestal bone-level implants with conical internal connection, platform switching and this abutment design; evaluator could not be blinded.
facts.key_finding: In a randomized trial of 64 implants, 3-mm cylindrical abutments showed less marginal bone remodeling and loss, and less bleeding on probing, than wide abutments during the first 12 months.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Choosing a cylindrical abutment shape over a wide one may help limit early marginal bone change around subcrestal bone-level implants.

facts.population: 120 implants (60 external hexagon, 60 Morse taper) with straight or 15 degree angulated abutments in methacrylate blocks
facts.intervention: Abutments screwed at 10, 20 or 30 Ncm, then thermal and cyclic loading
facts.comparison: External vs Morse taper connection; straight vs angulated abutments; 10 vs 20 vs 30 Ncm
outcomes: marginal misfit at implant-abutment interface (SEM, micrometers)
facts.main_result: Morse taper connections had the lowest misfit (0.6 µm with straight and angulated abutments at 30 Ncm), and misfit decreased as torque increased; all groups were below 3 µm.
materials_brands: Mozo-Grau MG-Osseous (external hexagon) and MG-Inhex (11 degree Morse taper) implants and abutments
facts.funding_coi: Research grant from University Complutense of Madrid and Mozo Grau S.A.; no conflicts declared
facts.key_finding: Morse taper connections fitted better than external hexagon connections, straight abutments better than angulated, and higher insertion torque (30 Ncm) gave the smallest implant-abutment misfit; all values stayed below 3 µm.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Tightening to the higher torque and using a Morse taper connection minimize the implant-abutment gap.

facts.population: 61 patients with single implant crowns after early placement in the anterior maxilla
facts.intervention: Bone level implant neck with hydrophilic micro-rough surface and platform-switching (n=20)
facts.comparison: Soft tissue level implant with machined neck and butt-joint interface (n=41)
outcomes: facial bone crest height and thickness by CBCT
facts.main_result: Facial bone crest was 0.2 mm above the shoulder for bone-level versus 1.6 mm below for soft-tissue-level implants, and the saucer-like defect width was reduced by 40% with the bone-level design.
facts.sample_size: 61 patients (20 bone level, 41 soft tissue level)
materials_brands: Straumann soft tissue level implant, SLA surface
Straumann bone level implant, SLActive surface
facts.funding_coi: Departmental funds and a research grant from Institut Straumann AG; no conflicts declared
facts.key_finding: At 5 to 9 years, bone-level platform-switched implants showed better facial bone crest stability than soft-tissue-level butt-joint implants in esthetic single-tooth sites, with similar soft tissue and esthetic scores.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: In the esthetic zone, a bone-level implant with a platform-switching neck preserved the facial bone crest better than a tissue-level butt-joint design.

facts.population: Four observational studies: 912 implants in 397 adult participants with restorations in function at least 3 years
facts.intervention: Implant restorations with emergence angle >30 degrees (or convex profile)
facts.comparison: Implant restorations with emergence angle of 30 degrees or less (or concave/straight profile)
outcomes: changes in peri-implant marginal bone level
facts.main_result: Emergence angle of 30 degrees or less gave less bone level change than >30 degrees, not significant (MD 0.80, p=0.09); convex profiles had higher peri-implantitis (57.8% vs 21.3%, RR 2.32).
facts.funding_coi: None of the included studies had external funding (review's own funding not stated in text)
facts.limitations: Evidence is of low to moderate certainty; included studies did not adjust for within-patient clustering.
facts.key_finding: Across four observational studies, restorative emergence angles above or below 30 degrees did not significantly change peri-implant bone level, though platform-matched implants with 30 degrees or less may do better, and convex profiles had more peri-implantitis.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Avoid convex restorative profiles; a 30 degree emergence angle cut-off alone is not a reliable predictor of bone loss.

facts.population: 25 patients each receiving two 4-mm implants in the posterior mandible
facts.intervention: Platform-switching implant (3.3-mm platform)
facts.comparison: Standard-platform implant (4-mm platform), within-patient
facts.main_result: At 3 years mean bone loss was 0.69 mm with platform switching and 0.74 mm with standard platform (difference 0.05 mm, 95% CI -0.19 to 0.29); no effect of platform type (p = .363).
facts.key_finding: In a three-year within-patient randomized trial, platform-switched and standard-platform implants showed similar crestal bone loss (about 0.7 mm), so platform switching gave no measurable bone benefit.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Platform switching should not be expected to reduce crestal bone loss in the posterior mandible compared with standard platform implants.

facts.population: 32 anterior monolithic screw-retained zirconia crowns on two-piece ceramic or titanium-zirconium implants (in vitro)
facts.intervention: Straight (0°) vs angulated (25°) screw-channel titanium bases under fatigue loading, on ceramic implants
facts.comparison: Two-piece titanium-zirconium implants (control) and straight screw-channel bases
facts.main_result: Mean bending moments were 241 N cm (Ti-Zr, 0°), 303 (Ti-Zr, 25°), 326 (ceramic, 0°) and 434 N cm (ceramic, 25°); angulated bases and ceramic implants gave significantly higher values; all survived fatigue.
facts.funding_coi: No specific grant; implants and abutments provided by Straumann; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Deviation from the ISO 14801 standard test setup

facts.population: 60 titanium implants placed in edentulous mandibular areas of five foxhounds
facts.intervention: Implants with SLA surface all the way to the top (no machined collar), microgap placed at different heights relative to the bone crest
facts.comparison: Implants with a 1.8 mm machined collar (control)
outcomes: crestal bone level (distance from microgap to first bone-to-implant contact) on non-decalcified histology
facts.main_result: At the same microgap level, machined-collar implants lost significantly more crestal bone than SLA-to-top implants (A vs E P=0.034; C vs D P<0.001).
facts.sample_size: 60 implants (30 machined, 30 SLA collar) in 5 foxhounds
materials_brands: Institut Straumann cp grade IV titanium implants, SLA surface (control with machined collar; test fully SLA)
facts.funding_coi: ITI Foundation grants; Hermann, Buser and Cochran received research funding from Institute Straumann, which supplied the implants

facts.population: 27 implant-abutment connections (9 designs, 3 each) from Southern Implants, Straumann, Ankylos and Neodent, inoculated with E. coli endotoxin
facts.intervention: Endotoxin placed in the implant lumen, abutment connected, implant submerged in pyrogen-free water and sampled up to 168 h (LAL test)
facts.comparison: External vs internal connection designs and different systems
outcomes: endotoxin leakage (EU) at 0 min, 10 min, 3 h, 24 h, 168 h
facts.main_result: All 6 external connections leaked; of 21 internal, 9 did not leak and 12 did; mean log endotoxin was higher for external than internal (p=0.015); Straumann Synocta, Cross-fit and Ankylos showed no measurable leakage.
materials_brands: Straumann Synocta, Straumann Bone Level Tapered Cross-fit, Dentsply Ankylos, Neodent Drive CM, Southern Implants connections
facts.funding_coi: Implants, abutments and accessories sponsored by the manufacturers; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Sample size was convenient, based on research questions and cost constraints

facts.population: 145 patients with 273 implants placed by a single clinician (retrospective chart and panoramic radiograph data)
facts.intervention: Prosthetic abutment height (customized abutments) as exposure
facts.comparison: Abutment height groups: <2 mm, 2 to <3 mm, >=3 mm
facts.main_result: Prevalence and mean marginal bone loss decreased as abutment height increased (Spearman rho -0.178, P=.006); abutment height should not exceed 4 mm.
facts.funding_coi: National Health Insurance Service grant; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Smoking (and periodontitis) not evaluated

facts.population: 36 partially edentulous patients with 72 bone-level implants (2 per patient) restored with 2- to 4-unit screw-retained prostheses
facts.intervention: Screw-retained prosthesis connected directly to the implant shoulder (no intermediate abutment)
facts.comparison: Prosthesis connected through a 3-mm standardised intermediate abutment
facts.main_result: At 12 months marginal bone loss was 0.17 ± 0.24 mm (direct, test) vs 0.09 ± 0.15 mm (with abutment, control), not significantly different.
materials_brands: Ticare Inhex implants (Mozo-Grau), RBM TC surface, platform-switching, tapered
facts.funding_coi: Sponsored by Ticare, Mozo-Grau; one author conducts grant research with Ticare

facts.population: 60 internal conical connection implants (4.3 mm, Conelog) with abutment-crown restorations, in vitro
facts.intervention: Monolithic lithium disilicate, zirconia or PICN abutment-crowns bonded to titanium bases, or lithium disilicate crown on customized titanium abutment, after thermo-mechanical aging
facts.comparison: Porcelain-fused-to-metal crowns on gold abutments
facts.main_result: Survival ranged from 100% (titanium abutment + lithium disilicate; titanium base + lithium disilicate) to 58.3% (titanium base + PICN); PICN had significantly lower bending moments.
facts.follow_up: Aging of 1,200,000 chewing cycles with thermocycling
facts.funding_coi: Grant from the Oral Reconstruction Foundation; manufacturers supplied materials

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Finite element model of a 12-mm ITI solid-screw implant with a 6-degree, 7-mm abutment
facts.intervention: 8-degree Morse taper implant-abutment connection modelled under axial and off-axis loading
facts.comparison: Hypothetical butt joint connection
outcomes: stress distribution in screw threads and joint
maximal thread tension at 30 degree off-axis load
facts.main_result: Axial preload was 53.2 N for the taper vs 358.6 N for the butt joint; at 30 degree off-axis load maximal thread tension was 1,176 MPa (taper) vs 1,403 MPa (butt joint), indicating superior mechanics of conical connections.
materials_brands: ITI Dental Implant System (Institut Straumann) solid-screw implant with solid abutment
facts.funding_coi: Two authors are affiliated with Institut Straumann AG; no funding statement

facts.population: 20 sterile Morse taper implant-abutment assemblies (10 Bicon, 10 Ankylos)
facts.intervention: Tapped-in (Bicon) vs screwed-in (Ankylos) Morse taper abutments, inner implant inoculated with Streptococcus sanguinis
facts.comparison: Bicon vs Ankylos
outcomes: bacterial leakage along the implant-abutment interface (solution cloudiness over 14 days)
facts.main_result: Bacterial leakage occurred in 2 of 10 assemblies of each system (20%), with no significant difference between them.
materials_brands: Bicon implants and abutments (Bicon Dental Implant)

facts.population: 40 patients with metal-ceramic cemented bridges on at least two healthy implants loaded for 5 years
facts.intervention: Four implant-abutment connections (external hex, double internal hex, internal hex with external collar, conical) sampled for bacteria by real-time PCR
facts.comparison: External hexagon connection (control group)
outcomes: absolute bacterial load (10 species and total count)
facts.main_result: All connections were contaminated after 5 years; connection design may influence bacterial levels, with conical and internal-hex-with-collar connections showing significantly lower total bacterial counts.
facts.follow_up: At least 5 years of functional loading

facts.population: 64 conical connection implants with their abutments (in vitro)
facts.intervention: CAD-CAM milled, laser-sintered and cast Co-Cr abutments and milled zirconia abutments, after chewing simulation and thermocycling, immersed in P. gingivalis methylene blue solution
facts.comparison: Cast Co-Cr abutments and other fabrication techniques/materials
facts.main_result: 47% (30/64) of implant-abutments leaked; lowest bacterial counts in milled Co-Cr (5.17E+02 CFU/ml) then zirconia (7.70E+03), higher in cast (9.39E+03) and laser-sintered Co-Cr (2.4E+05).
facts.funding_coi: Partly funded by Spanish Society of Prosthodontics Research Scholarship; no conflict of interest declared

facts.journal: Journal of Clinical and Diagnostic Research
facts.population: 30 included in vitro and human studies on implant-abutment connections
facts.intervention: Different implant-abutment connections (external hexagon, internal hexagon, Morse taper) under static or dynamic loading and various torques
facts.comparison: Between connection types, loading conditions, torque values and titanium vs zirconia abutments
facts.main_result: Nearly all studies showed some microleakage at the interface; Morse taper implants leaked much less than other connections and leakage rose under dynamic loading.
facts.follow_up: Included studies: five minutes to five years

facts.journal: Journal of Applied Biomaterials & Functional Materials
facts.population: 20 Sweden & Martina implants with prosthetic components (in vitro)
facts.intervention: Inoculation of the inner implant with E. faecalis or A. actinomycetemcomitans, 14-day broth turbidity check, and SEM measurement of the implant-abutment microgap
facts.comparison: Group 1 Kohno Straight implants vs Group 2 Kohno TG DES implants (both Morse taper)
facts.main_result: No leakage occurred in either connection (0/10 each); microgap differed significantly (0.0199 vs 0.6329 μm mean, p<0.01).

facts.population: A 45-year-old patient with partially edentulous maxilla and previous prosthodontic treatment failure
facts.intervention: Implant-supported restoration with multi-unit abutments and a definitive prosthetic construction six months after osseointegration
facts.main_result: Authors conclude multi-unit abutments give surgical flexibility (tilted posterior implants avoiding sinus grafting) and prosthetic benefits; no measured results reported in the available text.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 92 patients at seven international centers receiving single-tooth Brånemark implant restorations
facts.intervention: Single Brånemark system implants supporting single crowns
outcomes: abutment screw loosening and other complications
facts.main_result: After 3 years 82 of 92 patients remained, no further implants failed, cumulative success 97.2% and marginal bone loss about 0.1 mm annually.
facts.sample_size: 107 implants in 92 patients (95 implants in 82 patients at 3 years)

facts.population: Patients requiring implant-supported single-unit restorations (25 studies, mostly in vitro)
facts.intervention: CAD/CAM monolithic implant-supported ceramic restorations bonded to titanium inserts or bases
facts.comparison: Traditional screw-retained implant-supported restorations
facts.main_result: No clinical studies were found; laboratory studies suggest Ti inserts improve fracture strength, protect the connection from wear and give better marginal fit than full-zirconia abutments.
facts.limitations: No clinical studies exist and the in vitro studies were heterogeneous, so no meta-analysis was possible.

facts.population: 33 patients with thin peri-implant mucosa (≤2 mm) receiving 66 platform-switched bone-level implants
facts.intervention: 3 mm abutments with implants placed 2 mm subcrestally
facts.comparison: 1 mm abutments with equicrestal implant placement
outcomes: interproximal peri-implant bone loss at 3, 6 and 12 months
facts.main_result: Mean interproximal bone loss at 12 months was 0.95 mm with 1 mm abutments versus 0.12 mm with 3 mm abutments (significant at every time point).
facts.funding_coi: Sponsored by LASAK; authors declare no conflict of interest.
facts.limitations: Results apply only to bone-level platform-switched implants with internal-connection abutments placed with the one abutment-one time protocol.

facts.population: 40 participants aged 20 to 50 receiving single-tooth maxillary anterior and premolar implants
facts.intervention: Titanium-supported PEEK abutments (group PEEK, n=20), both groups restored with pressed lithium disilicate crowns
facts.comparison: Two-piece zirconia abutments (group ZIR, n=20)
outcomes: probing pocket depth, plaque control record, bleeding on probing
peri-implant mucosa color difference and crown discoloration
facts.main_result: At 5 years both PEEK and zirconia abutments had 100% survival and statistically similar biologic, bone-level and esthetic outcomes.
facts.sample_size: 40 participants (20 per group); 3 dropouts at 5 years
facts.funding_coi: Supported by Government of Kerala (facilities) and King Khalid University research group grant; no COI statement in text.
facts.limitations: Authors note long-term clinical trials are still needed to establish longevity.

facts.population: 64 patients receiving 98 two-piece implants with fixed restorations
facts.intervention: S1: OsseoSpeed TX (Astra Tech, Dentsply Sirona) implants with fixed restorations
facts.comparison: S2: Straumann Bone Level SLActive implants
facts.main_result: At 8 years patient-level survival was 97.6% (S1) vs 97.2% (S2); median marginal bone change was a 0.21 mm gain (S1) vs 0.24 mm loss (S2), clinically negligible.
facts.sample_size: 98 implants in 64 patients; 49 patients re-examined at 8 years
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the Clinic of Reconstructive Dentistry; some authors received research support and lecture fees from Straumann and Dentsply Sirona.
facts.limitations: No sample size calculation (convenience sample) and wide inclusion criteria.

facts.population: Edentulous patients with implant-supported full-arch prostheses, assessed through six systematic/narrative reviews
facts.intervention: Fixed and removable implant-supported full-arch rehabilitations of the edentulous maxilla and mandible
facts.comparison: Fixed versus removable prostheses
facts.main_result: Edentulous patients are frequently affected by peri-implant disease; fixed and removable prostheses both reach high survival (93.3-100% and 96.9-100%) with no prosthetic material of choice, and technical complications are unavoidable.
facts.limitations: Several areas lack data (esthetic outcomes, interarch space, opposing dentition, short implants in edentulous maxilla).

facts.population: 16 articles (12 evaluated): 3 human, 3 animal and 6 in vitro studies on abutment soft tissue response
facts.intervention: Abutment materials and surface topographies/macrodesign (laser-ablated, hydrophilic, oxidized titanium, zirconia)
facts.main_result: Human histology showed perpendicular fibroblast insertion into laser-ablated, hydrophilic and oxidized titanium abutment surfaces; epithelial cells slightly favored zirconia and polished titanium.
facts.sample_size: Preliminary pool of 206 articles, 12 evaluated plus 4 systematic reviews
facts.limitations: Heterogeneity of designs, statistics and results precluded meta-analysis.

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.intervention: Design of subgingival (critical and subcritical) and supragingival contours of the implant restorative emergence profile
facts.main_result: No convincing evidence on ideal emergence profile design; contours should mimic tooth/root shape but depend on implant position and phenotype, and a decision tree is proposed.
facts.funding_coi: Authors report no direct financial interests
facts.limitations: Authors note lack of convincing evidence and consensus on ideal emergence profile design

facts.population: 100 consecutive systemically healthy partially edentulous patients with subcrestally placed implants
facts.intervention: Xenograft grafting of the gap between bone crest and implant coronal aspect (Group A)
facts.comparison: Subcrestal implants without grafting material (Group B)
facts.main_result: Mean marginal hard-tissue loss was 0.11 mm in Group A and 0.08 mm in Group B with no significant difference between groups.
facts.funding_coi: No financial support; some authors received lecture stipends from DENTSPLY Friadent

facts.journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
facts.population: In vitro studies of implant-abutment connections
facts.intervention: Different implant-abutment connection types tested for preload, deformation and microleakage
facts.main_result: Conical connections gave fewer mechanical complications and higher torque preservation; all connections showed some microleakage.
facts.sample_size: 19 in vitro studies and 1 systematic review
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Studies used varied approaches and are difficult to compare

facts.population: Clinical trials, in vitro studies and reviews on implant-abutment connections
facts.intervention: Different implant-abutment connection types and their bacterial leakage
facts.main_result: All connections showed micro-gap and bacterial micro-leakage, though conical and mixed connections seemed to behave better.
facts.follow_up: In vitro mean 10.5 days; in vivo about 3 years
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Differences in study protocols, unspecified bacteria, mixed in vivo and in vitro designs, heterogeneous follow-up

facts.population: 54 implants in esthetically demanding sites of 41 patients
facts.intervention: Experimental concave (gingivally converging) titanium and zirconia abutments
outcomes: vertical soft tissue level changes at the facial aspect
facts.main_result: Vertical augmentation or no recession in 87% of situations and no recession greater than 0.5 mm; gingival level stable at 12-24 months; esthetic rating 4.5/5.
facts.funding_coi: Implant components provided by Nobel Biocare AB

facts.key_finding: A magazine feature giving a guide to abutment screw driver tip types (hex, square, Torx and others) by implant system, with a manufacturer chart of abutment screw torque values and drivers.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Before restoring an implant, identify the system and use the matching driver and manufacturer-specified torque value.

facts.population: 10 healthy patients with two implants each at healed posterior sites
facts.intervention: Concave circular macro-grooved titanium study abutments, immediately provisionalized
facts.comparison: Conventional convex control abutments
facts.main_result: Concave macro-grooved abutments did not give superior soft tissue development; control sites had higher PES values and marginal bone levels did not differ.
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare Replace Tapered Groovy implants
Nobel Biocare Curvy Esthetic titanium abutment

facts.population: 20 edentulous patients with two experimental abutments each in the interforaminal mandible
facts.intervention: Experimental healing abutments of titanium, zirconia, feldspar-veneered zirconia and PEEK with 3 months open healing
facts.comparison: Titanium abutments
facts.main_result: The four abutment materials showed no significant differences in clinical, microbiological, cytokine or bone outcomes; feldspar-veneered zirconia had fewer mononuclear inflammatory cells than titanium.
facts.funding_coi: Schilli Implantology Circle (SIC); Cendres+Métaux (C+M)
facts.limitations: Short observation period and small sample size

facts.population: 70 partially edentulous patients with one implant each in two groups by vertical mucosal thickness (thin vs thick)
facts.intervention: Prosthetic abutments 1 mm (short) or 3 mm (long) randomly assigned
facts.comparison: Long (3 mm) vs short (1 mm) abutments, in thin vs thick mucosa
facts.main_result: Short abutments gave greater marginal bone loss (0.59-0.80 mm) than long abutments (0.28-0.37 mm) at 12 months, irrespective of mucosal thickness.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Vertical mucosal thickness measurement method could be questioned due to soft tissue deformability

facts.main_result: Surgical trauma and periosteal elevation have not been shown to cause early implant bone loss; the pattern is more vertical than horizontal and surgical causes remain undetermined.

facts.journal: Journal of Dental Materials and Techniques
facts.population: 30 ITI solid abutments on fixture analogs with cast base metal crowns (in vitro specimens)
facts.intervention: Abutment surface roughening by sandblasting (50-µm aluminum oxide) or diamond bur, crowns cemented with TempBond
facts.comparison: Untreated abutments (control)
facts.main_result: Bur-treated abutments had the highest mean tensile strength (91.37±7.19 N) vs sandblasted 64.38±8 and control 58.61±1.93; sandblasted did not differ from control.
facts.funding_coi: Supported in part by Dental Research Center and Vice Chancellor for Research of Mashhad University of Medical Sciences

facts.population: Patients with dental implants (12 randomized trials included)
facts.intervention: Abutments made of materials other than titanium (alloys), mainly zirconia and alumina
facts.comparison: Titanium (alloy) abutments
facts.main_result: No difference in marginal bone level or probing depth between titanium and zirconia or alumina abutments at 1 or 5 years (zirconia MBL MD -0.24 mm, 95% CI -0.65 to 0.16).
facts.funding_coi: France Lambert receives research grants, lecturing and/or consulting fees from Straumann Group, Nobel Biocare, ITI
facts.limitations: Search limited to studies from January 2000, English only, and transmucosal components made of mixed materials excluded

facts.population: 40 dental implants with internal Morse-taper connection (in vitro)
facts.intervention: Dynamic loading in a chewing simulator (500 000 cycles of 50 N) while immersed in E. coli solution
facts.comparison: Unloaded implants in the same bacterial solution
outcomes: E. coli colonization of fixture-abutment interface (implants colonized, CFU)
facts.main_result: E. coli colonized the microgap in 1/20 unloaded vs 4/20 loaded implants (not significant by Fisher), with significantly higher CFU in the loaded group (mean 19.2 vs 3, P<.05).
materials_brands: Implant One fixtures with standard abutment (Custom Dental Implants)
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Custom Dental Implants; authors declare no commercial relationships
facts.limitations: Within the limits of the study; only minimal penetration to threaded part observed with a single bacterial species

facts.population: 20 patients with 36 two-part implants with gingivally convergent (tapered) abutments, one specialist center
facts.intervention: Implants restored with gingivally tapered/convergent abutment connection (Shelta XA)
facts.main_result: Mean marginal bone change one year after loading was -0.18 ± 0.72 mm with bone level staying above the platform (+1.16 ± 0.91 mm) and 100% survival.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 36 two-piece implants in the mandibles of six dogs
facts.intervention: Placement at bone crest, 1.5 mm subcrestal or 3.0 mm subcrestal
facts.comparison: Equicrestal placement (0 mm)
facts.main_result: Both subcrestal groups lost significantly less crestal and marginal bone than equicrestal implants, and the 3-mm group had the most bone-to-abutment contact; BIC was about 60% in all groups.
facts.funding_coi: Authors reported no conflicts of interest

facts.population: Literature on transmucosal components (abutments) and peri-implant tissues, mostly animal and some human studies
facts.intervention: Abutment type, composition, design, mobility, repeated disconnection and platform switching
facts.main_result: Severe lack of clinical information on the impact of implant type, connection and abutment composition on peri-implant bone remodelling; only one clinical study suggests one abutment-one time preserves bone.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest; supported by University of Liège and CHU de Liège
facts.limitations: Studies on platform switching are extremely heterogenous with controversial results

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Six partially edentulous patients with Brånemark implants
facts.intervention: Four titanium abutments with different surface roughness randomly placed
facts.comparison: Abutments of differing roughness compared within each patient
outcomes: probing depth, recession, bleeding on probing
facts.main_result: Smoothing below a roughness threshold had no major effect on microbiologic composition; spirochetes appeared only around the roughest abutments, which showed 0.2 mm attachment gain vs >0.8 mm loss for others.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the National Fund for Scientific Research (NFWO, Brussels)
facts.limitations: Long-term clinical observations are needed

facts.population: 167 posterior single-tooth implant restorations with CAD-CAM abutments (84 subcrestal, 83 equicrestal)
facts.intervention: Profile angle measured from implant platform or adjacent bone crest in subcrestally placed implants
facts.comparison: Equicrestally placed implants
facts.sample_size: 167 implants (84 subcrestal in 76 patients, 83 equicrestal in 73 patients)
facts.funding_coi: Yonsei-Dentium research grant; no competing interests declared

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Literature on prosthetic factors and peri-implant disease
facts.intervention: Prosthetic variables: implant position, abutment height, residual cement, splinting, occlusal forces
facts.main_result: Implant spatial positioning, abutment height, residual cement and splinting are associated with peri-implant disease pathogenesis; occlusal forces mainly affect prosthetic complications.
facts.funding_coi: Authors report no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Narrative review; too few randomized trials for a systematic review or meta-analysis

facts.journal: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
facts.intervention: Hybrid abutment design: feather-edge on buccal side and chamfer finish line on lingual side
facts.comparison: Traditional chamfer abutment design
facts.main_result: Proposes a hybrid abutment combining buccal feather-edge and palatal chamfer; no published data yet, a 5-year retrospective analysis is underway.
facts.limitations: Transfer of feather-edge results to implant abutments is not supported by published data

facts.population: Six Labrador dogs with implants placed in the mandibular premolar region
facts.intervention: Implants with abutments of titanium, zirconia or Au/Pt-alloy placed in randomized order, 5-month plaque control, histological analysis
facts.comparison: Titanium abutments compared with zirconia and gold-platinum alloy abutments
facts.main_result: Soft tissue dimensions at Ti and zirconia abutments stayed stable from 2 to 5 months, while Au/Pt-alloy abutments showed apical shift of barrier epithelium and marginal bone with less collagen and fibroblasts and more leukocytes.
facts.sample_size: 6 dogs, 47 remaining implant sites (one implant lost)
facts.follow_up: 5 months of healing (2 and 5 months assessed)

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 20 patients with a single missing maxillary central (10) or lateral (10) incisor treated with bone-level implants
facts.intervention: Soft tissue conditioning with a screw-retained implant provisional crown (dynamic compression technique), then digital volumetric analysis of the emergence profile
facts.comparison: Initial profile of the standardized circular healing abutment
outcomes: linear mesial-distal and buccal-lingual profile change
number of appointments and treatment time
facts.main_result: Supraimplant emergence profile extended by a mean 41.9 mm3 at central and 25.8 mm3 at lateral incisor sites, more than double the initial healing-abutment profile.
materials_brands: Straumann Bone Level implants (RC 4.1 mm, NC 3.3 mm)
facts.funding_coi: Financial support from Institut Straumann AG; no conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: IOS accuracy for volumetric soft tissue measurement not tested exhaustively; histologic studies needed.

facts.journal: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
facts.population: 407 patients with 1482 implants who attended the 10-year recall
facts.intervention: Implant therapy with Osseospeed implants, followed 10 years; early bone loss thresholds as predictor
facts.comparison: Implants with early bone loss above vs below thresholds of 0.5, 1 and 2 mm
facts.main_result: Implants with early bone loss of 0.5 mm or more in year one had 5.43 times higher odds of peri-implantitis; 10-year implant survival was 94.74% and peri-implantitis 11.8% of implants.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: 31.5% dropout; maintenance compliance unclear

facts.journal: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
facts.population: 20 different implant systems (13 conical, 6 flat, 1 gable-like connection), 5 implants each
facts.intervention: Dynamic and static loading up to 200 N in a chewing simulator with high-speed X-ray recording of gap length and width
facts.comparison: Conical versus flat implant-abutment connections
facts.main_result: Eight implant systems with conical connections showed no measurable gaps at 200 N, while all flat connection systems showed measurable gaps under dynamic and static loading.
facts.funding_coi: No specific grant; authors declare no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: In vitro design; clinical studies needed to state superiority of a connection type

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.main_result: About 1.5 to 2.0 mm of bone loss occurs around bone-level butt-joint implants with a contaminated interface, not seen around implants with no interface, and platform-switched connections show less bone resorption.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the ITI Foundation; no conflicts of interest

facts.population: 29 subjects with two non-adjacent implants in the esthetic zone
facts.intervention: Experimental curved abutment with circumferential groove plus temporary restoration
facts.comparison: Conventional divergent titanium abutment (control), split-mouth randomization
facts.main_result: Grooved and conventional abutments did not differ significantly in marginal recession or unseating force at 6 weeks, while angled abutments elicited labial recession.
facts.funding_coi: Nobel Biocare provided implants and abutments free of charge
outcomes: marginal mucosa level change at 6 weeks

facts.population: 26 subjects with two non-adjacent missing teeth in the esthetic zone (52 implants)
facts.intervention: Curved (concave) titanium abutment with circumferential groove
facts.comparison: Conventional divergent titanium abutment, randomized within each patient
facts.main_result: No significant difference in papilla fill between concave and conventional abutments (P = 0.25); papilla fill rose with maximum interproximal bone height.
facts.funding_coi: Grant from Smile Care, Mumbai; Nobel Biocare provided implants and abutments free
facts.limitations: Many radiographic measurements excluded because of overprojection or distortion
outcomes: maximum bone level between implant and adjacent root

facts.population: Hydroxyapatite powder (in vitro chemical model)
facts.intervention: MDP functional monomer reacted with hydroxyapatite for 5 min to 24 h, analysed by 31P CP-MAS NMR and powder XRD
facts.main_result: MDP leached Ca from HAp to form a MDP-calcium salt layered structure at short term, with CaHPO4·2H2O precipitating on it after longer reaction (up to 24 h).
facts.funding_coi: Grant-in-Aid from the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science and Medical-Techno-Okayama funds

facts.population: Adults with non-carious cervical lesions restored with composite resin (29 RCTs in meta-analysis)
facts.intervention: Self-etch adhesive strategy
facts.comparison: Etch-and-rinse adhesive strategy
facts.main_result: Self-etch and etch-and-rinse showed similar postoperative sensitivity and retention (RR 1.04), but etch-and-rinse gave less marginal discoloration at 18 months to 2 years (RR 1.51) and 4 to 5 years (RR 1.81).
facts.sample_size: 29 RCTs in the meta-analysis (42 included in the review)
facts.limitations: Review did not differentiate self-etch with mild versus strong acid

facts.main_result: Resin bond to silica-based ceramics is well documented (HF etching plus silane), whereas bonding to alumina and zirconia ceramics is less predictable and needs different methods such as airborne abrasion with phosphate-modified resin cement.
facts.sample_size: 68 articles on silica-based, 8 on alumina, 3 on zirconia ceramics
facts.limitations: Few in vitro studies on high-strength ceramics; clinical trials needed

facts.main_result: Opinion paper recommending a 3-step full etch-and-rinse route and a 3-step selective enamel etch plus 2-step self-etch route as gold standards, and appraising universal adhesives and self-adhesive restoratives.

facts.key_finding: An All-on-4 treatment concept e-book; only the title page and table of contents were extracted, so no findings are available.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: No clinical conclusion can be drawn from the extracted text.

facts.population: Edentulous patients (410 jaws, 371 patients) treated with bridges on osseointegrated titanium fixtures
facts.intervention: Osseointegrated titanium fixtures supporting bone-anchored bridges in edentulous jaws
facts.main_result: In the 5-9 year group, 81% of maxillary and 91% of mandibular fixtures remained stable; marginal bone loss was 1.5 mm in the first year, then 0.1 mm annually.
facts.sample_size: 2768 fixtures in 410 edentulous jaws of 371 patients
facts.follow_up: 1-15 years (10-15 years for the development group)

facts.key_finding: A Nobel Biocare roadmap for restoring a full arch with the All-on-4 concept, including treatment planning questions, VDO capture and an embedded clinical report of a milled titanium framework on an edentulous mandible with a 1-year follow-up.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Plan esthetics, function and vertical dimension before surgery, then load four implants (two tilted) with a provisional prosthesis.

facts.population: 156 consecutive fully edentulous patients
facts.intervention: Fixed prostheses on 4 or 6 screw-shaped titanium Branemark implants
facts.comparison: Prostheses on 4 implants versus 6 implants
facts.main_result: Survival of prostheses and of individual implants was the same with 4 or 6 implants at 10 years (implant survival lower jaw 88.4% vs 93.2%, upper jaw 80.3% vs 78.3%).
facts.sample_size: 156 patients; mandible 13 prostheses on 4 and 59 on 6 implants, maxilla 14 and 70
facts.limitations: Smoking habits and surgical aspects such as dehiscences or fenestrations could not be analyzed.

facts.key_finding: A laboratory step-by-step restorative protocol for a BruxZir all-zirconia fixed full-arch implant prosthesis, from preliminary impression through verification jig and final impression.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: At least 10 mm of vertical clearance is needed, and a verification jig is used to obtain a passive fit.

facts.key_finding: A laboratory step-by-step restorative protocol for a BruxZir all-zirconia fixed full-arch implant prosthesis, from preliminary impression through verification jig and final impression.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: At least 10 mm of vertical clearance is needed, and a verification jig is used to obtain a passive fit.

facts.key_finding: A laboratory step-by-step restorative protocol for a BruxZir all-zirconia fixed full-arch implant prosthesis, from preliminary impression through verification jig and final impression.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: At least 10 mm of vertical clearance is needed, and a verification jig is used to obtain a passive fit.

facts.main_result: After 1.2 million wear cycles BruxZir showed barely detectable wear (1 ± 1 µm) versus 54 ± 22 µm for Ceramco 3.
facts.funding_coi: Wear test sponsored by Glidewell Laboratories (manufacturer)
facts.key_finding: A manufacturer compendium for the BruxZir full-arch implant prosthesis, bundling laboratory wear, translucency and strength data and reprinted studies.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: The manufacturer positions the fixed all-zirconia prosthesis as stronger and more wear-resistant than an acrylic-metal hybrid.

facts.key_finding: A one-page guide on cementing or bonding BruxZir zirconia crowns with Ceramir, resin-modified glass ionomer or resin cements.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Clean the intaglio by sandblasting or Ivoclean, avoid phosphoric acid, and use zirconia primer only with resin cements.

facts.population: Four healthy non-smoking adults aged 45-74 with severely worn dentition
facts.intervention: Digital CAD/CAM chairside full-mouth rehabilitation protocol
facts.main_result: All four patients maintained the result at two years with almost 100% cumulative survival; one veneer chipped.

facts.population: 30 patients with totally edentulous mandible at three Italian centers
facts.intervention: Five inter-foraminal 6-mm-short implants with screw-retained full-arch prosthesis with distal cantilevers
facts.comparison: Five 11-mm-long implants with the same prosthesis
facts.main_result: No implant or prosthesis loss; MBLc at 3 years -0.10 mm (6 mm) vs 0.02 mm (11 mm), not significantly different
facts.sample_size: 30 patients, 150 implants (28 patients, 140 implants at 3 years)
facts.limitations: Non-standardized radiographs and short 3-year follow-up

facts.population: 25 consecutively treated fully edentulous patients (both jaws)
facts.intervention: Immediately loaded bimaxillary screw-retained metal-resin prostheses on two mandibular and three maxillary flapless-placed implants
facts.main_result: No prosthesis or implant failed and no patient dropped out at 6 months; three complications in two patients, all treated
materials_brands: Syra and Syra SL implants (Sweden & Martina)
facts.funding_coi: Self-financed, no financial support
facts.limitations: Short follow-up and single operator

facts.population: 10 edentulous patients (average age 68), 58 implants
facts.intervention: Implant-supported hybrid full-arch restorations with CAD/CAM-milled titanium frameworks (seven) and composite or ceramic veneering
facts.comparison: Cast chromium-cobalt frameworks (four designs); composite versus ceramic veneering
facts.main_result: 100% implant success at 40 months; prosthetic complications (screw fracture/loosening, chipping, debonding) only in cast restorations, none in milled ones

facts.population: One 55-year-old male with severely worn dentition
facts.intervention: Full-mouth reconstruction with PFM crowns after seating condyles in centric relation to gain restorative space without changing VDO
facts.main_result: Seating the condyles in centric relation gained 2.38 mm of anterior space without altering VDO
facts.funding_coi: Author declares no financial interest in any product

facts.population: 48 fully edentulous patients (24 maxillae, 24 mandibles) in 6 centres
facts.intervention: Immediately loaded metal-resin screw-retained cross-arch prosthesis on three implants (fixed-on-3)
facts.comparison: Same prosthesis on four implants (fixed-on-4)
facts.main_result: Implant and prosthesis failures did not differ significantly; at 1 year Fo3 implants lost 0.22 mm bone vs 0.40 mm for Fo4 (P=0.006)
facts.sample_size: 48 patients (24 per group), 72 implants in Fo3
materials_brands: Syra and Syra SL tapered implants (Sweden & Martina)
facts.limitations: Preliminary 1-year results; longer follow-up needed

facts.intervention: CAD/CAM titanium bar and acrylic hybrid denture at abutment level, delivered over six appointments
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare CT protocol / NobelClinician software
facts.key_finding: A dental laboratory (Haupt Dental Lab) protocol describing the appointment-by-appointment steps for a CAD/CAM titanium bar and acrylic hybrid denture on implants at abutment level, from diagnostics and CT planning to pick-up impression, passive-fit verification and delivery, plus a price list.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Passive fit of the titanium bar is critical; verify it with a quarter-turn screw test and torque the final prosthesis screws to 15 Ncm.

facts.intervention: Straight and angled (17 or 30 degree) multi-unit abutment placement with closed-tray and open-tray abutment-level impressions
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare Multi-unit Abutment (NobelReplace, Conical Connection, Branemark System)
facts.key_finding: Nobel Biocare quick guide giving step-by-step placement of straight and angled multi-unit abutments and closed-tray and open-tray abutment-level impression techniques, with a product list.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Tighten straight multi-unit abutment screws to 35 Ncm and angled ones to 15 Ncm (not more), and verify seating radiographically before impression.

facts.population: Patients with implant-supported fixed complete-arch prostheses in 93 included studies (maxilla and mandible)
facts.intervention: Fewer than five implants per arch supporting a complete-arch fixed prosthesis
facts.comparison: Five or more implants per arch
facts.main_result: No significant difference in implant or prosthesis survival between fewer than five and five or more implants per arch (p > 0.05), median follow-up 8 years

facts.intervention: Clear thermoformed co-polyester comfort bite splint (hard, or hard with soft inner surface) made on stone models with an open construction bite
facts.key_finding: Manufacturer clinical guide to prescribing clear thermoformed comfort bite splints for bruxism and clenching: a two-appointment technique with open construction bite registration, alginate impressions, thermoforming, trimming and polishing, and fit and occlusion check.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Record an open construction bite in centric relation (about 3 mm opening) with alginate impressions, then check fit and premature contacts with marking tape at delivery.

facts.intervention: Thermoforming technique for dental appliances (splints, trays, mouthguards, retainers, templates) with Erkodent materials and the Occluform device
facts.key_finding: Erkodent instruction brochure covering thermoforming principles and step-by-step fabrication of occlusal and bruxism splints, bleaching and fluoride trays, mouthguards, orthodontic appliances and implant templates, with material recommendations by application.
