facts.clinical_bottom_line: Use hard plaster models permeable to air and choose foil thickness per application (e.g. 1.5-5.0 mm hard Erkodur for occlusal splints); 1 cm model height costs 20-25% of foil thickness.

facts.key_finding: Manufacturer guide describing how Transition crowns and bridges, thermo-pressed polyoxymethylene provisionals, are prepared, tried in, relined and cemented as interim or long-term provisional restorations where permanent restorations are not viable.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Product protocol only; no outcome data are reported, so it supports technique steps rather than clinical evidence.

facts.population: U-shaped polyurethane model simulating mandibular bone with two implants (3.75 mm)
facts.intervention: Cantilevered frameworks in CoCr or PdAg loaded at 5, 10 or 15 mm of cantilever arm
facts.comparison: CoCr versus PdAg alloy at the same cantilever distances
facts.main_result: CoCr showed larger compression than PdAg at equal cantilever distances, and deformation increased with cantilever length (Pearson correlation).
facts.sample_size: Six groups, two implants in one polyurethane model, eight strain gauges
facts.funding_coi: FAPESP grants
facts.limitations: Conclusions drawn under the limited conditions of this in vitro study

facts.key_finding: Nobel Biocare procedure manual for the Trefoil system: three implants placed between the mental foramina in fully edentulous mandibles with guide templates and a pre-designed prosthetic bar, with surgical and prosthetic steps.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Product protocol with indications and contraindications; it contains no clinical outcome data.

facts.population: Six dogs with chronic ridge defects
facts.intervention: Collagen matrix (CM) augmentation of chronic ridge defects
facts.comparison: Autogenous subepithelial connective tissue graft (SCTG) and sham-operated control
outcomes: soft tissue volume change at 28 and 84 days (optical scan of casts)
facts.main_result: At 84 days CM gained 1.4 mm and SCTG 1.4 mm in volume per area versus a 0.3 mm loss in controls (p<0.001).
materials_brands: Prototype collagen matrix of porcine collagen (Geistlich)
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Swiss CTI, Geistlich Pharma AG and University of Zurich; two authors are Geistlich employees
Workshop supported by an unrestricted grant from Geistlich AB; authors disclose Geistlich, Straumann, Nobelbiocare and others

facts.population: 16 patients with bilateral Miller Class I/II gingival recessions
facts.intervention: Acellular dermal matrix allograft (ADMA)
facts.comparison: Subepithelial connective tissue graft (SCTG), split-mouth
facts.main_result: At 5 years complete root coverage was 20.0% (ADMA) versus 13.3% (SCTG) with no significant difference; both showed significant relapse.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by Dental Research Center of Tehran University of Medical Sciences; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Within the limitations of this study (not specified further)

off_topic_reason: Covers medical soft tissue repair (hernia, dural, urological) with no dental or oral application.

facts.journal: Extracellular Matrix-derived Implants in Clinical Medicine
facts.key_finding: Book chapter reviewing allografts and xenografts used in general soft tissue repair (dermis, pericardium, intestinal submucosa), their tissue sources, processing, products and future trends; it notes that strong clinical evidence is often lacking.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Product choice should rest on clinical evidence and cost rather than marketing; the chapter is mostly about non-dental (e.g. abdominal wall) repair.

facts.journal: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.population: 300 patients undergoing extraction of one maxillary tooth (anterior, premolar, molar strata)
facts.intervention: Buccal infiltration of 0.6 mL 4% articaine
facts.comparison: Buccal infiltration of 0.6 mL 2% lidocaine
facts.main_result: Buccal infiltration achieved palatal anesthesia in 82.7% with articaine versus 1.3% with lidocaine (P<.001).
facts.funding_coi: Financial support from Mashhad University of Medical Sciences (grant 961221)
Authors report no commercial, proprietary or financial interest

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.intervention: Modified impression post made on a PVS index of the provisional crown to transfer emergence profile
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.journal: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 20 healthy patients (13 females, 7 males), mean age 27.7 years, with healthy gingiva and unrestored maxillary anterior teeth (240 sites)
facts.intervention: Measurement on stone casts with digital calipers of gingival zenith position from the vertical bisected midline of each maxillary anterior tooth, and gingival zenith level of the lateral incisors relative to the line joining adjacent central and canine zeniths
outcomes: gingival zenith position (medial-lateral) per tooth group
gingival zenith level of lateral incisors (apical-coronal)
facts.main_result: Central incisor zeniths lay a mean 1 mm distal to the midline, lateral incisors 0.4 mm, canines were centred (97.5%), and lateral incisor zeniths were about 1 mm coronal to the line joining adjacent central and canine zeniths.
materials_brands: Jeltrate irreversible hydrocolloid impression material (Dentsply Caulk)
facts.funding_coi: Authors declare no financial interest in companies whose materials are included

facts.journal: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Lay public respondents to a web survey; 1934 from the United States and Canada analyzed (2185 valid responses from 45 countries)
facts.intervention: Web page showing five pairs of digitally altered anterior-tooth images (flat incisal embrasures, midline diastema, whiter teeth, altered proportion, midline discrepancy) ranked by respondents
facts.comparison: Within each pair, the altered image versus the unaltered one, rated on a five-point preference scale
outcomes: effect of age, gender, race and last dental visit on preference
facts.main_result: Strongest preferences were against diastema and midline shift and weakest for whiteness and proportion; females had stronger preferences, as did those under 40 for whiteness and against diastema.
facts.sample_size: 2185 valid respondents; 1934 from the US and Canada analyzed

facts.population: Illustrative clinical case of a patient treated with ceramic veneers using the DSD protocol (no formal sample)
facts.intervention: Digital Smile Design protocol: reference lines and shapes drawn over extra- and intraoral photographs in presentation software, transferred to cast, diagnostic wax-up, mock-up/provisional, then minimally invasive veneer preparation
facts.main_result: The authors describe DSD as a multi-use tool improving the team's understanding of esthetic issues and patient acceptance; no quantitative results reported.

facts.population: Dentists contacted by e-mail; 549 valid responses from 38 countries, 470 from the US or Canada
facts.intervention: Web page with computer-manipulated images of the 6 maxillary anterior teeth at 5 tooth heights, each in 4 proportions (62% golden, 70%, 80%, normal), ranked best to worst
facts.comparison: Four proportions compared within each tooth-height group (golden proportion vs 70% vs 80% vs normal)
outcomes: best and worst ranking of proportion per height group
association with gender, experience, specialty, patient load
facts.main_result: Dentists preferred the 80% proportion for short and very short teeth and the golden proportion for very tall teeth; golden proportion was worst for normal or shorter teeth.

facts.population: Orthodontic casts of 58 second-year dental students (University of Southern California)
facts.intervention: Measurement of apparent tooth widths on video-captured cast images (58) and direct caliper measurement of casts (52) to test golden proportion ratios between maxillary and mandibular incisors and canines
facts.main_result: Golden proportion (1.59-1.65:1) was found in the perceived maxillary central:lateral incisor ratio in only 10 of 58 images (17%) and in no lateral incisor:canine ratio.
materials_brands: Dental Dial Caliper (Masel Industries) with modified tips
facts.limitations: Sample size was limited (author's statement)

facts.journal: bpacnz (Best Practice Advocacy Centre New Zealand)
facts.population: Typical patients (adults and children) with infections commonly seen in general practice
facts.intervention: Consensus first-choice and alternative antibiotic regimens, with doses and durations, per infection (dental section covers dental abscess and endocarditis prophylaxis)
facts.main_result: Consensus guide recommending prescribing antibiotics only for significant or high-risk bacterial infections, using first-line narrow agents at recommended dose and duration.
facts.limitations: Individual patient circumstances and local resistance patterns may alter treatment choices.

facts.population: Oral cavity bacterial infections (dental caries, gingivitis, periodontitis, dental abscess) and their causative organisms; no study sample
facts.main_result: Oral bacterial infections are caused by many species; diagnosis is usually clinical but microbiologic diagnosis and susceptibility testing should guide antimicrobial choice to limit resistance.
facts.funding_coi: Authors declare nothing to disclose

facts.population: 263 patients (aged 10-79) treated at a cranio-maxillofacial department and outpatient clinic, 2013-2014; 485 cultured bacterial and fungal strains, mainly from submandibular and submental abscess pus
facts.intervention: Microbial culture and antibiogram analysis with a cost-minimisation model combining antibiotic efficacy, price and hospital cost per patient-day
facts.comparison: Sensitivity of Gram-positive vs Gram-negative bacteria and of antibiotics against each other (nine antimicrobial agents)
facts.main_result: Most common pathogens were S. epidermidis (18%), Str. mitis/oralis (14%) and S. aureus (6.5%); gentamycin, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole and vancomycin were cheapest per effective therapy.

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 54 patients with histologically and clinically proven chronic osteomyelitis of the mandible or maxilla from three maxillofacial departments in Israel (14 implant-induced)
facts.intervention: Primary treatment of debridement and antibiotic therapy; failures treated with mandibulectomy or maxillectomy
facts.comparison: Implant-induced osteomyelitis versus other etiologic groups (extraction, fracture, cyst, infected teeth)
facts.main_result: 40 patients remitted with primary treatment and 14 failed; a previous dental implant was an independent predictor of failure (P = .0001).
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: 38 healthy individuals receiving platform-switched implants (37 completed)
facts.intervention: Preoperative 2 g amoxicillin plus 7 days postoperative amoxicillin 500 mg tid
facts.comparison: Same preoperative amoxicillin dose followed by an identical postoperative placebo
outcomes: peri-implant crestal bone change at 1 year
facts.main_result: One-year crestal bone change was -0.44 ± 0.41 mm (antibiotic) vs -0.27 ± 0.56 mm (placebo), not significantly different; morbidity did not differ and survival was 100% in both groups.
materials_brands: OsseoSpeed TX or Astra EV implants (Dentsply Sirona)
facts.funding_coi: Supported by an Université de Montréal faculty research fund; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Small sample precludes generalization and an accurate implant survival rate; chlorhexidine rinse use was not logged.

facts.population: 236 medically and periodontally healthy patients receiving oral implants with simultaneous GBR at seven centres
facts.intervention: Systemic amoxicillin: 2 g one hour before surgery, then 500 mg three times daily on days 1-3
facts.comparison: Placebo
outcomes: PROMs (VAS pain, swelling, haematoma, bleeding, days 1-7 and 14)
facts.main_result: No statistically significant difference between antibiotic and placebo groups for PROMs or post-surgical complications (p > .05); 4 implants lost (3 test, 1 control).
facts.funding_coi: ITI Foundation research grant; Geistlich, Medochemie and Straumann supplied materials/medication; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Larger sample sizes are still required to support the clinical outcomes.

facts.population: Dental implant patients with a self-reported penicillin allergy
facts.intervention: Peri-operative penicillin (amoxicillin)
facts.comparison: Peri-operative clindamycin
facts.main_result: Patients given clindamycin because of self-reported penicillin allergy had over three times the odds of implant failure (OR 3.30, 95% CI 2.58-4.22).
facts.funding_coi: Authors declare no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Evidence is limited and based on retrospective observational studies.

facts.population: 8 beagle dogs, 64 implants in mandibular premolar regions
facts.intervention: Plateau root form (PRF, Bicon) titanium implants
facts.comparison: Screw root form (SRF, Straumann) implants
facts.main_result: BIC and BAFO tended to be greater for SRF but not significantly (P=0.07, P=0.06); both increased significantly with time and progressed in parallel.
materials_brands: Straumann Standard Plus Narrow Neck SLA implants
facts.limitations: BIC and BAFO reflect structural connection, not the functional properties of the bone-implant interface.

facts.population: 108 patients with 228 implants (posterior maxilla restorations)
facts.intervention: OsseoSpeed implants with internal conical connection and LILAC uni-abutments of different heights, giving different mismatching distances
facts.comparison: 4.5 mm vs 5 mm diameter implants (different mismatching distances); short vs long abutments
outcomes: marginal bone loss at 6 and 18 months post-loading
facts.main_result: Greater mismatching did not reduce MBL; MBL was greater with short abutments, grafted bone, heavier smoking and 5.0 mm implants.
facts.funding_coi: Research groups grant (Junta de Andalucia); authors declare no financial interest in listed products
facts.limitations: Results should be interpreted with caution and validated in wider randomized clinical trials.

facts.journal: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
facts.population: 219 patients with 270 single-tooth Branemark implants (215 upper jaw)
facts.intervention: Single-implant restorations on Branemark System implants
facts.main_result: Cumulative success 93% for implants and 96.5% for restorations over 11 years; bone loss 0.71 mm in first 6 months then 0.036 mm/year.

facts.population: Ten female Göttingen minipigs (nine analysed), healed mandibular ridges
facts.intervention: Fully tapered BLX implants placed at inter-implant thread-peak distances of 1, 2, 3 mm and at 3 distances from outer buccal bone
facts.comparison: Different thread-peak distances compared with each other
facts.main_result: Inter-implant bone height was maintained even at 1 mm thread-peak distance; buccal bone resorption was significant when thread-peak to outer buccal bone distance was < 0.5 mm.
materials_brands: Straumann BLX Roxolid SLActive 4.5 x 8 mm
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the Straumann Group; authors received no payment

facts.population: Partially edentulous patients with bone-level implants, University of Michigan clinics
facts.intervention: Groups by transmucosal abutment height (>2 mm vs <2 mm) and restorative emergence angle (<30 vs >=30 degrees)
facts.comparison: Long/Narrow, Long/Wide, Short/Narrow and Short/Wide groups compared
facts.main_result: Short abutment with wide emergence angle (SW) had 0.25-0.48 mm greater MBL than other groups and about 4 times the likelihood of peri-implantitis.
facts.follow_up: at least one year after T0 (T0 at 12-18 months after crown placement)
facts.funding_coi: No specific funding

facts.population: 5 beagle dogs, 6 Branemark implants each in the mandible
facts.intervention: Abutment connection after surgically thinning the ridge mucosa (test side)
facts.comparison: Contralateral control side with standard abutment connection
facts.main_result: Where ridge mucosa was thin (<=2 mm), wound healing consistently included bone resorption and an angular bone defect.

facts.population: 5 minipigs, 4 implants each placed flapless in the mandible
facts.intervention: Platform-switched implants (0.25 mm mismatch) placed flush, 1 mm below or 1 mm above the bone crest
facts.comparison: Conventionally restored implant at bone level
facts.main_result: Platform switching resulted in less crestal resorption (0.58 mm less); effect on biologic width limited to a shorter epithelial attachment when placed at crest level.

Narrative conclusion: CAD/CAM zirconia-based restorations give better marginal fit, less inflammation and better periodontal health and hygiene than conventional constructions, and supragingival margins are better than subgingival ones.
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest declared

facts.journal: The Journal of the American Dental Association
outcomes: evidence on gingival retraction techniques for implant versus tooth impressions
facts.main_result: The authors found insufficient evidence on gingival displacement techniques for impression making in implant dentistry; retraction methods are designed for natural teeth and further research and product development are needed.
facts.funding_coi: No disclosures reported
facts.limitations: No rigorous selection protocol was applied; all references were accepted because the literature on implants was scarce.

facts.population: 11 patients (27-77 years) each receiving two ITI implants in the same quadrant
facts.intervention: ITI implants placed with the polished-surface border about 1 mm subcrestal
facts.comparison: Control implants with the rough/smooth border at the alveolar crest
facts.main_result: Test implants lost 2.26 mm and control implants 1.02 mm of bone height in the first year; test implants' bone level was 0.38 mm lower at 12 months.
facts.funding_coi: Clinical Research Foundation (CRF), University of Bern

facts.population: Eight adult beagle dogs; implants placed in healed mandibular sites
facts.intervention: Tissue-level implant with a convergent transmucosal neck (Prama-type design)
facts.comparison: Conventional bone-level implant with cylindrical machined titanium abutment
facts.main_result: At 4 and 12 weeks there were no statistically significant differences between test and control implants in peri-implant hard and soft tissue height and thickness; test implants tended to have a more coronal free gingival margin and first bone contact.
facts.sample_size: 16 test and 16 control implants in 8 dogs
facts.funding_coi: Partially funded by a research contract with Sweden & Martina Dental Implants
facts.limitations: Animal model with a reduced sample size, so the null hypothesis could not be rejected.

facts.population: Nine dogs; mandibular premolar sockets

facts.funding_coi: Material support from Ribbond Inc. and Kuraray

facts.intervention: Biomimetic restorative protocols: 10 stress-reducing and 8 bond-maximizing protocols, illustrated by one case
facts.main_result: The authors present biomimetic restorative dentistry as combining stress-reducing and bond-maximizing protocols to increase restoration longevity, supported by 10 to 17 year old cases.

facts.population: Extracted sound human premolars and third molars, ground buccal enamel surfaces
facts.intervention: Two-step self-etching adhesives with MDP or Phenyl-P functional monomer in primer and/or bond (M-M, M-P, P-M, P-P)
facts.comparison: Clearfil SE Bond with MDP in both primer and bond (M-M) as control
facts.main_result: An acid-base resistant zone formed with every MDP-containing system but not with Phenyl-P in both (P-P); micro-shear bond strength was highest in M-M (43.08 MPa vs 33.29-36.12 MPa).
facts.sample_size: 20 third molars and 30 premolars; n = 10 per group for bond strength
facts.funding_coi: Chinese Government Graduate Student Overseas Study Program, GCOE Program (TMDU), JSPS grant

facts.population: Experimental barium glass filled Bis-GMA/TEGDMA composite (70 wt% resin, 30 wt% filler) disk specimens
facts.intervention: Irradiation for 2, 3, 6, 10 or 60 s at 450 mW/cm2 with simultaneous real-time shrinkage stress and NIR double bond conversion monitoring
facts.comparison: Different irradiation times against each other (60 s as full cure)
facts.main_result: 60 s irradiation gave the highest conversion (67.9%) and stress (2.9 MPa); stress relaxation occurred only before vitrification (up to about 40% at 2 s) and gave no significant benefit at clinically relevant conversion.
materials_brands: Bis-GMA/TEGDMA 70/30 experimental resin with barium glass filler (Schott)
facts.funding_coi: NIH and Department of Education grant DE10959; monomers and filler donated by Esstech and Confi-Dental

facts.main_result: Wet bonding, chlorhexidine, rubber dam, 'gold-standard' adhesives, sclerotic dentin roughening and bonding strategy lack RCT support for better restoration longevity, so the null hypothesis should be kept.
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no conflicts declared

facts.population: Extracted caries-free human third molars (occlusal deep coronal dentine), plus processed composite as a substrate
facts.intervention: Six single-step adhesives bonded to hydrated dentine, dehydrated dentine or processed composite, with immediate or 20 min delayed light-activation of the overlying composite
facts.comparison: Three-step adhesive All-Bond 2 as control; immediate versus delayed light-activation
facts.main_result: Delayed light-activation significantly lowered bond strength of all six single-step adhesives on hydrated dentine but not of the control three-step adhesive, nor on dehydrated dentine or processed composite.
facts.sample_size: 34 third molars (28 in experiment I, 4 groups of 2 teeth per adhesive subgroup); 20-23 beams per subgroup
facts.funding_coi: University of Hong Kong CRC grant, CNPq (Brazil) and NIDCR DE 06427; materials supplied by Sun Medical, Tokuyama, Shofu; one author at Bisco
facts.limitations: The 20 min delay is far removed from clinical practice (clinicians rarely leave composite unactivated more than 2-3 min).

facts.population: 43 Class II restorations in 22 patients (mean age 30 years), mostly molars
facts.intervention: Class II restorations of a fine particle hybrid composite (Tetric) placed with a decoupling incremental technique using polyurethane varnish to separate the gingival increment
facts.main_result: 41 of 43 restorations were reviewed at 18 months and 31 at 3 to 4 years; none showed significant deterioration, with no secondary caries or postoperative sensitivity.
facts.limitations: Single-center, practice-based explanatory study in selected patients; the authors call for a multicentered randomized controlled trial.

facts.main_result: Adhesive developments and adherend modifications allow bonding to metal and porcelain with enamel-like adhesion, with tooth conservation as the main advantage.
facts.funding_coi: Author owns stock in Danville Materials Inc.

facts.population: Caries-free extracted human premolars (dentin)
facts.intervention: Two all-in-one adhesives applied to dentin, followed by an acid-base challenge and SEM/TEM examination of the interface
facts.comparison: Clearfil Tri-S Bond versus G-Bond
outcomes: acid-base resistant zone morphology and thickness (SEM, TEM)
facts.main_result: An acid-base resistant zone formed beneath the hybrid layer with both adhesives, and its morphology was material dependent (about 300 nm with Clearfil Tri-S Bond versus about 100 nm with G-Bond on TEM).
facts.sample_size: 12 premolars for SEM and 6 for TEM
facts.funding_coi: Supported by a Global Center of Excellence program and a JSPS grant

facts.population: Two clinical cases (posterior teeth with large defects)
facts.intervention: First-appointment protocol for bonded indirect restorations: cavity preparation, immediate dentin sealing, impression and provisionalization
facts.main_result: Describes an updated first-appointment technique for bonded indirect restorations, sealing dentin with adhesive and a thin composite layer before impression and nonluted provisional placement.

facts.key_finding: A product table of bonding agents available in the Iranian market, grouped by adhesive class (etch-and-rinse 3-step and 2-step, self-etch 1- and 2-bottle, universal, unfilled resin) with brand and manufacturer.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: A product lookup for matching an available bonding agent to its adhesive class; it contains no clinical data.

facts.key_finding: A product table of primers (mostly silane, some with MDP or metal-primer monomers) available in the Iranian market, listing brand, country, functional monomer, volume and notes.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: A product lookup for choosing a ceramic or metal primer by functional monomer; it contains no clinical data.

authors: Wellington Luiz de Oliveira da Rosa
facts.population: In vitro studies of universal adhesive bond strength to enamel (shear) and dentin (microtensile) in sound permanent teeth
facts.intervention: Etch-and-rinse strategy (prior acid etching) with universal adhesives
facts.comparison: Self-etch strategy
facts.main_result: Etch-and-rinse improved enamel bond strength of universal adhesives and dentin bond strength for ultra-mild and intermediately strong ones; intermediately strong adhesives lost bond strength after aging while mild adhesives stayed stable (p < 0.05).
facts.sample_size: 59 in vitro studies in the meta-analysis
facts.funding_coi: Financed in part by CAPES and CNPq (Brazil)
facts.limitations: Most included in vitro studies scored poorly on selective reporting and examiner blinding.

facts.main_result: The review describes all generations and types of adhesive systems introduced over the last 30 years, from etch-and-rinse and self-etch to universal multi-mode adhesives.

facts.population: 60 extracted impacted molars (wisdom teeth) with large occlusal-proximal cavities
facts.intervention: Whole-ceramic inlays restored with the biomimetic adhesive method (bio-base of immediate dentin sealing and fluid composite)
facts.comparison: Classical method of ceramic inlay restoration; also Variolink Esthetic DC versus Maxcem Elite cement
outcomes: integrity and quality of cementing material
facts.main_result: The biomimetic method gave superior layer integrity; defects (microfissures, detached cement fragments) were about 2 times larger with the classical method, and Maxcem Elite showed discontinuities at the cement-inlay interface.

facts.population: Partially demineralized collagen matrices prepared from human dentin
facts.intervention: Storage of acid-etched demineralized dentin matrices in artificial saliva for 24 hrs, 90 and 250 days
facts.comparison: Artificial saliva with proteolytic enzyme inhibitors, or pure mineral oil
facts.main_result: Matrices were almost completely destroyed after 250 days in artificial saliva but not with enzyme inhibitors or mineral oil; dentin powder collagenolytic activity was inhibited 73% by protease inhibitors and to near zero by 0.2% chlorhexidine.
facts.sample_size: 8 per assay condition for the collagenolytic assay
facts.funding_coi: Supported by NIDCR grants and the Faculty of Dentistry, University of Hong Kong

facts.population: Composite cylinders (in vitro specimens) of a microfilled hybrid resin
facts.intervention: Surface treatments (air abrasion, HCl/HF etching, diamond bur roughening with or without phosphoric acid) before repair with Prime & Bond NT, with the adhesive cured in air or under nitrogen
facts.comparison: Different surface treatments against each other, and air versus nitrogen curing of the adhesive
facts.main_result: Air abrasion gave the highest bond strength (43.2 MPa in air, 42.4 MPa in nitrogen) while the other treatments were comparable (about 33 to 38 MPa); curing atmosphere had no significant effect.

facts.population: Teeth with dentinogenesis imperfecta or dentine dysplasia (37 in vitro studies, 164 teeth)
facts.intervention: Systematic review of enamel, dentine-enamel junction and dentine microstructure and properties in dentine disorders
facts.comparison: Normal (unaffected) tissue where available; DI versus OI compared by Mann-Whitney U test
facts.main_result: Dentine and the dentine-enamel junction are damaged in dentinogenesis imperfecta and osteogenesis imperfecta, and enamel is affected in dentinogenesis imperfecta (p = 0.0013) but not in osteogenesis imperfecta (p = 0.056).
facts.funding_coi: No competing interests declared
facts.limitations: The recommendations are mostly based on in vitro studies, with very few comparison samples and no blinded testing.

facts.main_result: Adhesive systems allow safe bonding of composite to enamel and dentin and more conservative cavities, but technique and ideal bonding conditions remain essential.
facts.funding_coi: No financial support and no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Success of adhesive materials in vitro should be supported by clinical follow-up of long-term durability.

facts.population: Published dentin bond strength data for six adhesives (147 references)
facts.intervention: Literature search pooling dentin bond strength data from shear, microshear, tensile and microtensile tests
facts.comparison: The four test methods compared with each other
facts.main_result: Bond strength data remain highly scattered whichever adhesive or test is used (coefficients of variation 20-50% even for microtensile), and product ranking depends on the test.

facts.population: Dentin surfaces of extracted human third molars
facts.intervention: Two-step self-etch adhesives (Clearfil SE Bond, FL-Bond, FL-Bond II) bonded to flat dentin, then acid-base challenge
facts.comparison: Fluoride-free Clearfil SE Bond versus fluoride-releasing FL-Bond and FL-Bond II
facts.main_result: Clearfil SE Bond had higher microtensile bond strength (46.3 MPa) than FL-Bond (31.3 MPa) and FL-Bond II (34.2 MPa), and an acid-base resistant zone formed in all groups but depended on the material.
facts.sample_size: 15 human third molars, 20 specimens per adhesive

facts.population: Three-dimensional finite element models of cervical dentine and 12 extracted single-rooted teeth (dentine slabs)
facts.intervention: Finite element simulation with or without hydrostatic pressure and elastic modulus gradient, compression testing and FTIR of hydrated dentine
facts.comparison: Hydrated versus partially dehydrated dentine; models with versus without hydrostatic pressure
outcomes: principal and von Mises stresses and strains
facts.main_result: Partially dehydrated dentine fractured at higher stress (157.8 vs 53.1 MPa, p = 0.014) while hydrated dentine tolerated higher strain at fracture (9.6 vs 3.7%, p = 0.037).

facts.population: Bovine incisor crowns, sound or artificially demineralized, with standardized Class V cavities
facts.intervention: Selective enamel etching with phosphoric acid for 10, 30, 60 or 120 s before a one-step or two-step self-etch adhesive and composite restoration
facts.comparison: Non-etched groups and sound versus demineralized enamel; iBond Self Etch versus Clearfil SE Bond
outcomes: percentage of continuous margins (%CM) on SEM
facts.main_result: Phosphoric acid etching significantly increased the percentage of continuous margins in both demineralized and sound enamel, and pre-etched demineralized enamel reached similar margin integrity to sound etched enamel.
facts.sample_size: 140 bovine incisor crowns in 14 groups of 10
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest

facts.population: 48 endodontically treated human upper molars
facts.intervention: Adhesive overlay or full crown preparation restored with high translucency zirconia or zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate, cemented and fatigue-loaded
facts.comparison: Low-retentive overlay versus high-retentive crown design; HTZ versus ZLS
outcomes: three-dimensional external gap progression by micro-CT
facts.main_result: External gap progression was lower for the full crown design than the overlay (p < 0.01) and lower for ZLS than HTZ (p < 0.01), the largest value being HTZ overlays (0.16 mm3).
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts declared; open access funding by Projekt DEAL
facts.limitations: Quantitative gap thresholding was harder in HTZ because of X-ray scatter artifacts.

facts.intervention: Ten light-activated restorative materials (3 RMGICs, 3 compomers, 4 resin composites) placed and light-cured; marginal gap, shrinkage-strain and shear bond strength measured
facts.comparison: Comparison among the ten materials and correlation between gap in tooth cavity, Teflon cavity gap, diametral shrinkage-strain and bond strength
outcomes: shear bond strength to enamel and dentin
facts.main_result: Marginal gap in tooth cavity correlated strongly with free shrinkage in Teflon cavity (r=0.914) but not with diametral shrinkage-strain or shear bond strength to enamel or dentin.
facts.sample_size: 10 specimens per material, 10 materials (100 cavities in 100 teeth)
facts.follow_up: Measured 3 min after start of light-activation

facts.main_result: Resin-dentin bond degradation involves hydrolysis of resin and collagen plus host proteases, and inhibiting collagenolytic activity or cross-linking collagen are the two main strategies to protect the hybrid layer.

facts.population: 2,157 dentin bond-strength tests extracted from 298 papers
facts.intervention: Systematic collection of dentin bond-strength data for current adhesive classes and neural-network modelling of influencing variables
facts.main_result: Research group and adhesive brand were the most determining variables for dentin bond strength; the mean best adhesive was almost twice the least-performing one, and bond strength decreased with water storage.
facts.funding_coi: K.U. Leuven Research Grant; authors declare no conflicts of interest
outcomes: effect of adhesive class, aging, storage time and research group

facts.population: Extracted human molars with coronal dentine caries (caries-affected vs normal dentine)
facts.intervention: Bonding with 2 total-etch and 2 self-etch adhesives, microtensile testing, DIAGNOdent laser fluorescence and Knoop microhardness of the substrate
facts.comparison: Normal dentine; total-etch vs self-etch adhesives
facts.main_result: All adhesives bonded better to normal than caries-affected dentine (e.g. Prime & Bond NT 56.3 vs 41.3 MPa), significant only for Prime & Bond NT and Clearfil SE Bond; total-etch adhesives outperformed self-etch ones.
facts.sample_size: 16 molars, 4 per adhesive, about 10 slabs per group
facts.funding_coi: NIDCR grant DEO14911 and CICYT (Spain) grant

facts.population: Two functional monomers (4-META, MDP) with atelocollagen as a triple-helical peptide model
facts.intervention: Saturation transfer difference NMR spectroscopy of monomer-collagen binding
facts.comparison: 4-META versus MDP
facts.main_result: MDP showed high STD intensities in its aliphatic protons (73.9% to 100%), indicating stable hydrophobic interaction with collagen, while 4-META showed no intense STD signals.
facts.funding_coi: GCOE program and JSPS grant; no conflicts of interest declared
outcomes: STD NMR signal intensities per proton

facts.main_result: Self-etch adhesives are promising because they are easy to use, bond chemically to tooth structure and maintain dentin hydroxyapatite, which supports bond durability.

facts.population: Simulated restorations: composite cylinders between silane-coated steel disks of 5, 10 or 15 mm
facts.intervention: Continuous recording of setting (shrinkage) stress of chemically initiated composites at varying configuration factor C
facts.comparison: Various configuration factors C and sample volumes
facts.main_result: In most clinically relevant cavity configurations the stress-relieving flow is not sufficient to preserve adhesion to dentin by dentin-bonding agents.
facts.sample_size: each experiment repeated at least three times

facts.population: Extracted human molars (108) bonded by 12 operators of differing bonding experience
facts.intervention: Bonding to enamel and dentin with one 4th-generation and two 7th-generation adhesives, then shear testing
facts.comparison: 4th-generation versus 7th-generation adhesives; inexperienced, resident and experienced operators
facts.main_result: The 4th-generation adhesive performed better than the 7th-generation adhesives even with inexperienced operators; dentin bonds (14.0 MPa) were stronger than enamel bonds (11.9 MPa).
facts.funding_coi: Supported by Heraeus Kulzer
outcomes: shear bond strength to enamel and dentin

facts.population: Bovine dentin samples and Class V cavities in bovine teeth
facts.intervention: Measuring composite-dentin bond strength over time against developing polymerization contraction stress, in linear and 3-D models
facts.comparison: Linear (tensilometer) versus three-dimensional (Class V cavity) model
facts.main_result: In the linear model the bond survived contraction stress through flow relaxation, whereas in 3-D Class V cavities flow is limited and contraction stress can exceed bond strength, disrupting the bond.
facts.sample_size: 24 Class V cavities (12 per composite); 5 repeats per linear experiment

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 27-year-old woman needing replacement of amalgam fillings in two mandibular molars; 34 restorations in preliminary evaluation
facts.intervention: Dual bonding technique: dentin bonding agent applied after preparation and again at final luting
facts.main_result: Dual application of the dentin bonding agent considerably increased bond strength values.

facts.population: Human dentin disk sandwiches with resin composite from extracted caries-free third molars
facts.intervention: Acid-base challenge of two-step self-etch adhesive interfaces after long-term water storage, with SEM
facts.comparison: Clearfil SE Bond (fluoride-free) versus Clearfil Protect Bond (fluoride-releasing)
facts.main_result: Outer lesion depth rose from about 10 μm to about 30 μm after 6 months; an ABRZ persisted in both adhesives and was thicker and more stable with the fluoride-releasing Protect Bond.
facts.funding_coi: Global Center of Excellence Program and JSPS grant

facts.population: Box-shaped cavities in bovine root dentin
facts.intervention: Restoration with four adhesive/restorative combinations followed by acid-base challenge (demineralizing solution then 5% NaOCl) and SEM
facts.comparison: Four adhesive/restorative combinations compared with each other
facts.main_result: Self-etch systems SE and ABF showed a thin acid-base resistant zone under 1 μm beneath the hybrid layer, the fluoride-releasing RB/RP showed a thick acid-resistant zone but a partly degraded bonding resin, and the Single Bond hybrid layer was partly degraded.
facts.funding_coi: Center of Excellence Program grant (Tokyo Medical and Dental University)
facts.limitations: Further studies simulating the oral environment are necessary

facts.funding_coi: JSPS KAKENHI grants

facts.key_finding: The book argues that restoration margins should be kept supragingival, using adhesive partial-coverage techniques instead of traditional mechanically retained full-coverage preparations with subgingival margins.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Placing margins supragingival is presented as the preferred approach for periodontal health and minimally invasive esthetic restorations.

facts.population: Extracted human premolars with large class II MOD cavities
facts.intervention: Class II composite restorations with etch-and-rinse or self-etch adhesives, total or selective bonding, with or without a flowable composite layer
facts.comparison: Total bonding technique versus selective bonding; with versus without flowable liner
facts.main_result: Selective bonding gave lower cuspal movement than total bonding for all adhesives, and a flowable liner had no influence.
facts.limitations: Results should be confirmed by long-term clinical evaluations.

facts.population: Primary and young permanent teeth with dentin caries in children
facts.intervention: Caries Check (acid red in polypropylene glycol), stained dentin completely removed
facts.comparison: Caries Detector (acid red in propylene glycol), pink-stained dentin retained
facts.main_result: DIAGNOdent readings after removal were higher with Caries Check than Caries Detector in permanent teeth, with no significant difference in primary teeth.
facts.funding_coi: Products donated by Nippon Shika Yakuhin KK

facts.population: EDTA-demineralized bovine dentin collagen powder
facts.intervention: Treatment with lactic acid at 0.001 to 1 M for 1, 5 or 24 h, then staining with 1.0% acid red in propylene glycol
facts.comparison: Untreated dentin powder and intact demineralized collagen controls
facts.main_result: Collagen stained only after lactic acid at 0.01 M (pH 3) or higher; 0.001 M and controls stayed unstained.

facts.journal: International Journal of Applied and Basic Medical Research
Journal of the Canadian Dental Association
The European Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
facts.intervention: Differentiated approaches for adhesive restorations with subgingival cervical margins: coronal relocation of the margin, surgical exposure of the margin, or clinical crown lengthening with immediate, early or delayed impression
facts.main_result: A two-parameter classification (isolation with dental dam, biologic width) defines three clinical situations with three therapeutic approaches; the combined surgical-restorative approach allows cementation after only 1 week.
facts.follow_up: 1 year recall in the illustrated case

facts.population: Adult patients with non-carious cervical lesions restored with composite and adhesive systems (randomized trials)
facts.intervention: Adhesive strategies: 3-step etch-and-rinse (3ER), 2-step etch-and-rinse (2ER), 2-step self-etch (2SE), 1-step self-etch (1SE)
facts.comparison: Different adhesive strategies against each other
outcomes: loss of retention at 12-24, 36-48 and >48 months
facts.main_result: No significant differences between any two adhesive strategies except 2ER vs 3ER at the shortest follow-up; 2SE ranked highest but only slightly.
facts.funding_coi: Partially supported by CNPq and CAPES; no competing interests declared
facts.limitations: Conclusions were based mostly on studies of unclear risk of bias.

facts.population: Seven in vitro studies and 5 clinical reports on cervical margin relocation
facts.intervention: Cervical margin relocation (deep margin elevation) before adhesive cementation of indirect restorations
facts.comparison: Conventional luting directly on dentin
outcomes: bond strength to proximal box floor
facts.main_result: No strong scientific evidence supports or discourages CMR; no randomized or prospective/retrospective clinical studies exist, and most in vitro studies found no difference in marginal quality versus conventional luting.
facts.sample_size: 7 in vitro studies and 5 clinical reports
facts.limitations: No randomized controlled clinical trials or prospective or retrospective clinical studies on CMR could be found.

facts.population: 29 subjects with a single tooth requiring subgingival restoration
facts.intervention: Deep margin elevation with composite resin, followed by histological evaluation of gingival tissue adjacent to the composite
facts.comparison: Gingival tissue adjacent to the natural root surface of the same tooth
facts.main_result: Gingival inflammation next to subgingival composite did not differ from that next to natural root surface (3.83 vs 3.71, P=0.36), with plaque, bleeding and probing depth decreasing at 3 months.

facts.population: 120 patients with 197 partial indirect restorations (143 molars, 54 premolars) with deep margin elevation
facts.intervention: Partial indirect restorations (lithium disilicate or indirect composite) combined with deep margin elevation using resin composite
facts.comparison: Subsets by baseline variables (composite vs ceramic, vital vs non-vital, good vs poor DME profile)
facts.main_result: Overall cumulative survival was 95.9% (SE 2.9%) up to 12 years with 8 absolute failures; composite restorations degraded more, ceramic caused more antagonist wear.
facts.funding_coi: Granted by the University Medical Center Groningen; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Longer follow-up is needed as degradation of the restorations is seen over time.

facts.intervention: Adhesive cementation protocol with immediate dentin sealing, flexible base lining, soft light-curing provisionals and highly filled viscous luting composites
facts.comparison: Classical approach (adhesive applied at cementation, conventional glass-ionomer base, low-viscosity dual-cure cements)
facts.main_result: Immediate dentin sealing with a flexible base lining and highly filled luting composites improves the safety and predictability of luting tooth-colored posterior restorations, reducing postoperative sensitivity and cement-excess problems.

facts.intervention: Dental dam (rubber dam) application procedures
facts.funding_coi: Published by Coltène/Whaledent, Inc.
facts.key_finding: A manufacturer handbook teaching basic dental dam application in lessons: benefits, product properties, five application steps (operating field, dam preparation, retainer selection, placement, removal) and tips, with glossary and self-evaluation questions.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Dental dam gives patient protection, access, efficiency, moisture control and infection control, and its application can be learned in a few simple steps.

facts.journal: The American Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
facts.intervention: Deep margin elevation: modified Tofflemire matrix, immediate dentin sealing and a direct bonded composite base raising the deep margin to a supragingival position
facts.comparison: Surgical crown lengthening
facts.main_result: Deep margin elevation is proposed as a useful noninvasive alternative to surgical crown lengthening; more research is needed to validate it.
facts.limitations: More research is needed to validate the technique.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
facts.population: Literature on periodontal response to deep margin elevation, plus three illustrative clinical cases
facts.intervention: Deep margin elevation instead of crown lengthening for deep cavities
facts.comparison: Surgical crown lengthening
facts.main_result: DME appears well tolerated by the periodontium with good bonding and isolation; histologically no connective attachment forms on the material, giving a long junctional epithelium and a slight connective attachment on dentin below it.
facts.limitations: Further clinical and histologic studies are needed to confirm the conclusion.

facts.population: Four all-in-one self-etching adhesives tested on extracted human incisors/molars (enamel, dentin) and cylindrical dentin cavities
facts.intervention: Light curing of the adhesives under nitrogen atmosphere
facts.comparison: Light curing under ambient air
outcomes: shear bond strength to enamel and dentin
facts.main_result: Inhibition layer under air ranged from 4 um (iBond) to 23 um (One-Up Bond F II) and vanished under nitrogen; enamel SBS was unaffected and dentin SBS was higher under nitrogen (p=0.013).
facts.sample_size: 3 disks per adhesive for inhibition depth; n = 8 per group for SBS and marginal adaptation

facts.population: Thirty noncarious human third molars (hemi-teeth with thick or thin smear layer on flat dentin)
facts.intervention: Three self-etching adhesives of different acidity applied to dentin with thick (60-grit) or thin (600-grit) smear layer
facts.comparison: Etch-and-rinse controls Single Bond and ScotchBond Multi-Purpose Plus
outcomes: buffering capacity and pH of primers
facts.main_result: Smear layer thickness did not affect microtensile bond strength but thick smear layers increased gap width; bond strength depended only on the adhesive, with Tyrian lowest; pH correlated with gap width (R=0.99).
facts.sample_size: 30 molars, 6 hemi-teeth per adhesive per smear layer thickness
materials_brands: Tyrian Self Priming Etchant + One Step Plus
facts.funding_coi: Partially supported by CAPES and CNPq grants

facts.population: 40 extracted human third molars with standardized MOD preparations (mesial box 2 mm below the CEJ)
facts.intervention: Cervical margin relocation with a 2-mm layer of conventional or flowable composite before CAD/CAM crowns of pre-cured resin or lithium disilicate
facts.comparison: Distal face of the same tooth without CMR
outcomes: marginal quality by SEM of epoxy replicas before and after thermomechanical loading
facts.main_result: No significant difference in marginal quality with or without CMR, before or after thermomechanical cycling (p > 0.05).
facts.funding_coi: Grants from MIUR (Italy)
facts.limitations: Further in vivo studies are needed to validate the technique.

facts.population: Fifteen freshly extracted human molars in 3 groups of 5 (flat midcoronal dentin)
facts.intervention: Immediate dentin sealing with OptiBond FL immediately after preparation, before impression
facts.comparison: Delayed dentin sealing (indirect) and a direct immediate bonding control
facts.main_result: Microtensile bond strength of control (55.06 MPa) and IDS (58.25 MPa) did not differ, while DDS was much lower (11.58 MPa, P=.0081).
facts.sample_size: 15 molars, 3 groups of 5 teeth, 11 beams per tooth

facts.population: Fifty freshly extracted human molars divided into 10 groups
facts.intervention: Immediate dentin sealing with Optibond FL or SE Bond, with provisional restorations for 2, 7 or 12 weeks before overlay placement
facts.comparison: Direct bonding control and delayed dentin sealing for each adhesive
facts.main_result: Control and all IDS groups did not differ and exceeded 45 MPa for both adhesives, whereas delayed dentin sealing groups had lower bond strength (P<.001).
facts.follow_up: Restoration placement after 2, 7 or 12 weeks; testing 24 h after restoration
facts.funding_coi: Materials provided by 3M ESPE, Kerr and Kuraray

facts.population: 40 human molars with Class II MOD cavities, margins in enamel or 2 mm below the CEJ
facts.intervention: Proximal margin elevation with composite (one 3 mm or two 1.5 mm layers of Tetric) before adhesive insertion of Cerec ceramic inlays
facts.comparison: Enamel-margin positive control and untreated dentin-margin negative control
outcomes: percentage of continuous margin by SEM before and after thermomechanical loading
facts.main_result: After loading, margin elevation groups did not differ from the untreated dentin-margin group; only the enamel interface of group EN (90.0%) was better than DE-2In (83.2%).

facts.population: 35 patients (aged 27-54) needing one posterior partial crown, with margins below the CEJ
facts.intervention: Cervical margin relocation (G-Premio Bond and universal flow composite) in one interproximal box before pressed lithium disilicate crowns
facts.comparison: Shoulder preparation
facts.main_result: At 12 months CMR sites had more bleeding on probing than shoulder preparation (53% vs 31.5%), with GI and PI not different.
facts.limitations: Within the limitations of this study, higher incidence of BoP can be expected around CMR margins and in coincidence with deep margins.

facts.population: 20 extracted human third molars with MOD cavities, proximal margins 1 mm below the CEJ
facts.intervention: Mesial margin elevation with flowable composite, then CAD/CAM composite overlays luted with a universal adhesive (selective etch) or three-step total-etch adhesive
facts.comparison: Non-elevated distal margins in the same teeth; universal vs three-step adhesive
outcomes: microleakage score at mesial and distal interfaces
facts.main_result: With the universal adhesive CMR sites leaked more than non-CMR sites, with the three-step adhesive no difference; non-CMR sites leaked less with the universal adhesive.
facts.funding_coi: Materials provided by GC Europe; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: More in vitro and in vivo research, especially randomized clinical trials, is needed to validate CMR.

facts.population: Technique demonstrated on a Typodont mesio-occlusal inlay preparation with a localized subgingival margin
facts.intervention: Matrix-in-a-matrix deep margin elevation: sectional band inside a circumferential matrix with Teflon tape packed between
facts.main_result: A modified matrix technique is described to isolate and adapt a subgingival matrix for deep margin elevation, potentially avoiding resective surgery or extraction.

facts.population: 39 extracted human molars with MOD cavities, mesial margins 1 mm below the CEJ
facts.intervention: Mesial cervical margin relocation with a hybrid composite (Essentia) or flowable composite (G-ænial Universal Flo), then adhesively cemented composite CAD/CAM MOD overlays
facts.comparison: No CMR (control)
outcomes: interfacial leakage by silver nitrate penetration depth
facts.main_result: Dentin-interface leakage was higher in both CMR groups (mean 2.40 and 2.04) than control (1.18), and higher at dentin than enamel interfaces.
facts.funding_coi: Materials provided by GC Europe; no conflict of interest declared

facts.population: 14 extracted human molars with MOD cavities, proximal margins about 1 mm below the CEJ
facts.intervention: Mesial CMR with total-etch adhesive and flowable composite (Group 1) or universal adhesive and bulk-fill flowable composite (Group 2), then CAD/CAM overlays
facts.comparison: Non-elevated distal margins
outcomes: marginal integrity by SEM of replicas
facts.main_result: Microleakage and SEM marginal integrity were not correlated; CMR margins leaked more than non-CMR margins and Group 2 leaked less than Group 1.

facts.population: Canine teeth of five dogs with surgically created buccal bone defects and root cavities
facts.intervention: Class V root cavities restored with composite resin or resin-modified glass ionomer cement and covered by a flap
facts.comparison: Unrestored cavities as control
facts.main_result: Both materials allowed apical epithelial migration and had markedly shorter connective tissue attachment than control (0.52 and 0.37 mm vs 2.22 mm).

facts.population: Bar specimens of five ceramic and five resin composite materials
facts.intervention: 4-point bending initial strength and staircase cyclic fatigue (10^4 cycles, 0.5 Hz) in water
facts.comparison: Ceramics versus resin composites
facts.main_result: Zirconia had the highest initial and fatigue strength (768 and 440 MPa); e.max Press and Clearfil Majesty Posterior lost least strength (29.6% and 32%).

facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.journal: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
facts.intervention: Adhesive cementation protocols for hybrid ceramics and CAD/CAM composite resins
facts.main_result: Hybrid ceramics should be etched with HF acid plus silane; CAD/CAM composites air-abraded with a universal bonding agent; all luted adhesively with light- or dual-cured resin cement.
facts.limitations: Clinical studies are needed on long-term bonding behavior and survival

facts.population: Blocks of six CAD/CAM materials (four ceramics, one hybrid ceramic, one composite)
facts.intervention: Mechanical and chemical surface treatments before luting with two dual-curing luting composites
facts.comparison: Untreated control surfaces and the two cements
facts.main_result: Bond strength of six CAD/CAM materials was significantly influenced by surface treatment (p < 0.05); HF+S gave the highest bond for e.max CAD and Vita Enamic.
facts.funding_coi: Companies donated materials
facts.limitations: The effect of aging needs to be examined in depth

facts.population: A 36-year-old woman with severe dental erosion due to gastroesophageal reflux disease
facts.intervention: Full-coverage crowns 0.5-1.5 mm thick milled from VITA ENAMIC, adhesively cemented without preparation
facts.main_result: At half a year and one year the crowns were still intact and soft tissues appeared healthy.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: No information on durability regarding cervical areas or discolorations; limited shade range

facts.population: Laboratory-fabricated nacre-like alumina/polymer composites (ceramic fractions 70-76%)
facts.intervention: Bi-directional freeze-casting, sintering, silanisation and UDMA/TEGDMA infiltration of alumina scaffolds
facts.comparison: Commercial CAD/CAM composite Vita Enamic
facts.main_result: The composites had flexural strength 135.08-172.65 MPa and fracture toughness 2.54-3.19 MPa.m1/2, all superior to Vita Enamic.
facts.limitations: Further work is needed to improve physical and mechanical properties and esthetics
facts.key_finding: Bi-directional freeze casting produced aligned alumina scaffolds that, after pressing, sintering and polymer infiltration, gave nacre-like composites (70-76 vol% ceramic) with flexural strength 135-173 MPa, higher than Vita Enamic, and good machinability.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: This is laboratory-stage work only: the material shows potential as a chairside CAD/CAM block, but there is no clinical data.

facts.population: Beams (2 x 2 x 25 mm) of two composite resins, direct and indirect
facts.intervention: Pre-tensioned unidirectional glass fiber bundles embedded in the composite
facts.comparison: Non-tensioned glass fibers and unreinforced composite
facts.main_result: Pre-tensioned fibers raised flexural strength to about 568 MPa in both composites, versus 425-443 MPa with non-tensioned fibers and 81-132 MPa unreinforced.

facts.population: Resin composite molds (4 mm deep) and cavities in 24 extracted human mandibular molars
facts.intervention: Plasma-treated polyethylene fiber (Ribbond Ultra) increment at the cavity floor under SDR bulk-fill
facts.comparison: Bulk placement (BLK), two-increment placement (INC) and an unbonded bulk-filled control
facts.main_result: MTBS was 13.8, 31.7 and 28.3 MPa for BLK, INC and FRC; FRC and INC did not differ and both exceeded BLK.
facts.sample_size: 24 molars for MTBS; n = 12 molds per group for gap volume

facts.population: an endodontically treated posterior tooth (case report)
facts.intervention: fiber-reinforced composite (FRC) layer incorporated into the resin coating of the tooth preparation before the final impression
facts.main_result: The technique may reduce the risk of catastrophic fractures and improve the success rate of endocrowns on nonvital teeth (no quantitative results)
facts.funding_coi: Authors declare no financial or other interest in any product

facts.population: 50 sound extracted human maxillary central incisors with window veneer preparations
facts.intervention: Li2Si2O5 (e.max Press) laminate veneers bonded after immediate dentin sealing (IDS) of exposed dentin
facts.comparison: delayed dentin sealing (DDS) after 2 weeks, and an enamel-only control group

facts.funding_coi: Materials provided by Ivoclar Vivadent and Kerr

facts.population: indirect restorations (in vitro bond strength to human dentin)
facts.intervention: immediate dentin sealing (IDS)
facts.comparison: delayed dentin sealing (DDS)
outcomes: bond strength to dentin (immediate and long-term)

facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest declared

facts.population: 88 articles on the IDS technique, in vitro and clinical studies on human permanent teeth
facts.intervention: immediate dentin sealing (IDS) for indirect restorations
facts.main_result: IDS seems advantageous for bond strength, gap formation, bacterial microleakage and dentin hypersensitivity
facts.funding_coi: Authors report no conflicts of interest

facts.population: teeth prepared for indirect bonded restorations
facts.intervention: immediate dentin sealing (IDS) with a dentin bonding agent before impression making
facts.comparison: delayed dentin sealing (DDS)
facts.main_result: IDS appears to achieve improved bond strength, fewer gap formations, decreased bacterial leakage and reduced post-cementation sensitivity
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest
facts.limitations: more research is required in this field

facts.population: extracted third molars with fully developed apices, standard Class II MO cavities
facts.intervention: immediate endodontic sealing (IES) of the access cavity before endodontic irrigation
facts.comparison: delayed endodontic sealing (DES) after irrigation
outcomes: internal adaptation (percentage of continuous margin, SEM)

facts.funding_coi: Authors declare no conflict of interest

authors: Stephan A M van der Made
facts.population: 104 patients (mean age 42.1 years) receiving 384 feldspathic ceramic laminate veneers on maxillary anterior teeth
facts.intervention: laminate veneers with immediate dentin sealing (IDS) when more than 50% of dentin was exposed
facts.comparison: veneers on teeth with more than 50% dentin exposure sealed without IDS
facts.main_result: In teeth with more than 50% dentin exposure, veneer survival was 96.4% with IDS versus 81.8% without (P = 0.017); overall survival was 95% over 11 years

facts.journal: Journal of the American Dental Association
facts.population: deep carious lesions approaching the pulp (23 relevant human studies)
facts.intervention: partial caries removal or stepwise excavation
facts.comparison: complete removal of infected tissue
facts.main_result: There is substantial evidence that removing all infected dentin in deep carious lesions is not required for successful treatment, provided the restoration seals the lesion

facts.funding_coi: No disclosures; NIDCR grant support acknowledged
facts.limitations: additional clinical trials may be needed

facts.population: 60 decoronated endodontically treated bovine incisors without a ferrule

facts.comparison: two previously published groups (2 mm ferrule with fiber post; no ferrule with fiber post)
facts.main_result: No post-and-core foundation matched the ferrule group (72 667 cycles); fiber post with bulk-fill core outperformed titanium post groups
facts.sample_size: 60 bovine incisors in 4 groups plus 2 comparison groups
facts.funding_coi: Supported in part by CAPES Foundation Brazil; materials provided by several manufacturers

facts.population: extracted human third molars ground flat to expose middle coronal dentin
facts.intervention: 50 µm aluminum oxide air abrasion of dentin before applying Clearfil SE Bond or One-Up Bond F
facts.comparison: no air abrasion
outcomes: microtensile bond strength at 1 day, 3 and 6 months

facts.follow_up: 1 day, 3 and 6 months of water storage

facts.population: Two commercial CAD/CAM composites (Shofu HC Hard, Cerasmart 300) as bar and plate specimens
facts.intervention: Alumina air-abrasion (50 um Al2O3) of the composite surface, with or without silanization and resin-cement bonding, tested by three-point bending and shear bond strength
facts.comparison: Specimens without air-abrasion
outcomes: shear bond strength to resin cement

facts.funding_coi: JSPS KAKENHI grant; no conflict of interest declared

facts.population: 32 bovine molar and premolar dentin bars (2 x 2 x 8 mm)
facts.intervention: Sandblasting dentin with 50 um aluminum oxide before etching, adhesive and composite
facts.comparison: Control bars with no sandblasting
facts.main_result: Sandblasted dentin gave higher tensile stress at maximum load (84.3 vs 35.1 MPa, p = 0.033) and fracture strength (18.5 vs 8.2 MPa, p = 0.008) than control.

facts.population: 30 patients needing a single implant at a premolar or first molar site, allocated to thin (n = 14) or thick (n = 16) vertical mucosal phenotype
facts.intervention: Tissue level implants with a partially smooth collar
facts.comparison: Thick (> 2 mm) versus thin (<= 2 mm) vertical mucosa
outcomes: clinical parameters (probing depth, recession, keratinized mucosa width, BOP, plaque, gingival index)
facts.main_result: No significant differences between thin and thick vertical mucosa for any clinical parameter or radiographic marginal bone level at one year; 100% implant survival.
facts.funding_coi: Osseointegration Foundation grant; implants donated by BioHorizons; one author receives BioHorizons speaker honoraria

facts.population: Patients with, or at risk for, MRONJ
facts.intervention: MRONJ prevention measures and stage-based management strategies
facts.main_result: The committee recommends renaming BRONJ as MRONJ and redefines the case definition (exposed bone for more than eight weeks in patients on antiresorptive or antiangiogenic agents without jaw radiation).

facts.population: Patients with, or at risk for, MRONJ
facts.intervention: Updated risk estimates, diagnosis and management algorithms for MRONJ
facts.main_result: AAOMS maintains the existing MRONJ staging system (including Stage 0) while updating risk, diagnosis and management guidance.
facts.funding_coi: Authors disclose consultancies and research grants (Amgen, AAOMS, OMS Foundation and others)

facts.intervention: Thione/thiol primers and 4-META/MMA-TBB resin for bonding Ag-Pd-Cu-Au alloy restorations and fixed partial dentures
facts.main_result: Clinical performance of Ag-Pd-Cu-Au alloy restorations and FPDs is overall excellent when seated with current noble metal bonding systems.
facts.funding_coi: Supported in part by JSPS Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research

facts.intervention: Selective and stepwise carious tissue removal with restorative materials over residual carious dentin
facts.main_result: Carious dentin can be left under provisional or permanent restoration without risk of caries progression.
facts.funding_coi: No disclosures

facts.population: In vitro studies of etched and silanized glass ceramics bonded to resin-based materials
facts.intervention: Adhesive layer application after HF etching and silanization
facts.comparison: Same silane without an adhesive layer
facts.main_result: Adhesive layer application did not improve bond strength; shear studies showed no significant difference and microtensile studies showed higher values without adhesive.

facts.population: 14 caries-free extracted human upper first premolars
facts.intervention: Seventh-generation bonding agent (iBond)
facts.comparison: Sixth-generation bonding agent (Adper Prompt L-Pop)
outcomes: penetration depth of bonding resin into dentinal tubules (SEM)
facts.main_result: Seventh-generation adhesive penetrated deeper into dentinal tubules than sixth-generation (12.451 vs 9.471 um, p = 0.032).
facts.key_finding: In 14 extracted premolars, the seventh-generation self-etch adhesive (iBond) penetrated deeper into dentinal tubules than the sixth-generation adhesive (Adper Prompt L-Pop), about 12.5 versus 9.5 micrometres (p = 0.032).
facts.clinical_bottom_line: The authors suggest deeper tubular resin penetration with the seventh-generation adhesive may improve bond strength, but bond strength itself was not measured.

facts.intervention: Contemporary adhesive strategies (etch-and-rinse, self-etch, universal) and the dynamic tooth-adhesive interface
facts.main_result: Adhesive interfaces are susceptible to biodegradation by biofilm, bacterial enzymes and activated endogenous enzymes, so adhesive choice and technique affect longevity.
facts.funding_coi: No disclosures

facts.population: In vitro studies of bond strength to human primary and permanent tooth enamel and dentin
facts.intervention: Adhesive bonding to primary teeth
facts.comparison: Bonding to permanent teeth
facts.main_result: Permanent teeth showed higher bond strength than primary teeth overall (p = 0.0005) and for dentin (p = 0.002), but not for enamel (p = 0.11); most studies had high bias risk.

facts.limitations: The majority of the studies had a high bias risk.

facts.intervention: Universal bonding agents used in total-etch, self-etch or selective enamel-etch modes
facts.main_result: Laboratory and initial clinical studies suggest universal bonding agents are a promising step in bonding to tooth substance.

facts.population: CAD-CAM ceramic blocks (2 zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate, lithium disilicate, leucite-based, Y-TZP) bonded to composite resin; in vitro microbars
facts.intervention: Six surface treatments (control, universal adhesive, HF, CoJet, HF+Uni, CoJet+Uni), tested with and without 100 000 thermal cycles

facts.funding_coi: Guangdong and National Natural Science Foundation of China grants

facts.key_finding: Course handout on resin adhesion: enamel is a predictable bonding substrate (etch 30-45 s), whereas dentin is variable and unpredictable, and durable bonds depend on short dentin etching (5-10 s), keeping dentin moist but not overdried, adequate primer time and moisture control.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Blot rather than over-dry etched dentin, etch enamel selectively with phosphoric acid, isolate well, and offset a high c-factor with incremental or flowable first layers.

facts.population: Bovine incisor enamel and dentin, resin composite and feldspathic porcelain specimens
facts.intervention: Scotchbond Universal in etch-and-rinse and self-etch modes
facts.comparison: Scotchbond Multipurpose, Single Bond 2, Clearfil SE Bond; silane + SB and no-treatment controls on composite and porcelain
facts.main_result: The universal adhesive was comparable to the other adhesives tested, with performance depending on the substrate.
facts.funding_coi: Composite resin donated by FGM; authors declare competing interests

facts.intervention: Self-adhesive resin cements for luting and bonding restorations
facts.main_result: Self-adhesive resin cements are easy to use and perform similarly to conventional cements in early short-term studies, but clinical evidence is insufficient for robust conclusions.
facts.funding_coi: UBC Start-Up grants

facts.population: Six commercial universal adhesives tested on films and on dentin from extracted sound human third molars

facts.population: Caries-affected dentin as a bonding substrate
facts.main_result: Caries-affected dentin gives lower bond strength and a poorer hybrid layer than normal dentin, which can compromise restoration longevity.
Composite restorations last about 10 years or less on average, failing mainly from secondary caries and fracture.
The relationship between the cement used and crown survival is not well understood.
facts.funding_coi: Authors have nothing to disclose

facts.population: 19 in vitro studies on repair of direct methacrylate-based resin composites
facts.intervention: Silane application combined with adhesive before composite repair

facts.main_result: Silane plus adhesive gave significantly higher repair bond strengths than adhesive alone (p=0.003), with a larger effect for nonhydrolyzed silanes (effect size 7.30).

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate (VITA Suprinity) ceramic discs
facts.intervention: HF-acid etching for 20, 40 or 60 seconds, with or without a resin-cement layer
facts.comparison: Shortest etching time (20 s) and specimens without resin cement
facts.main_result: Without resin cement, flexural strength rose with etching time (250.8 MPa at 20 s to 342.9 MPa at 60 s); a resin-cement layer raised strength at 20 s (341.8 MPa).

facts.population: Silver-palladium, gold-silver and cobalt-chromium alloys and titanium disks bonded to acrylic rods
facts.intervention: Thiophosphoric methacrylate primer modified with phosphoric methacrylates and/or benzoyl peroxide
facts.comparison: Acetone-only and single-monomer primers
facts.main_result: A primer mixing thiophosphoric and phosphoric methacrylates with benzoyl peroxide and heat gave bond strengths over 20 MPa that stayed unchanged after 2,000 thermocycles.

facts.population: Bovine incisor enamel

facts.funding_coi: Supported in part by Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research and the Sato Fund

facts.journal: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
facts.intervention: Universal adhesives (origin, chemistry, strengths, weaknesses, clinical use)
facts.funding_coi: Author declares no affiliation with the companies mentioned

facts.population: Disks cast in two type IV gold alloys (Maxgold, Sofard)

facts.comparison: Unprimed control specimens

facts.intervention: Bioactive composites and bonding agents with calcium phosphate nanoparticles and antibacterial or protein-repellent resins
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest; many cited studies supported by NIH and NSFC grants

facts.population: Healthy edentulous individuals or cadavers with atrophic or non-atrophic maxillary/mandibular ridges

facts.population: 22 patients with at least one implant with a small bony dehiscence defect (≤5 mm)

facts.comparison: Spontaneous healing without treatment
facts.main_result: Between implant placement and 6-month reentry, buccal vertical bone changed by -0.17 mm in the spontaneous healing group and +1.79 mm in the GBR group (p=0.017).

facts.population: Partially edentulous patients receiving implants in healed sites with native bone

facts.comparison: Group 1 BBT ≤0.5 mm vs Group 2 >0.5 and <1.5 mm vs Group 3 ≥1.5 mm
outcomes: buccal gingival margin change (tooth height) at 1, 2 and 3 years
facts.main_result: At 3 years the buccal gum receded 1.22 mm for BBT ≤0.5 mm and 0.64 mm for 0.5-1.5 mm, but grew coronally 0.77 mm for BBT ≥1.5 mm (p ≤ 0.01).

facts.population: healthy patients with at least one dental implant

facts.main_result: Thicker (>=2 mm) soft tissue was associated with significantly less marginal bone loss than thin tissue (0.54; p = .027), confirmed by trial sequential analysis.

facts.limitations: Half of the included studies came from the same group, and implant types, abutment geometry and positioning varied, giving high heterogeneity.

facts.population: clinical studies of soft tissue augmentation around dental implants

facts.population: patients receiving dental implants at a university implant center (maxilla and mandible, some with bone augmentation)

facts.population: predominantly white male patients (mean age 62.9 years) at 30 VA medical centers and two university clinics, with more than 3,000 root-form implants

facts.comparison: HA-coated versus non-HA-coated implants

facts.population: 36 patients with two adjacent machined titanium implants (radiographic assessment)

outcomes: lateral bone loss from implant shoulder
crestal bone loss between adjacent implants

facts.key_finding: The commentary defines the peri-implant phenotype as the morphologic and dimensional features of the tissues around osseointegrated implants, made of soft tissue (keratinized mucosa width, mucosal thickness, supracrestal tissue height) and bone (peri-implant bone thickness). facts.clinical_bottom_line: Use these standardized thresholds to describe and report peri-implant soft and hard tissue dimensions; short supracrestal tissue height (<3 mm) is linked with more marginal bone loss.

facts.journal: Journal of the Korean Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons
facts.population: clinical trials of bone-level and tissue-level dental implants reporting bone-level changes

facts.main_result: Methodology, follow-up and multifactorial causes of bone loss varied so widely that direct comparison of bone loss around the implant types was impossible.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: edentulous or extraction sites with insufficient bone for implant placement

facts.population: BOPT crowns over truncoconical implant abutments without finishing line, prepared on the working model

facts.funding_coi: Author is a key opinion leader for Sweden & Martina, supplier of the burs

facts.journal: Journal of Pre-Clinical and Clinical Research
facts.intervention: horizontal (finish line) versus vertical (shoulderless and edgeless verti prep) tooth preparation for crowns

facts.population: patients with a single missing molar or premolar, treated with single implants

facts.journal: The European Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
outcomes: soft tissue stability at the prosthetic/tissue interface

materials_brands: BOPT diamond drill assortment with stainless steel holder (code Z4999)

facts.journal: Journal of Clinical and Experimental Dentistry
facts.population: A 58-year-old patient without medical problems with missing upper posterior teeth and an old anterior fixed prosthesis
