facts.limitations: Medium- to long-term prospective studies are needed to confirm clinical behavior.

facts.intervention: BOPT feather-edge flapless preparation with provisional relining and a prosthetic margin placed in the sulcus
facts.comparison: Horizontal preparations with finishing lines (chamfer, shoulder)
facts.key_finding: The article describes the BOPT concept: a flapless feather-edge preparation where the crown margin and emergence profile are modified in the provisional and final restoration so the gingiva adapts around the new contour. It reports stable gingival position and no signs of inflammation in clinical cases.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: BOPT is presented as a simpler, minimally invasive preparation option for replacing old crowns, based on the author's clinical experience rather than a formal study.

facts.population: Adult non-smoking patients with old fixed restorations in the esthetic zone needing replacement
facts.intervention: Full-coverage zirconia-core restorations on teeth prepared with BOPT
facts.comparison: Single crowns versus fixed partial dentures
facts.main_result: At 4 years, 98.6% of teeth had stable margins, gingival thickness increased by 32.5%, and restoration survival was 96.6%.

facts.population: One beagle dog with artificial periodontal defects on premolar roots
facts.intervention: Cultured autologous periodontal ligament cells seeded on planed root surfaces under mucoperiosteal flaps
facts.comparison: Opposite side, same treatment without cell seeding
facts.main_result: Seeded root surfaces were almost completely covered with cementoblasts and showed new attachment on all 6 sites, whereas controls showed epithelial downgrowth.
facts.limitations: Done in only one dog with artificial defects; more dogs and natural defects are needed before clinical testing.

facts.population: One beagle dog, mandibular third and fourth premolars (four implant sites)
facts.intervention: Socket-shield technique: buccal root fragment retained with immediate titanium implant placed lingual to it
facts.comparison: Implant placed with versus without contact to the buccal tooth fragment
facts.main_result: All four implants osseointegrated without inflammation, and the tooth fragment showed no resorption and was attached to the buccal bone by a physiologic periodontal ligament.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by an unconditional research grant from Thommen Medical; no conflict of interest declared

facts.population: 5 bilayered porcelain-zirconia specimens (in vitro)
facts.intervention: Four-point bending interfacial delamination test of VITA VM9 porcelain on Y-TZP
facts.main_result: Mean strain energy release rate was 12.4 J/m2 with adhesive failure along the interface, indicating relatively poor adhesion.

facts.population: 36 metal-porcelain specimens in three groups
facts.comparison: Gold alloy with Vita Omega 900 ceramic (control)
facts.main_result: Titanium groups (63.54 and 68.17 MPa) had significantly higher shear bond strength than gold alloy (40.55 MPa), with no difference between milled and cast-and-milled titanium.
facts.funding_coi: Financial support from FAPESP
L. Fung is a paid consultant for SprintRay 3D printing technologies

facts.population: Maxillary partially edentulous typodont with 3 implant replicas
facts.intervention: Additively manufactured casts from three scan body and digital implant replica systems
facts.comparison: Conventional polyvinyl siloxane open-tray impression with stone cast
outcomes: linear discrepancy on x, y, z axes
facts.main_result: AM casts had lower 3D discrepancies than conventional casts; conventional was better on the apicocoronal position.

facts.journal: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
facts.intervention: Additive manufacturing technologies (stereolithography, material extrusion, powder-based fusion, inkjet printing, binder jetting) for all-ceramic crowns
facts.comparison: Subtractive CNC milling of ceramics (discussed as background)
facts.main_result: AM has shown promising experimental outcomes for all-ceramic crowns but has not yet reached a commercial breakthrough.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest disclosed
facts.limitations: Literature on AM of ceramic crowns is scanty and dispersed; heterogeneity makes outcomes hard to standardize.

facts.population: 41-year-old male with a fractured left maxillary second premolar
facts.intervention: Milled CAD/CAM Ti-6Al-4V coping veneered with porcelain, cemented with self-adhesive resin cement

facts.population: four labside and two production center dental NC milling machines
facts.intervention: mechanical-engineering comparison of technical and economic criteria of labside and production-center milling machines
facts.main_result: Production-center machines offer a wider range of materials and restoration shapes than labside machines, which offer more than chairside; more complex solutions need more skilled users and cost more

facts.intervention: VM9 veneering porcelain on zirconia frameworks (Vita YZ), with layering technique
facts.comparison: Other veneering porcelains and ceramics (VM7, Omega 900, MKII, Mz100, etc.) and enamel
facts.main_result: Fine-microstructure veneering porcelains such as VM9 and VM7 showed low opposing enamel wear and improved flexural strength compared with older porcelains.
facts.limitations: Long-term clinical data on zirconia as a replacement for metal ceramics are unavailable.

facts.population: Partially dentate and edentulous patients with cancer on high-dose antiresorptive medication
facts.intervention: Straumann Roxolid Bone Level implants placed without augmentation, restored with crowns or overdentures
facts.main_result: Implant survival and success after 2 years of loading were 100% and 97.4%, and OHLQoL increased in all groups.
facts.sample_size: 22 patients with 39 implants completed treatment; 13 patients (23 implants) completed 2 years
facts.funding_coi: Amgen, Institute Straumann AG, Tandlægeforeningen; no conflicts declared
facts.limitations: Feasibility study with few patients and a high dropout rate because patients died from cancer progression.

facts.population: Partially edentulous patients with implant-supported FDPs with cantilever extension in posterior areas
facts.intervention: Implant-supported fixed dental prostheses with mesial or distal cantilever extension (1 premolar unit), re-evaluated after at least 10 years
facts.comparison: Implant surfaces adjacent to versus distant from the cantilever extension
facts.main_result: Patient-based implant survival was 96.2% and marginal bone level change was not significant (1.2 to 1.6 mm) after a mean 13.3 years; loss of retention occurred in 34.6% of patients.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the authors' own institution; no conflicts of interest

facts.population: Partially dentate patients with implant-supported FDPs or single crowns in the posterior maxilla or mandible
facts.intervention: Implant-supported FDPs with cantilever extension
facts.comparison: Implant-supported crowns or FDPs without cantilever
facts.main_result: Mean peri-implant bone loss was 0.23 mm with cantilevers versus 0.09 mm without after 5.3 years, not significantly different.
facts.limitations: Study results are limited by the small number of patients and diameter-reduced implants (3.3 mm) that fractured under cantilevers.

facts.population: Patients with single or partial edentulism treated consecutively with sintered porous surface implants
facts.intervention: SPS implants restored with single crowns or partial fixed dentures, grouped by crown-implant ratio
facts.comparison: Implant groups with different crown-implant ratios
facts.main_result: Overall implant success was 98.1% with mean peri-implant bone loss of 0.48 mm at 36 months; success and bone loss correlated with C/I ratio, with thresholds of 3.10 (anatomical) and 3.40 (clinical).
facts.sample_size: 259 SPS implants in 136 patients followed up
facts.funding_coi: Authors declare no financial interest in any company or product mentioned

facts.population: Subjects with implant-supported single crowns or two-implant FDPs with one cantilever extension in the posterior maxilla or mandible
facts.intervention: Implant-supported single crowns or short-span FDPs with one mesial or distal cantilever extension
facts.comparison: Implants of FDPs adjacent to versus distant from the cantilever extension
facts.main_result: No implant loss (100% survival) and no significant differences in marginal bone level change or PPD between the three groups after a mean 5+ years
facts.sample_size: 19 SC implants and 21 two-implant FDPs in 38 subjects
facts.follow_up: mean 78.2 months for SCs and 67.8 months for FDPs
facts.limitations: Small sample size and follow-up from prosthesis delivery meant early failures could not be accounted for
materials_brands: Straumann Dental Implant System, SLA tissue-level implants

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Patients with partial fixed implant-supported prostheses
facts.intervention: Presence of a cantilever
facts.comparison: Absence of a cantilever
facts.main_result: Cantilevers did not compromise marginal bone loss or prosthesis survival, while minor complications were more frequent in groups without cantilevers (P = .008).
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: All included studies were low-quality by the Jadad scale and not randomized.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Patients with fixed complete dental prostheses with distal cantilevers on implants
facts.intervention: Distal implant-supported cantilever prostheses
facts.comparison: Traditional tooth-retained distal cantilever prostheses
facts.main_result: Weighted prosthesis survival was 95% over 7.3 ± 2.6 years; the most frequent complication was screw loosening.
facts.limitations: The majority of studies lacked specific data.

facts.population: Partially edentulous patients with implant-supported cantilevered fixed restorations (at least 10 patients, mean follow-up 5 years or more)
facts.intervention: Implant-supported cantilevered fixed dental prostheses
facts.main_result: Estimated 5-10 year survival was 98.4% for implants and 99.2% for rehabilitations, with cumulative complication rates of 28.66% (patients) and 26.57% (prostheses).
facts.sample_size: 9 papers selected for partially edentulous patients
facts.follow_up: Mean follow-up of at least 5 years in included studies
facts.limitations: Retrospective and prospective studies of different designs were analysed together.

facts.population: Patients with implant-supported fixed partial dentures with or without cantilevers, at least one year of loading
facts.intervention: Cantilever FDPs
facts.comparison: Non-cantilever FDPs
facts.main_result: Implant survival and success were 96.7% and 87.9% for cantilever FDPs versus 99.5% and 92.6% for non-cantilever FDPs, with no overall difference in bone loss (0.58 vs 0.59 mm).
facts.sample_size: 107 subjects with 128 cantilever FDPs on 132 implants and 99 subjects with 144 non-cantilever FDPs on 203 implants

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: One 67-year-old female patient with three implants in the mandibular left second premolar, first molar and second molar regions
facts.intervention: In vivo 3D load measurement with piezoelectric transducers under four implant configurations supporting a three-unit FPD
facts.comparison: Three-implant prosthesis vs central pontic, posterior cantilever and anterior cantilever two-implant prostheses
outcomes: 3D load on each implant during maximum voluntary clenching
load on implants during chewing gum
facts.main_result: Highest load was on the first molar implant in the posterior cantilever during chewing (318.90 ± 70.71 N); three-implant prosthesis and central pontic distributed loads more equally than cantilever designs.
facts.sample_size: 1 patient, 3 implants; MVC n = 5 and 17 chewing strokes per configuration
facts.follow_up: Implants functioning 3 years since prosthetic restoration
materials_brands: Brånemark System MKIII RP implants (Nobel Biocare)
facts.funding_coi: Grants-in-aid for Scientific Research (Japan MEXT); no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Single patient; results interpreted within the limitations of the study.

facts.population: Six longitudinal studies of implant-supported cantilever FDPs in partially edentulous patients
facts.intervention: Implant-supported cantilever fixed dental prostheses (ICFDPs)
facts.main_result: Estimated 5-year implant survival 98.9% and ICFDP survival 97.1%; biological complications 5.7% at implant level; veneer fracture was the commonest technical complication
facts.funding_coi: Authors declare no potential conflicts
facts.limitations: Limited literature with non-homogeneous study design and follow-up

facts.population: Standardized partially edentulous maxillary models (D2 bone) with 4 mm, 8 mm and >12 mm residual bone height and flat or oblique sinus floors
facts.intervention: Static computer-assisted implant placement (sCAIP)
facts.comparison: Free-handed implant placement
facts.main_result: sCAIP gave higher 3D accuracy independent of bone height and sinus morphology, whereas free-handed accuracy depended strongly on alveolar bone height and on sinus morphology.
materials_brands: Straumann TLX S 4.5 × 10 mm RT tissue-level implants
facts.funding_coi: University of Bern, Department of Oral Surgery and Stomatology; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: In vitro design, other instruments and implant designs not evaluated, and only single-tooth replacement scenarios.

facts.intervention: Review of CBCT use in preoperative implant planning
facts.comparison: Conventional lower-dose dental radiography
facts.main_result: CBCT should not be used routinely for initial implant site assessment; use it only when clinical and conventional radiographic information is inadequate, with the field of view limited to the area of interest.
facts.funding_coi: Authors have nothing to disclose

facts.population: 72 standardized stainless steel dies simulating a first mandibular premolar
facts.intervention: Cementation and hydrothermal aging (5 and 20 h) of CAD-CAM metal-ceramic, veneered zirconia and monolithic zirconia crowns
facts.comparison: Uncemented vs cemented crowns; non-aged vs aged zirconia
materials_brands: Z-CAD HD / Z-CAD HTL zirconia (Metoxit) with IPS e.max Ceram
facts.funding_coi: Research grant between University Complutense of Madrid and AVINENT Implant System SL

facts.population: Ten ITI hollow screw implants (3.8 mm) in acrylic blocks with solid titanium abutments and cast noble alloy copings
facts.intervention: Cementation of castings with six luting cements followed by pull-out retention testing
facts.comparison: Six cements compared with each other (Temp Bond NE, IRM, Hy-Bond, Protec Cem, Durelon, Panavia 21)
outcomes: load required to de-cement each coping
facts.main_result: Mean de-cementation load ranged from 3.18 kg (Temp Bond) to 36.53 kg (Panavia 21), with Durelon 23.55 and Protec Cem 18.98 kg.
facts.limitations: In vitro study; results with natural teeth abutments may not transfer to implant abutments.

facts.population: Titanium (grades 1-5) and Ni-Cr discs cemented to sliced extracted maxillary first molars
facts.intervention: Cementing titanium discs with zinc polycarboxylate, glass ionomer or zinc phosphate cement, then shear testing and SEM
facts.comparison: Ni-Cr control and the three cements against each other
facts.main_result: Mean shear bond strength ranged 0.31 to 15.6 MPa; zinc polycarboxylate cement was highest but corroded the titanium alloy.
facts.funding_coi: No financial support; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Short one-week duration, no time-dependent actions and no titanium surface treatment.

facts.population: Silver-palladium complete metal crowns on metal dies of a prepared dentoform premolar with three finish lines
facts.intervention: Cementation with zinc phosphate or glass-ionomer at seating forces of 25, 100 and 300 N on chamfer, shoulder or beveled-shoulder margins
facts.main_result: Higher seating forces improved seating but not retention; shoulder margins and glass-ionomer gave greater retention than chamfer and zinc phosphate
facts.sample_size: Crowns for three dies; each combination repeated 10 times

facts.population: Twenty stone dies (10 from a shoulder die, 10 from a shoulder-bevel die) with nonprecious alloy cast crowns
facts.intervention: Crown cementation with die spacer, 5 or 30 lb seating force, two cements and two seating aids
facts.comparison: No die spacer vs die spacer; zinc phosphate vs glass ionomer; 5 vs 30 lb; shoulder vs bevel
outcomes: crown seating discrepancy measured with micrometer
facts.main_result: Die spacer, 30 lb seating force and glass ionomer cement each significantly improved crown seating; the bevel improved seating under heavy force or glass ionomer.

facts.intervention: Literature analysis and market research on definitive resin composite cements to propose a classification
facts.main_result: Proposes classifying resin cements as adhesive/multi-step, self-adhesive/one-step, or universal (one- or multi-step); only three products meet the criteria for universal cement.
materials_brands: RelyX Universal with Scotchbond Universal Plus
Panavia SA Universal with Clearfil Universal Bond Quick
facts.funding_coi: Open access funding by Universita degli Studi di Bologna (CRUI-CARE); authors declare no financial interest in the companies
facts.limitations: Despite promising in vitro results, clinical trials and long-term laboratory studies are needed to confirm universal cements.

facts.population: Eighteen caries-free human molars (flat dentin) bonded to CAD/CAM resin blocks
facts.intervention: Novel experimental light-cured resin cement HL-100C
facts.comparison: Panavia V5 dual-cured resin cement and Clearfil AP-X composite
outcomes: microtensile bond strength at 24 h and 7 days
facts.main_result: Resin cement type significantly affected µTBS, and the experimental light-cured cement HL showed better bonding performance and higher KHN than Panavia V5.
facts.funding_coi: Grant in aid for scientific research, Ministry of Education of Japan; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: In vitro study limitations (not itemised).

facts.population: Fifty Co-Cr CAD-CAM implant abutment replicas with matching crowns
facts.intervention: Precementation of crowns on CAD-CAM precementation abutments with 25, 50, 75 or 100 µm reductions before definitive cementation
facts.comparison: Conventional cementation with glass ionomer cement (G0)
facts.main_result: Precementation with a 50 µm abutment (A50) reduced subgingival residual cement without affecting retention; cement weight G50 7.2 ±0.6 mg vs G25 6.0 ±1.1 mg.
facts.funding_coi: Zhejiang Provincial Health Commission grant 2018KY059
facts.limitations: In vitro study; limitations not itemised.

facts.population: Healthy patients aged 20 to 50 with single titanium implants in the premolar region
facts.intervention: Cementation of a modified metal-ceramic crown on a titanium abutment with three luting cements at three peri-implant collar heights, retrieving and measuring residual cement
facts.comparison: Low (<2 mm), medium (2-4 mm) and high (>4 mm) collar height groups, and resin vs glass ionomer vs zinc oxide noneugenol cement
facts.main_result: Residual cement increased with collar height (high collar about 2.1-2.3 mm3 vs low collar 0.08-0.33 mm3) and zinc oxide noneugenol cement left significantly less than resin or glass ionomer cement, which did not differ.
facts.sample_size: 30 implant sites (10 per collar-height group), each tested with 3 cements
materials_brands: GC Gold Label 1 glass ionomer cement
RelyX Temp NE zinc oxide noneugenol cement
facts.funding_coi: No specific grant funding

facts.key_finding: Magazine issue on ceramics and surface treatments: ceramic restorations are moving toward monolithic, more translucent zirconia and lithium disilicate, and chemical surface treatments (silane or MDP-containing primers) give the highest resin-cement bond strength. It also holds a NiTi endodontic file comparison and product evaluations.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Match the intaglio surface treatment to the ceramic: hydrofluoric acid plus silane for glass-ceramics, sandblasting plus MDP primer for zirconia.

facts.main_result: Current dental ceramics (glass-ceramics, polycrystalline ceramics, PICNs) have improved in strength and optical properties, and color-gradient/strength-graded blocks, CAD-CAM and 3D printing are advancing restoration production.
facts.funding_coi: No disclosures

outcomes: development, strengthening, strength, color and aesthetics of all-ceramic systems
facts.main_result: No single universal all-ceramic material or system exists for all clinical cases; choice must follow indications, contraindications, laboratory and clinical evidence and patient aesthetic needs.
facts.funding_coi: Grant from the University of Malaya (PG179-2014B); scholarship from the Iraqi government

facts.key_finding: Textbook chapter on dental ceramics: how porcelains and glass ceramics are made (sintering, casting, hot pressing, CAD-CAM milling) and how higher crystalline content raises strength and fracture toughness while lowering translucency, from feldspathic porcelain to Y-TZP cores.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Ceramic choice trades strength against translucency, so match the material and fabrication method to the restoration's load and esthetic demands.

facts.journal: American Journal of Materials Engineering and Technology
facts.main_result: Fabrication technology of dental ceramics has advanced greatly, with a ten-fold increase in flexural strength and fracture toughness.

facts.journal: International Journal of Dentistry and Oral Science
facts.main_result: Dental ceramics have reached a stage where long-span metal-free posterior FPDs can be made.

facts.intervention: Proposed classification of ceramic and ceramic-like materials into glass-matrix, polycrystalline and resin-matrix ceramics
facts.main_result: Ceramic and ceramic-like materials are organized into three families: glass-matrix, polycrystalline and resin-matrix ceramics
facts.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq grant; authors reported no conflicts of interest

facts.intervention: Fabrication of porcelain veneers and crowns on platinum foil
facts.main_result: Platinum foil restorations showed excellent esthetic results and good fit with shorter production times; thermal-expansion porcelain cracks are unheard of with the technique.

facts.intervention: Twin foil technique: inner unplated 0.025 mm platinum foil as matrix plus outer tin-plated oxidized foil bonded to aluminous core porcelain
facts.main_result: Aluminous porcelain crowns bonded to thin tin-oxide-coated platinum foil need metal linings under 0.05 mm, cutting cost and improving aesthetics, and allow a porcelain butt fit.
facts.funding_coi: Work done on behalf of the National Research Development Corporation

facts.population: Aluminous porcelain bonded to platinum foil and other metal substrates
facts.intervention: Coating the metal with a thin oxidisable metal layer (tin, indium, others) before firing porcelain
facts.main_result: Tin coating of 0.2-2.0 µm before firing gave good porcelain-platinum bonding; tin and indium were the acceptable coatings for dental use.
facts.sample_size: Bond strengths are means of at least eight tests
facts.funding_coi: Grants from the Department of Health and Social Security and the National Research Development Corporation

facts.main_result: Short-term clinical performance of zirconia-reinforced lithium silicates and lithium-aluminium disilicates is comparable to lithium disilicate.
facts.funding_coi: First author funded by a Saudi Arabian Cultural Bureau scholarship; funder had no role; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: LSC strength remains inadequate for multiunit prostheses in the molar region

facts.population: Aluminous porcelain disks (15 mm diameter, 2.0 mm thick) fired on platinum foil
facts.intervention: Platinum foil bonded to the porcelain via tin oxide coating
facts.comparison: Disks fired on pure (uncoated) platinum foil
outcomes: breaking stress in disk rupture test
facts.main_result: Mean breaking stress rose from 70.48 to 128.96 N/mm2, about 83% stronger with bonded platinum foil.
facts.limitations: Reduction of subsurface pores could not be confirmed by direct observation (micrography and SEM inconclusive).

facts.main_result: Silicate ceramics have the best esthetics but are weaker than polycrystalline and resin-based ceramics, so they are mainly used as veneering ceramics.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts declared

facts.main_result: Successful ceramic restorations depend on material selection, manufacturing technique and restoration design
facts.funding_coi: No disclosures

facts.population: 22 participants (110 implants) with full-arch mandibular prostheses re-examined at 25 years
facts.intervention: Three implants placed alternately between the mental foramina: microtextured 3.6 mm internal-connection machined collar, microtextured 1.2 mm external-connection collar, machined 1.2 mm external-connection collar
facts.comparison: Shorter (1.2 mm) vs longer (3.6 mm) machined collar; microtextured vs machined surface
facts.main_result: Microtextured implants with the 3.6 mm collar lost 1.77 mm of bone versus 0.85 mm (machined) and 1.00 mm (microtextured) with the 1.2 mm collar (p<.001).
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the Faculty of Dental Medicine, Université de Montréal; authors report no conflict of interest

facts.population: Human studies reporting bleeding on probing, probing depth or case definitions of peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis
facts.intervention: Design elements of the implant supracrestal complex: emergence profile and angle, tissue height, neck design, abutment/prosthesis material, retention and connection type
facts.main_result: With bone-level implants, a wide emergence angle combined with a convex emergence profile was linked to peri-implantitis; evidence on abutment/prosthesis material and retention type was limited or inconclusive.
facts.limitations: Limited by lack of consensus definitions, validated outcome measures and diverse methods

facts.main_result: Proposes a two-part definition of attached gingiva, measured from the sulcus base to the MGJ when the biologic width is supracrestal and from the bone crest to the MGJ when it is subcrestal.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.population: 45 patients needing a single ceramic crown
facts.intervention: Digital shade selection with a smartphone (iPhone XS) and a light-correcting device with a cross-polarizing filter, and with a digital camera
facts.comparison: Visual shade selection with a shade guide
outcomes: color difference (DE) between crown and adjacent tooth
facts.main_result: Mean DE was 5.32 for visual selection versus 2.75 for digital camera (P=.002) and 2.34 for smartphone (P=.001); the two digital methods did not differ (P=.857).
facts.funding_coi: Partially supported by Fondecyt

facts.population: Maxillary and mandibular complete dentures fabricated on edentulous models
facts.intervention: CAD-CAM-milled versus 3D-printed dentures with 90- or 45-degree build angles and light polymerization with or without the reference model
facts.comparison: CAD-CAM-milled dentures versus four 3D-printed subgroups
facts.main_result: CAD-CAM-milled dentures had the smallest dimensional deviations; in 3D printing a 90-degree build angle with additional light polymerization on the cast was most accurate
facts.sample_size: 10 sets per group (milled and four printed subgroups)
facts.funding_coi: Grants from National Taiwan University Hospital and Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau, Ministry of Science and Technology

facts.population: Published clinical case reports of floor-of-mouth hematoma after implant placement (1986-2010)
facts.main_result: Reported studies were mostly case series showing hematoma is a very rare complication; dental CT planning and accurate implant length are recommended to avoid it.
facts.limitations: No randomized controlled trials exist; all reports were case series

facts.population: 27 reported cases of life-threatening bleeding during or after implant placement
facts.main_result: Most of the 27 cases bled in the anterior interforaminal region, and most needed intubation or tracheotomy.

facts.population: 596 patients with implant-supported reconstructions, randomly sampled from a Swedish registry
facts.main_result: 42% of patients (251 of 596) had at least one technical or biological complication over about 9 years; extent of therapy and periodontitis were risk factors.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Swedish public and research grants; two authors report fees from Dentsply Sirona and/or Straumann outside the work

facts.main_result: Every study of dental-office curing lights found most were poorly maintained and delivered inadequate output, risking undercured resin.

facts.population: Patients undergoing gingival augmentation procedures with or without gingival recession defects, in 105 RCTs
facts.intervention: Gingival phenotype modification with autogenous (CTG, FGG), allogeneic (ADM) or xenogenic (collagen matrix) grafts, with coronally advanced flap or apically positioned flap
facts.comparison: Flap alone (root coverage) or apically positioned flap alone / untreated sites (non-root coverage)
facts.main_result: All grafts increased gingival thickness versus flap alone; keratinized tissue increased significantly only with CTG or ADM in root coverage; autogenous grafts (CTG/FGG) were superior in all comparisons.
facts.sample_size: 105 RCTs (95 root coverage with 3,539 treated recessions; 10 non-root coverage with 699 sites)
facts.follow_up: At least 12 months for root coverage, 6 months for non-root coverage
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts declared; partially supported by the University of Michigan Periodontal Graduate Student Research Fund

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: One 23-year-old woman with gingival recession on the mandibular left canine
facts.intervention: Single-incision technique to harvest subepithelial connective tissue grafts from the palate
facts.main_result: A single incision parallel to the gingival margin yields grafts of variable size and the palatal donor site heals by primary intention; the case showed root coverage and resolved hypersensitivity at 4 months
facts.limitations: Reduced visibility of the donor site during graft preparation

facts.population: Patients with buccal soft tissue dehiscence around single implants in the esthetic area
facts.intervention: Crown removal, abutment reduction, coronally advanced flap with connective tissue graft and final restoration
facts.main_result: Mean dehiscence coverage was 99.2% with 79% complete coverage at 5 years, with increases in soft tissue thickness (0.3 mm) and keratinized tissue height (0.5 mm) versus 1 year.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

facts.population: 20 patients with buccal soft tissue dehiscence around a single implant in the esthetic area
facts.intervention: Crown removal, abutment reduction, coronally advanced flap with connective tissue graft and final restoration
facts.comparison: Unrestored contralateral tooth used as reference
facts.main_result: One-year mean dehiscence coverage was 96.3% with complete coverage in 75% of sites; tissue thickness increased by 1.54 mm.

facts.population: 20 subjects with Seibert class I ridge defects (single tooth gaps) in the anterior maxilla
facts.intervention: Vascularized interpositional periosteal-connective tissue graft (pediculated)
facts.comparison: Free subepithelial connective tissue graft
facts.main_result: Both techniques augmented the ridge; after 6 months the pediculated graft showed significantly less shrinkage (P = 0.03).
facts.funding_coi: Ege University Research Foundation grant; no conflict of interest

facts.main_result: Soft tissue grafting at implant sites is advocated; increasing keratinized mucosa width benefits peri-implant health and soft tissue thickness helps prevent mucosal recession.

facts.population: 20 patients with Miller Class I or II recession defects (52 teeth)
facts.intervention: Coronally advanced flap with subepithelial connective tissue graft using full-thickness flap reflection
facts.comparison: CAF with SCTG using partial-thickness flap reflection
facts.main_result: Mean root coverage was 97% (full-thickness) versus 95% (partial-thickness); no significant difference in GR reduction, KT gain or PD.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: More expanded studies are needed to confirm the findings

facts.population: seven monkeys
facts.intervention: Free connective tissue grafts from keratinized gingiva transplanted into alveolar mucosa pouches, then exposed to epithelialize from surrounding alveolar mucosa
facts.comparison: Alveolar mucosa connective tissue grafts (controls)
facts.main_result: Gingival connective tissue grafts became covered with keratinized epithelium like normal gingiva, whereas alveolar mucosa grafts were covered by non-keratinized epithelium

facts.journal: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
facts.population: Patients needing single-tooth replacement in the anterior maxilla after extraction (48 in final sample)
facts.intervention: Immediate-load post-extractive implant with subepithelial connective tissue graft placed by tunnel technique
facts.comparison: Immediate-load post-extractive implant without raising a flap (no graft)
facts.main_result: Grafted sites gained 35% in thickness versus -10% in non-grafted, and had higher mean PES (8 vs 6.65) at 2 years.
materials_brands: Straumann Tapered Effect / Bone Level SLActive implants

facts.population: 33 stone casts from 30 patients with single posterior tooth defects
facts.intervention: Digital design and 3D thickness analysis of individual soft tissue substitutes with clustering to derive average shapes
facts.main_result: Three average STS shapes were identified (maxilla square n=13, rectangle n=11; mandible n=9) with highest thickness in the buccal portion (median 2 mm).
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Geistlich Pharma AG; one author is a Geistlich employee; no conflicts declared

facts.population: Patients with dental implants treated with soft tissue augmentation, from prospective clinical studies
facts.intervention: Soft tissue augmentation (bilaminar or apically positioned flap) with FGG, CTG, ADM or collagen matrix
facts.comparison: Non-augmented implants where reported

facts.population: 14 sites in 8 subjects with less than 2 mm keratinised gingiva and pocketing under 1 mm
facts.intervention: Free connective tissue grafts harvested by three methods to widen keratinised gingiva

facts.population: Systemically healthy humans with dental implants
facts.intervention: Connective tissue graft to increase peri-implant soft tissue thickness
facts.comparison: No grafting, or soft tissue substitutes

facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest reported

facts.population: Patients with buccal soft tissue dehiscence around loaded dental implants, without peri-implantitis

facts.comparison: Baseline or any other augmentation procedure

facts.funding_coi: No competing interests declared
facts.limitations: Only one RCT with high risk of bias, high heterogeneity and limited sample sizes

facts.population: systemically healthy patients with dental implants
facts.intervention: soft tissue grafting to increase keratinized tissue width or mucosal thickness at implant sites
facts.comparison: no grafting (maintenance) or a different graft type

facts.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation grant; authors report no conflict of interest

facts.funding_coi: Funded by Geistlich Pharma AG and the University of Zurich clinic
facts.limitations: Heterogeneity of results between centers

facts.population: six beagle dogs with surgically created gingival recession defects

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: patients with a failing maxillary anterior tooth treated with immediate implant placement and provisionalization (24 without graft, 31 with graft)

facts.intervention: soft tissue augmentation (keratinized mucosa or volume), alone or combined with hard tissue augmentation

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants

facts.population: single implants adjacent to teeth and two adjacent implants in the anterior maxilla

facts.journal: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Five patients aged 32-53 years with hyperplastic tissue response after connective tissue grafting

facts.funding_coi: Authors declare no financial interest in companies whose materials are included

facts.population: patients in need of soft tissue augmentation around single or multiple implants

facts.population: 44 patients undergoing epithelialized gingival graft harvesting from the palate

facts.main_result: Pain was significantly lower in the cyanoacrylate group on every day studied and analgesic consumption was lower; graft width < 14 mm was associated with less discomfort.

facts.population: clinical studies of soft tissue augmentation around dental implants reporting PROMs

facts.population: 16 patients with small buccal bone dehiscences (<=3 mm) after single implant placement, plus 6 negative-control patients without dehiscence

facts.population: Patients with a single implant in the esthetic zone (15-25) placed with simultaneous guided bone regeneration

facts.population: 37 patients with 114 bilateral single Miller Class I and II gingival recession defects

facts.main_result: Bacterial penetration at the implant-abutment interface may relate to early crestal bone loss, but an association with peri-implant diseases is not demonstrated.

facts.population: 50 consecutive partially edentulous patients with 69 implants

facts.funding_coi: No financial support; two authors received honoraria from DENTSPLY Friadent

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants

facts.population: 428 patients with 898 internal conical connection implants (Oneplant FIT, Warantec) treated 2006-2014 at Seoul National University Dental Hospital

facts.main_result: Mechanical complications occurred in 47.9% of implants (screw loosening 46.4%, abutment fracture 11.4%); molars and male sex raised risk, splinting and gold screws (for loosening) lowered it.

facts.funding_coi: Korea Medical Device Development Fund grant (Korean government ministries)

facts.population: Four designs of direct-to-implant BTI butt-joint restorations (specimens)

facts.journal: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
facts.population: 18 patients with edentulous mandibles (107 implants)

facts.journal: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
facts.population: 85 patients with 228 delayed-loaded Ankylos implants
facts.intervention: Subcrestal placement (shoulder at least 0.5 mm below bone crest) of platform-shifted implants

outcomes: mesial and distal crestal bone loss
facts.main_result: Mean mesial bone loss was 1.84 mm (subcrestal) versus 1.41 mm (crestal) with no significant difference (p = .130), and cumulative survival was 97.8%.
facts.funding_coi: Self-supported; no conflicts of interest declared

facts.journal: Journal of Biomedical Materials Research: Part A

facts.intervention: Conical (Morse Taper) implant-abutment connection systems

authors: Thiago de Almeida Prado Naves Carneiro
facts.population: External hexagon implants with conical abutments (in vitro assemblies)
facts.intervention: Abutment tightening torques of 10, 20 and 32 Ncm with E. coli inoculation
facts.comparison: Different bacterial suspension volumes (phase 1) and torque groups compared with each other
outcomes: bacterial microleakage by broth turbidity over 14 days

Escherichia coli ATCC 35218 in BHI broth

facts.population: Human osteoblastic cells in culture

facts.comparison: Metal ion-free culture medium
outcomes: IL-6, IL-8, COX-2, caspase-8, OPG and RANKL expression

facts.main_result: No significant difference in cumulative implant survival between implant-level CoCr/titanium prostheses and abutment-level titanium prostheses after five years (98.6% vs 97.6%).

facts.population: Eight commercial dental alloys (four high-noble, two noble, two base metal)
facts.intervention: Electrochemical polarization resistance and static immersion elemental-release tests in acidified artificial saliva
facts.main_result: Polarization resistance and elemental release were inversely correlated (R2 = 0.886; F about 44 vs critical F 13.7).

facts.population: Seven dental alloys coupled with titanium and Ti6Al4V implant specimens
facts.intervention: Electrochemical measurement of galvanic coupling in artificial salivas plus Auger surface analysis
facts.main_result: All implant-alloy couples showed very low galvanic corrosion rates, confirmed by surface analysis.

facts.population: 198 patients with 270 implant-supported fixed prostheses on 1117 implants

facts.comparison: Type 3 gold alloy frameworks veneered with ceramic or acrylic
facts.main_result: Success, survival and complication rates were similar for cobalt-chromium and type 3 gold frameworks, and biomaterial combination did not influence implant survival.

facts.population: Titanium discs coupled with dental alloys (gold-based, palladium-based, non-precious) in artificial saliva

facts.main_result: Titanium in the oral environment can degrade progressively by combined wear and corrosion (tribocorrosion), affecting implant and prosthesis performance and releasing potentially toxic debris and ions.

facts.population: Eight CAD/CAM implant bars (six Co-Cr, two titanium) milled from the same design on reproduction casts of a mandibular edentulous master cast with four implants

facts.comparison: Bars from different manufacturers (laboratory vs central production) compared with each other
outcomes: surface roughness (Sa, Ra) in transmucosal, labial and basal regions

facts.funding_coi: No funding; no conflict of interest

facts.population: One leading academic expert in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery or Oral Surgery per European country

outcomes: influenza virus in air and surface samples
facts.main_result: No pH1N1 virus was found in any air or surface sample; seasonal influenza A (H3N2) was found in air near exam chairs at the pediatric practice on one visit.

facts.population: 28 adults seeking dental treatment at Ohio State University College of Dentistry
facts.intervention: Aerosols collected during ultrasonic scaling, implant osteotomy and restorative procedures, analysed by RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2 and 16S sequencing with source tracking

off_topic_reason: A general medical face-mask material test specification with no dental clinical management content.

facts.intervention: Test methods and classification (Level 1-3 barrier) of medical face mask materials
facts.limitations: The specification evaluates only the mask materials, not the seal against the face or other design features
facts.key_finding: This ASTM standard defines minimum performance requirements and test methods for medical face mask materials, classifying them into Level 1, 2 and 3 barrier classes by bacterial filtration, differential pressure, sub-micron particle filtration, synthetic blood penetration resistance and flammability.

off_topic_reason: A generic face-mask blood-penetration test standard with no dental content.

facts.population: Medical face mask specimens
facts.intervention: About 2 mL of synthetic blood projected horizontally at a face mask at 450, 500 and 635 cm/s
outcomes: penetration of synthetic blood to inner mask face (pass/fail)
facts.limitations: It does not address mask design, filtration efficiency, breathability or airborne exposure pathways

facts.clinical_bottom_line: A mask's rating reflects only splash and splatter penetration resistance, not filtration, fit or airborne protection.

off_topic_reason: Hospital room surface disinfection article with no dental setting or dental relevance.

facts.intervention: Abutment and crown contour modifications in critical and subcritical zones of implant restorations

facts.population: Randomly selected Swedish patients provided with implant-supported restorative therapy in 2003 (2,765 patient files; 596 examined clinically)

facts.main_result: Early implant loss occurred in 4.4% of patients (1.4% of implants) and late loss in 4.2% of examined patients (2.0% of implants); 7.6% of examined patients lost at least 1 implant.

facts.funding_coi: Swedish Social Insurance Agency, Swedish Research Council, TUA research Gothenburg and Swedish Dental Society; some authors report fees from Dentsply Implants IH

facts.population: 15 3D-printed mandibular models with missing first molar and single implant analog, cleaned by 30 volunteers (periodontists, hygienists, laypersons)

facts.population: Three clinical cases of patients with overcontoured implant crowns and peri-implantitis or high risk of it

facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: The authors note there was no randomized clinical trial on restorative design and contour, and call for future studies.

facts.population: Digest of a cross-sectional study: 83 patients with 168 implants (101 bone-level, 67 tissue-level)

facts.limitations: Few tissue-level patients (only two with peri-implantitis), implant status rather than bone loss as outcome, and facial/lingual contours not visible radiographically.
facts.key_finding: This digest summarizes a cross-sectional study of 83 patients (168 implants, mean 10.9 years): an emergence angle above 30 degrees was a significant risk indicator for peri-implantitis in bone-level implants but not tissue-level implants, and a convex profile added risk.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Avoid over-contoured implant restorations (emergence angle above 30 degrees, convex profile), particularly on bone-level implants.

facts.main_result: Hyperglycaemia negatively influences bone formation and remodelling, reduces osseointegration and increases implant failure percentages in diabetic patients.

outcomes: clinical diagnostic parameters (probing depth, bleeding on probing, suppuration)

facts.funding_coi: The authors declared no direct conflicts of interest.

facts.main_result: Recent clinical studies and systematic reviews suggest implant survival is manageable even with poor glycemic control, while long-term vulnerabilities such as marginal bone loss and peri-implantitis risk remain in question.

facts.journal: The Journal of the American Dental Association

facts.population: Sixty-six patients with a single posterior edentulous site

outcomes: early implant failure in patients on antiresorptive drugs

facts.funding_coi: Conferences fully funded by the EAO to avoid commercial influence

facts.population: Preclinical in vivo (dog) studies and clinical studies of dental implants with or without peri-implantitis, via two systematic reviews and one critical review

facts.journal: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry

facts.intervention: Preparation, prevention and management of medical emergencies, including an emergency drug kit

facts.population: 48 devitalized human upper first premolars cut at the CEJ
