facts.comparison: Flat overlays without endo-core (negative control) and crowns with post and core (positive control)
outcomes: marginal integrity (closed margins) before and after thermo-mechanical loading
facts.main_result: Survival after stepwise fatigue loading did not differ significantly between groups (4/8 overlays, 5/12 endocrowns with 2 mm core, 6/12 with 4 mm core, 3/12 post-and-core crowns survived 105000 cycles); four overlays debonded early.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the Swiss Dental Association (SSO); materials supplied by Ivoclar-Vivadent; authors declare no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Authors frame conclusions as limited to this in-vitro study and call for further studies.

facts.population: 42 sound human mandibular molars, endodontically treated and cut 2 mm above the CEJ
facts.intervention: Endocrowns made of conventional composite, bulk fill composite, composite modeled with adhesive (SBMP or SBU), or IPS e.max
facts.comparison: IPS e.max lithium disilicate endocrowns (positive control) and unprepared sound teeth (negative control)
facts.main_result: Load-to-fracture (1979.2 N e.max to 2681.4 N bulk fill) and work-of-fracture did not differ among materials, but e.max endocrowns had about 71% irreparable fractures versus about 14% for composite with SBMP.
facts.funding_coi: Financed in part by CAPES (Brazil); authors declare no conflict of interest

authors: Wellington Luiz de Oliveira da Rosa
facts.population: 8 studies: 3 clinical trials and 5 in vitro studies of endocrowns
facts.intervention: Endocrown restorations
facts.comparison: Conventional treatments (intraradicular posts, direct composite resin, inlay/onlay)
facts.main_result: Clinical success of endocrowns was 94 to 100%; pooled fracture strength was higher than conventional treatments overall (p = 0.03) but not in posterior teeth alone (p = 0.07).
facts.sample_size: 8 studies; 102 teeth in the in vitro studies
facts.follow_up: Clinical trials: up to 6, 15 or 36 months
facts.limitations: Caution is needed interpreting in vitro results; clinical trials scored poorly on bias items.

facts.journal: Journal of Istanbul University Faculty of Dentistry
facts.intervention: Endocrown restorations for endodontically treated teeth with extensive coronal loss
facts.comparison: Conventional post-core and fixed partial dentures
facts.main_result: Endocrowns are presented as an alternative to post-core restorations with better esthetics and mechanical performance, lower cost and shorter clinical time.
facts.funding_coi: No funding and no conflict of interest declared

facts.journal: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
facts.population: One adult male patient with worn teeth and amalgam restorations with recurrent caries, seeking a smile makeover
facts.intervention: Lithium disilicate vonlays (onlay with extended buccal veneer surface) on posterior teeth, with anterior porcelain veneers
facts.main_result: Authors report, from experience, under 1% annual failure for bicuspid vonlays with enough enamel and no documented failures for monolithic lithium disilicate molar vonlays.

facts.population: 3D finite element model of a maxillary central incisor
facts.intervention: Endocrowns of composite, sintered alumina or feldspathic ceramic
facts.comparison: Sound tooth and glass fiber post restorations with feldspathic or alumina crown
facts.main_result: High modulus materials such as alumina altered the natural biomechanical behavior with high interface stress, while composite endocrowns gave low stress concentration.
facts.limitations: Conclusions apply within a linear static analysis using an arbitrary 10 N load.

facts.population: 320 automated osteotomies in standardised bone specimens
facts.intervention: Ceramic (zirconia-based) implant drills of four diameters, with and without external saline irrigation, at 10 and 16 mm depth
facts.comparison: Stainless steel implant drills
outcomes: temperature change at 1 and 2 mm from the osteotomy
facts.main_result: Steel drills produced significantly lower temperatures than ceramic drills; with irrigation all steel drills stayed below 47 C while small-diameter ceramic drills reached or exceeded it at 16 mm depth.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the authors' institutions and ITI Research Grant 772_2011

facts.journal: Medicina Oral Patología Oral y Cirugia Bucal
facts.population: 25 patients with single-tooth edentulism receiving 30 implants
facts.intervention: Low-speed (50 rpm) drilling without irrigation
facts.comparison: Conventional high-speed (800 rpm) drilling with saline irrigation
outcomes: peri-implant marginal bone loss at 12 months
facts.main_result: Mean bone loss was 0.83 mm with irrigation versus 0.62 mm without (p>0.05), and success was 93.3% versus 100%.
facts.funding_coi: Authors declare no competing interests

facts.intervention: Cosmetic dentistry guided by smile design principles
facts.key_finding: A patient-facing brochure from a cosmetic dentist listing about 21 smile design principles, for example a central incisor width/height ratio of 75-80%, 2-4 mm of upper teeth showing at rest, 1-3 mm of gum showing in a full smile, and golden proportion tooth widths, followed by a self-assessment quiz.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: It is practice marketing and patient education with unreferenced rules of thumb, so it is useful only as a plain checklist of commonly cited smile analysis criteria, not as evidence.

facts.intervention: Use of the golden ratio (phi) as a measure of facial proportion and symmetry
facts.main_result: The authors conclude that the golden ratio can characterize symmetrical forms and propose its use in facial aesthetics.
facts.funding_coi: No financial disclosures or conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Phi ratio has difficulty explaining facial harmony in the moving face and inter-racial mixtures.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
facts.population: One patient with an excessively worn dentition (case report)
facts.intervention: Rehabilitation of the worn dentition using a digital workflow combined with conventional procedures
facts.main_result: The digital workflow aims at faster, more predictable treatment, but a combination of digital and conventional procedures is still needed for complex cases.
facts.limitations: Digital technology alone is not sufficient; digital and conventional procedures must be combined in complex cases.

facts.population: Maxillary anterior teeth with tooth size and proportion discrepancies (clinical examples)
facts.intervention: Aesthetic measurement gauges (T-Bar and In-Line Proportion Gauge tips, preset 78% width/length ratio) used to diagnose and correct tooth size discrepancies
outcomes: clinical crown length after crown lengthening
facts.main_result: The gauges give objective width/length targets for maxillary anterior teeth (lateral 6.5/8.5, canine 7.5/9.5, central 8.5/11 mm) at a preset 78% ratio.
facts.funding_coi: Author is the inventor of Chu's Aesthetic Gauges and a consultant to Hu-Friedy

facts.population: Patients accepted for treatment in an Advanced Education in General Dentistry program
facts.intervention: Seven-point dental esthetic checklist (midline, vertical axis, horizontal, central incisors, incisal edge line, smile line, profile and phonetics) for diagnostic work-up
facts.main_result: A seven-point checklist prompts residents to assess lip, cheek, tongue, smile and facial features and so aim treatment at dentofacial harmony.
facts.limitations: The checklist is not a complete list of all possible categories and nuances of an esthetic assessment.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Healthy Caucasian adults aged 19-29 with natural anterior dentition
facts.intervention: Standardized photographic analysis of smile parameters (midlines, lip position and curvature, incisal curve vs lower lip, teeth displayed, tooth form, tooth and lip arc slope)
outcomes: tooth arc and lip arc slope
facts.main_result: Average smile: coinciding midlines (85%), average smile line (52%), straight upper lip curvature, no lower-lip contact (75%), teeth to second premolar (45%), oval tooth most common (63%); tooth arc slope 9 degrees, lip arc 13 degrees.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Additional research is needed to verify the findings in other populations and with advanced methods.

facts.population: 146 extracted human maxillary anterior teeth from white subjects, worn and unworn
facts.intervention: Measurement of crown width (W), length (L) and width/length ratio (R) on standardized digital images
facts.comparison: Worn versus unworn teeth within each tooth group
facts.main_result: Incisal wear did not change crown width but shortened crowns; width/length ratio was highest in worn central incisors (87%) and lowest in unworn canines and lateral incisors (73%), unworn central incisors 78%.
facts.sample_size: 146 teeth (44 central incisors, 41 lateral incisors, 38 canines, 23 first premolars)

facts.intervention: Tooth-colored restorations: posterior composite resin, ceramic inlays/onlays, CEREC, porcelain laminate veneers, all-ceramic crowns and fixed partial dentures
facts.main_result: Prognosis of esthetic restorations depends mainly on choice of material, precise technique and patient selection.
facts.sample_size: Medline search 1986-2006 plus manual search of textbooks
facts.limitations: For zirconia, 5- to 10-year clinical studies on success rate and mode of failure are lacking.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Patients with implant-supported restorations in the esthetic zone (maxillary and mandibular anterior teeth and premolars) in 58 included studies
facts.intervention: Prosthodontic parameters: 3D implant position, provisional restorations and their timing, platform size and form, abutment and definitive restoration material, retention mode
outcomes: esthetic outcome indices (PES/WES, papilla score, midfacial mucosal level)
facts.main_result: Facial malpositioning of implants consistently increased mucosal recession; no significant esthetic difference between all-ceramic and metal-ceramic prostheses, and no firm conclusion for cement vs screw retention.
facts.sample_size: 58 studies (15 RCTs, 6 cohort studies, 37 case series)
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: The literature is small and generally of low quality, and most studies concern single-tooth replacement.

facts.population: Partially dentate adults needing fixed implant-supported prostheses
facts.intervention: Definitive fixed implant-supported prosthesis without a prior interim restoration
facts.comparison: Interim fixed implant-supported prosthesis before the definitive prosthesis
facts.main_result: Only two RCTs qualified; evidence is insufficient to support or refute providing an interim restoration, though interim restorations may improve esthetics and omitting them may reduce chair time.
facts.limitations: Heterogeneity of study methodologies and outcome measures prevented meta-analysis.

facts.population: Patients with single-tooth implant rehabilitation in the esthetic area
facts.intervention: Objective esthetic indices and patient-reported outcome measures for assessing single-implant outcomes
outcomes: agreement between professional and patient esthetic ratings
facts.main_result: No consensus exists on a universal esthetic index for implant-supported crowns, and patients rate cosmetic outcomes more favorably than professionals do.
facts.limitations: It is not yet possible to provide evidence-based conclusions on success assessment in implant dentistry.

facts.main_result: Very few studies of plastic surgery around teeth and implants consider patient needs (true end points), and no validated questionnaire exists to quantify patient esthetic satisfaction.
facts.key_finding: Editorial introducing a Periodontology 2000 volume on esthetics: smile esthetics must be judged within the whole face, and periodontal plastic and implant surgery in the esthetic zone aim at restoring function and meeting patients' esthetic demands. Few studies measure patient-centred outcomes, and clinicians rate results less favorably than patients do.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Assess esthetic results of plastic surgery around teeth and implants with patient-reported measures as well as clinician judgement.

facts.population: Natural dentitions of populations in 6 studies: 395 men and 446 women
facts.intervention: Evaluation of the golden proportion in maxillary anterior tooth width ratios
facts.comparison: Tooth width ratios of male versus female participants
facts.main_result: The golden proportion was not prevalent; lateral-to-central incisor ratio did not differ by sex (P=.22, I2=89%), canine-to-lateral ratio was greater in men (P<.001).
facts.funding_coi: No specific funding received
facts.limitations: High heterogeneity among studies reduced precision of results

facts.intervention: Historical overview of the evolution of aesthetic dentistry over the past 100 years
facts.main_result: Aesthetic dentistry has progressed tremendously over 100 years, especially through digital tools and workflows for 3D interdisciplinary smile design.
facts.funding_coi: No financial support; no conflicts declared

facts.journal: The Journal of Contemporary Dental Practice
facts.population: 376 dental students with natural dentition (Arab subjects)
facts.intervention: Measuring maxillary anterior tooth widths on standardized frontal smile images and testing the golden proportion, RED proportion and golden percentage
outcomes: golden proportion between successive tooth widths
facts.main_result: Golden proportion between right central and lateral incisors in 31.3% of men and 27.1% of women; golden and RED proportions unsuitable, golden percentage usable if adjusted (central 23%, lateral 15%, canine 12%).
facts.funding_coi: Supported financially by the Deanship of Scientific Research, University of Jordan

facts.intervention: Discussion of implant placement alternatives in the esthetic area: timing, 3D position, multiple missing teeth, infected sites, abutment and crown morphology
facts.main_result: Immediate placement can succeed esthetically but is technique sensitive; aiming the implant axis at the incisal edge with a shoulderless abutment allows a natural cervical contour.

facts.journal: Journal of the American Dental Association
facts.intervention: Interdisciplinary approach to diagnosis and management of anterior dental esthetics, planning starting from esthetics
facts.main_result: Treatment planning should start with esthetics, then function, structure and biology, using restorative, orthodontic and periodontal disciplines as needed.

facts.population: Partially edentulous patients with single-unit implants in the esthetic zone (RCTs, minimum 10 patients, 1-year follow-up)
facts.intervention: Immediate or early implant placement and/or immediate loading protocols
facts.comparison: Conventional (delayed) placement and loading protocols
facts.main_result: Immediate and early placement gave stable esthetic outcomes at 1, 2 and 10 years; loading protocols did not influence esthetic outcomes short and medium term.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared; funding not stated
facts.limitations: Small number of included RCTs and limited extracted data

facts.journal: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
facts.key_finding: Full issue 4 of volume 32 (2020) of the Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry, a collection of separate articles, for example a digital full-arch maxillary reconstruction case and in-vitro studies of marginal gap and toothpaste abrasives.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: It is an issue compilation, not a single study; use the individual articles for clinical conclusions.

facts.population: Patients 18 or older with single-tooth implants in the esthetic zone
facts.intervention: Soft tissue augmentation with autologous, allogeneic, xenogeneic or synthetic grafting material
facts.comparison: No soft tissue augmentation or a different graft material
facts.main_result: Grafting gave 0.34 mm less recession and 0.66 mm thicker mid-buccal mucosa after immediate placement, and 0.17 mm less recession after delayed placement, versus no graft at 1 year.
facts.follow_up: At least 1 year after implant placement
facts.funding_coi: No financial support, no conflicts declared
facts.limitations: Large heterogeneity in study designs and few eligible studies per topic

facts.intervention: Macroesthetic smile design criteria based on the facial midline and tooth reveal
facts.main_result: Macroesthetic criteria are organized by facial midline and tooth reveal, and serve as guidelines only.

facts.population: Patients requiring anterior esthetic rehabilitations
facts.intervention: Mathematical tooth proportions: golden proportion, golden percentage and RED proportion
facts.comparison: Not using such formulas
facts.main_result: No formula gave consistent esthetic results; golden proportion occurs between central and lateral incisor in some cases but rarely lateral-canine; golden percentage is a starting point if adjusted.

facts.population: 45 patients with maxillary anterior single-tooth implants
facts.intervention: Early implant placement with GBR, provisional then PFM crown; esthetic outcome by PES/WES
facts.main_result: Mean total PES/WES was 14.7 (range 11 to 18) with all 45 implants meeting osseointegration success criteria
materials_brands: Straumann Dental Implant System (sandblasted acid-etched titanium implants)
facts.funding_coi: Departmental funds of the Universities of Bern and Geneva; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Retrospective design; authors state prospective trials are needed to validate the index

facts.intervention: Review of principles governing smile design
facts.main_result: Smile design should be esthetically appealing, functionally sound, conservative and multidisciplinary

facts.key_finding: Only the title is available: the article presents a proportional smile design method based on the recurring esthetic dental (RED) proportion.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: The RED proportion is offered as a way to plan tooth widths in smile design; details are not in the extracted text.

facts.intervention: Prosthetically driven design measures (white crown morphology, pink ceramics) to compensate peri-implant soft tissue deficiencies in the esthetic zone
facts.main_result: Minor-to-moderate soft tissue deficiencies can be compensated by morphological crown design alone; major deficiencies may need pink ceramics

facts.intervention: Literature review of esthetic guidelines, patient preference studies and anatomic norms for complete dentures
facts.main_result: Little useful evidence-based information exists for restoring dentate appearance in edentulous patients; 3 esthetic concepts identified

facts.intervention: Review of literature on facial bone, implant diameter, implant-tooth distance, abutment design and provisionalization for esthetics
facts.main_result: Generous facial bone, implants under 4 mm, platform-switched abutments, 2-4 mm implant-to-tooth distance, avoiding adjacent implants and early provisionalization favor esthetics

facts.intervention: Prosthetically induced soft tissue topography via custom provisional crown and abutment

facts.journal: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 10 patients with 43 interdental papilla sites in the maxillary anterior region
facts.intervention: Injectable hyaluronic acid gel applied up to five times at 3-week intervals
outcomes: black triangle area, height and width
facts.main_result: 29 of 43 sites had complete papilla reconstruction and 14 improved by 39 to 96%
materials_brands: Teosyal Puresense Global Action hyaluronic acid gel
facts.funding_coi: No financial interest declared
facts.limitations: Results beyond 6 months are not known

facts.intervention: Step-by-step Photoshop technique for smile analysis and digital smile design
facts.main_result: Digital smile design can be completed in about three to four minutes and aids communication between dentist, ceramist and patient

facts.intervention: Review of scientific and artistic principles of smile design
facts.main_result: A comprehensive approach analyzing face, lips, gingiva and teeth is needed for a natural smile that also enhances oral health

facts.population: Published clinical and preclinical studies on hard- and soft-tissue deficiencies at implant sites
facts.intervention: Narrative review of factors and conditions associated with hard- and soft-tissue deficiencies at implants
outcomes: etiological factors of hard- and soft-tissue deficiencies
facts.main_result: Deficiencies at implant sites result from many factors (post-extraction resorption, trauma, periodontitis, peri-implantitis, overload, thin tissues, lack of keratinized mucosa, malpositioning, tooth migration, systemic disease), and combined factors can worsen severity.
facts.funding_coi: Hämmerle and Tarnow report research support and consulting/lecture fees from implant and biomaterial companies (Straumann, Geistlich and others).
facts.limitations: No formal quality assessment or statistical analysis was done, the search was limited to English, and evidence varies from strong to scant across factors.

facts.population: One 44-year-old woman seeking an esthetic consultation
facts.intervention: Facial flow (FF) concept: organic orofacial analysis of the vertical component (facial midline, dental midline, tooth axis)
outcomes: harmony of dental midline and tooth axis with facial structures
facts.main_result: The facial flow concept offers a more organic, perception-based alternative to straight-line, symmetry-driven smile design, using green and red zones to guide decisions.
facts.limitations: Authors state research is needed to define the relationship between facial flow and the lips, and the horizontal component needs further research.

facts.intervention: Application of principles of visual perception (composition, unity, proportion, shade) to denture esthetics
facts.main_result: Understanding perceptual principles can free dentists from confusion in dental esthetics and let them approach denture construction with confidence.

authors: Jéssica Janine Freire Batista de Araújo
facts.journal: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
facts.population: Teeth receiving ceramic veneers, e.g. conoid teeth, diastemas, worn teeth
facts.intervention: Mock-up driven technique: step-by-step conservative preparation for ceramic veneers guided by the desired final contour
facts.comparison: Classic preparation technique (reduction driven by the existing tooth surface) and silicone index technique
facts.main_result: The mock-up driven technique considers the final veneer contour and gives considerably less invasive preparations (cited: 80.5% of preparations confined to enamel).
facts.sample_size: One illustrated case with eight maxillary anterior veneers

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Two esthetic-zone cases with bone-level implants: one single implant and one two adjacent implants
facts.intervention: Dynamic compression technique: soft tissue conditioning with an implant-supported provisional (initial pressure, then release by undercontouring)
facts.main_result: The dynamic compression technique (initial provisional pressure, then undercontouring) is presented as a method to shape peri-implant soft tissue; stable soft tissues at 1 year in both cases; needs further validation.
facts.sample_size: 2 cases (1 single implant, 1 two adjacent implants)
facts.funding_coi: Authors reported no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Authors state clinical studies and in vivo histologic analyses are needed to confirm validity and long-term soft-tissue stability.

facts.intervention: Aesthetic crown lengthening guided by measurement gauges (Chu's Aesthetic Gauges) that link ideal tooth proportion to the amount of osseous resection
facts.main_result: Using tooth proportion and measured osseous resection with the gauges was described as beneficial for aesthetic crown lengthening in a presented case.
facts.follow_up: Recalled at 4 months; restorations cemented at 6 months post-surgery
facts.funding_coi: Dr. Chu is creator of Chu's Aesthetic Gauges and consultant for Hu-Friedy

facts.population: Five male beagle dogs, microgrooved implants placed in the mandible
facts.intervention: Microgrooved-collar one-piece implants of titanium, Y-TZP and Ce-TZP/Al2O3
facts.comparison: The three implant materials (Ti, Y-TZP, Ce-TZP/Al2O3) compared with each other
outcomes: epithelial, connective and soft tissue length
facts.main_result: All implants osseointegrated, with no significant differences in any histomorphometric parameter among Ti, Y-TZP and Ce-TZP/Al2O3 microgrooved implants.
facts.sample_size: 18 implants (6 per material) in 5 dogs; 16 samples measured
materials_brands: Ti: ASTM F67 Grade4 (Allegheny Technologies Japan)
facts.funding_coi: Supported by Nanto, which also processed the implants
facts.limitations: Soft tissue frequently detached from the implant surface on sections; fractured Y-TZP implants reduced that group to four samples.

facts.intervention: Suturing materials and techniques for primary wound closure and flap stabilization in periodontal and implant surgery
facts.main_result: Stable flap adaptation with appropriate suturing is a key prerequisite for optimal surgical outcomes; as few sutures as needed, left 7-10 days.

facts.population: Patients with dental implants (clinical studies)
facts.intervention: Reduced keratinized tissue width (KT < 2 mm) as exposure
facts.comparison: KT width >= 2 mm
outcomes: prevalence of peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis
facts.main_result: Implants with KT < 2 mm had significantly worse BOP, plaque indices, marginal bone loss and mucosal recession than KT >= 2 mm, and higher peri-implantitis prevalence (10.5-44% vs 5.1-8%).
facts.sample_size: 22 articles describing 21 studies (15 cross-sectional, 5 longitudinal comparative, 1 case series)
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded by the authors' departments; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Over half of the studies (13) did not report periodontal health, and mixed KT cut-offs (2 and 0 mm) were pooled, adding heterogeneity.

facts.population: Dental implants and patients in published studies on implant loss
facts.intervention: Narrative review of the etiology, occurrence and consequences of early and late implant loss
facts.main_result: Early implant loss occurs in about 1.5% of implants (1 in 67) and about 4% of patients; late loss in about 3% of implants over 10 years and about 4% of patients; smoking is a risk indicator for early loss and peri-implantitis the main cause of late loss.
facts.follow_up: Late loss assessed over observation periods of 10 years
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Authors note few evaluations of the consequences of implant loss and patient-reported outcomes.

facts.population: Commercially available implants (Astra Tech EV) with multispecies biofilm mounted in 3D-printed intra-bony defect models
facts.intervention: Air-polishing or rotating titanium brush, each combined with saline, alkaline electrolyzed water or N-acetyl-L-cysteine
facts.comparison: Wiping with gauze soaked in saline, AEW or NAC; untreated contaminated implants as negative control
facts.main_result: Air-polishing and rotating titanium brush removed more biofilm and reduced surface carbon more than gauze wiping; chemical adjuncts gave no benefit over saline and no method removed biofilm completely.
facts.sample_size: 123 implants (33 analysed by SEM, n=3 per group)
materials_brands: Astra Tech Implant EV OsseoSpeed (Dentsply Sirona)
Airflow Prophylaxis Master with erythritol powder (EMS)
facts.funding_coi: TUA research funding and Patentmedelsfonden; authors declare no conflicts, though some report honoraria/grants from implant companies
facts.limitations: One implant brand, artificial short-term biofilm without calcified deposits, bacterial viability not assessed, differences from clinical anatomy.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Patients who received Bicon implants at one implant centre, 1992-2000
facts.intervention: Bicon dental implant placement (exposure analysis of demographic, medical, implant, anatomic, prosthetic and reconstructive risk factors)
facts.main_result: Overall complication frequency was 13.9% (10.2% inflammatory, 2.7% prosthetic, 1.0% operative); smoking, 1-stage implants and reconstructive procedures increased complication risk.
facts.sample_size: 677 patients (677 implants analysed, 1 per patient; 2,349 placed)
facts.funding_coi: Institutional research funds, OMS Foundation award and NIH/NIDCR awards

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 1,140 consecutively treated patients who received dental implants from one surgeon, 1982-2003
facts.intervention: Dental implant placement; exposure analysis of patient factors (age, gender, smoking, medical conditions, implant location)
facts.comparison: Patients without the risk factor (e.g. age under 40, healthy patients)
facts.main_result: Implant failure was 8.16% in the maxilla and 4.93% in the mandible; age 60-79 (RR 2.24), smoking (1.56), diabetes (2.75), head and neck radiation (2.73) and postmenopausal estrogen therapy (2.55) raised failure risk.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Published literature on biologic complications and failing oral implants (to December 1998)
facts.intervention: Literature review of diagnosis and treatment of biologic complications and failing implants
facts.main_result: Infection, impaired healing and overload are the major etiologic factors; few clinical and animal studies validate the treatments, which remain largely empirical.
facts.funding_coi: Public research funds; no support from any oral implant company
facts.limitations: Treatment of failing implants lacks systematic scientific validation and rests on empirical experience and in vitro extrapolation.

facts.journal: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
facts.population: Consecutively treated patients at one specialist clinic (Brånemark Clinic), 1986-2012
facts.intervention: Implant placement with turned (Brånemark) and moderately rough (TiUnite, Osseospeed) surfaces
facts.comparison: Turned versus moderately rough surface, upper versus lower jaw, first year versus later
outcomes: annual incidence of first implant failure
failure by jaw and surface type
facts.main_result: 857 patients (10.0%) had at least one failure; first failures were more frequent in upper jaws, mostly within the first year (69%), and with turned versus moderately rough surfaces.
facts.funding_coi: Grants from Nobel Biocare and Swedish foundations

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Patients who received implants at Yonsei University Dental Hospital, 1991-2009
facts.intervention: Implants from Nobel Biocare, Straumann and Biolok; analysis of risk factors for early and late failure
facts.main_result: 150 of 2,796 implants failed (86 early, 64 late); early failures were mainly due to inflammation (47%) and late failures to overloading (53%), with machined surface, reconstructive procedures and two-stage surgery associated with higher failure.
facts.follow_up: Between Feb 1991 and May 2009 (19-year study period)
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare, Straumann and Biolok implants
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.population: Controlled clinical human studies of endosseous root-form titanium implants reporting failure (311 publications)
facts.intervention: Review of factors associated with dental implant failure (surgical, patient, implant and prosthetic factors)
outcomes: implant failure (complete loss of the implant)
facts.main_result: Failure rate was correlated with low insertion torque under early/immediate loading, inexperienced surgeons, maxilla, posterior region, heavy smoking, bone type III-IV, small bone volume, short implants, and overdentures, among others.

facts.population: Seven healthy patients, each with at least 2 periodontally hopeless teeth scheduled for extraction
facts.intervention: Extraction sockets grafted with DFDBA or autologous bone, re-entered 3-13 months later for biopsy and implant placement
facts.comparison: Autologous bone graft in the paired socket
outcomes: presence of vital versus dead graft particles
facts.main_result: DFDBA sockets showed dead graft particles with no bone formation on them, whereas autologous sockets showed vascular channels with woven and lamellar bone.
facts.sample_size: 7 patients, 7 paired sites; biopsies from 6 evaluated
materials_brands: Freeze-dried cortical allograft (DFDBA), LifeNet Transplant Services, 250-500 micron

facts.population: Forty patients needing extraction of a single-rooted non-molar tooth and planning an implant
facts.intervention: Ridge preservation with demineralized freeze-dried bone allograft (DFDBA)
facts.comparison: Mineralized freeze-dried bone allograft (FDBA) from the same donor
facts.main_result: DFDBA gave 38.42% vital bone versus 24.63% for FDBA and fewer residual particles (8.88% vs 25.42%), with no difference in ridge dimension changes.
facts.sample_size: 40 patients (20 per group); 32 received implants with biopsy
facts.follow_up: 19 weeks (18 to 20 weeks) to biopsy and implant placement
materials_brands: FDBA and DFDBA from a single donor, LifeNet Health
facts.funding_coi: LifeNet Health supplied graft materials; authors report no conflicts of interest

facts.population: Subjects with sites completely lacking attached gingiva associated with gingival recession, treated in one private practice
facts.intervention: Free gingival graft, placed at the presurgical margin level (MFGG) or submarginally (SMFGG)
facts.comparison: MFGG versus SMFGG (no untreated control)
facts.main_result: From baseline to 1 year the margin shifted coronally 0.8 mm and KT increased 4.2 mm; over 10 to 25 years the margin shifted a further 0.6 mm coronally, KT decreased 0.7 mm and PD stayed stable.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: 55 subjects with 73 sites lacking attached gingiva associated with recessions
facts.intervention: submarginal or marginal free gingival grafts
facts.comparison: 73 untreated contralateral homologous sites

facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.population: 47 patients with thin biotype, 64 sites lacking attached gingiva with recession
facts.intervention: marginal or submarginal free gingival grafts
facts.comparison: 64 untreated contralateral homologous sites

facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Population selected for motivation and compliance, and only unrestored natural teeth, so external validity is limited

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral Implantology and Clinical Research
facts.population: 44-year-old systemically healthy woman with missing mandibular incisors, severe resorption and no keratinized tissue
facts.intervention: free gingival graft before implant placement, then two one-piece implants

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Biopsies from 10 patients previously grafted for severe mucogingival defects
facts.intervention: strip autograft combined with xenogeneic collagen matrix
facts.comparison: 3 reference palatal strip autograft samples
facts.main_result: Strip autograft/XCM biopsies were histologically indistinguishable from palatal autograft references in morphology, keratin and collagen expression, indicating normal keratinized gingiva.
facts.follow_up: Biopsies taken 6 months to 1.5 years postoperatively
facts.funding_coi: Lead author received honoraria from Geistlich Pharma; other authors none

facts.intervention: apically positioned flap, free gingival graft and subepithelial connective tissue graft
facts.main_result: These procedures augment attached gingiva effectively and predictably, the gain can be maintained long term, and they can halt recession progression.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.population: Two patients with severe mandibular ridge resorption, lack of keratinized tissue and shallow vestibule
facts.intervention: free gingival graft with modified button-suture lingual sulcoplasty
facts.main_result: Case 1 gained 5 mm lingual and 4 mm buccal vestibular depth at 10 months; case 2 reached 6 mm lingual sulcus and 7 mm buccal depth at 6 months with stable keratinized tissue.
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Very small sample size limits interpretation
materials_brands: Straumann Standard Plus tissue-level implants (SP, RN, 10 mm x 4.1 mm)

facts.intervention: vascularized flaps (gingivectomy, sliding pedicle, rotated papilla, internal pedicle) at nonsubmerged implants
facts.main_result: Four vascularized flap techniques are described with illustrated cases showing preserved or extended peri-implant keratinized mucosa at 3 months.

facts.intervention: free gingival graft and subepithelial connective tissue graft at nonsubmerged implants
facts.main_result: Both illustrated cases healed uneventfully, and the connective tissue graft case showed excellent peri-implant soft tissue health after 8 weeks.

facts.population: 8 edentulous patients (mean age 65) with <2 mm keratinized tissue around implant overdentures
facts.intervention: apically positioned flap, pedicle graft, connective tissue graft or free gingival graft
facts.comparison: Techniques compared with each other, no untreated control
facts.main_result: Second-stage apically repositioned flap gave a mean 3.1 mm keratinized tissue gain and pedicle flap 2.8 mm; an APF before implant placement gave 5 mm in case 1.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.population: 5 implant candidates (3 women, 2 men, mean age 47) with major loss of attached gingiva
facts.intervention: free gingival graft immobilized with a newly designed acrylic stent
facts.main_result: After 1 year the remaining graft averaged 37% of its initial size, with a proper increase in attached gingiva width.

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 20 patients with at least one site without keratinized tissue and loss of vestibular depth after advanced ridge augmentation
facts.intervention: Combination graft: apically placed autogenous strip gingival graft plus xenogeneic collagen matrix (Mucograft)
facts.main_result: Mean keratinized tissue width at 12 months was 6.33 mm (SD 2.16), with 43% graft contraction.
facts.funding_coi: Partially funded by Geistlich Pharma; authors reported no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: No control group, so no firm conclusions could be drawn.

facts.population: One 60-year-old edentulous woman with four mandibular interforaminal implants and no keratinized mucosa
facts.intervention: Free gingival graft from the palate on the buccal side of the interforaminal area after placing a mandibular fixed implant-supported prosthesis
facts.main_result: A 3 mm increase in keratinized mucosa height at 6 months, with good peri-implant health and easier hygiene.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest reported
facts.limitations: The technique involves two surgical sites, causing morbidity in both, and some graft shrinkage is expected.

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 20 partially edentulous patients needing horizontal or vertical bone augmentation in the maxilla
facts.intervention: Suspended external-internal (SEI) suture after periosteal release, with flap tension measured by dynamometer
facts.comparison: Flap tension before the SEI suture (after periosteal release only), same patients
facts.main_result: Mean flap tension fell from 32.9 g to 4.1 g (87.6% reduction) after the SEI suture, and all 20 patients healed uneventfully.
facts.sample_size: 20 patients (15 GBR sites, 5 autogenous bone block sites)
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.journal: Journal of IMAB - Annual Proceeding (Scientific Papers)
facts.population: Three patients with Miller class II-IV gingival recessions and small vestibule depth in the frontal mandibular region
facts.intervention: Strip free gingival graft with longitudinal division of the donor palatal tissue
facts.main_result: Strip free gingival graft gave a mean 4.33 mm gain of attached gingiva, with initial healing complete in two weeks.
facts.limitations: The authors only note that results are within the limitations of the three presented cases.

facts.population: 10 patients aged 25-30 years with 12 mandibular Miller class I and II recession sites and thin gingival biotype
facts.intervention: Single-step free gingival graft with root biomodification (citric acid)
facts.main_result: Mean recession depth fell from 3.66 to 0.91 mm (82% root coverage) at 9 months, with attached gingiva rising from 0.33 to 2.92 mm.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

facts.population: Literature on autologous platelet concentrates in oral and maxillofacial pathologies (in vitro and in vivo studies)
facts.intervention: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP), platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) and fibrin adhesives
facts.main_result: Evidence on the efficacy of platelet concentrates in the oral and maxillofacial region is controversial and limited.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Medical University Sofia (Grant 42/2015); no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Quality of platelet concentrates varies with donor state and protocols are inconsistent, making outcomes hard to compare.

facts.population: Mouse ST2 bone stromal cell line cultured on fibrin sealant
facts.intervention: TISSEEL fibrin sealant loaded with rhBMP9 (100 ng/ml)
facts.comparison: Tissue culture plastic and TISSEEL alone
facts.main_result: TISSEEL retained about 65% of rhBMP9 with slow release over 10 days; TISSEEL plus rhBMP9 raised ALP activity threefold and osteoblast markers versus TISSEEL alone.
facts.sample_size: Triplicate wells, three independent experiments per condition
facts.funding_coi: Departmental support (Inselspital, Bern); no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: In vitro only; animal studies are still needed.

facts.population: Blood-derived biomaterials (fibrin sealant, platelet gel, platelet fibrin glue) across surgical fields
facts.intervention: Fibrin sealant, platelet gel and platelet fibrin glue: production, properties and clinical uses
facts.comparison: Synthetic glues and other biomaterials (qualitative)
facts.main_result: Fibrin sealant gives sealing and haemostasis, while platelet gel and platelet fibrin glue release growth factors that support tissue regeneration; all are biocompatible and biodegradable within days to weeks.
facts.funding_coi: Two authors are employed by HPPS, a company providing R&D services for this project; others declare none

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 6 mongrel dogs, 18 titanium implants in tibia with a 2.0 mm peri-implant gap
facts.intervention: Gap filled with autogenous particulate bone mixed with platelet-enriched fibrin glue
facts.comparison: Autogenous particulate bone with PRP, and empty gaps (control)
facts.main_result: At 6 weeks bone-implant contact was 59.7% with fibrin glue, 29.2% with PRP and 10.2% in controls (P<.05).
facts.funding_coi: Korean Science & Engineering Foundation grant R13-2003-13

facts.intervention: Fibrin glue as a tissue adhesive for wound closure in periodontal and oral surgery
facts.comparison: Conventional sutures
facts.main_result: Fibrin glue is presented as having great potential for periodontal and oral surgery and as a possible alternative to sutures; further clinical trials are needed.
facts.limitations: Fibrin sealant cannot be used in people hypersensitive to bovine protein or for massive arterial or venous bleeding.

facts.journal: University of Milan, doctoral thesis (Oral Sciences)
facts.population: 13 patients with partial edentulism, keratinized mucosa under 2 mm or inadequate soft tissue volume, receiving 21 implants
facts.intervention: Connective tissue graft at second-stage surgery around implants with BOPT abutments and immediate provisionalization (test group)
facts.comparison: Delayed provisionalization (control group)
facts.main_result: Both approaches were valid for limited horizontal defects; control soft tissue gain 1.17 mm vs test 0.82 mm, recession change about 0 mm in both groups; sample too small to say which is better.
facts.limitations: Preliminary results from a small sample, so it is impossible to assess which option is best.
facts.key_finding: A pilot study of 21 implants in 13 patients compared immediate and delayed provisionalization on BOPT abutments after connective tissue grafting. Soft tissue gain and gingival level change were similar and not significantly different, but the sample was too small to name the better protocol.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Both immediate and delayed provisionalization with BOPT abutments can be used to thicken peri-implant soft tissue without bone grafting, but no superiority is shown.

facts.intervention: Geistlich Fibro-Gide collagen matrix for soft-tissue augmentation
facts.comparison: Subepithelial connective tissue graft
facts.main_result: Manufacturer claims comparable soft-tissue volume change to connective tissue grafts.
facts.key_finding: Product brochure presenting Geistlich Fibro-Gide, a porcine volume-stable collagen matrix offered as an alternative to connective tissue grafts for soft-tissue thickening around implants and teeth, with clinical case examples.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Promotional material only: it asserts non-inferiority to connective tissue grafts and fewer donor-site problems, which should be checked against the cited trials.

facts.population: Patients receiving soft tissue augmentation during implantation or around existing implants
facts.intervention: Soft tissue augmentation with a substitute material (xenogeneic collagen matrix or acellular dermal matrix)
facts.comparison: Subepithelial connective tissue graft
facts.main_result: Seven RCTs: both CTG and substitutes increased mucosal thickness; five showed no significant difference and two favored CTG.
facts.limitations: Methodological quality of included studies was low and heterogeneity prevented meta-analysis.

facts.journal: Journal of the International Academy of Periodontology
facts.population: Patients with single or multiple Miller I/II gingival recessions treated with coronally advanced flap
facts.intervention: Coronally advanced flap plus de-epithelialized gingival graft
facts.comparison: Coronally advanced flap plus subepithelial connective tissue graft
facts.main_result: Mean root coverage at 1 year was 89.3% with SCTG and 94.0% with DGG; DGG was modestly better on secondary outcomes (within 1 mm).
facts.follow_up: At least 1 year (up to 5 years in two studies)
facts.limitations: Limited evidence is available comparing the two techniques.

facts.population: 50 Wistar rats with four subcutaneous dorsal pouches each (ectopic model)
facts.intervention: Cross-linked (CCM) and non-cross-linked (NCCM) collagen matrices, with or without rhPDGF-BB
facts.comparison: Matrices soaked in saline
facts.main_result: rhPDGF-BB had no significant effect (all P > 0.05); NCCM stayed 440-570 um thick to 8 weeks then vanished by 16 weeks, while CCM peaked near 2690 um at 2 weeks, lost about 40% by 8 weeks and persisted to 24 weeks.

facts.population: 76 patients (mean age 36) with 235 teeth, 136 anterior and 99 posterior, needing full crowns
facts.intervention: Monolithic lithium disilicate full crowns bonded to feather-edge preparations
facts.main_result: Only 1 of 235 monolithic crowns fractured (a molar after 3 years, in severe parafunction); no biological or technical complications otherwise.
facts.follow_up: Recall every 6 months; range given in Table 1 (not in text)
facts.limitations: Authors state prospective clinical studies are needed to validate the approach.

facts.population: 398 patients with 1,132 zirconia-based single crowns on natural teeth
facts.intervention: Porcelain-veneered zirconia single crowns with chamfer or knife-edge preparations
facts.comparison: Patients with parafunction versus without
outcomes: USPHS/FDI esthetic, functional and biologic criteria
facts.main_result: Cumulative survival 98.1% and success 94.3% over up to 5 years; parafunction raised technical complications (OR 2.60).
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Retrospective design with lower level of evidence than RCTs.

facts.population: 20 pressed lithium disilicate molar crowns bonded to epoxy resin abutments
facts.intervention: Knife-edge finish line abutments
facts.comparison: Large chamfer finish line abutments
facts.main_result: Finish line did not significantly change fracture strength (KE 1655 N vs LC 1618 N, p = 0.7898).
facts.funding_coi: Authors deny conflicts of interest

facts.journal: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
facts.population: 53 patients with 265 veneers, mostly maxillary anterior teeth
facts.intervention: Lithium disilicate veneers with a vertical (feather-edge) finish line
facts.main_result: Survival 99.63% over a mean 54.4 months; one adhesive failure after trauma; nearly all veneers rated Alfa.
facts.funding_coi: Manufacturer gave the authors a positive opinion on the finish line; no funding statement
facts.limitations: Authors state further long-term clinical studies are needed.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 52 patients with posterior mandibular partial edentulism and bone height under 7 mm above the canal
facts.intervention: Coronal advancement of the lingual flap by detaching the mylohyoid muscle insertion during vertical GBR
outcomes: maintenance of primary closure for 6 months
facts.main_result: Primary closure was maintained in all 69 sites for 6 months; 4 sites (5.8%) failed from infection, 3 of them in smokers.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry

facts.population: 173 GBR-treated sites in 169 patients
facts.intervention: A new flap design used with previously described flap designs to maintain primary closure after GBR
outcomes: maintenance of passive primary soft tissue closure for 6 months
facts.main_result: 171 of 173 GBR sites maintained primary closure at 6 months (98.8%).

facts.population: 47-year-old healthy non-smoking man missing an upper first molar
facts.intervention: Buccal peri-implant soft tissue augmentation with a volume-stable porcine collagen matrix and a modified flap
outcomes: marginal bone and soft tissue stability
facts.main_result: Single case: the technique gave satisfying functional and esthetic results with marginal bone and soft tissue stability.
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Single case

facts.population: 60-year-old woman, partially edentulous 24 to 27, with severe maxillary ridge atrophy
facts.intervention: Maxillary bone reconstruction with cortical autogenous bone plates harvested from the external oblique ridge with a computer-designed surgical guide
facts.main_result: At re-entry and at 6 and 12 months the reconstruction showed volume stability without complications.

facts.population: 60 patients scheduled for single implant installation
facts.intervention: Measurement of wound closing force with an electronic tension device before suturing
facts.main_result: 72% of sites had 0.01-0.1 N tension with 10% dehiscences; higher tension increased dehiscences significantly.

facts.population: 38 patients with immediately placed post-extraction implants
facts.intervention: Palatal advanced flap, a pedicle flap rotated coronally for primary coverage
facts.main_result: Complete primary coverage in all cases, maintained for 6-8 months, with no implant lost over 1-5 years.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Consecutive cases of vertical GBR in the posterior mandible
facts.intervention: Brushing technique to enhance coronal advancement of the buccal flap after periosteal releasing incision
facts.main_result: Primary closure over d-PTFE membranes was maintained in 97% of cases.
materials_brands: Cytoplast Ti-250 XL titanium-reinforced d-PTFE membrane
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: 5 patients with bilateral atrophic alveolar ridges
facts.main_result: Both materials gave equivalent bone gains; horizontal gain 5.8 mm autogenous vs 6.1 mm allogeneic.
facts.funding_coi: No funding; first author receives honoraria from Botiss and Straumann
facts.limitations: Needs replication in larger studies including a control group without relining

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.intervention: Classification of healing (Class I-IV) and surgical (A-C) complications of GBR with nonresorbable membranes
facts.main_result: A classification of GBR complications with nonresorbable membranes is proposed to aid identification and treatment.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 16 patients with 23 vertical/horizontal ridge defect sites (Seibert Class III)
facts.intervention: Double-flap incision (DFI) for flap advancement in GBR
facts.comparison: Conventional periosteal releasing incision (PRI)
facts.main_result: DFI gave 9.64 mm flap advancement vs 7.13 mm for PRI (P<.001), with lower pain and swelling scores.

facts.population: One 61-year-old man with severe vertical and horizontal ridge deformity in the posterior mandible (bilateral)
facts.intervention: Double flap incision (separate mucosal and periosteal layers) for tension-free closure over GBR with titanium-reinforced e-PTFE membrane and allograft
facts.main_result: No dehiscence or membrane exposure; 3-5 mm vertical gain and increased horizontal thickness, then two implants per side placed with good primary stability
facts.follow_up: 6-8 months of healing before implants; 1 year after loading

facts.funding_coi: Authors report no conflicts of interest

facts.population: 30 patients scheduled for implant surgery with bone augmentation (Seibert Class I deficiency)

facts.main_result: First VI +1.1 mm, second VI +1.9 mm, PRI +5.5 mm (171.3% of original length, P<0.001); no differences by gender, site or operator experience

facts.intervention: Stepwise periosteal releasing incision (and muscle release) for flap advancement over augmented sites
outcomes: tension-free flap coverage of augmented site
facts.main_result: A PRI cut 1-3 mm deep apical to the mucogingival junction, checked for 3-5 mm buccal margin overlap, gives tension-free closure; illustrated clinically without complications at 3 months.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: One patient with a 7 mm vertical deficit in the posterior maxilla

facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.population: 102 participants with a missing mandibular first molar (single-tooth gap), healed site
facts.intervention: Flapless (tissue punch) single implant placement with immediate functional loading

facts.funding_coi: No specific grant funding

facts.population: Systemically healthy patients needing implant placement (14 RCTs)

facts.main_result: Flapless showed better papilla preservation (PPI WMD 0.32), less 1-day pain and less peri-implant PD; SR, BOP, KM width and CBL were comparable.

facts.limitations: More high-quality, aesthetics-related RCTs are needed

facts.population: Patients rehabilitated with dental implants in 23 clinical studies (randomized or not)
facts.intervention: Flapless implant surgery
facts.comparison: Open flap implant surgery
facts.main_result: Flapless surgery had higher implant failure (RR 1.75, 95% CI 1.07-2.86, P=0.03), but sensitivity analysis by risk of bias differed; no significant effect on infection or marginal bone loss.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq (Brazil); no competing interests
facts.limitations: Sixteen studies at high risk of bias; results must be interpreted carefully

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 40 patients, one posterior single interdental implant each, with healthy adjacent teeth
facts.intervention: Intrasulcular incision (including adjacent-tooth sulci, no release incisions) for single implant placement
facts.comparison: Trapezoidal incision with two release incisions sparing the interproximal tissue
facts.main_result: No significant differences between incision types in probing depth, recession or papilla; across the whole sample recession, scar and papilla index changed significantly by 1 year postloading.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 80 patients, 195 implants analysed (no augmentation procedures needed)

facts.comparison: Implant insertion after full-thickness mucoperiosteal flap
outcomes: peri-implant crestal bone level change at 12 months (radiographic)
facts.main_result: Mean bone loss 0.55 mm with flap vs a 0.09 mm gain flapless at 1 year (P<.001)
materials_brands: Dentsply titanium drill sleeves / surgical guide
facts.funding_coi: No external support; author later received contributions from Dentsply Implants

facts.population: Adult human subjects needing one or more dental implants
facts.intervention: Flapless computer-aided fully guided (static or dynamic) implant placement
facts.comparison: Flapped conventional implant placement (free-handed or partially guided)
facts.main_result: Flapless static fully guided placement improved accuracy versus the planned position and was linked to shorter surgery and less morbidity (very low/low certainty), with about 24 minutes shorter surgery.
facts.follow_up: Mostly up to 12 weeks; one trial longer
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Only five RCTs, frequent non-low risk of bias, short follow-up and no long-term clinical outcomes.

facts.population: Single dental implants placed immediately in the anterior esthetic region
facts.intervention: Immediate interim restoration
facts.comparison: No interim restoration / delayed interim restoration
facts.main_result: No significant difference in mid-facial mucosal level (MD 0.01 mm), mesial papilla (MD 0.12) or marginal bone loss (MD 0.01) with immediate interim restoration at 12 months; esthetic scores and PROMs improved.
facts.funding_coi: No specific grant; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Additional well-designed trials with long-term follow-up are needed.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Healthy candidates for immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla (39 teeth)
facts.intervention: CBCT measurement of labial and palatal bone thickness
facts.comparison: Direct caliper measurement after extraction (gold standard)
facts.main_result: CBCT overestimated labial bone thickness (0.76 vs 0.50 mm direct); correlation 0.795, ICC 0.840, better when bone exceeded 1 mm.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.population: Immediate implants placed in compromised extraction sockets (buccal plate defect, periapical pathology, periodontal lesion)
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement in compromised sockets
facts.comparison: Noncompromised sockets
facts.main_result: Compromised sockets showed no significant difference in implant survival (RR 0.992) or 12-month marginal bone level (MD 0.033) versus noncompromised sockets.
facts.funding_coi: No specific grant received
facts.limitations: Randomized trials with large samples are still needed for a definite conclusion.

facts.population: Patients with maxillary extraction sites (teeth 15-25) scheduled for immediate implants
facts.intervention: Intra-operative caliper measurement of buccal and palatal socket wall width, 1 mm apical to the crest
facts.comparison: Buccal versus palatal walls, anterior versus premolar sites
outcomes: proportion of walls 2 mm or wider
facts.main_result: Mean buccal wall was 1 mm and palatal 1.2 mm; 87% of anterior buccal walls were 1 mm or thinner and only 3% were 2 mm wide.
materials_brands: Astra Tech OsseoSpeed and MicroThread implants

facts.population: Two patients with hopeless maxillary anterior teeth (socket class I and II with Miller class I recession)
facts.intervention: Marginal Migration Concept protocol: immediate implant, tulip-shaped temporary abutment, membrane and bone replacement graft, immediate provisionalization
facts.main_result: The protocol gave esthetically sound results in type I and II sockets with Miller class I recession; tested in over 25 cases with up to 3 years follow-up.
facts.funding_coi: No external funding
facts.limitations: Prospective randomized controlled trials are needed to evaluate efficacy and validity.

facts.population: Five beagle dogs, mandibular fourth premolar distal sockets (10 sites)

facts.comparison: Contralateral sites without grafting
outcomes: buccal bone crest position and thickness
facts.main_result: Grafted sites had a thicker buccal crest at or near the SLA border and better marginal bone-to-implant contact than ungrafted controls after 6 months.

facts.population: 33 patients needing anterior maxillary extraction with complete or partial buccal bone plate deficiency

facts.main_result: Keratinized mucosa gained 2.3 mm at 5 months (3.2 mm at 1 year), bone level improved by about 0.7-0.8 mm, and no implant failed in 1 year.

facts.population: Single dental implants placed in the anterior maxilla (premolar to premolar)
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement and loading protocols and augmentation materials
facts.comparison: Early/delayed placement; delayed loading; other augmentation materials
facts.main_result: Buccal bone thickness did not differ significantly between immediate, early and delayed placement or between immediate and delayed loading.

facts.population: 25 subjects with a maxillary anterior tooth to be extracted and replaced by an implant
facts.intervention: New extraction socket classification based on soft and hard tissue parameters
facts.main_result: The classification had 96% interobserver agreement (weighted kappa 0.94); 80% of sockets were adequate on soft tissue parameters.

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 100 patients (40 men, 60 women; mean age 53.1 years) with CBCT scans, all maxillary anterior teeth present

outcomes: frequency of each sagittal root position class
facts.main_result: Of 600 maxillary anterior teeth, 81.1% were Class I, 6.5% Class II, 0.7% Class III and 11.7% Class IV.

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 45 patients (mean age 48 years) receiving single-tooth implants in anterior or premolar regions of maxilla or mandible

facts.population: 101 randomly selected patient CBCT scans, 202 healthy maxillary central incisors
facts.intervention: CBCT measurement of facial alveolar bone width 1-10 mm apical to the crest

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.intervention: Placement of implants in extraction sockets, with a new four-type classification of placement timing (types 1-4)
facts.comparison: Immediate (type 1) versus early/delayed (types 2-4) placement

facts.population: 5 male adult cynomolgus monkeys; buccal aspect of the mandibular angle bilaterally
facts.intervention: Titanium mesh over perforated cortical bone covered with an ePTFE membrane (test side)
facts.comparison: Titanium mesh without membrane, periosteum-lined flap covering the mesh (control side)
outcomes: percentage of new bone under the mesh
mineralized tissue vs marrow spaces in new and old bone
facts.main_result: New bone filled 77.2% of the space on test sides versus 68.6% on control sides (P=0.018); mineralized tissue content did not differ between groups.
facts.funding_coi: Partly supported by W.L. Gore & Associates

facts.population: 14 adults (2 males, 12 females, mean age 57.1 years) needing immediate implants in the anterior maxilla (incl. premolars) with buccal bone dehiscence of at least 5 mm
facts.intervention: Flapless immediate implant placement with collagen-enriched bovine xenograft blocks filling the buccal dehiscence and gap, no membrane
facts.comparison: Contralateral natural tooth
facts.main_result: Buccal wall height at 6-12 months did not differ from the contralateral tooth and exceeded baseline (P<0.01); treated sites had thicker buccal walls and wider ridges than contralateral teeth.
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: 73 clinical human studies (randomized or not) comparing implants in fresh sockets with healed sites
facts.intervention: Dental implants inserted in fresh extraction sockets
facts.comparison: Dental implants inserted in healed sites
facts.main_result: Implants in fresh sockets had a higher failure rate (RR 1.58, 95% CI 1.27-1.95, P<0.0001); 4.00% vs 3.09%.
facts.sample_size: 73 publications: 8,241 implants in sockets and 19,410 in healed sites
facts.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq (Brazil)
facts.limitations: Results should be interpreted with caution due to uncontrolled confounding factors in the included, mostly non-randomized studies

facts.population: Adults aged 18 years or older receiving implants, from 10 eligible studies (6 RCTs, 4 non-randomised comparative studies)
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement in fresh sockets at the time of extraction
facts.comparison: Delayed implant placement in healed sites at least two months after extraction
facts.main_result: No significant difference in implant survival between immediate and delayed placement (RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.96-1.02, p=0.45); 97.4% vs 97.5%.
facts.follow_up: Varied by study, from 1 year up to about 10 years
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Some included studies had one-year follow-up and small samples

facts.population: 50 patients (22 males, 28 females, age 21-50) with one Miller Class I/II recession each
facts.intervention: Coronally advanced flap with de-epithelialized gingival graft (test group)
facts.comparison: Coronally advanced flap with connective tissue graft harvested by trap-door approach (control)
facts.main_result: No differences in post-operative pain or root coverage between CAF+CTG and CAF+DGG (root coverage 96.2% vs 92.3%); the CTG group had lower stress and better chewing, DGG gave greater thickness gain.
facts.funding_coi: Self-supported by the authors; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: The lack of difference may reflect considerable within-group variability; larger studies are needed

facts.population: Photoelastic model of a partially edentulous left mandible with 3 screw-type implants (3.75 x 10 mm)
facts.intervention: Splinted restorations: five cemented 3-unit fixed partial dentures
facts.comparison: Non-splinted individual crowns with five levels of interproximal contact tightness (open to heavy)
outcomes: stress distribution under non-loaded and loaded (6.8 kg) conditions
facts.main_result: Splinted restorations shared occlusal loads and distributed stress more evenly than non-splinted ones, and heavier interproximal contacts in non-splinted crowns increased tensile stresses between implants.
facts.sample_size: 1 model; 5 FPDs and one set of 3 single crowns

facts.journal: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
facts.population: 42 patients with 51 maxillary central incisor sites treated with immediate implant placement and buccal gap grafting
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement with the buccal gap grafted with deproteinized bovine bone mineral, grouped by gap width at surgery
facts.comparison: Wide gap (>2 mm) versus narrow gap (<=2 mm)
outcomes: buccal and palatal bone wall thickness on CBCT
percentage of implant height covered by bone
position of buccal and palatal bone crests
facts.main_result: Buccal bone was thicker with wide gaps (1.9 ± 0.9 mm) than narrow gaps (0.5 ± 0.6 mm), and gap width was the only predictor of buccal wall thickness.
facts.sample_size: 51 implants in 42 patients (34 wide gap, 17 narrow gap)
facts.follow_up: At least 1 year in function (mean 5 ± 4 years)
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded; two authors give lectures sponsored by Geistlich Pharma
facts.limitations: Retrospective design, one experienced periodontist, wide follow-up range (1-15 years) with changing techniques, and CBCT implant artifacts.

facts.population: Adults with socket defects in the esthetic zone receiving immediate implants (23 studies)
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement into defective sockets (with or without flap)
facts.main_result: Pooled implant survival was 98.1%, MBL 0.72 mm at 12 months, gingival recession 0.25 mm and PES 12.34 at 12 months.
facts.follow_up: At least 12 months with definitive prosthesis
facts.funding_coi: Natural Science Foundation of Liaoning Province grant; no other conflicts declared

facts.population: Systemically healthy patients with at least one abutment connected to an implant
facts.intervention: Any change in abutment material, design or surface manipulation
facts.comparison: Any other abutment material, design or surface manipulation
facts.main_result: Zirconia abutments showed a smaller BOP increase than titanium (WMD -26.96%, p = .003); other abutment characteristics had no significant effect, except decontamination method on bone loss.
facts.follow_up: At least 6 months after implant loading
facts.funding_coi: Partially funded by the Oral Reconstruction Foundation; no conflicts declared
facts.limitations: Small number of included studies in some comparisons and short follow-up

facts.journal: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.population: 23 consecutive patients (mean age 39.5) with a failing maxillary anterior tooth and a facial bony defect over 3 mm
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement with immediate provisionalization and guided bone regeneration, sites classified by defect shape (V, U, UU)
facts.comparison: V-shaped versus U- and UU-shaped facial defects
facts.main_result: Implant success was 100% (23/23); facial recession >1.5 mm occurred in 8.3% of V-, 42.8% of U- and 100% of UU-shaped defects.
facts.sample_size: 23 implants in 23 patients (12 V, 7 U, 4 UU defects)
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare Replace Select / NobelPerfect (TiUnite) implants
facts.limitations: Small sample of 23 patients prevented assessment of less dominant factors.

facts.population: 58 adults with 71 single Branemark fixtures and their adjacent teeth
facts.intervention: Single-tooth replacement with Branemark implants
outcomes: marginal bone loss at tooth surfaces facing implants
effect of tooth-fixture distance and jaw region
facts.main_result: Bone loss at adjacent tooth surfaces averaged 0.97 mm up to crown installation versus 0.08 mm the following year, largest at lateral upper incisors and increasing with smaller fixture-tooth distance.
facts.follow_up: up to 3 years after crown installation
materials_brands: Branemark System fixtures, standard and self-tapping (Nobelpharma)

facts.key_finding: Narrative overview of how esthetics around implants is rated: clinician measures (mucosal margin level, papilla fill, soft-tissue volume, mucosa color, PES/WES/ICAI scores) and patient-reported outcomes, which agree only weakly with clinician ratings; clinicians tend to be more critical than patients.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Esthetic evaluation should be part of implant outcome assessment, but heterogeneous scoring systems limit comparison across studies.

facts.population: 20 consecutive patients needing a single anterior maxillary implant (incisor or canine region)
facts.intervention: Screw-retained implant-supported provisional crown with soft tissue conditioning (dynamic compression technique) for 6 months before the definitive all-ceramic crown
facts.comparison: Definitive crown inserted directly after reopening, without a provisional phase
outcomes: modified pink esthetic score and white esthetic score
facts.main_result: Combined modPES and WES were 16.7 with provisional conditioning versus 10.5 without (p = .00044); bone loss was similar (about 0.09 vs 0.08 mm).
facts.sample_size: 20 single implants in 20 patients (10 per group)
facts.funding_coi: Research grant, study material and financial support from Institut Straumann AG

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Single-tooth implants placed after extraction of maxillary anterior and premolar teeth
facts.intervention: Immediate (type 1) and early (types 2/3) implant placement, with or without simultaneous bone augmentation
facts.comparison: Immediate versus early implant placement
outcomes: pink esthetic score and other esthetic indices
facial bone wall detectability on CBCT
facts.main_result: Immediate placement showed more variable outcomes and recession >1 mm at midfacial mucosa in a median 26% of sites (range 9-41%), versus none in early placement.
facts.sample_size: 50 studies (6 RCTs, 6 cohort, 5 cross-sectional, 33 case series)
facts.follow_up: 1 to 3 years after placement for trend analysis
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Considerable heterogeneity in study design; no meta-analysis of controlled studies; mostly case series

facts.population: Systemically healthy patients with dental implants
facts.intervention: Soft tissue grafting to increase keratinized tissue width or mucosal thickness around implants
facts.comparison: Implant sites without grafting (or other grafting materials)
facts.main_result: Grafting to widen keratinized tissue improved gingival and plaque indices, and connective tissue grafts for thickness gave less marginal bone loss (WMD 0.110 mm); limited evidence supports soft tissue augmentation for peri-implant health.
facts.sample_size: 10 studies in the underlying review (6 mucosal thickness, 4 keratinized tissue)
facts.funding_coi: Grant of the Osteology Foundation; no conflicts declared, three authors are Foundation board members
facts.limitations: Peri-implant disease incidence based on clear case definitions was not sufficiently reported in the studies

facts.population: Patients with horizontal alveolar ridge deficiencies
facts.intervention: Lateral bone augmentation procedures (simultaneous or staged) before or with implant placement
facts.comparison: Different bone regenerative interventions compared with each other
facts.main_result: Lateral bone augmentation was associated with stable peri-implant tissues (minimal, non-significant changes in BOP, PD and marginal bone levels) over 1-10 years, without significant differences between interventions.
facts.sample_size: 8 studies (12 publications) in the underlying review
facts.funding_coi: Grant of the Osteology Foundation; no conflicts declared, three authors are Foundation board members
facts.limitations: Case definitions of peri-implant health versus disease were used inconsistently across studies

facts.journal: Journal of the California Dental Association

facts.population: Patients receiving flapless maxillary anterior immediate implant placement and provisionalization with scarf-connective tissue graft, min 1-year follow-up
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization with simultaneous scarf-connective tissue graft
facts.main_result: All 22 implants osseointegrated, mean midfacial gingival level change 0.19 mm was non-significant and midfacial gingival thickness rose from 1.1 mm to 2.5 mm.
facts.funding_coi: Authors declared no financial interests in products mentioned

facts.population: 40 pig-jaw bone blocks with titanium or zirconia implants and abutments at variable buccal bone thickness
facts.intervention: CBCT imaging with two units, two voxel sizes and two reconstruction thicknesses, with 1-3 implants and Ti/Zr combinations
facts.comparison: TiTi vs TiZr vs ZrZr implant-abutment; Scanora vs Cranex; 0.2 vs 0.13 mm voxel
outcomes: detectability (conspicuity) of buccal bone condition by three examiners
facts.main_result: Zirconia implant-abutment and three implants most impaired buccal bone detection; thinner bone and lower resolution also raised risk, thicker reconstruction helped.
facts.sample_size: 40 bone blocks, 80 buccal bone registrations, three examiners
materials_brands: Thommen Medical internal hexagon Ti and Zr implants and abutments

facts.population: Forty patients with a failing tooth in the aesthetic zone
facts.intervention: Immediate single implant placement with immediate provisionalization
facts.comparison: Immediate placement with delayed provisionalization
facts.main_result: Immediate provisionalization was non-inferior for marginal bone level at 1 year (about 0.7 mm loss in both groups).
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest; unrestricted grant and implant materials from Nobel Biocare Services AG

facts.population: 16 beagle dogs, mandibular premolar sockets
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement in the distal socket after premolar extraction
facts.comparison: Mesial socket left to heal spontaneously
facts.main_result: Implant sites showed greater B’L’ distance than controls at 2 and 8 weeks and a 62% reduction in crest width in the test group.
facts.follow_up: Five healing periods, up to 8 weeks (2 to 8 weeks reported)
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest; partially supported by Biomet 3i research grant

facts.population: Subjects with chronic periapical infection of a tooth scheduled for extraction and immediate implant, with intact cervical facial and lingual plates
facts.intervention: Extraction, flapless immediate implant placement and provisionalization with perioperative amoxicillin (or clindamycin)
facts.comparison: Placebo (sucrose capsule) instead of antibiotic
facts.main_result: One implant failed in each group; overall survival 84.7% (87.5% placebo, 80% antibiotic), suggesting antibiotics gave no added benefit.
facts.funding_coi: Partly supported by ACP Educational Fund, AAID research grant and unrestricted fund from Zimmer Dental, which supplied implants and abutments
facts.limitations: Small sample; authors call for further large-scale trials

facts.population: Single missing teeth in the anterior maxilla (aesthetic zone)
facts.intervention: Type 1A protocol: immediate implant placement with immediate loading/restoration
facts.main_result: Type 1A protocol in the anterior maxilla under favorable conditions is predictable with high survival rates, though complications can occur.
facts.sample_size: Underlying review: 43 prospective and 25 retrospective studies, 2531 implants
facts.follow_up: Minimum 12 months in included studies (mean 2.6 years)
facts.funding_coi: All participants declared no conflicts
facts.limitations: Statements rest on studies with highly selective populations
