facts.population: 18 healthy subjects with 21 extraction sockets (incisors, canines, premolars)
facts.intervention: Immediate implant installation in extraction sockets without membrane or filler, flaps repositioned with healing cap exposed
outcomes: buccal and lingual bone wall width
facts.main_result: Over 4 months buccal bone width resorbed about 56% and lingual/palatal 30%, while marginal gaps largely resolved by bone fill.
materials_brands: Straumann ITI solid screw implant with SLA surface, 4.1 mm diameter

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: One patient with a nonrestorable maxillary left canine
facts.intervention: Immediate implant at the palatal aspect of the socket with straight-profile healing abutment, healing by secondary intention, no flap closure, graft or membrane
outcomes: histologic bone-to-implant contact at the buccal wall interface
facts.main_result: Biopsy at 10 months showed intimate bone contact to the first thread despite a 4.2 mm gap, with biologic width re-established coronally.
facts.follow_up: Loaded at 5 months, biopsied at 10 months

facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization of maxillary anterior single implants

facts.population: 40 patients with hopeless teeth needing extraction and immediate implants (42 sites, maxilla and mandible, anterior and lateral)
facts.intervention: Atraumatic extraction, immediate tissue-level implant, socket filled with PRGF and/or deproteinized bovine bone, covered by collagen membrane or cyanoacrylate and left exposed (open healing)
facts.main_result: Open healing gave uneventful healing with 100% survival and 95.2% success at 4 years, with no differences in crestal bone stability between augmentation materials.
materials_brands: TRI Octa tissue-level implant (TRI Dental Implants)

facts.population: Eight beagle dogs, 32 implants in fresh extraction sockets of mandibular premolars
facts.intervention: Immediate placement of four commercial implant systems (3i Osseotite Certain, Astra MicroThread OsseoSpeed, Thommen SPI Element, Straumann ITI standard) into fresh extraction sockets
facts.comparison: The four implant systems compared with each other
facts.main_result: At 6 weeks the biological width comprised 2-2.7 mm junctional epithelium and 1-1.8 mm connective tissue, with no significant differences among the four systems.
facts.funding_coi: Partially supported by Thommen Medical; no conflict of interest declared

facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement in fresh extraction sockets (type-1 protocol)
facts.main_result: Survival, osseointegration and interdental bone levels are not negatively affected by immediate placement, but buccal bone resorption is variable and esthetic/soft-tissue data are limited.
facts.limitations: Scarce data on biological complications because of the lack of long-term studies.

facts.population: 5 patients scheduled for extraction of remaining teeth (severe chronic periodontitis); 10 immediate implants, 7 retrieved for histology
facts.intervention: SLA titanium implants placed into extraction sockets and completely covered with a connective tissue (resorbable collagen) membrane with primary closure
facts.comparison: Horizontal defect dimension 0.0-1.5 mm as controls versus 1.5-4.0 mm and >4.0 mm
facts.main_result: Osseointegration occurred across all HDDs; bone-to-implant contact was 69.29% (0-1.5 mm), 39.37% (1.5-4.0 mm) and 64.72% (>4.0 mm).
facts.limitations: It remains undetermined which of membrane type, membrane placement or implant surface was responsible; further study needed.
outcomes: vertical distance to first bone-to-implant contact
facts.funding_coi: Funds from the first and second authors and in part an ITI Foundation grant

facts.journal: Journal of the International Clinical Dental Research Organization
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement in the aesthetic zone
facts.main_result: Guiding and maintaining extra bone and soft tissue volume around implants is key to long-term esthetics, to compensate for the lack of a periodontal ligament.
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no conflicts of interest

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Clinical studies (trials, cohorts, case-control, case reports of at least 10 cases) on immediate and delayed implants after extraction
facts.intervention: Immediate and delayed (early) implant placement following tooth extraction
facts.comparison: Immediate versus delayed placement, and implants in healed ridges
facts.main_result: Short-term survival and clinical outcomes of immediate and delayed implants were similar and comparable to implants in healed ridges.
facts.follow_up: At least 12 months for survival/success studies
facts.limitations: Most studies were short-term and not randomized with respect to timing of placement and augmentation methods.

facts.population: 32 patients with hopeless maxillary premolars (25 analysed) in three private clinics
facts.intervention: Immediate definitive platform-switched abutment never disconnected (one abutment-one time)
facts.comparison: Provisional abutment later replaced by definitive abutment
facts.main_result: 100% success in both groups at 3 years; marginal bone loss 0.34 mm (definitive abutment) versus 0.55 mm (provisional abutment), significantly lower with the definitive abutment.
facts.sample_size: 25 patients analysed (10 PA, 15 DA) after 7 exclusions
facts.funding_coi: No financial interest in the products listed

facts.population: 124 subjects needing single anterior or premolar tooth extraction, seven private practices
facts.intervention: Immediate placement of tapered Thommen SPI Contact implants at extraction, with Bio-Oss and Bio-Gide when needed
facts.comparison: Delayed placement after 12 weeks of socket healing
facts.main_result: Immediate placement needed more augmentation (72% vs 43.9%), had more wound failure (26.1% vs 5.3%), deeper probing depth and inadequate pink esthetic score in 42% vs 19% of cases.
facts.limitations: Longer follow-up is needed to assess differences in complication rates.
facts.funding_coi: ERGOPerio; partly an unrestricted grant from Thommen Medical AG; materials from Geistlich

facts.population: 81 patients in three private practices (27 single, 27 partial, 27 full-arch)
facts.intervention: Immediate (within 48 h) and early (6 weeks) loading of implant prostheses
facts.comparison: Conventional (delayed) loading at 3 months
facts.main_result: No implant or prosthesis failed and no complications occurred in any group up to 4 months post-loading.
facts.limitations: Limited sample size, too low to detect a significant difference; protocol deviations.
facts.funding_coi: Partially funded by MegaGen, which did not interfere with conduct or publication

facts.population: 210 patients needing a single implant-supported crown to replace a tooth to be extracted
facts.intervention: Immediate and immediate-delayed (6 weeks) post-extractive single implants
facts.comparison: Delayed implants after 4 months of healing
facts.main_result: Implant failures were 6%, 6.2% and 1.6% (not significant); marginal bone loss was 0.25, 0.29 and 0.31 mm; esthetic scores were higher with immediate and immediate-delayed placement.
facts.limitations: Limited sample size despite being the largest RCT on implant timing.
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare implants (manufacturer of the implants evaluated)
facts.funding_coi: Partially funded by Nobel Biocare Services, manufacturer of the implants

facts.population: Mandibular premolar extraction sockets of four fresh-frozen human cadavers
facts.intervention: Immediate placement of ITI TE and solid screw implants (4.1 and 4.8 mm) into fresh extraction sockets
facts.comparison: TE implant versus 4.1 mm and 4.8 mm solid screw implants
facts.main_result: The TE implant had higher ISQ than the 4.1 mm implant (P<0.01) and values comparable to the 4.8 mm implant.
facts.sample_size: Four cadavers (number of implants not stated in extracted text)
facts.limitations: The clinical value of radiographic analysis is a matter of debate.

facts.population: Partially edentulous patients treated with implant-supported fixed prostheses
facts.intervention: Immediate or early implant placement combined with immediate, early or conventional loading
facts.comparison: Late placement and conventional loading
facts.main_result: Weighted cumulative survival was 98.4% (Type 1A), 98.2% (1B) and 96.0% (1C) for immediate placement, with the loading protocol influencing outcome of immediate placement
facts.funding_coi: Supported by Harvard department and ITI Foundation; authors declare no conflict of interests
facts.limitations: Considerable heterogeneity in study design prevented meta-analysis of controlled studies

facts.population: 20 patients needing immediate implants in fresh extraction sockets (second premolar to second premolar)
facts.intervention: Internal grafting only of the peri-implant gap when implant-to-buccal-plate distance (I-BP) was below 4 mm (group A)
facts.comparison: Internal plus external grafting (IEG) in group B
facts.main_result: After 1 year of loading, buccal volume decreased slightly in group A and increased in group B (P=0.02), with higher IAS in group B
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Studies with a larger sample size are needed to confirm the outcome
outcomes: buccal and palatal contour change by superimposed optical scans

facts.population: Patients with compromised teeth to be extracted who required dental implants, with or without bone augmentation
facts.intervention: Immediate (same-day) and immediate-delayed (within 8 weeks) implants in fresh extraction sockets
facts.comparison: Delayed implants placed at least 2 months after extraction
facts.sample_size: 7 randomised trials included of 14 potentially eligible
facts.follow_up: at least 1 year under functional loading

facts.journal: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.main_result: An ideal implant position in all 3 dimensions is required, defining comfort and danger zones in the anterior maxilla

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry

facts.population: Humans with periodontal intra-bony defects (comparative trials, at least eight defects, follow-up of 6 months or more)
facts.intervention: rhPDGF-BB or rhFGF-2 applied to intra-bony defects
facts.comparison: Carrier alone
facts.main_result: PDGF gave significantly more linear defect fill (0.95 mm) and CAL gain (0.34 mm) than carriers alone, and FGF-2 more percentage defect fill (21.22%)
facts.funding_coi: Two authors are research investigators for a trial supported by Sunstar Corp.; no external funding
facts.limitations: Only one included study was at low risk of bias

facts.population: 20 patients with a terminal maxillary dentition (fully edentulous maxilla)
facts.intervention: Immediate placement of six implants per maxilla with immediate loading by a fibre-reinforced temporary fixed prosthesis
facts.comparison: Implants in fresh extraction sockets versus healed edentulous sites
facts.main_result: Mean marginal bone level was -0.35 mm 18 months after loading, with no significant effect of extraction-socket versus healed placement; survival 100%
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Patients treated with single implants in different locations
facts.intervention: Immediate or early placement and loading protocols (Types 1A to 4B)
facts.comparison: Conventional placement and loading protocol
facts.main_result: The anterior maxilla was the most reported site (35 studies, 1,391 implants, weighted survival 97.5% to 99.6%), with Types 1C and 4A validated there
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Meta-analysis was not possible because few controlled studies had the same comparison

facts.population: 591 maxillary anterior teeth on CBCT scans from 150 patients
facts.intervention: Classification of tooth position and inclination in the alveolus (classes I to V) with facial and palatal bone wall measurement
facts.main_result: Thin facial bone predominated at the crest (83%) and mid-root (92%), and class II (retroclined) was the most common position (76.5%)
outcomes: facial and palatal bone wall thickness

facts.population: Patients with a single failing tooth or single tooth gap in the anterior maxilla (IIT cohort 16 treated, CIT cohort 23 treated)
facts.intervention: Immediately restored single implant (Astra Tech OsseoSpeed) placed in an extraction socket (IIT)
facts.comparison: Immediately restored single implant placed in a healed ridge (CIT)
outcomes: buccal bone and soft tissue thickness on CBCT
facts.main_result: After at least 8 years a buccal bone wall under 2 mm was found at all implant sites and under 1 mm at 42%, while vertical soft tissue levels and PES stayed stable.
facts.sample_size: 11 IIT and 18 CIT patients evaluated of 16 and 23 initially treated
materials_brands: Astra Tech Implant System OsseoSpeed (Dentsply Sirona Implants)
facts.funding_coi: Departmental funds and Dentsply Sirona Implants; Prof. De Bruyn has a research collaboration agreement with Dentsply Sirona, Prof. Cosyn with Nobel Biocare
facts.limitations: Limited sample size and subjective PES scoring may have hidden differences; CBCT rarely taken before placement.

facts.population: 60 healthy adults (26 thin biotype, 34 thick/average) with maxillary anterior teeth (360 teeth)
facts.intervention: Clinical classification of periodontal biotype correlated with CBCT labial plate thickness, crest position and other clinical measures
facts.comparison: Thin versus thick/average periodontal biotype
outcomes: labial plate thickness at 4, 6, 8, 10 mm from CEJ
facts.main_result: A thin biotype had thinner labial plate (P<.001, roughly half the thickness, 0.3 to 0.5 mm less), narrower keratinized tissue and greater CEJ-to-crest distance, with probe visible in 84% of thin-biotype teeth vs 7%.
facts.limitations: Only 6.1% of teeth had recession so recession results need caution; tooth malposition may influence measurements.

facts.population: Ten freshly frozen unembalmed human head and neck cadaver specimens (edentulous maxillae and fresh maxillary extraction sockets)
facts.intervention: Implant placement after bone condensation with an electrical mallet, late (edentulous) or immediate (fresh socket)
facts.comparison: Contralateral sites without condensation, placed per manufacturer drilling protocol
facts.main_result: Torque and ISQ correlated in edentulous jaws in both untreated (r=0.63) and condensed bone (r=0.82), but in extraction sockets only in untreated bone (r=0.78), not condensed (r=0.15).
facts.sample_size: 10 specimens; 26 implants in edentulous jaws and 29 in extraction sockets
facts.funding_coi: No funding; authors declare no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Low sample size, implants removed before measuring postoperative BV/TV, and high donor age.

facts.population: Five beagle dogs, mandibular third and fourth premolar extraction sockets
facts.intervention: Implant (Straumann SLA) placed in fresh extraction sockets of distal roots
facts.comparison: Contralateral extraction sockets left for spontaneous healing
outcomes: bone crest level relative to SLA margin
vertical distance between buccal and lingual bone walls
facts.main_result: At 3 months the buccal bone crest was 2.6 mm apical of the SLA level at implants; at edentulous sites buccal and lingual walls differed vertically by 2.2 mm, so implant placement did not prevent socket-wall remodelling.
materials_brands: Straumann Standard Implant, SLA surface, 4.1 mm diameter, 6-8 mm long

facts.population: 39 patients needing single-tooth replacement in the anterior maxilla after inevitable tooth extraction
facts.intervention: Flapless tooth extraction with collagen sponge in the socket, with two consecutive CBCTs (baseline and 8 weeks) analysed in 3D
outcomes: vertical and horizontal facial bone loss
facial bone wall thickness at baseline
facts.main_result: Central sites showed median vertical bone loss of 5.2 mm; thin-wall phenotypes (<=1 mm) lost a median 7.5 mm versus 1.1 mm for thick-wall phenotypes.
facts.sample_size: 39 patients (29 central incisors, 8 lateral incisors, 2 canines)
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the ITI Foundation; authors declare no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Only anterior maxillary sites and an eight-week healing period, so results apply only to esthetic-zone extraction sites.

facts.population: Six male Beagle dogs; maxillary first premolar fresh sockets with surgically created buccal bone defects (4x4x5 mm)
facts.intervention: Sockets filled with tunnel structured beta-TCP blocks
facts.comparison: Extraction alone, no graft (contralateral control sites)
outcomes: alveolar ridge width at coronal, middle, apical levels
woven bone, connective tissue, bone marrow percentages
facts.main_result: Ridge width at coronal and middle levels was greater at test sites (3.2 and 3.6 mm) than controls (1.2 and 2.0 mm), with more woven bone (62.4% vs 26.8%).
facts.sample_size: 6 Beagle dogs, bilateral defects (test vs control)
materials_brands: Tunnel structured beta-tricalcium phosphate (beta-TCP) blocks, about 70% porosity
facts.funding_coi: Supported by Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (KAKENHI 23792465); no conflicts of interest

facts.population: Five beagle dogs, third mandibular premolar sockets
facts.intervention: Bio-Oss Collagen (90% deproteinized bovine bone, 10% porcine collagen) placed in the fresh extraction socket
facts.comparison: Contralateral ungrafted socket (blood clot)
outcomes: tissue composition (woven bone, lamellar bone, marrow, graft particles)
facts.main_result: After 6 months the alveolar process dimension and ridge profile were better preserved at Bio-Oss Collagen sites (marginal reduction three times smaller than ungrafted), but the graft did not enhance new bone formation.

facts.population: Forty patients with 71 Miller class I and II gingival recessions
facts.intervention: Modified microsurgical tunnel technique (MMTT) with connective tissue graft
facts.comparison: Coronally advanced flap (CAF) with connective tissue graft
facts.main_result: At 12 months root coverage was 98.3% for CAF and 97.2% for MMTT with no significant difference; both gave high aesthetic scores (RES about 9.2).
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest; no funding other than the department's own

facts.population: Patients needing single tooth replacement in the anterior maxilla (15-25 FDI)
facts.intervention: Type 1A protocol: immediate implant placement with immediate loading, grouped by site selection criteria
facts.comparison: Immediate placement and loading without one or more site-specific selection criteria
facts.main_result: Weighted mean survival of Type 1A single implants in the maxillary esthetic zone was 97.7%; pre-2012 studies had lower survival (-1.9 PP), as did facial gaps and endodontic infection groups.
facts.sample_size: 68 articles included from 3118 identified (mean 37.2 implants per study)
facts.funding_coi: Authors report no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Heterogeneity in study duration, no multivariate analysis possible, English-only search, and inclusion of lower-quality case series with inherent risk of bias.

facts.population: 90 consecutive patients (50 female, 40 male, 18-69 years) scheduled for periodontal or peri-implant plastic surgery requiring palatal mucosal graft harvesting
facts.intervention: Free palatal mucosal graft harvesting with patient-reported pain (VAS) recorded postoperatively
facts.main_result: Pain peaked on day 1 and declined; thicker grafts increased pain while thicker palatal mucosa reduced it, and wound surface area had no effect
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared; supported by the Clinical Research Foundation (CRF), Brienz, Switzerland

facts.journal: The Journal of the American Dental Association
facts.population: 20 participants with a single edentulous gap in the anterior maxilla receiving an implant-supported crown (commented trial)
facts.intervention: Screw-retained implant-supported provisional crown conditioning soft tissue for 6 months before the definitive crown
facts.comparison: Definitive crown placed immediately without provisional phase
facts.main_result: At 3 years the provisional-crown group had a mean total pink esthetic score 2.6 points higher; only mesial and distal papilla differed significantly; white esthetic score did not differ
materials_brands: Bone Level Implant, RC, SLActive, Straumann
facts.funding_coi: Commentary author reported no disclosures
facts.limitations: Small number of participants, which may explain missing significance or suggest chance findings
facts.key_finding: A commentary on a small randomized trial (20 patients) found that single anterior maxillary implants given a 6-month screw-retained provisional crown had higher pink esthetic scores at 3 years than those restored directly with the definitive crown, mainly in papilla scores.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Provisionalizing and soft-tissue conditioning before the definitive crown may improve esthetics in the anterior maxilla, but the evidence comes from a small trial.

facts.population: Three consecutive cases of single failing anterior maxillary teeth (e.g. vertical root fracture of a central incisor)
facts.intervention: Socket seal surgery with a free gingival graft combined with immediate, early or delayed implant placement
facts.main_result: Healing occurred without complication and soft tissue stability was confirmed at 2 years in case 1
facts.limitations: Technique is skill sensitive and increases treatment time and number of procedures

facts.population: Maxillary front teeth situated close to the buccal plate in the esthetic zone
facts.intervention: Socket transformation: buccal concavity grafting with elective root canal and apicectomy, then extraction and immediate implant months later
facts.main_result: Socket transformation is proposed as feasible for suitable cases but may not always solve long-term esthetic problems in Type B3 cases
facts.limitations: Further clinical studies are needed to evaluate long-term bony and soft tissue stability

facts.journal: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
facts.population: One patient with a horizontally fractured maxillary central incisor (tooth No. 9)
facts.intervention: Atraumatic flapless extraction, immediate implant with bone graft in the buccal gap and screw-retained provisional as prosthetic socket seal
facts.main_result: At 6 months bone levels around the platform-switched implant were good and there was little to no contour difference versus the untreated contralateral tooth

facts.population: Adult patients in need of a single implant
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement (IIP)
facts.comparison: Delayed single implant placement (>=3 months post-extraction)
facts.main_result: Implant survival was lower for IIP (94.9%) than DIP (98.9%), RR 0.96; probing depth and pink esthetic score were similar
facts.sample_size: 3 RCTs and 5 non-randomized studies, 473 single implants (IIP 233, DIP 240)
facts.limitations: One RCT had unclear risk of bias and all other studies high risk of bias

facts.population: 420 maxillary anterior teeth in 70 participants with CBCT scans
facts.intervention: CBCT classification of sagittal root position (classes I-IV) and measurement of bone housing
facts.main_result: Class distribution was 65.2%, 9.3%, 0.7% and 24.8% for classes I-IV; bone housing measurements differed between classes except alveolar ridge height
facts.funding_coi: Supported in part by CAPES, Brazil (Finance Code 001)

facts.intervention: Immediate placement of implants into fresh extraction sockets (literature through December 1996)
facts.comparison: Delayed implantation after socket healing
facts.main_result: Implants in fresh sockets showed survival of 93.9% to 100%; no consensus on gap filling, membranes not better and exposure may cause complications

facts.population: 22 fresh cadaver heads, maxillary anterior teeth (#6-#11)
facts.intervention: Clinical caliper and CBCT measurement of labial/palatal gingival and bone thickness
facts.comparison: Clinical measurements versus CBCT measurements
facts.main_result: CBCT and clinical thickness did not differ except palatal soft tissue; labial gingival thickness was moderately associated with bone thickness (R = 0.429)

facts.population: Systemically healthy patients requiring a single immediate post-extraction implant in the maxillary esthetic zone
facts.intervention: Surgical modifications during IIP: connective tissue grafts, bone grafts, flapless surgery, palatal implant positioning
facts.comparison: IIP without the individual surgical modifications
outcomes: horizontal and vertical soft and hard tissue changes
facts.main_result: Connective tissue grafts improved facial gingival level (MD -0.51 mm) and bone grafts reduced horizontal buccal bone resorption (MD -0.59 mm); flapless and palatal positioning gave no significant gains
facts.limitations: Additional longitudinal studies are required

facts.population: Patients needing tooth extraction and implant replacement (evidence mostly from single-tooth extraction)
facts.intervention: Alveolar ridge preservation/bone grafting, immediate, early and delayed implant placement, and bone augmentation at implant placement
facts.comparison: Unassisted socket healing (for ridge preservation); different implant placement timings against each other
facts.main_result: The group formulated 23 consensus statements and 12 clinical recommendations; ridge preservation via socket grafting may prevent 1.5-2.4 mm horizontal and 1-2.5 mm vertical mid-buccal resorption versus extraction alone
facts.sample_size: 25 articles from 22 RCTs in the ridge preservation review
facts.funding_coi: Participants declared research funding/consultancy from several implant and biomaterial companies (e.g. Straumann, Geistlich)
facts.limitations: None of the RCTs in the ridge preservation review had low risk of bias

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 20 patients (8 men, 12 women) with one missing tooth distal to the canine and a shallow buccal bone dehiscence
facts.intervention: Transmucosal implant placement with submarginal connective tissue graft covering the dehiscence
facts.main_result: Buccal soft tissue thickness and vertical soft tissue level improved significantly at 6 months, 1 and 3 years, with no recession, no significant marginal bone loss and no mucositis or peri-implantitis
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Case series design; RCTs comparing bone augmentation with submarginal CTG are needed

facts.population: Postextraction sites in the esthetic zone requiring implant therapy
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement with immediate prosthetics, alveolar ridge preservation, early or delayed placement with bone augmentation, socket shield
facts.main_result: For an intact alveolus, immediate placement with immediate prosthetics is the reference choice if primary stability and the buccal bone plate are present; a compromised alveolus favors staged placement with augmentation
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the non-profit Fondazione Giuseppe Cardaropoli; authors declare no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Expert-opinion based; socket shield technique lacks well-designed prospective controlled studies

facts.population: Patients needing extraction of maxillary anterior teeth with immediate implant placement (three clinical examples)
facts.intervention: Eight-step protocol: provisional on tooth to be extracted, atraumatic extraction, guided placement, >35 Ncm stability, 3D bone packing, custom abutment, provisional reline, tuberosity CTG
facts.main_result: Case examples with up to 13 years follow-up showed stable buccal bone where bone graft was packed into the gap, and resorption where no graft was used

facts.population: Patients with early implant placement and contour augmentation in the esthetic zone (case series of 20 implants)
facts.intervention: Early implant placement with contour augmentation using autogenous bone chips, DBBM particles and a collagen membrane
outcomes: facial bone wall thickness on CBCT
facts.main_result: At 6 years all 20 implants had a visible facial bone wall with mean thickness about 1.9 mm; one implant (5%) was at risk with a thin wall and slight recession
facts.key_finding: Lecture slides by Daniel Buser describing early implant placement with soft tissue healing and contour augmentation (autogenous bone chips plus DBBM particles under a collagen membrane). A 6-year case series of 20 implants showed a visible facial bone wall (mean about 1.9 mm) at all implants, with one implant at risk.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Early placement with contour augmentation using autograft chips plus DBBM under a collagen membrane gives stable esthetic outcomes with low recession risk in the esthetic zone.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Single implant sites with horizontal ridge defects treated with GBR
facts.intervention: Periosteal vertical mattress suture with resorbable sutures to fix the collagen membrane and stabilize particulate graft
facts.comparison: Fixation with pins or osteosynthesis screws (discussed, not tested)
facts.main_result: Authors report a low rate of dehiscence and good bone regeneration in their clinical experience with the technique
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Limited by tensile strength and resorption time of the suture; not enough stability for multiple missing teeth

facts.intervention: Transfer soft tissue contours of an interim implant restoration to the definitive cast using gingival contour elastomer material
materials_brands: Zimmer Dental healing abutment and impression post
ResinRock Type IV dental stone (Whip Mix)

facts.population: 12 single implant sites in the maxillary esthetic zone of 10 participants
facts.intervention: Intraoral scans at 0 seconds to 20 minutes after removal of the interim restoration
facts.comparison: Scan with the interim restoration in place (baseline)
facts.main_result: After removal, papilla height fell up to 0.27 mm at 20 minutes and emergence profile discrepancy was significant immediately and increased over time
facts.funding_coi: Foundation of State Key Laboratory of Oral Diseases, Sichuan University

facts.population: Humans undergoing tooth extraction (20 included studies)
facts.intervention: Tooth extraction with undisturbed healing
outcomes: horizontal and vertical hard tissue change
facts.main_result: At 6 months horizontal hard tissue reduction (3.79 mm) exceeded vertical reduction (1.24 mm buccal); re-entry studies showed horizontal bone loss of 29-63% and vertical 11-22%
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

facts.population: Five Beagle dogs, four immediate implants each in the lower jaw
facts.intervention: Flapless immediate implant placement
facts.comparison: Flap surgery (control side)
facts.main_result: Bone-implant contact was similar (64.8% vs 65.1%); buccal mucosa-to-bone distance was 3.02 mm flapless vs 3.69 mm flap (significant), buccal bone crest 0.82 vs 1.33 mm apical to SLA level (not significant)
facts.funding_coi: Partially supported by Straumann Iberian; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Animal model with implants well within the socket

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 46 patients (31 women, 15 men) referred for extraction of a maxillary or mandibular premolar or molar before single-tooth implant treatment
facts.intervention: Single-tooth extraction of a premolar or molar, then 12 months of healing without prostheses (in 44 of 46) with clinical and radiographic evaluation
outcomes: alveolar ridge width and height on study casts
adjacent tooth pocket depth and attachment level
facts.main_result: Ridge width fell about 50% (12.0 to 5.9 mm), two thirds of it in the first 3 months; height changes were under 1 mm.
facts.limitations: Subtraction radiography was limited: 11 patients excluded because of reference-point or alignment problems, and radiographic magnification means measurements are approximate.

facts.population: Eight adult beagle dogs; third and fourth mandibular premolar sockets
facts.intervention: Immediate placement of one of four implant systems (3i Osseotite, Astra OsseoSpeed, Thommen SPI Element, Straumann ITI) in the distal socket of extracted premolars
facts.comparison: Adjacent mesial sockets left to heal spontaneously
outcomes: relative vertical buccal bone loss versus lingual crest
absolute buccal bone loss at implant sites
woven bone area in healing sockets
facts.main_result: Relative buccal bone resorption was similar at implant and control sites; absolute buccal bone loss at implant sites was 2.32 mm (SD 0.36).
facts.sample_size: 8 dogs; 32 implant sites and 32 edentulous sites
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts declared; supported by a research grant from Thommen Medical
facts.limitations: The limitations of the histological evaluation method preclude a definite conclusion.

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Five 1-year-old beagle dogs; third and fourth mandibular premolar fresh extraction sockets
facts.intervention: Small-diameter (3.25 mm) implants placed in fresh extraction sockets of hemisected premolars with the neck at the buccal bone crest, submerged healing
outcomes: distance from implant shoulder to buccal and lingual bone crest
facts.main_result: Mean vertical buccal bone resorption was 0.5 mm; buccal crest 0.8 mm and lingual -0.3 mm from the implant shoulder at 12 weeks, and buccolingual crest width fell from 4.5 to 3.5 mm.
facts.follow_up: 15 days to 3 months (assessments at 2, 4 and 12 weeks)

facts.population: 17 molars extracted because of advanced periodontitis in patients planned for implant-retained replacement
facts.intervention: Minimally invasive flapless molar extraction with natural healing, CBCT at baseline and 6 months
outcomes: horizontal ridge width change at -1, -3, -5 mm
vertical ridge height change at nine points
facts.main_result: After 6 months the central buccal crest width fell 0.59 mm (maxilla) and 0.72 mm (mandible) at -1 mm, with no significant volumetric bone loss in either jaw.
facts.funding_coi: Capital Medical Development and Research Fund and Capital foundation for Clinical Characteristics and Application Research; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Small sample size with limited statistical power, no correction for multiple tests in this pilot study.

facts.main_result: Thin facial bone walls (1 mm or less) lose a median 7.5 mm (62%) of facial bone height by 8 weeks versus 1.1 mm (9%) for thick walls.

facts.population: 45 adult patients needing an immediate implant to replace a maxillary premolar with sufficient buccal bone
facts.intervention: Immediate implant with open flap and bone grafting (flap-graft)
facts.comparison: Open flap without grafting (flap-nograft) and flapless without grafting (noflap-nograft)
outcomes: CBCT buccal bone dimensions at apical, medial and bevel levels
facts.main_result: Treatment technique had no relevant effect on bone outcomes; the three techniques nearly filled the marginal gap (residual vertical gap 0.27 mm, horizontal 0.5 mm) and noflap-nograft was less painful.
facts.sample_size: 45 patients, one implant each (15 per arm), one lost to follow-up
facts.funding_coi: Implants supplied by Bone System; other costs self-funded; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: CBCT cannot confirm osseointegration quality or soft tissue changes, applies only to maxillary premolar sites with an intact facial wall, and follow-up was only 6 months.

facts.population: Twelve mongrel dogs, mandibular 3rd and 4th premolar extraction sites
facts.intervention: Hemi-sectioning of 3rd and 4th mandibular premolars and removal of the distal roots, sites covered with mobilized gingiva, histology at 1, 2, 4 and 8 weeks
outcomes: height of buccal and lingual bone walls
width of bone walls at 1, 3 and 5 mm below the crest
facts.main_result: Marked dimensional alterations occurred in the first 8 weeks, with bone wall height reduced more on the buccal than the lingual side in two overlapping resorption phases.
Four systematic reviews showed mean ridge reduction of 3.8 mm in width and 1.24 mm in height within 6 months; immediate implants give high survival but a high recession risk in esthetic sites.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.population: 20 consecutively enrolled patients with a single-tooth gap in the anterior maxilla
facts.intervention: Flapless extraction, 4-8 weeks soft-tissue healing, early placement of a bone-level SLActive implant with simultaneous contour augmentation (autogenous chips, DBBM, collagen membrane)
outcomes: clinical parameters (plaque, bleeding, probing depth, keratinized mucosa)
facial bone wall thickness on CBCT
facts.main_result: At 6 years all 20 implants were integrated with mean DIB 0.44 mm, and all had a detectable facial bone wall (mean thickness 1.06 to 1.93 mm).
facts.funding_coi: Departmental funds of Bern and Geneva universities and a research grant from Institut Straumann AG; one author is consultant to the cited companies

facts.population: Six beagle dogs; mandibular third premolar and first molar fresh extraction sockets
facts.intervention: Immediate placement of Straumann standard implants (4.1 mm wide, 6 or 8 mm long) in fresh extraction sockets of distal roots, semi-submerged healing
outcomes: buccal and lingual bone wall width at 1, 2 and 3 mm
marginal level of bone crest and bone-to-implant contact relative to the implant surface
facts.main_result: Implant placement failed to preserve ridge dimensions: both buccal and lingual walls were resorbed, with more bone loss at molar than premolar sites and some marginal loss of osseointegration buccally.
materials_brands: Straumann Standard Implant, SLA surface, 4.1 mm

facts.population: 20 Labrador dogs with mandibular premolars extracted and 3 months healed
facts.intervention: Four c.p. titanium ITI implants per animal placed non-submerged with mucosa sutured to the implant, biopsies from day 0 to 12 weeks of healing
outcomes: histological composition of the peri-implant soft tissue over time
epithelial proliferation and barrier epithelium maturation
facts.main_result: A mature barrier epithelium occurred after 6-8 weeks and collagen fibers were organized after 4-6 weeks; the soft-tissue barrier developed its final characteristics within 6 weeks.
facts.follow_up: Healing periods from day 0 (2 h) to 12 weeks
materials_brands: ITI Dental Implant System (Straumann), 4.1 mm solid screw implants
facts.funding_coi: Supported by an ITI Foundation research program grant

facts.population: Adult human subjects (>18 years) undergoing single tooth extraction, excluding mandibular incisors and third molars (28 included studies)
facts.intervention: Standard-of-care tooth extraction with unassisted socket healing
outcomes: horizontal and vertical (mid-facial, mid-lingual) ridge reduction
facts.main_result: Pooled clinical horizontal ridge reduction in non-molar sites was 2.73 mm, with greater reduction in molar sites (3.61 mm radiographic horizontal).
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts; supported by University of Iowa Periodontics Graduate Student Research Fund

facts.population: Patients needing a single anterior maxillary tooth extraction (canine to canine) with thin or thick facial bone wall; 33 analysed
facts.intervention: Flapless extraction with collagen sponge in the socket, healing monitored over 8 weeks by sequential digitized impressions and CBCT superimposition
facts.comparison: Thin (<1 mm) versus thick facial bone wall phenotype
outcomes: facial soft tissue thickness at extraction and 8 weeks
vertical and horizontal soft tissue and bone loss
facts.main_result: In thin bone phenotypes facial soft tissue thickness rose from 0.7 to 5.3 mm over 8 weeks, so vertical soft tissue loss was only 1.6 mm versus 7.5 mm of vertical bone loss; thick phenotypes were unchanged.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the ITI Foundation; no conflicts declared

facts.population: 35 patients with a single maxillary molar extraction
facts.intervention: Alveolar ridge preservation after maxillary molar extraction
facts.comparison: Spontaneous healing
outcomes: crestal, buccal and palatal gingival thickness at 6 months
facts.main_result: Crestal gingiva was thinner in ARP (2.17 mm) than spontaneous healing (3.33 mm), and buccal/palatal gingiva at implant shoulder were also thinner with ARP (p<0.05); MGJ change was similar.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the Osteology Foundation (grant 16-048); no conflicts of interest

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: CBCT scans of patients referred for implant therapy in the anterior maxilla (125 scans, 498 teeth from first premolar to first premolar)
facts.intervention: Measurement of facial bone wall thickness on sagittal CBCT slices at crest level (MP1) and mid-root (MP2)
outcomes: facial bone wall thickness at MP1 and MP2
frequency of missing, thin (<1 mm) and thick (>=1 mm) walls
effect of age, sex and tooth position
facts.main_result: The facial bone wall was missing in 25.7% of teeth at MP1 and thin (<1 mm) in 62.9%, with only 11.4% >=1 mm; thickness decreased from premolars to incisors.
materials_brands: Morita 3D Accuitomo XYZ Slice View Tomograph

facts.population: Human subjects undergoing tooth extraction (12 included publications, 7 to 46 subjects each)
facts.intervention: Tooth extraction with post-extraction healing
outcomes: mid-buccal, mid-crestal and mid-lingual height change
facts.main_result: Alveolar ridge width reduced by 3.87 mm, with mean clinical mid-buccal height loss of 1.67 mm; loss in width exceeded loss in height.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest; self-funded

facts.population: Nine periodontal patients with pockets to or beyond the mucogingival junction (7 surgically re-evaluated, 21 teeth per flap type)
facts.intervention: Apically repositioned partial thickness flap
facts.comparison: Apically repositioned full thickness flap on the opposite side of the arch
outcomes: crestal radicular alveolar bone height loss
facts.main_result: Mean crestal bone loss was 0.62 mm after full thickness and 0.98 mm after partial thickness flaps, both significant, with greater loss after partial thickness (p<.01).
facts.sample_size: 9 patients (7 surgically re-evaluated), 21 teeth per flap type

facts.population: One 32-year-old healthy non-smoking male with a lost upper-right central incisor and horizontal and vertical soft tissue deficiency
facts.intervention: NobelReplace CC PMC 3.5 x 13 mm implant with Slim Healing Abutment and palatal connective tissue graft placed simultaneously, then NobelProcera ASC abutment with zirconia crown
facts.main_result: After three months of healing the soft tissue had grown vertically and horizontally and the contour developed correctly; final restoration placed at six months.
materials_brands: Slim Healing Abutment CC NP 7 mm
NobelProcera ASC Abutment with zirconia crown
facts.funding_coi: Manufacturer-published case (Nobel Biocare products)
facts.key_finding: A single-case report showing that a palatal connective tissue graft placed over a Slim Healing Abutment at implant placement gave vertical and horizontal soft tissue gain at three months in a lost upper central incisor site, followed by a zirconia crown at six months.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Placing a connective tissue graft together with a slim healing abutment at implant surgery can rebuild lacking soft tissue in the esthetic zone, but this is a single manufacturer-presented case.

facts.population: Patients with a tooth extracted in the esthetic zone who received immediate implant placement
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement with simultaneous or delayed connective tissue graft
facts.comparison: Immediate implant placement without connective tissue graft
facts.main_result: In four RCTs the mean buccal gingiva level difference between immediate implants with and without CTG was 0.09 mm (95% CI -0.54 to 0.72), i.e. CTG maintained but did not increase the gingival level.
facts.sample_size: 5 RCTs, 245 patients (4 RCTs in quantitative analysis)
facts.follow_up: At least 6 months (included studies mostly 12 months)
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Low level of evidence and study limitations acknowledged

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 24 consecutive patients receiving implants in the maxillary anterior area at the time of tooth extraction
facts.intervention: Immediate implant with subepithelial connective tissue graft using the tunnel technique (last 12 patients)
facts.comparison: Immediate implant without flap and without graft (first 12 patients)
outcomes: labial tissue volume/ridge width change at 6 months
facts.main_result: Nongrafted group lost 1.063 mm of labial tissue dimension whereas the grafted group gained 0.34 mm after 6 months.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 20 patients (ages 27-87) with a single failing maxillary tooth in the esthetic zone
facts.intervention: Single immediate implant placement and provisionalization with subepithelial connective tissue graft
facts.comparison: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization without connective tissue graft
facts.main_result: Facial gingival level change at 1 year was significantly greater without graft (-0.70 mm) than with graft (-0.25 mm); marginal bone change did not differ significantly and all implants survived.
facts.funding_coi: Partially funded by Straumann USA; authors declare no financial interests in the products
facts.limitations: Short-term (1-year) follow-up with a small sample; longer-term studies are needed.

facts.population: Adults with single immediate implant placement (within 24 h post-extraction); 8 studies, 409 implants
facts.intervention: Submucosal buccal connective tissue graft with immediate implant placement
facts.comparison: Immediate implant placement without CTG
facts.main_result: Meta-analysis showed 0.41 mm less vertical mid-facial soft tissue change with CTG than without (95% CI 0.21-0.61), and 12 times lower risk of >=1 mm asymmetry.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts declared; senior author has a collaboration agreement with Nobel Biocare and Straumann
facts.limitations: Only 1 RCT showed low risk of bias; results inconclusive for horizontal soft tissue change and papilla height.

authors: Ariádene Cristina Pértile de Oliveira Rosa
facts.population: Patient with an abscessed right central incisor and absent buccal bone wall (clinical report)
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement with a triple graft (cancellous and cortical bone plus connective tissue) from the maxillary tuberosity to reconstruct the buccal wall and repair recession
outcomes: buccal bone wall stability on CBCT
facts.main_result: Technique reconstructs the buccal bone wall and gingival recession with a triple tuberosity graft in a single procedure; no quantitative outcome reported.
facts.limitations: Difficult donor-site access in small mouth opening; limited tuberosity tissue for large or multiple-tooth defects; insufficient residual bone may prevent primary stability.

facts.population: 60 patients with a failing maxillary tooth (first bicuspid to first bicuspid) in the esthetic zone
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization with a tuberosity connective tissue graft
facts.comparison: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization without soft tissue graft
facts.main_result: CTG did not reduce mucosal volume loss (-0.68 vs -0.49 mm, p=.189) but gave a more coronal mid-facial mucosa level (+0.20 vs -0.48 mm, p=.014).
facts.sample_size: 60 patients (30 test, 30 control); 25 per group analysed
facts.funding_coi: Unrestricted grant from Nobel Biocare Services AG; authors declare no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Post-extraction facial bone wall thickness was not included as a risk factor; CBCT data needed.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Two cases of single hopeless anterior tooth / fractured teeth 11 and 21 in the esthetic zone
facts.intervention: Vertical or horizontal double-parallel mattress suture to fix a subepithelial connective tissue graft in a tunnel during immediate implant placement and provisionalization
facts.main_result: The two cases gave similar esthetic outcomes with vertical and horizontal sutures; the technique achieved stable passive graft fixation (preliminary, no quantitative data).
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Additional randomized controlled studies are required; turning the graft over during suturing may confuse the surgeon.

facts.population: 60 patients with a single failing maxillary anterior tooth (incisor, canine, first premolar)
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization with a tuberosity connective tissue graft
facts.comparison: Immediate implant placement and provisionalization without graft
facts.main_result: At 5 years mid-buccal mucosa level change was 0.6 mm recession in controls versus 0.1 mm in grafted sites (p=.008); bone, esthetics and satisfaction did not differ clinically.
facts.sample_size: 60 patients (30 per group); 27 per group analysed at 5 years
facts.follow_up: 5 years (60 months after final crown placement)
facts.funding_coi: 1-year study supported by Nobel Biocare Services AG grant; no funding for 5-year evaluation; authors declare no conflicts
facts.limitations: Risk factors for soft-tissue loss and ideal timing of soft-tissue augmentation remain unclear from this study.

facts.population: 30 adults needing extraction of one anterior tooth (premolar to premolar)
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement plus sub-epithelial connective tissue graft, without bone graft in the gap
facts.comparison: Immediate implant placement alone
outcomes: vertical and horizontal buccal bone resorption
facts.main_result: CTG did not affect vertical buccal bone resorption but reduced horizontal ridge change coronally and maintained tissue contour (change 0.32-0.04 mm vs 1.94-1.08 mm in controls) via greater soft tissue thickness.
facts.funding_coi: Partially supported by a grant from BioSAF IN Srl; no conflicts reported

facts.main_result: Narrative overview: tunneling flap elevation without papilla detachment or vertical releasing incisions is proposed to improve blood supply, wound healing and esthetics across root coverage and implant soft-tissue augmentation.
facts.limitations: Long-term data are lacking and controlled clinical trials are needed.

facts.population: 250 subjects aged 17-66 with all maxillary front teeth present
facts.intervention: CBCT measurement of facial bone wall thickness and CEJ-to-bone-crest distance at 1, 3 and 5 mm apical to the crest
outcomes: distance from CEJ to facial bone crest
facts.main_result: The CEJ-bone crest distance was 1.6-3 mm; the facial bone wall was thin, with about 85% of sites under 1 mm and 40-60% under 0.5 mm.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 43 implant patients; maxillary first premolars and anterior teeth (1,036 measurable sites)
facts.intervention: CBCT measurement of CEJ-to-buccal-crest distance and buccal bone thickness at crest, midroot and apex
outcomes: distance from CEJ to buccal bone crest
buccal bone thickness at crest, midroot, apex
facts.main_result: Median CEJ-to-crest distance was 2.79 mm; buccal bone 1 mm below the crest was 1.13 mm at premolars and 0.83 mm at anterior teeth, with few anterior teeth exceeding 1 mm.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: Eight beagle dogs with premolar and molar sites
facts.intervention: Flapless immediate implant placement in fresh extraction sockets (test)
facts.comparison: Flapped delayed implant placement in healed ridges (control)
facts.main_result: Vertical buccal crest resorption was similar in both protocols (about 0.5 mm) with marked horizontal buccal resorption; immediate implants had a thinner buccal crest than delayed implants and teeth.
materials_brands: Premium straight implants (Sweden & Martina), ZirTi surface
facts.funding_coi: Partially funded by Sweden & Martina; authors declare no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: The model compared a flapless immediate with a flapped delayed protocol, so flap elevation may partly explain differences.

facts.journal: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.intervention: Anatomic harmony abutment: in vivo chairside customized composite healing abutment placed on an immediate molar implant
facts.main_result: Technique report: the custom abutment preserves the anatomic emergence form with sutureless implant site sealing and improves predictability of final restoration fabrication.

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Patients with anterior maxillary extraction sockets treated with immediate implant placement
facts.intervention: Flapless immediate implant placement in anterior postextraction sockets with or without bone graft and/or provisional restoration (four groups)
facts.comparison: No bone graft and no provisional restoration (No BGPR)
facts.main_result: Peri-implant soft tissue height was greater at grafted than nongrafted sites (2.72 vs 2.29 mm), and net gain in height and thickness was about 1 mm.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Retrospective cohort design, lack of long-term follow-up, and no measurement of preimplant labial soft tissue thickness.

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Patients with anterior maxillary extraction sockets treated with postextraction socket implant placement
facts.comparison: Contralateral untreated natural tooth sites and the no-bone-graft/no-provisional group
outcomes: facial-palatal ridge dimension change at 0-9 mm from the free gingival margin
facts.main_result: Bone grafting combined with a contoured healing abutment or provisional restoration gave the smallest ridge contour change (about 0.4 mm or less).
facts.follow_up: 6 months to 4 years after delivery of the definitive restoration
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 23 patients with implants placed in anterior maxillary extraction sockets
facts.intervention: Flapless immediate implant with provisional restoration alone or with bone grafting
facts.comparison: Contralateral natural tooth site (color); provisional-only vs bone graft plus provisional groups
outcomes: gingival color difference (deltaE) at 2.0 and 5.0 mm below the free gingival margin
facts.main_result: Mean deltaE was 2.6 (PR) and 2.4 (BGPR) at 2.0 mm and 1.9 and 2.5 at 5.0 mm; about 80% of sites were below the visible perception threshold (3.1).
facts.follow_up: 12 months after the final restoration (clinical views); photographs taken at least 6 months after delivery
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Color was measured retrospectively from photographs rather than with spectrophotometers.

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 14 patients requiring extraction of a single maxillary incisor
facts.intervention: Lingualized flapless implant placement into fresh extraction sockets with immediate nonocclusal loading, gap grafted with bovine xenograft
outcomes: buccal alveolar plate thickness on CBCT at coronal, mid and apical levels
distance from implant surface to buccal plate
facts.main_result: Buccal plate resorption was not significant over 6 months (overall change in labial plate-to-implant distance 0.08 ± 0.20 mm).
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Single-tooth immediate replacement in maxillary anterior and premolar regions, intact (Type 1) extraction sockets
facts.intervention: Novel macro-hybrid (inverted body-shift) implant with dual-zone grafting and immediate provisional restoration
outcomes: labial plate dimension change (CBCT, L1 and L2)
facts.main_result: Mean labial plate dimension change was 0.33 mm at L1 and 0.34 mm at L2 at 1 year, with primary stability around 60 Ncm.
facts.funding_coi: No financial support; Drs Chu, Saito and Nevins are consultants for Southern Implants
facts.limitations: Single-arm design without a comparison group.

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics and Restorative Dentistry
facts.intervention: Partial extraction therapies: root submergence, socket-shield and pontic shield procedures
facts.main_result: Technical report giving step-by-step procedures, guidelines and complication management for root submergence, socket-shield and pontic shield; no outcome data.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Socket-shield and pontic shield are in their clinical infancy and need long-term clinical data.

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Patients needing single-tooth replacement in the anterior maxilla or mandible (premolar to premolar)
facts.intervention: Flapless single-tooth immediate implant placement with healing abutment or immediate provisional, with or without bone graft (4 groups)
facts.comparison: Healing abutment without graft (group 1)
outcomes: buccopalatal dimension at 1, 3 and 5 mm apical to the free gingival margin
facts.main_result: Buccopalatal dimension contraction was greatest with healing abutment alone, smaller with graft or provisional alone, and minimal with provisional plus graft.
materials_brands: Endobon bovine xenograft with autogenous bone (Biomet 3i)
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: More studies and larger samples are needed to validate the conclusion.

facts.population: 45 patients with a single-tooth implant crown in the anterior maxilla
facts.intervention: Early implant placement (4-8 weeks after extraction) with simultaneous GBR using autogenous chips, DBBM and a collagen membrane
outcomes: mucosal margin to implant shoulder distance
facts.main_result: All 45 implants were successful, with mean facial mucosal margin -1.93 mm to the implant shoulder and mean implant shoulder to first bone contact 2.18 mm.
facts.funding_coi: Departmental funds; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Retrospective design gives a low level of evidence for predictability and long-term soft tissue stability.

facts.population: Patients needing single-tooth extraction and implant replacement, upper or lower jaw
facts.intervention: Single implant placed early (about 10 days) or delayed (about 3 months) after extraction
facts.comparison: Late (conventional, about 17 months) placement
facts.main_result: No significant differences among groups in implant survival or marginal bone level at 10 years (1.15, 1.53 and 1.42 mm for early, delayed, late).
facts.limitations: Dropout of 11.7% by 10 years and radiographs missing for some late-group patients at T1.

facts.population: Patients with a single missing tooth in the anterior area (2nd premolar to 2nd premolar)
facts.intervention: Early implant placement 4-16 weeks after extraction (Type 2 and Type 3)
facts.comparison: Late implant placement at least 16 weeks after extraction (Type 4)
facts.main_result: Type 3 implants showed survival comparable to Type 4 (95% vs. 100%); both early protocols had high survival, few complications and high aesthetic scores.
facts.sample_size: 19 articles from 6 studies, 140 patients and 140 implants
facts.follow_up: minimum 1 year after implant placement (inclusion criterion)
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the authors and their institutions; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Limited number of cases, heterogeneity and high risk of bias reduce generalizability.

facts.population: Single tooth extraction sites in the esthetic zone
facts.intervention: Immediate, early and late implant placement after extraction, reviewed historically with clinical recommendations
facts.main_result: Immediate placement is advised only with ideal anatomy (intact thick facial wall, thick biotype); otherwise early placement with soft tissue healing and contour augmentation (type 2, used in over 80% of the authors' cases).

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Patients needing a single premolar or molar extraction and implant
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement in fresh extraction socket, flapless, with socket-gap grafting
facts.comparison: Implant placed 12 weeks after extraction in healed site with flap
facts.main_result: Implant success 100% in both groups; ISQ at insertion and loading did not differ; CBL at 12 months was 0.68 mm (immediate) vs 0.40 mm (delayed), P = .02.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Small sample size; longer follow-up needed.

facts.population: Patients needing extraction and immediate implant at a non-molar site
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement with grafting of the buccal gap with anorganic bovine bone, flapless approach (test group)
facts.comparison: Same procedure with a mucoperiosteal flap (control group)
outcomes: influence of initial buccal plate width
facts.main_result: About 0.5 mm mean loss in height and width at 6 months, with no significant difference between flap and flapless.

facts.population: Patients needing extraction of premolar or molar teeth and later implant
facts.intervention: Ridge preservation with porcine bone and collagen membrane using a flapless procedure with secondary soft tissue closure (test)
facts.comparison: Same ridge preservation with full-thickness mucoperiosteal flap and primary soft tissue closure (control)
facts.main_result: No histological or histomorphometric difference between flap and flapless: new bone 22.5% vs 22.5%, marrow spaces 59.3% vs 59.4%, residual graft 18.6% vs 18.2%.
facts.follow_up: 3 months to bone biopsy at implant placement

facts.population: Six Labrador dogs, implants in distal alveoli of second mandibular premolars
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement without flap elevation (flapless, test site)
facts.comparison: Immediate implant placement with full-thickness mucoperiosteal flap (control site)
outcomes: remaining gap between implant and socket wall
facts.main_result: Buccal crest resorption was 1.7 mm (flap) and 1.5 mm (flapless), with no significant differences between approaches.

facts.population: Patients with a non-restorable single tooth in the esthetic zone
facts.intervention: Flapless immediate implant placement with provisionalization
facts.comparison: Flap-involving immediate implant placement with provisionalization
facts.main_result: Flap elevation caused more mesial and distal gingival margin recession at 3 months (p=0.02 and p=0.01), with no other significant differences up to 12 months.
facts.funding_coi: Implants and abutments supplied free by Biomet 3i; conflict of interest: none

facts.population: Adults needing a single maxillary anterior or premolar tooth extraction with intact buccal plate
facts.intervention: Immediate implant with minimal split-thickness envelope flap (MSTEF), with GBR and connective tissue graft
facts.comparison: Immediate implant with conventional flap (control)
facts.main_result: No significant differences between flap and MSTEF: PES 10.54 vs 10.80, WES 6.97 vs 6.95, survival and success 100%; esthetic failures were common in both groups.

facts.population: Adult patients with a single immediate implant in incisor, cuspid or premolar position
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement without flap elevation (flapless)
facts.comparison: Immediate implant placement with flap elevation
outcomes: papillary and midfacial soft tissue change
facts.main_result: Flapless surgery gave 0.48 mm less horizontal buccal bone change (95% CI 0.13-0.84, p = .007) with no difference in implant survival (RR 1.00).
facts.sample_size: 5 RCTs, 140 patients with 140 implants (68 flapless, 72 flap)
facts.limitations: Scarce data prevented meta-analysis of secondary outcomes; three RCTs at high risk of bias.

facts.population: Eight beagle dogs, mandibular premolar sockets with thin buccal bone
facts.intervention: Flapless extraction with socket filled with deproteinized bovine bone mineral (MinerOss X), no membrane
facts.comparison: Sockets left with a blood clot only
outcomes: socket composition (bone, connective tissue, residual graft)
facts.main_result: Grafted sockets had a better buccal crest level (0.09 vs 0.51 mm apical to lingual), wider ridge (5.08 vs 3.88 mm) and more total bone (73.51% vs 45.84%) than blood clot sockets.
materials_brands: MinerOss X (BioHorizons) deproteinized bovine bone mineral
facts.funding_coi: CNPq and FAPESP funding; BioHorizons donated the graft material

facts.population: Three beagle dogs with surgically created dehiscence defects around implants
facts.intervention: Bilayer bone augmentation: autogenous particulated bone inner layer plus xenogenous bone outer layer
facts.comparison: Autograft alone, xenograft alone, and untreated control
facts.main_result: Mean bone volume was 11.08 mm3 (xenograft), 10.42 mm3 (BBA), 8.1 mm3 (control) and 7.01 mm3 (autograft) with no significant difference between the 4 groups.
facts.sample_size: 19 implants analysed in 3 dogs (24 sites planned)
facts.funding_coi: No financial conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Preliminary study; larger sample size required

facts.intervention: Bone grafting of the buccal gap at immediate implant placement, with membrane, flapless, socket shield and immediate dentoalveolar restoration options
facts.main_result: Grafting the buccal void preserves, at least in part, ridge dimensions after immediate implant placement, mainly in the anterior maxilla; no graft material is clearly superior and membranes do not seem to improve outcomes in intact sockets.
facts.limitations: Evidence for immediate dentoalveolar restoration is limited and needs controlled studies.

facts.population: Eight beagle dogs with surgically created semi-saddle peri-implant bone defects
facts.intervention: GBR with equine bone block + collagen membrane, bovine DBBM block + CM, or particulated DBBM + CM
facts.comparison: Empty control defects
outcomes: horizontal thickness of augmented region and mucosa
facts.main_result: All GBR groups gave larger augmented area than empty control (equine block 11.2, DBBM block 9.5, particulated DBBM 7.9 vs 2.4 mm2), with no significant differences between GBR groups.
materials_brands: Bio-Oss granules and Bio-Oss spongiosa block (Geistlich)
facts.funding_coi: University of Zurich clinic plus a research grant from Geistlich Pharma

facts.population: 18 patients needing single tooth replacement in compromised maxillary esthetic-zone sockets
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement with immediate dentoalveolar restoration (IDR) of facial bone defects using maxillary tuberosity graft
facts.main_result: Mean soft tissue dimension was 12.85 mm at baseline and 12.79 mm at final follow-up (no recession), and papillary heights increased slightly.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: 61 patients receiving immediate implants in fresh extraction sockets with intact buccal bone
facts.intervention: Static guided immediate implant placement with R2Gate teeth-supported surgical guides
facts.comparison: Freehand immediate implant placement
facts.main_result: Static guided surgery had lower crestal mesiodistal (0.34 vs 1.13 mm) and angular deviation (0.83 vs 6.09 degrees) than freehand; depth deviation did not differ (p=0.09).
facts.follow_up: Implant position scanned 6 weeks after placement
materials_brands: R2Gate surgical guides and Anyridge implants (Megagen)

facts.population: Patients receiving dental implants, studies reporting planned versus placed implant position
facts.intervention: Computer-aided implant surgery (pilot-drill, partially and fully guided static, and dynamic navigation)
facts.comparison: Freehand implant placement
facts.main_result: Mean angular, entry and apex deviations were 7.46 deg, 1.56 mm and 2.22 mm for freehand versus 2.57 deg, 0.72 mm and 0.88 mm for fully guided static CAIS.
facts.sample_size: 55 studies in the data extraction/meta-analysis (1609 initial articles)

facts.population: 18 patients needing posterior implant-supported single crowns
facts.intervention: Digitally static guided implant placement 1 mm subcrestal by a non-expert operator
facts.comparison: Freehand placement by a skilled operator
outcomes: marginal bone level change at 3 years
facts.main_result: The difference in marginal bone level change between guided and freehand groups was 0.11 mm at 3 years, not statistically significant (p=0.61).

facts.population: Patients in 10 RCTs receiving implants by static computer-aided, partially guided or free-handed placement
facts.intervention: Static computer-aided implant placement (sCAIP)
facts.comparison: Partially guided (PGIP) and free-handed (FHIP) implant placement
facts.main_result: sCAIP had lower angular (MD 4.41 deg), coronal (0.65 mm) and apical (1.13 mm) deviation than free-handed placement, and lower angular deviation than partially guided placement (MD 2.11 deg).
facts.sample_size: 10 RCTs (14 articles); 8 studies, 383 patients, 878 implants in the main accuracy comparison
facts.follow_up: Survival assessed up to 12 months post-loading

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.population: 41 patients undergoing extraction of all remaining teeth for full-arch fixed implant prostheses
facts.intervention: Implants placed immediately into fresh extraction sockets
facts.comparison: Implants placed in healed bone
facts.main_result: Success rate was 97.8% in both immediate and non-immediate groups, with no significant difference.
facts.sample_size: 512 implants in 41 patients (93 immediate, 419 in healed bone)
facts.limitations: Immediate-placement sample was significantly smaller than the healed-bone sample

facts.population: 13 patients (20 teeth with infection) scheduled for single-rooted tooth extraction
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement in infected fresh sockets with bone graft and membrane
facts.main_result: All 20 implants osseointegrated with no infection at 12 months; mean CAL 0.8 to 0.9 mm and DIB increased 0.5 mm.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Hypothesis must be verified by additional comparative trials

facts.population: 28 patients (33 immediate implants) with posterior compromised sockets
facts.intervention: Reactive soft tissue raised as pedicled primary wound closure over the implant
facts.comparison: Reactive soft tissue elevated but failed to cover the site
outcomes: buccal and lingual bone height and width (CBCT)
facts.main_result: 100% implant survival; buccal bone height loss 0.80 vs 1.78 mm (EG vs CG, P=.018) and keratinized mucosa recession 0.78 vs 1.65 mm (P=.021); MBL did not differ.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by National Natural Science Foundation of China and National Key R&D Program; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Small patient group; larger and longer studies needed

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.intervention: A three-type (A, B, C) classification of molar extraction sockets with treatment protocols for immediate implants
facts.main_result: Immediate implants can be placed predictably in molar sockets when primary stability is achievable within septal bone (types A, B) or by engaging the socket periphery (type C); otherwise a delayed protocol is used.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest

facts.population: 82 patients (42 males, 40 females) needing molar extraction, recruited in 8 centers
facts.intervention: Immediate transmucosal placement of tapered implants (4.8 mm, shoulder 6.5 mm) into molar sockets with GBR of marginal defects
outcomes: mesial and distal crestal bone level change
facts.main_result: All 82 implants healed uneventfully (100% survival) with healthy soft tissue at 12 months; crestal bone levels changed significantly from baseline (P<0.0001).

facts.population: 30 subjects: 15 with molar extraction sockets with buccal dehiscence (test) and 15 with healed molar sites (control)
facts.intervention: Immediate transmucosal tapered implants in molar sockets with buccal dehiscence, treated with GBR
facts.comparison: Implants in healed molar sites with intact buccal walls
facts.main_result: All 30 implants survived (100%); PPD and CAL were significantly higher at test sites than control sites (e.g. buccal PPD 3.7 vs 2.2 mm).

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 139 patients with implants in premolar/molar region adjacent to a tooth, loaded at least 3 years
facts.intervention: Vertical implant position more than 3 mm apical to the CEJ of the adjacent tooth
facts.comparison: Vertical position 3 mm or less from the CEJ
outcomes: peri-implant marginal bone loss (mesial and distal)
facts.main_result: Implants placed more than 3 mm apical to the adjacent CEJ had 0.57 mm (mesial) and 0.83 mm (distal) more peri-implant bone loss.
facts.funding_coi: Grant from the American Academy of Implant Dentistry Foundation; no financial interests declared

facts.population: 26 patients with single-tooth implants in the anterior maxilla (52 papillae)
facts.intervention: Modified uncovering technique designed to generate papilla-like formation
facts.comparison: Standard uncovering technique
outcomes: distance from contact point to bone crest
facts.main_result: Papilla present almost 100% of the time when contact point to bone crest was 5 mm or less, and 50% or less when 6 mm or more.
facts.follow_up: mean 35 months since crown insertion (6 to 75)
facts.limitations: Small sample prevented statistical analysis

facts.population: 40 patients with single-tooth implants in the anterior maxilla and a natural contralateral tooth
facts.intervention: Single-tooth implants in anterior maxilla, analysed for factors affecting mucosal and papilla level (observational)
facts.comparison: Natural contralateral tooth
facts.main_result: Thin biotype was the most significant factor for apical facial mucosal level; increased contact point to bone crest distance was the only factor associated with less papilla fill (half or more fill in 89%).
facts.follow_up: implants in function for at least 6 months
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the 90th Anniversary of Chulalongkorn University Fund
facts.limitations: Cross-sectional design; mucosal level referenced to contralateral tooth; factors analysed separately though inter-related

facts.population: 46 patients (46 teeth) scheduled for extraction in need of single-tooth replacement
facts.intervention: Immediate single implant placement into fresh sockets, restored with single crowns after 4 months
facts.main_result: 100% implant survival at 12 months; papilla significantly present when inter-implant-tooth distance was 3-4 mm (84.2% present) and contact point to bone distance 3-5 mm.

facts.population: Patients (10 or more per study) with a single implant-supported crown in the anterior maxilla, at least 12 months follow-up
facts.intervention: Single implant-supported crown; vertical distance from interproximal bone level to prosthetic contact point
outcomes: vertical distance from bone crest to contact point
facts.main_result: 12 papers included; bone-to-contact-point distance ranged 2 to 11 mm and partial or complete papilla fill ranged 56.5% to 100% of cases
facts.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation grant; authors declare no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Search limited to English-language articles and two databases; heterogeneous reference points prevented pooling of data

facts.population: 59 titanium implants in edentulous mandibular areas of 5 foxhounds
facts.intervention: Six implant types (A-F): 1-piece or 2-piece, non-submerged or submerged, with the rough/smooth border or the implant-abutment microgap at, above or below the bone crest
facts.comparison: Side-by-side comparison of the six implant types (non-submerged vs submerged, 1-piece vs 2-piece)
outcomes: distance from rough/smooth border and microgap to first bone-to-implant contact
facts.main_result: In 1-piece implants the first bone-to-implant contact lay within about 0.2 mm of the rough/smooth border; in 2-piece implants the microgap position determined crestal bone loss, greatest (2.25 mm) when it lay 1 mm below the crest (type F).
facts.follow_up: 6 months (abutment connection of submerged implants at 3 months)
materials_brands: Straumann grade IV commercially pure titanium implants, machined coronal part and SLA apical part
facts.funding_coi: ITI Foundation, Swiss Society of Periodontology, Swiss National Science Foundation and a Swiss stipend foundation; Straumann manufactured the implants

facts.population: 59 titanium implants placed at different levels to the alveolar crest in 5 foxhounds
facts.intervention: Six types of unloaded titanium implants (1-part or 2-part, nonsubmerged or submerged, microgap and rough/smooth interface at different levels) followed with standardized radiographs
facts.comparison: Side-by-side comparison of the implant types
outcomes: distance from implant/abutment top to most coronal bone-to-implant contact (DIB)
facts.main_result: In 2-part implants the most coronal bone-to-implant contact lay about 2 mm below the microgap whether non-submerged or submerged; in 1-part implants it followed the rough/smooth interface; changes occurred within the first month.
materials_brands: Straumann grade IV commercially pure titanium implants with SLA surface
facts.funding_coi: ITI Foundation, Swiss Society of Periodontology, Swiss National Science Foundation and a Swiss stipend foundation

facts.population: Patients with at least two adjacent implant-supported crowns in the anterior maxilla (4 studies, 114 patients)
facts.intervention: Multiple adjacent implant-supported crowns in the anterior maxilla
facts.comparison: Radiographic horizontal distance between the outer surfaces of the two adjacent implants
facts.main_result: No precise threshold for the optimal horizontal distance between adjacent implants could be defined; incomplete inter-implant mucosa fill tended to occur at distances under 3 mm in 3 of 4 studies (one significant, p = .008).
facts.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation grant supported the consensus meeting
facts.limitations: Few studies fulfilled the inclusion criteria and heterogeneity prevented meta-analysis

facts.population: 30 partially edentulous patients receiving two adjacent implant-supported crowns (60 implants)
