facts.intervention: Two adjacent implants placed at a horizontal interimplant distance of about 2 mm, 3 mm or over 4 mm, restored with single crowns after 3 months
facts.comparison: 2-mm vs 3-mm vs over 4-mm interimplant distance groups
outcomes: probing depth, bleeding on probing, plaque
facts.main_result: No statistically significant differences in marginal and midproximal bone crest loss between the 2-mm, 3-mm and over 4-mm groups at any time point (marginal bone loss at 24 months 0.27, 0.23 and 0.44 mm).

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 41 pairs of platform-switched implants placed less than 3 mm apart in 37 patients
facts.intervention: Platform-switched implants placed less than 3 mm apart, evaluated radiographically
outcomes: height of the interimplant bone peak relative to the line connecting implant-abutment interfaces
facts.main_result: Mean vertical bone resorption was 0.62 mm and horizontal 0.60 mm; the interimplant bone peak stayed on average 0.24 mm above the line connecting the two implant-abutment interfaces (preserved in 64% of pairs).

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.intervention: Four-dimensional (timing) concept and classification of extraction sites for immediate implant placement in the esthetic region
facts.main_result: Timing of extraction and implant placement is added as a fourth dimension to 3D implant positioning, with a four-class site classification guiding when immediate placement is indicated.

facts.population: 93 adults needing a maxillary tooth (15-25) replaced by an immediate implant
facts.intervention: Immediate placement of OsseoSpeed implants in fresh extraction sockets, without additional grafting
facts.comparison: Cylindrical (3.5/4.0 mm) vs conical/cylindrical (4.5/5.0 mm) implant configuration
facts.main_result: After 3 years the mean gingival zenith change was 0.23 mm (not significant) and 79% mesial and 72% distal papillae were more than half-filled or complete, independent of implant configuration, tooth category, smoking and buccal wall thickness.

facts.population: 40 subjects with a hopeless maxillary anterior or premolar tooth
facts.intervention: Immediate single implant placement with immediate provisionalization (non-occluding temporary crown)
facts.comparison: Immediate placement with a healing abutment (no immediate provisionalization)
facts.main_result: At 12 months mucosal level, papilla height and marginal bone changes did not differ significantly between groups; implant survival was 90% (test) vs 100% (control); immediate provisionalization did not improve the esthetic outcome.
facts.follow_up: 12 months after permanent restoration (placed at 4 months)
facts.funding_coi: University of Michigan Graduate Student Research Grant and a Neobiotech gift (implants provided); one author received speaking honoraria from Neobiotech
facts.limitations: Two test implants failed early, possibly leaving the marginal bone analysis underpowered

facts.population: 40 patients with a failing tooth in the maxillary anterior region
facts.intervention: Immediate single implant placement (NobelActive) with immediate provisionalization (group A)
facts.comparison: Immediate implant placement with delayed provisionalization (group B)
facts.main_result: After 5 years mean marginal bone level change was about 0.71 mm (group A) vs 0.49-0.54 mm (group B), not significantly different; implant and restoration survival was 100%.
facts.sample_size: 40 patients (20 per group); 35 analysed at 5 years
facts.funding_coi: Unrestricted grant from Nobel Biocare Services AG; implant materials provided
facts.limitations: Fewer patients analysed at 5 years (35 of 40) reduced power; university setting with selected patients

facts.population: 70 patients with a failed maxillary anterior tooth
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement with immediate provisionalization (screw-retained provisional crown)
facts.comparison: Immediate implant placement without provisionalization (healing abutment)
facts.main_result: Marginal bone loss did not differ significantly between groups and survival was 100%; Group A had significantly higher ISQ at 3, 6, 9 and 12 months.

facts.population: Participants with a failing tooth in the maxillary aesthetic zone needing a single implant restoration
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement with immediate provisionalization (IP), grafted gap, NobelActive TiUnite implant
facts.comparison: Immediate implant placement with delayed provisionalization (DP) after free gingival graft closure
facts.main_result: After 10 years mean mesial/distal marginal bone level change was 0.47/0.49 mm with IP and 0.58/0.41 mm with DP, with no significant difference (p = .61; p = .71)
facts.funding_coi: Nobel Biocare provided implant materials/grant; authors declare no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: University setting with experienced clinicians; unequal buccal defect distribution between groups and different wound closure methods in the two groups

facts.population: 49 patients with a single failing tooth in the anterior maxilla
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement with instant connection of a provisional crown (immediate restoration)
facts.comparison: Submerged healing with a removable partial denture, provisional crown after 3 months (delayed restoration)
facts.main_result: Delayed restoration caused initial papilla loss and midfacial recession 2.5-3 times higher (about 0.75 mm additional loss) than immediate restoration at 1 year

facts.population: Adult patients receiving single immediate implants (323 patients in 7 RCTs)
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement with immediate provisionalization (IIP + IP)
facts.comparison: Immediate implant placement without immediate provisionalization
facts.main_result: In intact alveoli, IIP + IP gave 0.87 mm (95% CI 0.57; 1.17) less apical migration of the midfacial soft tissue than IIP alone; survival, papillae, bone level, probing depth and BOP were unaffected
facts.sample_size: 7 RCTs, 323 patients with 323 single immediate implants
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts declared; senior author has collaboration agreement with Nobel Biocare and Straumann
facts.limitations: Risk of bias raised some concerns in five RCTs and high risk in two; GRADE strength of conclusion rated low; insufficient data for horizontal changes and PES

facts.intervention: Tooth extraction without flap, 3-D implant placement, contour augmentation with connective tissue graft and heterologous bone chips, with provisionalization

facts.population: 7 patients (mean age 59) with 11 Straumann SLA implants placed in soft bone without primary stability
facts.intervention: Straumann tissue-level SLA implants placed with insertion torque below 10 N/cm and slight mobility, left to heal 4-6 months
facts.main_result: All 11 implants lacking primary stability osseointegrated, were restored, and remained functional at a mean of 28.5 months after restoration
facts.funding_coi: Authors claim no financial interest
facts.limitations: Small number of implants prevented statistical analysis; short period since restoration

facts.population: Patients with single dental implant restorations in eight included studies
facts.intervention: Screw-retained single implant restorations
facts.comparison: Cemented single implant restorations
facts.main_result: BOP and MBL did not differ significantly between cemented and screw-retained implants (p = 0.8093 and 0.5813)
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest

facts.population: Adults needing implants to replace teeth to be extracted in the maxilla, region 15-25
facts.intervention: Immediate placement into the extraction socket of a cylindrical implant (group A)
facts.comparison: Immediate placement of a tapered implant (group B)
outcomes: buccal and palatal crest dimension change
facts.main_result: Over 16 weeks the buccal ridge dimension fell 43% (cylindrical) and 30% (tapered) and the horizontal gap closed 80% and 63%; differences between implant shapes were not significant
facts.sample_size: 93 implant sites in 93 subjects (45 cylindrical, 48 tapered)

facts.population: 93 subjects with single maxillary teeth (15-25) extracted and replaced by immediate implants
facts.intervention: Immediate single-tooth implant placement, sites stratified by location, cause of extraction, buccal wall thickness and horizontal gap size
facts.main_result: Implant location, buccal bone thickness and horizontal gap size significantly influenced hard tissue change over 4 months; premolar sites showed more gap fill and less vertical crest reduction than incisor-canine sites
facts.limitations: Some stratified samples were too small, and no adjustment for multiple tests was applied

facts.population: Eighteen female beagle dogs with surgically created non-contained mandibular buccal bone defects
facts.intervention: Augmentation of healed defects with DBBM-collagen graft alone (T1), collagen membrane alone (T2) or both (T3)
facts.comparison: The three augmentation modalities compared with each other
facts.main_result: Mineralized tissue proportion was significantly larger with membrane alone (T2) than with graft alone or combined; with larger defects the graft-containing groups gave a larger total ROI
materials_brands: Bio-Gide native bilayer collagen membrane, Geistlich
facts.funding_coi: Partially supported by a research contract with Geistlich Pharma AG

facts.population: Eight Labrador dogs; distal alveoli of fourth mandibular premolars after hemisection
facts.intervention: Implants placed immediately into extraction sockets, tilted toward the buccal wall (B-sites) or lingual wall (L-sites)
facts.comparison: Buccal versus lingual implant position within the same animal (split-mouth)
facts.main_result: Buccal vertical resorption was 1.6 mm at B-sites versus 0.4 mm at L-sites, and lingually placed implants were about 1 mm deeper; BIC was similar (31.2-35.2%).
materials_brands: Alvim CM implants (Neodent), sandblasted and acid-etched, 11.5 x 3.5 mm
facts.funding_coi: Grant from Ariminum Research and Dental Education Center; implants provided by Neodent

facts.population: 21 patients receiving single-tooth implant replacement in maxillary sites distal to the canine (27 implants, 23 biopsies)
facts.intervention: Experimental abutment connected at implant placement, with soft tissue biopsies after 2, 4, 8 or 12 weeks of healing for histological and ESEM analysis
facts.comparison: Different healing times (2, 4, 8, 12 weeks)
facts.main_result: At 8 weeks the soft tissue was about 3.6 mm (barrier epithelium 1.9 mm, connective tissue 1.7 mm), similar at 12 weeks; differences across healing times were not significant.

facts.population: 36 non-grafted immediate implant sites in the esthetic zone (maxillary second bicuspid to second bicuspid) from an RCT
facts.intervention: Immediate single implant placement with immediate screw-retained provisional crown, with or without flap elevation; no bone graft
facts.main_result: Gingival phenotype was the only parameter associated with both buccal gingival recession and buccal ridge dimensional reduction; mean mid-buccal recession was 0.32 mm at 12 months.
facts.sample_size: 36 implants with radiographs, 34 with gingival and ridge measurements, of 39 placed
materials_brands: Super T Temporary Crown & Bridge Material (AMCO)
facts.funding_coi: Implants and provisional abutments provided free by Biomet 3i; no conflict of interest declared

facts.population: 97 patients (60 females, 37 males; mean age 51) with a single implant in the anterior maxilla placed in 2006-2007
facts.intervention: Single implant in the anterior maxilla via flap surgery with or without ridge re-contouring (GBR or onlay block grafting)
facts.comparison: Surgery with versus without ridge re-contouring
facts.main_result: Ridge re-contouring (OR 3.4) and pre-operative tooth bone level (OR 2.1) predicted mesial papilla recession; a buccal shoulder position predicted midfacial recession (OR 17.2).
facts.follow_up: On average two and a half years of function (restorations 31 months in function)
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest; supported by the Department of Dentistry of the Free University of Brussels (VUB)

facts.population: 86 subjects, one immediate implant each in the anterior maxilla (15-25)
facts.intervention: Grafting the gap between implant and socket walls with demineralized bovine bone mineral with 10% collagen (Bio-Oss Collagen)
facts.comparison: Immediate implants with the gap left ungrafted
facts.main_result: Buccal horizontal crest reduction was 1.1 mm (29%) with DBBM-C versus 1.6 mm (38%) without graft (P = 0.02).

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 113 patients needing single anterior maxillary implants: 55 in fresh sockets, 58 in healed ridges
facts.intervention: Immediate provisionalization of single OsseoSpeed implants in extraction sockets
facts.comparison: Implants placed in healed ridges
facts.main_result: Survival was 94.6% in sockets and 98.3% in healed ridges (not significant), with mean crestal bone levels of 0.43 and 0.38 mm at 5 years.
facts.sample_size: 113 patients (55 sockets, 58 healed ridges); 45 and 49 remained at 5 years
materials_brands: Bio-Gide/Bio-Mend collagen membrane (Osteohealth) for grafted sites

facts.population: 38 subjects needing a single extraction (premolar to premolar), 32 completing 3-month follow-up
facts.intervention: Immediate (Type 1) implant placement
facts.comparison: Early (Type 2) implant placement
outcomes: probing pocket depth, modified plaque index, modified sulcus bleeding index
facts.main_result: No significant differences at 3 months after crown delivery: 100% survival, mid-facial soft tissue loss about 0.5 mm in both groups, PES/WES 13.7 vs 12.5.
facts.sample_size: 32 patients completed follow-up (Type 1 n = 17, Type 2 n = 15)
facts.funding_coi: Other authors report no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Preliminary short-term results that need long-term confirmation

facts.population: 50 periodontally healthy non-smoking patients with a failing anterior maxillary tooth (15-25) and high aesthetic risk (42 without, 8 with mid-facial recession)
facts.intervention: Flapless extraction with ridge preservation (collagen-enriched bovine xenograft), flapless NobelActive implant, screw-retained provisional, connective tissue graft and permanent crown (M.I.S.I.T.)
facts.main_result: At 12 months all implants survived, papillary recession was at most 0.3 mm, mid-facial recession 0.1 mm in the non-recession group, and PES/WES were 10.9/14 and 8.2/10.
facts.funding_coi: Biomaterials supplied by Geistlich Pharma and components by Nobel Biocare; Cosyn has a collaboration agreement with Nobel Biocare, De Bruyn with Dentsply Implants and Southern Implants
facts.limitations: Short-term prospective study offering a proof of principle

facts.population: 30 patients with 30 immediate transmucosal implants in maxillary anterior extraction sites
facts.intervention: Grafting the marginal defect with Bio-Oss, alone or with a resorbable collagen membrane, at non-submerged immediate implants
facts.comparison: No graft (control)
outcomes: vertical defect height and horizontal defect depth reduction
facts.main_result: Horizontal buccal bone resorption was 48.3% in controls versus 15.8% (BG) and 20% (BG+M); 33.3% of sites showed mucosal recession.
facts.sample_size: 30 implants in 30 patients (10 per group); 19 patients followed long term
facts.follow_up: 3-4 years after restoration (mean 4.0 years in 19 patients)
materials_brands: ITI Implant System, sand-blasted and acid-etched (Straumann)

facts.population: Animal and human studies of implants placed immediately into sites with periapical, endodontic, perioendodontic or periodontal infection
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement into infected extraction sockets after site decontamination
facts.main_result: High implant survival in several studies supports successful osseointegration after immediate placement into sites with endodontic and periodontal lesions when appropriate site decontamination is performed.
facts.sample_size: 21 human case series and 7 animal studies (from 706 references, plus 5 hand-searched)
facts.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq (Brazil); no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: More RCTs with longer follow-up are needed; infection classification was vague and varied among studies

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.population: 270 patients needing an implant-supported partial fixed prosthesis or single crown
facts.intervention: Two-piece platform-switched Morse taper implants (Osseothread, ImplaDent) placed in a two-stage submerged protocol
outcomes: crestal bone level change at 60 months
influence of biological, anatomical and implant-related variables
facts.main_result: At 60 months mean marginal bone remodelling was -0.59 ± 1.34 mm; bone loss was significantly higher with subcrestal and anterior implants.
materials_brands: Osseothread implants (ImplaDent), SLA surface, Morse taper connection
Ketac Cem glass ionomer cement (3M Espe)
facts.funding_coi: No funds for the research

facts.population: 12 male Hound Labrador mongrel dogs with surgically created critical-size supraalveolar peri-implant defects in the mandibular premolar region
facts.intervention: Three 10-mm titanium implants per jaw quadrant placed 5 mm into premolar extraction sites, leaving 5 mm supraalveolar, flaps advanced for primary closure, 8 weeks healing
outcomes: buccal bone resorption (incandescent vs fluorescent microscopy)
facts.main_result: Buccal bone resorption was significantly greater when the buccal ridge width was under 2 mm; the association with ridge width was about twice as strong below 2 mm (beta 1.62 vs 0.80) and fluorescence microscopy showed more resorption than incandescent light.
facts.sample_size: 12 dogs, three implants in one jaw quadrant each
materials_brands: TiUnite porous oxide titanium implants (Nobel Biocare)
facts.funding_coi: Co-author Jan Hall works in Research & Development at Nobel Biocare AB; no funding statement in extracted text

facts.population: Animal and human studies of implants placed immediately into infected extraction sites (periapical or periodontal infection)
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement into infected sites after debridement, usually with antibiotics and GBR
facts.comparison: Pristine or non-infected sites
facts.main_result: Implants can be placed into infected sites with survival similar to non-infected sites, though animal data suggest bone-to-implant contact may be impaired.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Evidence limited to few studies and patients; infection classification vague.

facts.population: Patients treated with implant-supported full-arch fixed prostheses at one specialist clinic (1980-2018)
facts.intervention: Implant-supported full-arch fixed dental prostheses
facts.main_result: Cumulative prosthesis survival was 93.3% at 10 years and 87.1% at 20 years; bruxism raised risk of failure (HR 3.276) and technical complications.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Folktandvården Skåne AB; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Retrospective design with incomplete records; non-standardized treatment and bruxism diagnosis by self-report.

facts.intervention: ACP classification system (Class I-IV) for diagnosis of the completely dentate patient
facts.main_result: The ACP defines four classes of completely dentate patients, from uncomplicated (Class I) to most complex (Class IV), using diagnostic criteria for tooth condition and occlusal scheme.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the American College of Prosthodontists

facts.population: Patients with at least one edentulous jaw, tooth loss mainly due to periodontitis
facts.intervention: Fixed or removable full-arch implant-supported prostheses
facts.comparison: Fixed versus removable full-arch designs
facts.main_result: Cumulative implant loss at 5 years was 1.85% for fixed versus 4.45% for removable prostheses; 1-year loss was similar (0.64% vs 0.71%).
facts.follow_up: At least 12 months; analysis up to 5 years
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Limited low-quality data; no assessment beyond 5 years.

facts.population: Adults with an edentulous mandible undergoing implant treatment
facts.intervention: Three implants supporting a fixed mandibular prosthesis
facts.comparison: Mandibular fixed complete prosthesis with more than three implants
facts.main_result: Mean cumulative implant survival was 96.2% over 3.35 years, with mean marginal bone loss of 1.25 mm and high patient satisfaction.
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no competing interests
facts.limitations: Longer-term comparative data lacking.

facts.journal: Platelet Rich Fibrin in Regenerative Dentistry: Biological Background and Clinical Indications
facts.population: Patients with complete edentulism treated with full arch immediate implants
facts.intervention: Full-arch immediate implant placement and loading with PRF and i-PRF (Simonpieri technique)
facts.main_result: Author reports over 98% success in full-arch immediate loading with PRF over 14 years.
facts.key_finding: The author describes a full-arch immediate implant and immediate loading protocol using PRF and injectable PRF to support wound healing and graft stability, reporting over 98% success across more than 1100 cases.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Combining tension-free closure, palatal implant placement, PRF/i-PRF and a rigid screwed provisional may support long-term tissue stability in full-arch immediate loading, based on the author's own case experience.

facts.population: Critical-sized dehiscence defects in mandibular canines of dogs
facts.intervention: β-TCP alloplast with modified perforated collagen membrane
facts.comparison: β-TCP alloplast with occlusive collagen membrane
facts.main_result: Both groups regenerated periodontal tissues, but the perforated membrane gave higher bone surface area (70.9% vs 44.5% at 1 month; 82.5% vs 73.2% at 2 months).
facts.limitations: Small sample; further larger studies needed.
materials_brands: BioTECK equine type I collagen membrane

facts.population: Mouse ST2 bone marrow stromal cells (osteoblast lineage) in culture
facts.intervention: DBBM particles pre-coated with bone-conditioned medium (BCM)
facts.comparison: DBBM particles alone
facts.main_result: BCM coating increased cell adhesion 2-fold, raised COL1A2, ALP and OCN mRNA, and gave 3-fold more alizarin red staining.
facts.funding_coi: DBBM supplied by Geistlich AG; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: In vitro only; animal study needed.

facts.population: Patients receiving posterior implants with small non-contained buccal bone dehiscences (≤5 mm)
facts.intervention: Spontaneous healing of the dehiscence
facts.comparison: Guided bone regeneration (DBBM + collagen membrane)
facts.main_result: Survival was 100% in both groups at 7.5 years; remaining buccal dehiscence was larger with spontaneous healing (2.51 mm) than GBR (1.66 mm, p=0.02), with no difference in marginal bone levels.
facts.sample_size: 22 patients with 28 implants; 20 patients with 26 implants recalled
facts.funding_coi: Implant material from Oral Reconstruction Foundation grant; three authors report grants and fees from Geistlich Pharma outside the work
facts.limitations: No power calculation possible due to lack of data
materials_brands: Deproteinized bovine bone mineral with collagen membrane (GBR group)

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.population: Experimental (mostly animal) studies of bone regeneration with cortical perforations in the recipient area
facts.intervention: Cortical perforations combined with GBR, autologous bone blocks or periosteal distraction
facts.main_result: Evidence that cortical perforations increase bone formation in GBR and with bone blocks is limited; number and size of perforations did not appear to matter.
facts.funding_coi: No funding source declared
facts.limitations: Moderate to high risk of bias; studies not comparable.

facts.population: Murine bone marrow cell cultures exposed to conditioned medium from porcine fresh cortical bone and demineralized bone matrix
facts.intervention: Conditioned medium from fresh bone (BCM, also heated to 85°C) and from demineralized bone matrix (DCM) added to RANKL and M-CSF induced osteoclastogenesis
facts.comparison: Cultures with RANKL and M-CSF alone, and unheated BCM
outcomes: osteoclast marker and fusion gene expression
facts.main_result: Unheated BCM did not change osteoclastogenesis, heated BCM approximately doubled TRAP-positive multinucleated cells, and DCM significantly stimulated osteoclastogenesis irrespective of heating.
facts.sample_size: Experiments repeated at least four times in duplicate
materials_brands: Porcine cortical bone chips (BCM) and demineralized bone matrix (DCM)
facts.limitations: Most but not all preparations of heated BCM supported osteoclastogenesis, and the resorption assay was not quantified because of large variation.

facts.population: Patients with a single tooth gap in the anterior maxilla and a horizontal alveolar defect, bucco-palatal bone at least 6 mm
facts.intervention: Single implant with CTG in a buccal envelope to re-establish buccal convexity (test)
facts.comparison: Single implant with GBR using DBBM (Bio-Oss) and a collagen membrane (control)
facts.main_result: PES did not differ (10.11 GBR vs 10.48 CTG, p=0.577) but MSI was lower with CTG (1.10 vs 2.53, p=0.017); GBR had more oedema, hematoma and painkillers (7.10 vs 4.86).
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared; implants and prosthetic components supplied free by Nobel Biocare; Prof. Cosyn has agreements with Nobel Biocare and Straumann.

facts.population: Patients with severe vertical alveolar atrophy and missing teeth needing vertical bone augmentation for implants
facts.intervention: Self-inflating hydrogel tissue expander (TissueMax) placed subperiosteally for ~4 weeks, then tunneling vertical bone graft without full flap reflection
facts.comparison: Conventional vertical GBR with full flap and periosteal releasing incisions
outcomes: radiographic vertical bone gain and retention
facts.main_result: Vertical bone gain was higher with the expander (5.12 vs 4.22 mm, P<0.05) and 6-month vertical bone reduction was smaller (30.7% vs 55.0%); mean soft tissue gain was 6.88 mm vertically.
facts.follow_up: 6-month retention after grafting, then mean 10.2 months of prosthetic loading
materials_brands: Cytoplast RTM collagen membrane (Osteogenics) and OssMem (Osstem)
Cytoplast Ti-250XL d-PTFE titanium reinforced membrane
Straumann bone level SLActive and Osstem TS III SA implants
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared; supported by a Korea Health Technology R&D Project grant (Ministry of Health & Welfare); some authors affiliated with Osstem Bio R&D Center.
facts.limitations: Studies comparing the two techniques without tissue expanders are needed to elucidate the net effect of tissue expansion.

facts.population: In vitro: bone chips from fresh pig mandibles and human mesenchymal cells (oral fibroblasts)
facts.intervention: Preparation of bone-conditioned medium from native, pasteurized, autoclaved or demineralized pig bone and a bioassay on TGF-b regulated gene expression
facts.comparison: Un-stimulated controls and medium from autoclaved (121 °C) bone
outcomes: expression of ADM, PTX3, IL11, IL33, NOX4 and PRG4 in oral fibroblasts
facts.main_result: BCM from fresh, pasteurized or demineralized bone changed target gene expression (ADM and PTX3 down to 0.4-fold, IL11, IL33, NOX4, PRG4 up to 200-fold), whereas medium from autoclaved bone did not.
facts.funding_coi: Authors have nothing to disclose; one author received a scholarship from the Foundation of Dental Research and Education, Basel.
facts.limitations: BCM cannot be fully standardized because of variations between donors and harvesting techniques.

facts.population: Four young adult mongrel dogs, membranes placed subperiosteally in the maxilla
facts.intervention: Subperiosteal placement of three membranes: bovine collagen (GenDerm), collagen (Genoss, Dentium) and porcine dermis (Kytinon M.O.R.)
facts.comparison: The three membranes compared with each other, and with normal gingival tissue samples
facts.main_result: Absorption was <35% at 15 days for all membranes; at 90 days GenDerm bovine collagen was completely absorbed, Dentium collagen >65% and porcine dermis only 35-65%.
facts.funding_coi: Self-supported; authors declare no conflicts of interest.

facts.population: 40 clinical studies of lateral ridge augmentation (simultaneous, staged or ridge expansion) pooling 1,242 patients and 1,881 implants
facts.intervention: Lateral bone augmentation (GBR with particulate grafts and membranes, or autogenous bone blocks) staged or simultaneous with implant placement
facts.comparison: Comparisons between grafting materials and membrane types (RCTs/CCTs); otherwise baseline vs final
facts.main_result: Simultaneous approach gave a significant defect height reduction (WMD -4.28 mm) and staged approach a bone width gain (WMD 3.90 mm); implant survival and success were high (>95%).
facts.funding_coi: No financial support; no conflicts of interest declared.
facts.limitations: Case series did not meet the quality categories and well-designed long-term RCTs are lacking.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.main_result: Buccal bone augmentation of more than 2 mm beyond the implant platform and vertical augmentation to a line joining adjacent interproximal bone peaks are needed for stable esthetic soft tissue around multiple implants; strategic pontics help preserve papilla height.
facts.follow_up: 2-year periapical radiograph of the illustrated case
facts.limitations: Very few long-term studies exist on compromised cases with multiple implants.

facts.main_result: Osteoinduction, osteoconduction and osseointegration are interrelated but distinct; osteoinduction produces most new bone in healing, while osseointegration is stable direct bone anchorage of an implant maintained over time.

Collagen membranes show advantageous biological and clinical features versus non-resorbable and other resorbable membranes but need graft support and fixation, and cross-linked types have higher exposure rates.
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest declared.

facts.population: One 43-year-old woman with a hopeless maxillary left central incisor (palatal root fracture) and a thin periodontal phenotype
facts.intervention: Surgical veneer grafting: flapless extraction, immediate implant (Tapered Screw-Vent) with dual-zone allograft packed to the gingival margin, partial-thickness epithelial connective tissue graft, screw-retained provisional
facts.main_result: At 24 months CBCT showed optimal amount and stability of peri-implant marginal bone and the facial ridge contour was stable at 18 months (single case, no measurements).
facts.funding_coi: Authors reported no disclosures
facts.limitations: Long-term clinical data for this technique are not yet available and it is technique-sensitive

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 10 patients with severe horizontal alveolar ridge atrophy (under 3 mm), mean age 46.6 years
facts.intervention: Staged horizontal augmentation with mandibular (external oblique ridge) bone laminae plus particulated autograft, then at implant placement relining with anorganic bovine bone mineral (Bio-Oss) and a collagen membrane
outcomes: horizontal ridge width before and after augmentation
facts.main_result: Ridge width rose from 2.1 to 6.9 mm after grafting, remodeling over 4 months was 0.25 mm (6.6 mm), and after ABBM/membrane relining the width was 7.7 mm at abutment connection.
facts.follow_up: 8 months (4 months to implant placement, 4 more to abutment connection)
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Short-term data; long-term outcomes are needed to confirm the volume-maintenance effect

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 12 fresh human cadaver heads with bilateral posterior mandibular edentulism (11 analyzed)
facts.intervention: Novel lingual flap advancement preserving the mylohyoid muscle attachment (retromolar pad lifting, blunt separation, semiblunt periosteal release)
facts.comparison: Classic lingual flap release technique detaching the mylohyoid muscle
outcomes: vertical lingual flap release in zones I, II and III (mm)
facts.main_result: The preserving technique gave 8.273, 10.09 and 10.273 mm more vertical flap release than the classic technique in zones I, II and III (P < .0001).
facts.sample_size: 11 heads, 22 surgical sites analyzed (one specimen excluded)
facts.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation grant; no financial interests declared
facts.limitations: Examiners were not blinded to the technique and ridge anatomy was not perfectly symmetric between sides

facts.population: Four adult male foxhound dogs with surgically created mandibular premolar-region bone defects (about 8 x 12 x 10 mm)
facts.intervention: Defects covered with a standard e-PTFE membrane or a prototype reinforced e-PTFE membrane, fixed with screws, sacrificed at 2 and 4 months
facts.comparison: Nonmembrane control defect
outcomes: histomorphometry of regenerate (cortical layer vs spongiosa)
facts.main_result: Membrane sites healed significantly better than controls, but regeneration was incomplete at 4 months; the cortical layer made up 38% of the regenerate at 4 months vs under 1% at 2 months and reinforced membranes kept their form while standard ones partially collapsed.
materials_brands: GoreTex Augmentation Material e-PTFE membrane (W.L. Gore)
Reinforced prototype e-PTFE membrane (r-GTAM, W.L. Gore)
facts.funding_coi: Grants from W.L. Gore and Associates and the Swiss AO/ASIF Foundation

facts.population: 25 patients needing sinus augmentation (21 treated, 24 sinuses, 20 sinuses analyzed)
facts.intervention: Lateral window sinus augmentation with particulated allograft, with CBCT-measured bucco-palatal distance at 8, 10 and 12 mm and bone core biopsy at about 6 months
facts.main_result: Mean vital bone was 22.71 +/- 19.08% and was inversely related to bucco-palatal distance (r = -0.376, P < 0.001); 96% graft success.
facts.sample_size: 25 recruited; 21 patients, 24 sinuses grafted; 20 sinuses analyzed
facts.funding_coi: Partly supported by BioHorizons and ICOI foundation; several authors report research support or fees from BioHorizons, Zimmer, OraPharma, Straumann
facts.limitations: Limited sample size per category prevented establishing a BPD cutoff

facts.population: 24 patients (28 sites) with horizontally deficient maxillary ridges (residual width under 5 mm)
facts.intervention: Two-stage horizontal augmentation with autogenous ramus block graft (RBG), 13 sites, covered with deproteinized bovine bone and collagen membrane
facts.comparison: Guided bone regeneration (GBR), 15 sites, with autogenous particles plus DBB and a tacked resorbable collagen membrane
facts.main_result: Mean volume reduction was 12.48 +/- 2.67% with GBR vs 7.20 +/- 1.40% with RBG (P < 0.001); horizontal gain was greater with GBR; insertion torque was similar.
facts.funding_coi: No relevant financial relationships declared

facts.population: 48 randomized patients with atrophic alveolar ridges (width 4 mm or less) needing 3D augmentation before implants
facts.intervention: Expanded autologous iliac crest-derived mesenchymal cells seeded on a synthetic biphasic calcium phosphate substitute (MBCP) covered with a titanium-reinforced non-resorbable membrane
facts.comparison: Autogenous bone block graft
outcomes: bone volume change by CBCT at 5 months
facts.main_result: The cell therapy group gained more bone volume, mean difference 480.01 mm3 (p = 0.032), with change from baseline of 1066.91 vs 586.9 mm3; all implants integrated in both groups.
facts.sample_size: 48 randomized (36 test, 12 control); 7 test patients could not be treated for insufficient expanded MSCs
facts.follow_up: 5 months to CBCT and implant placement
materials_brands: MBCP biphasic calcium phosphate granules (Biomatlante), HA/beta-TCP 20/80
facts.funding_coi: EU H2020 Maxibone project; authors declare no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Phase 2 trial was underpowered and baseline augmentation volume may have been higher in the test group

facts.population: Human gingival fibroblasts from two donors seeded onto collagen membranes pre-soaked in porcine bone-conditioned medium
facts.intervention: Collagen membranes incubated with bone-conditioned medium from fresh or demineralized bone chips
facts.comparison: Recombinant human TGF-b1 as control
outcomes: expression of adrenomedullin, pentraxin 3, interleukin 11, proteoglycan 4
facts.main_result: Membranes incubated with BCM for at least one minute made fibroblasts decrease ADM and PTX3 and increase IL-11 and PRG4 expression, showing rapid adsorption of TGF-beta activity, with viability and morphology unchanged.
facts.sample_size: Fibroblasts from two donors; two independent BCM preparations

facts.population: Partially dentate patients with horizontal alveolar ridge defects
facts.intervention: Prosthetically guided horizontal bone augmentation protocol (diagnosis, defect classification, augmentation techniques)
facts.main_result: Review concludes that prosthetically guided regeneration allows reconstruction of lost alveolar and soft-tissue contours and implant placement in positions permitting optimal functional and esthetic restorations.

facts.population: Full or partially edentulous patients with vertical alveolar defects needing augmentation for implant rehabilitation
facts.intervention: Vertical augmentation by onlay bone grafting or guided bone regeneration
outcomes: description of initial defect features (site, edentulism type, dimensions)
facts.main_result: 40 studies (528 vertical cases) met inclusion; defect features were inconsistently reported, so a classification by number of bony walls and base width was proposed
facts.limitations: Information on the initial vertical defect characteristics was not comprehensively reported in most included studies

facts.population: Patients with implants in the anterior maxilla (canine to canine) after buccal bone augmentation
facts.intervention: Buccal augmentation by guided bone regeneration, autogenous block grafting, or both, followed by implant placement
facts.comparison: Three augmentation protocols compared descriptively and in a mixed model
outcomes: esthetic parameters (Pink Esthetic Score, Papilla Presence Index)
facts.main_result: Baseline buccal bone volume correlated strongly negatively with volume change (r = -.80); baseline volume above 105 mm3 predicted volume loss with 100% specificity and 96% sensitivity
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Small sample size, underpowered for intergroup comparison, and augmented volume not standardized because of the retrospective design

facts.population: Eleven patients with at least two lateral bone defects, eight re-examined
facts.intervention: Implants placed with GBR using a xenogenic bone substitute loaded with rhBMP-2 (test) under a collagen membrane
facts.comparison: Same GBR without rhBMP-2 (control, split-mouth)
facts.main_result: Implant survival was 100% after at least 17 years; marginal bone levels did not differ significantly between rhBMP-2 test and control sites
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared; funding not stated
facts.limitations: Small sample of eight patients and a 27% drop-out rate

facts.population: 21 patients with three-dimensional bone defects reconstructed with patient-specific titanium meshes at least 5 years earlier
facts.intervention: Customized bone regeneration with patient-specific titanium mesh and 1:1 autogenous bone and xenograft
facts.comparison: Flap designs compared: crestal incision, crestal incision with vertical release, poncho flap
facts.main_result: Crestal incision without vertical release gave significantly better esthetics and mesial/distal bone levels than poncho flaps or crestal incision with release; mean PES 11.09
facts.funding_coi: No specific funding
facts.limitations: Pink Esthetic Score is a subjective measurement tool

facts.population: Sixty-three lithium disilicate (IPS e.max Press) blocks luted to dentin of extracted human third molars
