facts.comparison: HF concentrations and the two resin cement matrices against each other
outcomes: microtensile bond strength at 24 h and 6 months
facts.main_result: 10% HF gave higher and more stable microtensile bond strength than 1% with the BisGMA/TEGDMA cement; with the UDMA cement HF concentration made no difference, and water aging lowered bond strength except 10% HF with BisGMA/TEGDMA.
facts.follow_up: 24 hours and 6 months of water storage
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Fapesp and NIH/NIDCR; authors declare no conflict of interest

facts.population: 104 lithium disilicate (IPS e.max Press) blocks
facts.intervention: Etching with 5% or 10% hydrofluoric acid with previous heating of the acid (70 °C), the ceramic (85 °C) or both
facts.comparison: Unheated control etching at each HF concentration
facts.main_result: Heating raised the bond strength of 5% HF to that of unheated 10% HF, while 5% HF without heating gave significantly lower values than 10% HF.

facts.population: Lithium disilicate-based ceramic plates (100 plates, 10 groups)
facts.intervention: Five ceramic primers (silane agents) applied with or without post-silanization heating at 100 °C for 1 min, then RelyX CRA dual-cure resin cement
facts.comparison: Unheated primed plates and the different primers against each other
facts.main_result: Heating the primer did not improve bond strength; Clearfil Ceramic Primer gave the lowest values (37.4 and 31.8 MPa) versus about 43-49 MPa for the other silanes.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by FAPEAM and CNPq
facts.limitations: Long-term effects of post-silanization heating were not evaluated and need further study.

facts.intervention: Review of hydrofluoric acid etching, silane, abrasion and silica coating protocols for preparing porcelain and high-strength ceramic surfaces for bonding
facts.main_result: No single HF concentration and etching time is optimal for all porcelains, and both under- and over-etching are possible; alumina and zirconia cores cannot be etched with HF.

facts.population: 45 ceramic specimens: feldspathic, alumina and zirconia (15 each)
facts.intervention: Etching with 40% hydrofluoric acid gel for 2 minutes followed by SEM
facts.comparison: Unetched control specimens of each ceramic
facts.limitations: Conclusions drawn within the limitations of the SEM-only investigation.

facts.population: Ten samples and ten cusp-shaped abraders per restorative material (gold alloy, two lithium disilicates, feldspathic porcelain, zirconia, three heat-cured composites)
facts.intervention: Two-body wear in a dual-axis chewing simulator for 120,000 cycles with each material opposing itself
facts.comparison: Type 3 gold alloy as the traditional reference
facts.main_result: Monolithic zirconia (Katana ML) wore least, total volumetric loss 0.052 mm3, while IPS e.max Press wore most, 0.796 mm3; gold alloy 0.220 mm3.
facts.funding_coi: Authors certify no proprietary, financial or personal interest
facts.limitations: Conclusions apply only to an in vitro model of a material opposing itself.

facts.population: 90 CAD-CAM bar specimens (12×4×3 mm) of lithium disilicate, lithium disilicate-strengthened aluminosilicate glass ceramic and zirconia
facts.intervention: Mastication simulation (1,200,000 cycles, 5-55 °C) before 3-point flexural strength testing
facts.comparison: Nonaged specimens and the three materials against each other
facts.main_result: Zirconia (1136 MPa) was far stronger than lithium disilicate (304 MPa) and lithium aluminosilicate glass ceramic (202 MPa); aging reduced both glass ceramics by about 14.5% but zirconia only 4.3% (not significant).
facts.funding_coi: Materials supplied by Ivoclar Vivadent AG and Institut Straumann AG

facts.population: Sixty subjects needing a single implant crown in the maxillary or mandibular anterior or premolar region
facts.intervention: Immediate or early placed bone-level tapered implants restored with buccally micro-veneered lithium-disilicate or zirconia crowns bonded to titanium-base abutments
facts.comparison: Lithium-disilicate (n = 30) versus zirconia-ceramic (n = 30) crowns
facts.main_result: At about 13 months implant survival was 98.3% and restoration survival 100%, with a 3.7% technical complication rate and no difference between the two ceramics (p = .558).
facts.funding_coi: Funded with financial and material support from Institut Straumann AG; authors report grants and non-financial support from the company.

facts.population: CAD/CAM glass-ceramic specimens cut from blocks (30 per material per test)
facts.intervention: Zirconia reinforced lithium silicate glass-ceramic (Vita Suprinity)
facts.comparison: Lithium disilicate glass-ceramic (IPS e.max CAD)
facts.main_result: Vita Suprinity had higher fracture toughness (2.31 MPa m0.5), flexural strength (443.63 MPa), elastic modulus (70.44 GPa) and hardness (6.53 GPa) than IPS e.max CAD (P < 0.001) but a higher brittleness index (2.84).
facts.sample_size: 30 specimens per material for fracture toughness, flexural strength and hardness

facts.population: Cylindrical specimens of 5 dental ceramics, a Type III gold alloy and human enamel (n=10 each)
facts.intervention: 2-body wear test in a dual-axis mastication simulator for 120 000 cycles against zirconia cusps
facts.comparison: Human enamel and Type III gold alloy as controls
facts.main_result: Gold alloy wear depth (0.223 mm) was closest to enamel (0.217 mm); only milled, unglazed Celtra Duo wore more (0.320 mm, P<.05), and glaze firing removed the difference.
facts.sample_size: 10 specimens per material (7 groups plus enamel control)
materials_brands: IPS e.max Press and IPS e.max CAD (Ivoclar Vivadent)

facts.population: Standardized human enamel specimens (n¼72) opposing ceramic specimens
facts.intervention: Monolithic Y-TZP zirconia, lithium disilicate and feldspathic porcelain with rough, smooth (polished) or glazed surfaces in a 3-body wear simulator, 50 000 cycles
facts.comparison: Three ceramics (zirconia, lithium disilicate, feldspathic porcelain) and three surface finishes against each other
facts.main_result: Smooth zirconia caused the least enamel wear (1.26 mm2) and glazed groups the most (ZG 5.58, PG 4.2, EG 3.29 mm2); zirconia wear was similar to feldspathic porcelain and polished surfaces wore enamel less than glazed ones.
facts.sample_size: 72 ceramic specimens in 9 groups of 8, with 72 enamel specimens
facts.limitations: Findings are limited to this in vitro setting.

facts.population: Zirconia, lithium disilicate, veneering porcelain and enamel specimens (n = 8) with extracted molar cusps as antagonists
facts.intervention: Adjusted (A), adjusted and polished (AP) or adjusted and glazed (AG) zirconia and lithium disilicate, 400,000 chewing-simulator cycles
facts.comparison: Veneering porcelain and enamel as controls
facts.main_result: Veneering porcelain caused the most enamel wear (2.15 mm3); polished lithium disilicate (0.36 mm3) and zirconia (0.33 mm3) caused the least, comparable to enamel-enamel wear.
facts.limitations: Results apply only to the materials used and the test conditions.

facts.population: Ceramic specimens (n=10 per test; n=8 for wear) with isolated human molar cusps for wear
facts.intervention: 5Y-ZP (Katana UTML) tested for flexural strength, translucency, bond strength and wear
facts.comparison: 3Y-TZP (Katana HT) and lithium disilicate (e.max CAD)
facts.main_result: Flexural strength was 1194 MPa (Katana HT), 688 MPa (Katana UTML) and 450 MPa (e.max LT); bond strength and opposing enamel wear did not differ and 5Y-ZP showed no measurable wear.
facts.funding_coi: Supported partially by a grant from Kuraray.

facts.population: CAD/CAM block specimens (bars n = 10; hardness n = 2) and human incisor and premolar enamel
facts.intervention: Flexural, hardness and 400,000-cycle wear testing of lithium disilicate, lithium silicate/zirconia, three resin composites and a polymer infiltrated ceramic
facts.comparison: Human enamel and the other CAD/CAM materials
facts.main_result: E.max CAD and Celtra Duo were stronger, stiffer and harder than the resin composites and Enamic; resin composites and the infiltrated ceramic wore less than enamel and caused less opposing enamel wear than the glass ceramics.
facts.sample_size: 10 bars per material for flexural testing
facts.funding_coi: All materials were provided by their manufacturer.

facts.population: Human enamel specimens (n¼5) opposing lithium disilicate glass ceramic (n¼5) and Type III gold (n¼5)
facts.intervention: Ball-on-flat reciprocating friction-wear test with 9.8 N load for up to 1100 cycles in distilled water
facts.comparison: Type III gold versus lithium disilicate glass ceramic against enamel
facts.main_result: Type III gold had a lower steady-state friction coefficient (0.25 vs 0.64, P=.009) and caused less enamel wear damage than lithium disilicate; lithium disilicate showed abrasive wear, gold adhesive wear.
facts.funding_coi: Kirkpatrick Bequest Fund Scholarship (Grant PL108227), Sir John Walsh Research Institute.

facts.population: Hemispherical styli of four ceramics and enamel against flattened enamel antagonists (8 specimens per group)
facts.intervention: 100,000-cycle two-body wear test of lithium disilicate, leucite-reinforced glass, yttria-stabilized zirconia and feldspathic porcelain styli
facts.comparison: Human enamel styli and the four ceramics against each other
outcomes: enamel antagonist height and volume loss
facts.main_result: Zirconia (Aadva Zr) showed the smallest stylus wear and caused the least enamel wear, while leucite-reinforced glass, lithium disilicate and feldspathic porcelain were closer to enamel.

facts.population: Pressible lithium disilicate glass-ceramic disks with different surface finishes
facts.intervention: Pin-on-disk abrasive wear against alumina pins at 5 N and 25 N contact loads
facts.comparison: Different initial surface finishes (28 to 1846 nm roughness) and loads
facts.main_result: Initial surface finish and contact load significantly affected friction coefficients, wear volumes and surface roughness changes; wear and friction increased with load, with three-body wear dominant on rough and two-body wear on fine surfaces.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by James Cook University Collaboration Grants Scheme and NIDCR grant 2R01 DE017925; authors declare no conflict of interest.

facts.population: 335 patients with 627 posterior teeth (premolars, molars) restored with single crowns
facts.intervention: Pressed monolithic lithium disilicate single crowns with feather-edge margins, cemented with resin-based self-etching cement
facts.main_result: Nine crowns fractured and four teeth were extracted; overall survival was 97.93%, lower for second molars

facts.population: One patient with moderate dental biocorrosion
facts.intervention: Full-mouth rehabilitation with ultrathin CAD-CAM ceramic occlusal veneers (posterior) and bilaminar veneers (maxillary anterior: lingual direct composite plus labial ceramic veneers)
outcomes: clinical integrity of restorations at 1.5 years
facts.main_result: At 1.5-year reevaluation the restorations were well integrated with no cracks or chipping in the posterior restorations
facts.funding_coi: FAPERJ research grant; manufacturers supplied discounts/materials

facts.intervention: Narrative review of lithium disilicate and zirconia dental ceramics: properties and indications
facts.main_result: Lithium disilicate and zirconia are materials of choice for modern prosthetic dentistry owing to their properties and versatility
facts.funding_coi: No competing interests declared

facts.journal: University of Illinois at Chicago (MS thesis, Oral Sciences)
facts.population: 20 glazed IPS e.max CAD lithium disilicate discs (10 adjusted and polished) tested against zirconia spheres
facts.intervention: Ball-on-disc reciprocating tribometer wear test in artificial saliva (100,800 cycles, 8.5 N)
facts.comparison: Glazed versus glazed-then-polished surfaces of lithium disilicate and zirconia
facts.main_result: Mixed surface-treatment pairs lost more volume than matched pairs, but friction and volume loss did not differ significantly among the four groups; roughness did
facts.limitations: The zirconia counter bodies could not be analyzed
facts.key_finding: In a ball-on-disc test in artificial saliva, glazed and glazed-then-polished lithium disilicate opposing zirconia showed no significant difference in friction coefficient or wear volume among the four material-finish groups, while surface roughness differed significantly; mixed-finish pairs tended to lose more volume.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: The low wear of lithium disilicate depends in part on the surface finish delivered, and it wears against both glazed and polished zirconia.

facts.population: Lithium disilicate glass-ceramic bar (N = 40) and plate (N = 32) specimens made from remelted IPS e.max Press glass
facts.intervention: Two-step heat treatment at 765, 810, 855 or 915 °C to produce different crystal sizes (G1-G4)
facts.comparison: Heat-pressed (GC-P) and original ingot (GC-O) lithium disilicate controls
facts.main_result: Medium-sized crystals (G3) gave the highest flexural strength, hardness, elastic modulus and fracture toughness and the lowest wear loss
facts.funding_coi: National Natural Science Foundation of China and Shaanxi Natural Science Foundation grants

facts.intervention: Review of lithium disilicate ceramics: properties, manufacturing, in vitro and in vivo survival and clinical indications
facts.main_result: Lithium disilicate is considered one of the most promising dental materials in digital dentistry
facts.funding_coi: No competing interests declared

facts.intervention: Celtra Duo zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate CAD blocks for crowns, partial crowns, inlays, onlays and veneers
facts.key_finding: Manufacturer brochure for Celtra Duo zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate (10% zirconia, 500-700 nm crystallites) reporting 3-point flexural strength of 210 MPa when only polished and 370 MPa after firing, indicated for crowns, partial crowns, inlays, onlays and veneers.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Marketing material based on in-house data, not independent clinical evidence.

facts.population: Eight commercial chairside CAD/CAM materials
facts.intervention: Elastic constants by resonant ultrasound spectroscopy, resonant beam technique and pulse-echo; microstructure by SEM, EDX, Raman and XRD
facts.main_result: Young's modulus ranged from 10.9 (Lava Ultimate) to 201.4 (e.max ZirCAD) and Poisson's ratio from 0.173 (Empress CAD) to 0.47 (Lava Ultimate)
facts.funding_coi: Materials donated by the manufacturers
facts.limitations: For materials with a considerable polymeric fraction, all tested methods show important limitations

facts.population: 48 glass-ceramic samples (1.5 mm) of six A2 MT ceramics (96 surfaces)
facts.intervention: Thermocycling (10,000 cycles) with glazed or polished surfaces
facts.comparison: Heat-pressed versus milled feldspathic, lithium disilicate and ZLS ceramics; glazed versus polished
facts.main_result: Thermocycling reduced translucency and opalescence in all samples and roughened glazed surfaces; ZLS ceramics changed most and heat-pressed lithium disilicate least
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest

facts.population: 140 ZLS ceramic discs (12 mm diameter, 1.2 mm thick) of Vita Suprinity and Celtra Duo
facts.intervention: Crystallization firing of two ZLS glass-ceramics
facts.comparison: Fired versus unfired discs of each material
facts.main_result: Fired Celtra Duo had the highest characteristic strength (251.25 MPa) and unfired Vita Suprinity the lowest (106.95 MPa)

facts.journal: Journal of the Mechanical Behavior of Biomedical Materials
facts.population: Blocks of pre-crystallized ZLS and lithium metasilicate (becoming lithium disilicate) glass ceramic, sliced to 5 x 10 x 10 mm
facts.intervention: Diamond grinding with a computer-assisted high-speed handpiece and coarse diamond burs, simulating dental adjustment of ZLS
facts.comparison: Lithium disilicate glass ceramic (IPS e.max CAD) ground under the same conditions
facts.main_result: ZLS needed higher forces (tangential 0.56-2.03 N vs 0.43-1.59 N) and energy (1228-312 vs 912-253 J/mm3) than LDGC, while edge chipping depth did not differ (101 vs 110 um at the highest removal rate).
facts.funding_coi: National Natural Science Foundation of China, Natural Science Foundation of Tianjin and an Australia-China science fund

facts.population: Monolithic CAD/CAM posterior crowns (mandibular first molar form) on composite dies and milled bars of four materials
facts.intervention: Fracture-strength testing of adhesively cemented monolithic crowns and three-point flexural testing of bars of lithium disilicate, ZLS, a high-performance polymer composite and a PICN
facts.comparison: The four materials compared with each other (e.max CAD, Suprinity, Cerasmart, Enamic)
facts.main_result: Glass-ceramic crowns fractured at higher loads (e.max 4100 N, Suprinity 3659 N) than hybrids (Enamic 2003 N, Cerasmart 1562 N); flexural strength was LD 289 > ZLS 230 > HPP 141 > PICN 103 MPa.
facts.sample_size: 10 crowns and 10 bars per material (40 crowns, 40 bars)
facts.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq; no conflict of interest reported

facts.population: Published studies on zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate (ZLS) CAD/CAM ceramics (in vitro and clinical)
facts.intervention: ZLS glass-ceramics (Vita Suprinity PC, Celtra Duo) for CAD/CAM restorations
facts.comparison: Other glass-ceramics such as lithium disilicate
facts.main_result: There is no undisputed evidence that ZLS is stronger than lithium disilicate; its fracture resistance withstands physiological occlusal forces and internal marginal gaps are clinically acceptable (<=150 um).
facts.funding_coi: No competing interests declared
facts.limitations: Data on ZLS biocompatibility are scarce and controversial

facts.population: Partially edentulous patients and edentulous patients receiving implants (consensus of four systematic reviews)
facts.intervention: Immediate or early implant placement and loading
facts.comparison: Conventional (delayed) placement and loading protocols
facts.main_result: Different timings of implant placement/loading gave high survival rates; further research is needed for detailed guidelines.
facts.limitations: Further research is required to provide detailed guidelines for the different protocols

facts.population: Adults with maxillary single-tooth implants in the aesthetic zone (upper incisors and canines)
facts.intervention: Immediate/early implant placement and immediate/early loading
facts.main_result: Pooled data from 29 studies (965 implants) and 7 controlled trials showed no differences in survival or marginal bone remodelling between timing protocols up to 5 years.
facts.limitations: Insufficient data for meta-analytic comparison of all placement and loading combinations

facts.population: Patients with implant-supported multiple-unit fixed dental prostheses (>=10 patients, >=2 implants, >=3 years)
facts.intervention: Immediate or early implant placement and loading
facts.comparison: Delayed/conventional placement and loading
facts.main_result: High survival rates (>90%) for all studied combinations except IPIL; a meta-analysis of 3 RCTs found no difference in survival between DPIL and DPDL (p = .227).
facts.funding_coi: Departmental funding only; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Heterogeneity of the data did not allow conclusions on biological complications

facts.population: Patients treated with implant-supported single, short-span, full-arch or overdenture reconstructions
facts.intervention: Immediate or early implant placement or loading
facts.comparison: Traditional delayed placement and/or loading
facts.main_result: There is no strong evidence that timing of placement or loading affects patient discomfort or satisfaction; full-arch patients are more satisfied with immediate loading in the short term but not after one year.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest to disclose
facts.limitations: The quality evaluation showed some concerns among most studies

facts.population: Extracted human molars mounted for crown preparation
facts.intervention: Preparation refinement with a dental operating microscope up to x10 magnification
facts.comparison: Preparation refinement with x3.0 loupes
facts.main_result: Mean marginal gap was 145.0 um with loupes vs 35.6 um with the microscope (P<.001); gap volume 0.975 vs 0.250 mm3 (P=.023).
facts.sample_size: 18 extracted molars (2 groups); 24 gap points per specimen
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the Department of Endodontics, University of Pennsylvania

facts.population: Five dogs; second mandibular premolars hemi-sected, distal roots extracted
facts.intervention: Root extraction after elevation of full-thickness flaps
facts.comparison: Flapless root extraction on the contralateral side
facts.main_result: After 6 months the coronal ridge lost about 35% of its dimension, with no significant difference between flap and flapless extraction.

facts.population: 92 adult patients with single implants placed immediately into extraction sockets in the maxilla (15-25)
facts.intervention: Multilevel multivariate modelling of factors affecting bone changes after immediate implant placement (cylindrical vs tapered implants in the source RCT)
outcomes: implant surface to outer bony crest distance
facts.main_result: Residual gap size depended on initial gap and bone crest thickness, buccal crest resorption depended on implant position, and age affected vertical gap reduction.

facts.population: 28 freshman dental and hygiene students without signs of mandibular dysfunction
facts.intervention: Interocclusal centric relation registrations with the Williamson leaf gauge technique, two operators, repeated 30 days later
facts.comparison: Roth power centric bite technique
outcomes: number of matching bite registrations on split-cast mountings
condylar displacement from centric occlusion to centric relation on the Mandibular Position Indicator
facts.main_result: No significant difference between operators or between techniques for any MPI measurement; the leaf gauge appeared less reliable over 30 days than the power centric bite.
facts.key_finding: In 28 students without mandibular dysfunction, centric relation registered with the leaf gauge and the Roth power centric bite showed no significant differences between two operators or between the techniques on MPI readings. The leaf gauge looked less reliable over 30 days and needed more remounts.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Both techniques produced a posterior-superior condylar displacement from centric occlusion to centric relation, and the power centric bite was the more repeatable of the two in this sample.

facts.population: 42 healthy dentate adults (20 men, 22 women, 21 to 40 years) with normal occlusion and no TMD
facts.intervention: Lucia jig on the upper central incisors for 0, 5, 10, 15, 20 and 30 minutes with surface EMG of masseter and temporalis
outcomes: RMS electromyographic activity of masseter and temporalis muscles at rest
facts.main_result: No statistically significant difference in masseter and temporal EMG activity across 0 to 30 minutes; the jig changed EMG activity, mostly lowering it.
materials_brands: Duralay chemically activated acrylic resin (Reliance Dental Mfg Co.)
facts.funding_coi: Authors declared no commercial or associative interest

facts.population: 10 asymptomatic subjects with intact dentitions (6 women, 4 men)
facts.intervention: Photographic comparison of wire angulation on acrylic overlays on the mandibular right first molar and left central incisor, closed versus maximum open
facts.comparison: Most closed versus maximum open mandibular position
outcomes: angular (rotational) change between molar and incisor
facts.main_result: Mean linear flexure was 0.0028 inches and mean angular change about 3.1 degrees, significant at the 0.01% level.

facts.population: 20 in vivo and in vitro studies on mandibular flexure and implant-framework systems
facts.intervention: MEDLINE and PubMed literature search (1950 to May 2010)
outcomes: effect of mandibular flexure on the implant-framework system
facts.main_result: Mandibular flexure is multifactorial and the effect of the implant-framework system is unclear; sectional prosthesis designs may minimize its effect.
facts.limitations: No randomized, nonrandomized controlled or case-control studies were found, and no studies addressed long-span unilateral implant fixed prostheses.

facts.intervention: Posterior bilateral implants supporting the distal cantilevers through unconnected cantilever rests (gold cylinders) on a framework attached only to the anterior implants
facts.main_result: Author proposes that unconnected posterior abutments support the cantilevers, reducing torque on anterior implants and avoiding flexure-induced microdamage (no data reported).

facts.population: 3D finite element model of a human edentulous mandible
facts.intervention: Six implant-prosthesis designs (six or four implants, with or without distal cantilevers, cross-arch or midline-divided bar) loaded with 10 N at the condyles
facts.comparison: Mandible with implants but no prosthetic superstructure
outcomes: relative displacement at the condylar level
von Mises stress in implants and superstructure
facts.main_result: Cross-arch bridges restricted mandibular flexure (relative displacement 0.53 with six implants) while midline-divided superstructures restored flexibility (0.83) and were less stressed.
materials_brands: Titanium implants 3.25 mm x 13 mm with gold-ceramic superstructure
facts.limitations: Linear static analysis assuming complete osseointegration and an arbitrary 10 N load.

facts.population: 25 patients with 77 implants placed in healed posterior sites
facts.intervention: Concave (Slim) screw-retained abutments on 4x10 mm hexagonal internal connection implants
facts.comparison: Cylindrical (Straight) abutments
outcomes: early marginal bone loss at 8 weeks and 6 months
facts.main_result: Early global MBL was -0.6 ± 0.7 mm with cylindrical versus -0.4 ± 0.6 mm with concave abutments (p=0.030).
facts.follow_up: 6 months after loading (8 months after implantation)
materials_brands: IPX hexagonal internal connection implant (Nueva Galimplant)
facts.funding_coi: Supported by Nueva Galimplant and the University of Santiago de Compostela; nothing to declare
facts.limitations: Results must be confirmed by a study with a longer follow-up.

facts.population: Published reports on platform switching: human radiographic studies, animal histology and finite element analyses
facts.intervention: Platform switching (abutment narrower than the implant platform)
facts.main_result: Most reports conclude that platform switching prevents crestal bone loss, but the evidence is limited in quantity and quality.
facts.funding_coi: Partly supported by a JSPS Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research
facts.limitations: Scientific evidence is lacking in both quantity and quality.

facts.population: 60 titanium implants in edentulous mandibular areas of 5 hounds
facts.intervention: Two-piece non-submerged implants with microgaps of <10, 50 or 100 µm, abutments screwed on
facts.comparison: Laser-welded abutments allowing no movement between components
outcomes: distance from the interface to the first bone-to-implant contact
facts.main_result: Bone-to-implant contact lay more apically with screwed than welded abutments (about 1.7 vs 1.2 mm from the interface), independent of microgap size.
materials_brands: Straumann titanium test implants with SLA surface
facts.funding_coi: ITI Foundation grants and Swiss society and foundation stipends

facts.population: 130 dental implants placed and restored by 24 post-graduate students
facts.intervention: C1 implants placed and restored by inexperienced post-graduate students
outcomes: 24 patient, site, implant and prosthetic variables
facts.main_result: Five implants failed before loading; survival 96.15%, success 94.62%, mean MBL 0.53 mm at 1 year, affected by diabetes, implant depth, KT and probing depth.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by MIS Implants Technologies; authors declare no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Authors describe it as a short-term cohort study.

facts.population: 115 patients with 417 dental implants placed with static computer-assisted implant surgery
facts.intervention: Clinical and radiographic assessment of implant and prosthetic parameters (implant connection, loading, CIR, surface, prosthesis type, emergence angle, cantilever, etc.)
facts.main_result: Peri-implantitis OR 2.16 for removable versus fixed prostheses; marginal bone loss linked to higher interproximal contact level, greater emergence angle, shorter abutment height, longer cantilever and anodized surface.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Cross-sectional design

facts.main_result: Smooth titanium surfaces are proposed to give inadequate biomechanical coupling with bone, so the stress range they induce is too limited to maintain crestal bone, unlike textured surfaces.
facts.limitations: Authors state the report addresses only strain-related processes and purposely omits infection, molecular surface features, bioactive molecules and bone structure differences.

facts.population: 87 patients with missing incisors receiving 108 zirconia cantilever RBFDPs
facts.intervention: Single-retainer zirconia ceramic cantilever resin-bonded FDPs bonded with Panavia 21 TC or Multilink Automix
facts.comparison: Groups by reason for missing incisors: congenital, trauma, other
facts.main_result: 10-year survival rate 98.2% and success rate 92.0%; reason for missing incisors had no significant influence.
facts.limitations: Few debondings and only one failed RBFDP in the trauma group limited statistical analysis

facts.main_result: Single-retainer zirconia RBFDPs: 5-year complication-free rate 93.3% and 100% survival in a cited randomized trial.
Cited evidence: RBB survival 87.7% at 5 years (systematic review) and 80.4% at 10 years (771 bridges); case selection and design drive longevity.
Contemporary cp grade 4 titanium, TiZr and micro-rough zirconia implants are well tolerated and osseointegrate quickly (mostly animal data).

facts.population: 9 studies of deep-learning identification of dental implant systems on panoramic and periapical radiographs
facts.intervention: Deep-learning algorithms identifying and classifying dental implant systems
facts.main_result: Pooled sample 46,645 with overall accuracy 92.16%; range 70.75% to 98.19%.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by a National Research Foundation of Korea grant; no conflict of interest reported
facts.limitations: High risk of bias and applicability concerns in most studies

facts.main_result: PFM, veneered Zr and monolithic Zr iFDPs and splinted crowns had similarly high short-term survival; veneered restorations chipped more often than monolithic ones.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

facts.population: Patients with 3-4 mm subantral residual bone (case reports)
facts.intervention: 6 mm short Anyridge implants with deep threads placed without sinus augmentation
facts.main_result: Short deep-thread implants engaged in 3-5 mm of ridge bone without sinus augmentation gave successful rehabilitation in the reported cases.

facts.key_finding: MegaGen's AnyRidge drilling protocol offers stopper-drill or trephine sequences with a constant core diameter (3.3 mm for 4.0-5.5 mm fixtures, 4.8 mm for 6.0-8.0 mm fixtures), with the final implant diameter chosen by bone density.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Choose the AnyRidge diameter by bone density (softer bone, wider implant) while following the constant-core drilling sequence.

facts.key_finding: MegaGen slide presentation explaining the AnyRidge internal-connection implant, designed for thin and low ridges with a small strong core and wide threads to use more bone and minimize grafting.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Manufacturer design rationale only; it gives no clinical outcome evidence.

materials_brands: MegaGen AnyRidge healing abutments, impression copings and EZ Post final abutments
facts.key_finding: A two-page MegaGen flow chart showing the AnyRidge restorative sequence from healing abutments through impression copings, lab analogs and EZ Post final abutments to the final bridge. It states that all prosthetic components fit all 10 implant diameters through one common connection.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Manufacturer reference for choosing healing-abutment emergence profile and prosthetic components in the AnyRidge system, with a stated final abutment torque of 25-30 Ncm.

facts.key_finding: A 40-page MegaGen AnyRidge product catalog (Spanish distributor edition) covering the tapered knife-thread fixture, XPEED calcium-ion surface, 5 degree internal Morse connection, abutment options, overdenture system and surgical and prosthetic kits. It gives dimensions and product codes and no clinical study data.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Reference for AnyRidge product specifications and the manufacturer's drilling and placement advice; it is promotional and not evidence of clinical performance.

facts.population: Two edentulous mandible patients with narrow ridges (61- and 73-year-old women) in the ridge-split report, plus posterior mandible narrow-ridge cases
facts.intervention: Ridge split with Piezo and AnyRidge implant placement, grafted with FDBA
facts.limitations: Authors note ridge splitting needs experience and bone fracture of the buccal plate can occur
facts.key_finding: Two clinicians describe ridge splitting with a Piezo instrument and the tapered AnyRidge implant on narrow edentulous mandibular ridges. They report that it needed fewer surgeries and a shorter healing time than GBR, and that a small platform kept buccal bone.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Ridge split with Piezo and a tapered narrow-platform implant is presented as an option for narrow ridges, based only on a few uncontrolled cases and the authors' experience.

facts.population: Seven clinical cases of single-tooth replacement, including extraction sites, a compromised molar and a ridge needing GBR
facts.intervention: AnyRidge implant placement, with provisional restorations and in some cases GBR with titanium mesh or Bio-Oss
facts.key_finding: A photographic series of seven AnyRidge cases by one clinician covering atraumatic extraction with immediate placement, provisional restoration, soft-tissue shaping, and GBR with titanium mesh. Follow-up ranges from 2 weeks to about 1.2 years and the document gives no measurements.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Illustrative cases only; they show handling of the AnyRidge implant in extraction and augmentation sites but cannot support conclusions on outcomes.

off_topic_reason: A patient leaflet on hormonal contraceptive implants has no dental relevance.

facts.key_finding: A patient leaflet explaining the progestogen contraceptive implant placed under the skin of the upper arm, including effectiveness, advantages, risks, insertion and removal. It is not about dental implants.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Not relevant to dentistry; it concerns hormonal contraception.

facts.intervention: Bioactive approaches for GTR membranes and the use of polycaprolactone
facts.funding_coi: Faculty of Dentistry Research Fund, Chulalongkorn University
facts.limitations: Authors state further investigations are required
facts.key_finding: A book chapter reviewing how GTR membranes work in periodontal healing and how bioactive membranes (growth factors, bioactive ceramics, antimicrobials) are being developed. It proposes polycaprolactone, possibly decorated with the Notch ligand Jagged1, as a candidate material.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Polycaprolactone membranes are still experimental for periodontal GTR and need further investigation before clinical use.

facts.population: Healthy adults (18-82 years, smokers excluded) needing vertical bone augmentation with GBR or GTR before dental implants
facts.intervention: Eleven barrier membrane types used for vertical GBR/GTR
facts.comparison: Other membranes in a network comparison, with non-crosslinked collagen membrane the most frequent comparator
facts.main_result: A titanium-reinforced e-PTFE membrane may be the best choice for vertical GBR/GTR; membrane exposure and soft tissue complications were relatively common
facts.sample_size: 27 articles in the review, 19 in the network meta-analysis, 530 patients

facts.population: Laboratory cell cultures and an ex-ovo chick chorioallantoic membrane assay
facts.intervention: A bilayer PCL barrier membrane: 250 µm photocurable PCL polyHIPE layer plus an electrospun nanofibrous PCL layer
facts.main_result: The electrospun PCL layer limited cell infiltration for at least four weeks, while the PCL polyHIPE supported cell infiltration, mineral deposition and blood vessel ingrowth
facts.funding_coi: Turkish Ministry of National Education, EPSRC and MRC grants; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Authors say in vivo performance of the membrane still needs to be explored

facts.population: Maxillary bone lesion model with human bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells on membranes
facts.intervention: PCL biomembrane functionalized with BMP-2 and seeded with hBM-MSCs
facts.comparison: Non-functionalized PCL membrane
outcomes: filling of the lesion by new bone
facts.main_result: The PCL membrane with BMP-2 and hBM-MSCs gave faster bone regeneration in the maxillary lesion
facts.funding_coi: Fondation des Gueules Cassées and INSERM; no conflict of interest

facts.intervention: Selective review of new resorbable GBR membrane materials: modified collagen, aliphatic polyesters, platelet rich fibrin and silk
facts.main_result: Resorbable membranes with new materials aim to improve physical properties and bone regeneration, but clinical data are limited
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Authors note clinical research data remain limited

facts.population: Partially edentulous healthy human subjects who received or were to receive dental implants (edentulous ridges and peri-implant dehiscence sites)
facts.intervention: GBR for horizontal ridge augmentation or for peri-implant dehiscence defects, analysed by membrane exposure
facts.comparison: GBR sites without membrane exposure versus sites with exposure
outcomes: percentage of horizontal bone gain at edentulous ridges
percentage of peri-implant dehiscence defect reduction
facts.main_result: Sites without membrane exposure achieved 74% more horizontal bone gain at edentulous ridges and 27% more defect reduction at peri-implant dehiscence defects than sites with exposure.
facts.limitations: All included studies were judged to have moderate to high risk of bias.

facts.population: Rabbit bone marrow-derived MSCs in vitro and rabbit calvarial defects in vivo
facts.intervention: Electrospun PBSGL (poly(butylene succinate-co-glycolate)) membranes with increasing glycolate ratio (PBSGL10, 20, 40)
facts.comparison: PBSGL0 membrane without glycolate
facts.main_result: Higher glycolate ratios gave better MSC attachment, metabolic activity and osteogenic potential, and more bone formation in rabbit calvarial defects with no adverse inflammatory response.
facts.sample_size: 5 rabbits per time point, 4 calvarial defects each

facts.population: 13 patients, each with 2 maxillary premolars scheduled for orthodontic extraction
facts.intervention: e-PTFE membrane over the extraction socket, flap replaced so the membrane remained intentionally partially exposed (Group II), removed at 4 weeks
facts.comparison: Group I: flap rotated to completely cover the e-PTFE membrane
outcomes: radiographic alveolar depth, width and area
facts.main_result: Covered membranes (Group I) gave significantly higher clinical and radiographic bone gain than intentionally exposed ones (Group II) for all parameters (p<0.05), e.g. alveolar depth 12.01 vs 10.23.

facts.population: Patients needing alveolar ridge augmentation before or with implant placement (review topic)
facts.intervention: GBR with barrier membranes with or without particulate bone grafts or bone substitutes
facts.main_result: GBR can be achieved with particulate autogenous grafts, allografts, xenografts or alloplasts combined with resorbable or non-resorbable barrier membranes in 1-2 tooth defects.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared.

facts.population: Macor dental ceramic specimens
facts.intervention: Rotary ultrasonic machining varying spindle speed, feed rate, coolant pressure and ultrasonic power (response surface methodology)
facts.main_result: Best surface roughness was 0.5130 um at run 17 (lower feed rate, moderate other parameters); feed rate was the most influential factor.

off_topic_reason: Industrial product brochure for Macor with no dental or clinical content.

facts.key_finding: Corning industrial brochure for MACOR machinable glass ceramic, a material of 55% fluorophlogopite mica and 45% borosilicate glass, listing its thermal, mechanical, electrical and chemical properties and industrial applications.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: No clinical or dental content: it is an industrial product brochure.

facts.population: Sintered pellets of mica glass ceramic with 0-20 wt.% yttria-stabilised zirconia (laboratory specimens)
facts.intervention: Addition of 3 mol% YSZ (5-20 wt.%) to fluorophlogopite mica glass ceramic
facts.comparison: Pure mica glass and commercial IPS e.max Press lithium disilicate
facts.main_result: With 20 wt.% YSZ: hardness 9.2 GPa, elastic modulus 125 GPa, indentation toughness 3.6 MPa·m1/2 and solubility about 30 µg/cm2, within ISO limits.
facts.sample_size: At least 5 specimens per composition (10 for solubility)
facts.funding_coi: Wellcome Trust DBT India Alliance fellowship; Department of Biotechnology, Government of India

facts.population: Workpieces: Macor-M and Bioram-M machinable glass-ceramics, composite resin typodont tooth enamel and bovine enamel
facts.intervention: Weight-load cutting with a diamond point in an air-turbine handpiece at applied loads of 20 to 80 g
facts.comparison: Composite resin typodont tooth enamel and bovine enamel
facts.main_result: Macor-M showed the second-most reduced cutting speed and the maximum cutting volume, whereas Bioram-M showed the least reduced cutting speed and the minimum cutting volume.
materials_brands: Nissin A20-500 composite resin typodont teeth
facts.funding_coi: Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research, Ministry of Education, Science and Culture, Japan

facts.population: Macor machinable glass ceramic bars used as the cutting substrate
facts.intervention: Mouthwash (Scope) added to handpiece coolant water at 1:1, 1:2.5, 1:5 and 1:10 with medium-grit diamond and cross-cut carbide burs
facts.comparison: Distilled water coolant
outcomes: change in cutting rate over prolonged cutting
facts.main_result: Mouthwash:water 1:5 and 1:10 mixtures raised carbide bur cutting rates from 0.21 to 0.64 and 0.66 mm/s, and also raised diamond bur rates, versus water alone.
facts.sample_size: 6 burs per irrigant mixture, 3 cuts each

facts.population: Mandibular edentulous patients rehabilitated with implant-retained overdentures
facts.intervention: Mini-implants retaining mandibular overdentures
facts.comparison: Standard-diameter implants retaining mandibular overdentures
facts.main_result: Mini-implants had fewer abutment adjustments (RR 0.23), retentive-element replacements (RR 0.41), occlusal adjustments (RR 0.53) and overdenture fractures (RR 0.46), with similar pain, probing depth, bone loss and survival.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq, CAPES and FAPESP grants
facts.limitations: Certainty of evidence was mostly very low to low.

facts.key_finding: A Wiley reference glossary (2018) that defines the terms of dental implantology in alphabetical entries, such as abutment, abutment analog and abutment driver.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: A terminology reference for looking up implant terms; it reports no clinical findings.

facts.population: 71 primary studies (in vitro and in vivo) testing mouthwashes against viruses of the oral cavity
facts.intervention: antimicrobial mouthwashes (CHX, PVP-I, essential oils, CPC, H2O2, others) used to reduce viral load
facts.main_result: Essential oils, cetylpyridinium chloride and povidone-iodine showed antiviral potential with no significant side effects in short-term use; other solutions need further studies.
facts.funding_coi: No specific funding; no competing interests declared
facts.limitations: Other solutions need further randomized clinical studies with larger patient numbers and more controlled situations.

facts.population: 100 patients with congenitally missing maxillary lateral incisors, one implant each
facts.intervention: Ø2.9 mm narrow-diameter Roxolid SLActive implant with cement-retained bi-layered zirconia crown
facts.comparison: Ø3.3 mm implant of the same type
facts.main_result: 1-year implant survival was 99%; CBL change was -0.19 ± 0.25 mm (Ø2.9) vs -0.25 ± 0.31 mm (Ø3.3), not significantly different.
facts.sample_size: 100 implants in 100 patients (50 per group); 7 dropouts
facts.funding_coi: ITI Foundation grant; implants and components supplied free by Straumann AG; authors declare no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Non-randomized allocation by mesio-distal space, cemented crowns only, soft tissue dehiscence not assessed, short 12-month follow-up.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Medical Robotics and Computer Assisted Surgery
facts.intervention: computer-assisted/guided implant surgery (CT-based planning, image-guided navigation, RP-CT surgical guides)
facts.comparison: conventional implantation techniques
facts.main_result: Image-guided templates and RP-CT-based surgical guides give similar accuracy and allow precise implant positioning, at higher cost and training demands than conventional implantology.
facts.limitations: Little has been done regarding patient demands, including cost; techniques are complex and need training.

facts.intervention: mill, polish and adhesively seat n!ce glass-ceramic restorations (crowns, partial crowns, inlays, onlays, veneers)
materials_brands: Straumann n!ce fully crystallized glass-ceramic blocks
facts.key_finding: Manufacturer brochure for Straumann n!ce, a fully crystallized lithium aluminosilicate glass-ceramic reinforced with lithium disilicate that is milled, polished and adhesively seated without a crystallization firing. Stated flexural strength is 350 ± 50 MPa (ISO 6872, type II class 2), in two translucencies.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Marketing document: n!ce is presented as a chairside CAD/CAM glass-ceramic for single-tooth restorations with a mill-polish-seat workflow, with no clinical outcome data in the brochure.

facts.key_finding: Quick processing guide for Straumann n!ce glass-ceramic restorations: mill with the dedicated CAD/CAM program, then either polish only or stain and glaze (firing at 770 to 800 °C, never above 820 °C), condition with 5 % hydrofluoric acid for 20 seconds plus silane, and seat adhesively.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Follow the n!ce minimum thicknesses (1.0 mm for most restorations, 0.6 mm for veneers), rounded preparations without sharp edges, and lithium-disilicate-compatible polishing and cementation systems; autoclave at 132 °C for 3 minutes when sterilization is needed.

facts.key_finding: Multilingual instructions for use of Straumann n!ce glass-ceramic blocks (lithium aluminosilicate ceramic reinforced with lithium disilicate, flexural strength at least 350 MPa) for inlays, onlays, veneers, partial crowns and crowns, with preparation, milling, polishing, stain and glaze, cementation and sterilization instructions.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Contraindicated in allergy to the ingredients, severely reduced residual dentition and bruxism; use only lithium-disilicate-compatible grinding, polishing and cementation systems, avoid sandblasting and overheating, and follow minimum thickness guidelines.

facts.key_finding: Instructions for use of Straumann n!ce A14 blocks, pre-milled lithium disilicate-reinforced glass-ceramic blocks for single-unit restorations cemented on Variobase C or CEREC Ti-Bases, available in HT and LT translucency and small and large interface sizes, with minimum wall thickness 1.0 mm.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Use only for single-unit restorations on compatible Ti-Bases, avoid bruxism and severely reduced residual dentition, and place in occlusion only when the implant is completely osseointegrated.

materials_brands: n!ce glass-ceramic (Straumann), lithium aluminosilicate ceramic reinforced with lithium disilicate
Twist Step Drills and Screw Taps
facts.key_finding: Nobel Biocare procedures manual for NobelActive implants (3.0, NP, RP, WP), covering indications, drill protocols by bone quality (soft, medium, dense), flap and flapless surgery, implant insertion with orientation adjustment, placement in extraction sockets and temporary restorations.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Do not exceed 45 Ncm insertion torque (maximum 70 Ncm for NP, RP, WP with screw tap in dense bone, 45 Ncm for 3.0); NobelActive 3.0 is for single-unit lateral and mandibular central incisors only, and narrow platform implants are not recommended in the posterior region.

facts.key_finding: Nobel Biocare product overview for NobelActive: tapered implants with apical drilling blades, back-tapered coronal design with platform shifting, internal conical connection with hexagonal interlocking and TiUnite grooved surface, with product reference numbers for implants and prosthetic components.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Sales material presents NobelActive for soft bone, the esthetic area and extraction sockets with immediate function; NobelActive 3.0 is only for single-unit maxillary lateral incisors and mandibular lateral and central incisors, and NP is not recommended posteriorly.

facts.key_finding: Nobel Biocare sales brochure for NobelActive: an expanding tapered implant with double lead threads (advancing 2.4 mm per turn), apical drilling blades, reverse-cutting flutes, TiUnite oxidized surface with macroscopic grooves, back-tapered collar and a dual-function internal conical connection with built-in platform shifting.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Presented for soft to medium bone and extraction sockets, where bone condensing and adjustable implant orientation during manual insertion are claimed to give high initial stability and better prosthetic positioning; claims rest on manufacturer-cited studies.

facts.intervention: Minimally invasive nonsurgical therapy (MINST) with magnification, minicurettes and thin ultrasonic tips, plus the periodontal endoscope
facts.comparison: Conventional scaling and root planing, and minimally invasive surgery (MIST)
facts.main_result: MINST gave PPD reduction of 3.13 mm and CAL gain of 2.56 mm at 6 months in intrabony defects, similar to MIST (3.51 mm and 2.85 mm), with half the chair time
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Limited evidence; histological and biologic-mechanism data on MINST healing are lacking

facts.intervention: Description of occlusal patterns, jaw movements and posterior occlusal morphology in the class III (macrognathic mandible) patient
facts.main_result: Class III patients lack anterior guidance, so occlusal morphology is dictated by condylar movement and mandibular size, balancing contacts are physiologic, and 0.5 to 1 mm rest interocclusal distance suffices
Lecture slides review the history and concepts of complete denture occlusion, favouring a balanced articulation while noting no occlusal scheme is proven superior
facts.key_finding: Lecture slides reviewing the history, terminology and concepts of complete denture occlusion: balanced versus non-balanced schemes, centric concepts, curves of occlusion, tooth forms and monoplane and lingualized occlusion. The author states no occlusal scheme is proven superior but that balanced articulation appears most appropriate.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: For complete dentures, choose the occlusal scheme to suit ridge condition, jaw relation and esthetics, since no scheme has scientific proof of superiority.

facts.journal: Journal of the Indian Prosthodontic Society
facts.main_result: Overview of occlusal concepts for full mouth rehabilitation (gnathologic, freedom in centric, PMS, Hobo twin-stage, Wiskott-Belser); authors favour posterior disclusion and cusp-to-fossa contacts, with no single rule for all patients

facts.key_finding: Course handout (based on John Kois's work) on functional risk assessment: patients are classified by functional diagnostic category (acceptable function, constricted chewing, occlusal dysfunction, parafunction, neurologic), and risk and disease status together set treatment intensity. It describes the 'three P's' of occlusion: Position (P1), Place (P2, home/MIP) and Pathway (P3, anterior guidance).
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Diagnose function and functional risk first, then use MIP only for acceptable function with no vertical change, and centric relation when function is not acceptable or the vertical dimension changes.

facts.population: Ninety Sprague-Dawley rats, divided into three diet groups
facts.intervention: Rearing on a gruel-like soft diet, or soft diet with dry pellets one day in seven
facts.comparison: Group I fed hard pelleted rat chow
facts.funding_coi: Biomedical Research Support Grant from Wright State University

facts.population: 43 squirrel monkeys (Saimiri sciureus), wild-raised on tough natural foods versus laboratory-raised on soft artificial diet
facts.intervention: Rearing on a soft artificial diet
facts.comparison: Rearing on naturally tough (hard) foods
facts.main_result: Soft-diet monkeys had occlusal deviations in 14 of 18 versus 3 of 22 on hard diets, with more tooth displacement and narrower arches
facts.sample_size: 43 squirrel monkeys (24 hard diet, 19 soft diet)
facts.funding_coi: NSF grants and Wright State University research services

facts.population: 413 subjects in 11 experiments: bruxism, temporomandibular disorders, headache with TMD, chronic cervical pain
facts.intervention: Occlusal adjustment therapy
facts.comparison: Mock adjustment or a comparison treatment
facts.main_result: Data from the 11 experiments did not show greater efficacy of occlusal adjustment than control or contrasting therapy
facts.limitations: Included studies were small, mostly unblinded or uncalibrated examiners, mixed disease groups

facts.population: A 79-year-old man missing maxillary left first and second molars
facts.intervention: Digital functionally generated path (FGP) technique with intraoral scanner, FGP wax table and design software to design an implant-supported fixed prosthesis
facts.main_result: The method designed an interference-free prosthesis and can reduce chairside time

facts.population: Fellows of the Academy of Prosthodontics
facts.intervention: CR Attributes Survey on definitions of centric relation (5 domains, agree-uncertain-disagree)
facts.main_result: 100 of 146 fellows responded (68.5%); strong agreement that CR is clinically determined, repeatable, independent of tooth contact and a starting point for movements; insufficient evidence on condyle and disk position
facts.limitations: Attributes with weak agreement indicate need for further research

facts.population: 17 Rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta), 5 on soft diet, 11 analysed as hard-diet controls
facts.intervention: Soft diet mixed to the consistency of fudge for 4 to 14 months before sacrifice
facts.comparison: Hard diet (Purina Monkey Chow biscuits)
facts.limitations: Small samples, and dietary differences were not maintained over the animals' lifetime
facts.key_finding: In macaques fed a soft diet, maxillary arch breadth was smaller relative to arch length than in hard-diet animals after age correction (t=2.16, p=.05); the raw mean difference was not significant.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Soft diets may narrow the maxillary arch in growing animals, analogous to maxillary arch collapse in humans, but samples were small and the evidence is only suggestive.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 62 subjects with single-tooth implants opposed by natural teeth
facts.intervention: Active tactile sensibility test with interocclusal copper foils of 0 to 200 µm, analysed by logistic regression
facts.comparison: Implant surfaces: titanium plasma-sprayed, sandblasted/acid-etched, machined
facts.main_result: Mean 50% tactile threshold was 20.2 ± 10.9 µm; sandblasted/acid-etched implants were more sensitive than plasma-sprayed (mean difference 8 µm, P = .016)

facts.journal: The Journal of the American Dental Association
facts.population: Eskimos in Alaska and Indians in northern and central Canada at various stages of modernization
facts.main_result: No dental caries occurred in Eskimo and Indian groups living on a diet adequately reinforced with minerals and activators; caries rose to 30 to 50 per cent of teeth with liberal contact with modern foods.

facts.intervention: Four-stage Dawson Academy protocol: functional-esthetic analysis, three-dimensional treatment planning, prototype restorations, definitive restorations
facts.main_result: Predictable, durable, esthetic restorations are said to come from a reproducible four-stage protocol.

facts.population: 89 patients with unilateral posterior missing teeth (38 men, 51 women)
facts.intervention: Unilateral posterior tooth loss analyzed on panoramic and cephalometric radiographs
facts.comparison: 20 patients without missing posterior teeth or orthodontic treatment
facts.main_result: Patients with unilateral missing teeth had lower articular eminence inclination, smaller cranio-cervical angle and fewer occlusal planes passing through the C1-C2 intersection.
facts.sample_size: 178 joints from 89 patients, plus 40 control joints
facts.funding_coi: Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau

facts.intervention: Gnathological method versus Pankey-Mann-Schuyler technique for oral rehabilitation
facts.main_result: The two methods achieve similar results via different routes.
facts.key_finding: This master's project reviews the history of gnathology and the Pankey-Mann-Schuyler technique and compares them for oral rehabilitation; the two methods reach a similar, fully functional stable occlusion by different routes.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Most restorative work does not need a pantograph or functionally generated path, but the restorative dentist should understand the concepts behind both techniques.

facts.population: Clinical human studies with at least 10 implants
facts.main_result: Seven articles were identified; occlusal overloading was positively associated with peri-implant marginal bone loss.
facts.funding_coi: No financial interest declared
facts.limitations: Significant heterogeneity among study methodologies, mostly retrospective

facts.journal: Oral Surgery, Oral Medicine, Oral Pathology and Oral Radiology
facts.population: 8 New Zealand white rabbits, 12 weeks old
facts.intervention: Unilateral molar extraction
facts.comparison: Non-extraction side of the same rabbit
facts.main_result: At 12 weeks bone metabolism was 39.96% on the extraction side versus 60.04% on the non-extraction side (P < .05); calcium and osteoclast differences were not significant.
facts.funding_coi: National Research Foundation of Korea

facts.population: 109 consecutive patients with mandibular implant-supported fixed prostheses opposing maxillary complete dentures
facts.intervention: Mandibular implant-supported fixed prostheses (Branemark system)
facts.main_result: Occlusal factors were of limited importance for patient satisfaction and treatment outcome; 61% had bilateral balanced occlusion and mean bone loss was 0.5 mm.

facts.population: 100 Eskimo children aged 11 to 20 from Kotzebue, Alaska
facts.comparison: Average values for a white population
facts.main_result: 82 per cent of the children had malocclusion; Class I predominated and arch widths did not differ between normal and malocclusion groups.
Little scientific evidence supports a direct cause-effect relationship between occlusal factors and deleterious biological outcomes for osseointegrated implants.
facts.limitations: Most articles reviewed were descriptive, so findings were reported descriptively rather than as a systematic review

facts.key_finding: Price compared isolated primitive groups with modernized groups of the same peoples and reported that those on primitive foods had excellent teeth and dental arches, while those on modern foods showed tooth decay and deformed dental arches.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: A 1939 observational field survey linking diet to dental and facial form; historical background, not clinical evidence for practice.

facts.main_result: There is currently no evidence-based, implant-specific concept of occlusion; guidelines are based on biomechanics and limited in vitro, animal and retrospective data.

facts.key_finding: Occlusal trauma cannot by itself induce periodontal breakdown, but it causes alveolar bone resorption and increased tooth mobility and may enhance disease progression in teeth with progressive plaque accumulation.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Treat periodontal disease first; adjust occlusion or splint when mobility is excessive, bothersome, or during regenerative surgery.

facts.main_result: Gnathological concepts offer a structured methodology for prosthodontic procedures, but further research is needed to corroborate current occlusal treatment approaches.

facts.journal: Journal of Clinical and Diagnostic Research
facts.main_result: Published data suggest that a peripheral sensory feedback pathway can be restored with osseointegrated implants (osseoperception).

facts.funding_coi: Course made possible through an unrestricted educational grant
facts.key_finding: Bruxism, sleep or awake, contributes to tooth wear, fractured teeth and restorations, and temporomandibular disorders; preventive intervention with a nightguard (laboratory-made or chairside) protects teeth from uncontrolled wear, although changing the parafunctional habit itself is rarely successful.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Identify bruxism, treat fractures or caries first, and use a nightguard to preserve tooth structure in patients with tooth wear.

facts.population: Human in vivo studies of crowns, removable prostheses and implant-borne reconstructions
facts.main_result: There is little scientific evidence specifying occlusal and superstructure design for fixed prostheses on teeth or implants, and no evidence that a particular design is superior.
Subjects with a history of TMD adapt less well to experimental occlusal interferences than subjects without, and individual vulnerability differs.
facts.limitations: Human studies are limited by small sample size, short observation time and low interference intensity.

facts.population: One test patient with deflective occlusal contacts
facts.main_result: Analysis of stress direction in centric versus eccentric closures discloses one of the important causes of pathologic wear of teeth and effects on supporting structures.
The occlusal perception threshold is higher for implant-supported prostheses than for natural dentition, so clinicians should not rely on patient perception when checking occlusion.

facts.population: 741 individuals aged 21-60 years with missing posterior teeth, 386 with and 355 without TMD
facts.comparison: TMD group versus prosthetic group without TMD signs or symptoms
facts.main_result: Fewer missing posterior teeth but spread over more quadrants, plus younger age and female gender, were associated with higher TMD prevalence (OR 0.51 for number missing, 7.71 for quadrants).
facts.funding_coi: National Nature Science Foundation of China (NSFC) No. 30540130469
outcomes: presence of TMD signs and symptoms
association with gender, age, number of missing posterior teeth and number of quadrants with missing posterior teeth

facts.population: 20 complete denture wearers (46 to 80 years) with clinically unsatisfactory dentures
facts.intervention: Occlusal correction of gross prematurities, denture adhesive, and soft tissue-conditioning reline, applied in sequence
facts.comparison: Original dentures before modification
facts.main_result: The three denture modifications did not significantly change masseter EMG activity or masticatory performance (maximum improvement 2.4% after occlusal correction; p > .05).
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the Medical Service of the Veterans Administration
facts.limitations: Testing was done at the same sitting, so patients had no time to adapt neuromuscularly to each modification, and the order of conditions could not be randomized.
outcomes: ipsilateral and contralateral masseter EMG activity

facts.funding_coi: No financial support; no conflicts of interest

facts.journal: The Journal of Indian Prosthodontic Society
facts.funding_coi: No financial support; no conflict of interest

facts.comparison: 2-stage (submerged) implant placement

facts.population: 84 partially dentate patients needing 115 fixed partial dentures, implants in posterior load-carrying regions

facts.population: 40 edentulous patients (Cawood & Howell class V-VI) receiving mandibular overdenture treatment
facts.intervention: Two IMZ two-part implants inserted in a one-stage procedure
facts.comparison: Two-stage surgical procedure
facts.main_result: No striking clinical differences between groups; mean bone loss in the first year was 0.6 mm in both.

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.population: 30 consecutive patients with extremely resorbed maxillae
facts.intervention: Iliac crest (ala iliaca) onlay bone graft with endosseous implants in a one-stage procedure
facts.comparison: Development group (first 10 patients) versus routine group (following 20 patients)
facts.main_result: Marginal bone loss averaged 4.6 mm up to the 3-year examination in the routine group with no significant change to 10 years; implant success rate was 83.1% in the routine group.

facts.population: Extensive alveolar bone deficiency (technique description; number of patients not stated)
facts.intervention: Two-tier intraoral autogenous block graft (ramus, then ramus or symphysis 5 months later) before implant placement
facts.main_result: A multitier intraoral block graft technique is described as an option for extensively atrophic alveolar bone augmentation; no outcome data are reported.
facts.funding_coi: No financial interest declared
facts.limitations: The technique requires several operations, which could cause patient discomfort.

facts.population: 70-year-old woman on bisphosphonates (alendronate, then ibandronate) with right maxillary sinusitis and oroantral communication after implant placement
facts.intervention: Functional endoscopic sinus surgery plus two-layer closure with pedicled buccal fat pad and buccal advancement flap
facts.main_result: Healing was uneventful and complete after 4 months, with no new oroantral communication or oral lesions at 12 months.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: The buccal fat pad can only be used once and the size of defects it can cover is limited.

facts.population: Three patients with large oroantral defects
facts.intervention: Reconstruction with a pedicled buccal fat pad
facts.main_result: Follow-up photography and imaging showed successful closure of the oroantral defects, with no operative site complications and no patient-reported discomfort.
facts.funding_coi: Funding not applicable; no competing interests

facts.population: Patients with chronic orofacial pain (head and neck cancer, MS-related trigeminal neuralgia-like symptoms, post-herpetic neuralgia, TMD, burning mouth syndrome)
facts.intervention: Cannabis and cannabinoid medications (self-administered cannabis, topical PEA, topical cannabis extract, cannabis sativa oil, nabiximols, nabilone)
facts.main_result: Of 8 included sources, 6 concluded the cannabinoid treatment gave some therapeutic benefit for chronic orofacial pain and all concluded it was safe.
facts.funding_coi: No specific grant funding; no competing interests declared
facts.limitations: The included studies are few, small and have significant limitations preventing definitive conclusions.

facts.population: Partially or fully edentulous patients (14 included studies)
facts.intervention: Implant-supported prostheses
facts.comparison: Conventional prostheses or no therapy
facts.main_result: Meta-analyses showed no benefit of implant-supported over conventional prostheses for alveolar bone resorption, but a significant benefit for masseter muscle thickness.
facts.funding_coi: No financial support; no competing interests
facts.limitations: Only one included study was an RCT.

facts.main_result: Osseointegration is proposed to be the lack of a negative tissue response rather than an advantageous biological response.

facts.population: One male foxhound (18 months, 38 kg) with an unintentionally retained palatal root of the first molar
facts.intervention: One sandblasted, acid-etched titanium implant placed next to the retained root, 8 weeks non-submerged healing
facts.main_result: Mean contact of osteodentin/osteocementum to the implant was 67.4% versus 63.5% bone-to-implant contact at the vestibular aspect.
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded by the authors’ department; no conflict of interest

facts.population: Clinical studies using RFA and/or Periotest
facts.intervention: Resonance frequency analysis and Periotest
outcomes: validity and prognostic value for detecting implants at risk of failure
facts.main_result: Single readings with either technique are of limited clinical value, and their prognostic value for predicting loss of implant stability remains to be established in prospective studies.
facts.sample_size: A limited number of clinical reports
facts.funding_coi: One author is affiliated with Nobel Biocare
facts.limitations: No randomized controlled trials or prospective cohort studies were found for validity testing.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 20 implants in 20 patients lost before loading, from 3,786 implants placed
facts.intervention: ISQ by resonance frequency analysis at placement (immediate) and at 4 months (delayed)
facts.comparison: 56 randomly selected stable implants
facts.main_result: Immediate and delayed ISQ were significantly related to early failure (OR 4.27 and 9.20), but ISQ was judged unreliable for predicting it.
facts.sample_size: 3,786 implants evaluated; 20 early failures in 20 patients; 56 controls
facts.funding_coi: Supported by FEDICOM and Junta de Andalucía; no financial interests in listed products

facts.population: 158 patients with edentulous mandibles receiving a single midline implant
facts.intervention: Immediate loading of a single midline implant with a ball-attachment overdenture
facts.comparison: Delayed (conventional) loading three months after implant placement
facts.main_result: Immediate loading had significantly lower 5-year implant survival (9 failures vs 2 in delayed loading; p=0.011) and non-inferiority was not shown.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft; one author reports grants and fees from Camlog, Straumann and others
facts.limitations: Results of the 5-year follow-up should be interpreted exploratively.

facts.population: Studies of CAD-CAM removable partial denture frameworks: 2 clinical and 5 in vitro studies
facts.intervention: Digital (CAD-CAM) fabrication of RPD frameworks
facts.comparison: Conventional lost-wax cast frameworks / conventional impressions
facts.main_result: The digital technique for RPD frameworks is accurate, with clinically acceptable discrepancies (<311 µm); PEEK frameworks fitted better than cast metal and Co-Cr made by laser melting showed the highest discrepancies.
facts.limitations: Results were heterogeneous because studies used different measurement methods; only 2 clinical studies assessed frameworks.

facts.population: Edentulous patients wearing a maxillary complete denture opposed by a mandibular implant overdenture or a complete denture
facts.intervention: Maxillary CD opposing a mandibular 2-implant overdenture (IRO)
facts.comparison: Maxillary CD opposing a mandibular complete denture
outcomes: blood flow in anterior maxillary mucosa (laser Doppler)
facts.main_result: IRO produced greater blood flow disturbance (103 vs 183 BPU initially) and about three times more anterior maxillary bone volume loss than CD (7.3% vs 2.6% at 1 year).
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Universiti Teknologi MARA and a Malaysian research grant; no conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Unequal group sizes (9 vs 4) due to ethical limits on repeat CBCT

facts.intervention: ACP classification system for partial edentulism (Class I to IV) based on four diagnostic criteria: edentulous area, abutment condition, occlusion, residual ridge
facts.main_result: The ACP defines a four-class diagnostic classification of partial edentulism, from uncomplicated (Class I) to complex (Class IV).
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the American College of Prosthodontists
facts.limitations: The system is not a predictor of treatment success.

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 41 edentulous maxilla patients receiving implant prostheses (193 implants)
facts.intervention: CAD/CAM titanium-bar overdenture and CAD/CAM implant fixed prosthesis
facts.comparison: Conventional soldered gold-bar overdenture
facts.main_result: Maintenance rates were 1.24 (gold OD), 1.36 (Ti OD) and 0.98 (IFP) events/year, not significantly different; OHIP was significantly better for the fixed prosthesis.
facts.limitations: Randomization was not used; patients chose their prosthetic option.

facts.population: Completely edentulous patients rehabilitated with implant-supported fixed complete dentures or implant overdentures (28 studies, 1457 patients)
facts.intervention: Implant-supported fixed complete dentures (IFCDs)
facts.comparison: Implant overdentures (IODs)
facts.main_result: Both prosthesis types produced large positive effects on dPROs (IFCD ES 1.68, IOD ES 1.26, no significant difference); only denture stability was rated higher for IFCDs, and two implants beat one for mandibular IODs.
facts.funding_coi: Open access funding by Universitat Bern; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Findings should be interpreted cautiously given high heterogeneity and limited direct comparisons.

facts.population: 103 patients with mandibular two-implant overdentures (206 implants)
facts.intervention: Mandibular overdentures on two implants with Dolder bar with cantilever (36), Spherblock ball (58) or Locator (9) attachments
facts.comparison: Splinted cantilever bar versus unsplinted ball/Locator attachments
outcomes: gingival and plaque index, pocket depth, BOP
facts.main_result: Implant survival was 100% with 0.22 mm mean bone loss at 5 years; ball attachments had more complications (wear, fracture) while bar attachments needed fewer replacements and appointments.
materials_brands: Straumann tissue-level implants and Dolder bar
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Isfahan University of Medical Sciences; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Only two practitioners, no randomization, small Locator group (n=9) and retrospective design.

facts.population: Edentulous patients with 2-implant mandibular overdentures (16 RCTs, 599 participants, 1198 implants)
facts.intervention: Different overdenture attachments (ball, bar, LOCATOR, telescopic, magnet) with delayed or immediate loading
facts.main_result: All attachment types with immediate or delayed loading had similar effects on peri-implant health; bar+immediate loading ranked best for bone loss and ball+delayed loading for probing depth.

facts.journal: Indian Journal of Public Health Research and Development
facts.population: 12 completely edentulous patients (aged 50-70) receiving two mandibular canine implants
facts.intervention: Two-implant mandibular overdenture on a Co-Cr bar with 7 mm bilateral distal extensions
facts.comparison: Co-Cr bar with no distal extensions
outcomes: posterior ridge resorption on panoramic radiographs at 6 and 12 months
facts.main_result: No significant difference in posterior ridge resorption between bars with and without distal extensions (12-month mean ratio 0.310 vs 0.381, p=0.236).
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflict of interest declared

facts.population: 40 disks of one CAD-CAM PMMA denture base resin (Polident)
facts.intervention: Milling with a new tungsten carbide bur set
facts.comparison: Milling with a used tungsten carbide bur set (250 PMMA crowns previously milled)
facts.main_result: New-bur specimens had higher Ra (about 1.3 vs 0.93 micrometer) and lower contact angle (70 vs 80 degrees) than used-bur specimens (P<.05); thermocycling lowered the contact angle of used-bur specimens to 66 degrees.

facts.population: 19 in vitro studies of 3D-printed resins (provisional, denture base, occlusal device, orthodontic, denture teeth, surgical guide)
facts.intervention: Factors affecting flexural strength (fillers, printing orientation, layer thickness, post-polymerization, rinsing)
facts.main_result: Most factors (fillers or nanofillers, printing orientation or angulation, layer thickness, post-polymerization time and temperature) significantly affected flexural strength; no meta-analysis was possible.

facts.population: 74 edentulous patients with mandibular overdentures retained by four titanium-zirconium mini implants (296 implants)
facts.intervention: Four Ti-Zr mini implants (Straumann Mini Implant System) retaining a mandibular overdenture, placed flapless or flapped and loaded immediately or delayed
facts.comparison: 2x2 factorial: immediate vs delayed loading and flapless vs flapped surgery
facts.main_result: 1-year implant survival/success was 100% with no major biological complications; mean marginal bone loss was 0.68 mm at 3 months and 0.89 mm at 1 year, slightly higher with flapless surgery.
materials_brands: Straumann Mini Implant System (Roxolid Ti-Zr, SLA)
facts.funding_coi: ITI grant 1447_2019; implants and components supplied by Institut Straumann AG; three authors received other Straumann/ITI funding
facts.limitations: Short 1-year timeframe; longer follow-up and patient-centered outcomes are needed.

facts.population: Edentulous patients treated 2006-2015 in a Dutch general practice with 2, 3 or 4 implants and a mandibular overdenture (295 treated)
facts.intervention: Two, three or four interforaminal implants with a bar-clip attachment and mandibular overdenture
facts.comparison: 2-implant vs 3-implant vs 4-implant groups (non-randomized)
facts.main_result: Cumulative implant survival was 100%, 99.1% and 97.8% in the 2-, 3- and 4-implant groups with mean bone loss of 0.53, 0.61 and 0.40 mm; satisfaction was high.
materials_brands: Dyna Helix implant system (Dyna Dental Engineering)
facts.funding_coi: No funding was acquired

materials_brands: LOCATOR R-Tx removable attachment system (ZEST Anchors)
