facts.key_finding: Manufacturer technique manual for the LOCATOR R-Tx overdenture attachment: components, abutment placement, direct and indirect processing of denture housings, reline, maintenance and cleaning; the housing is stated to pivot to treat up to 60 degrees of implant convergence or divergence without pre-angled abutments.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Product-specific procedural reference from the manufacturer; its performance claims are not independent evidence.

facts.population: 31 edentulous-maxilla patients aged 50+ with a dentate or implant-restored mandible
facts.intervention: 5-6 flaplessly placed one-piece mini dental implants with provisional denture, final overdenture connection at 6 months
facts.main_result: 164 of 204 MDIs (78.4%) were in situ at 3 years; OHIP-14 fell from 21.3 at baseline to 7.3 at final connection (p=0.006), improving less with multiple implant losses.
facts.funding_coi: MDIs provided by Southern Implants

facts.population: 18 patients with maxillary complete dentures opposing mandibular implant-retained overdentures and 4 with conventional dentures
facts.intervention: Mandibular two-implant (Ankylos) overdenture opposing a maxillary complete denture
facts.comparison: Conventional maxillary and mandibular complete dentures (4 patients)
outcomes: anterior maxillary bone volume change on CBCT at 1 year
facts.main_result: Anterior maxillary bone volume fell 7.25% with the overdenture versus 2.60% with conventional dentures (p=0.011).
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Universiti Teknologi MARA and Malaysian FRGS grant; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Pilot study with a very small control group because repeat CBCT in controls was deemed unethical

facts.population: 40 edentulous participants with maxillary complete dentures and mandibular two-implant overdentures
facts.intervention: CAD-CAM milled titanium bar with long distal extensions plus gold clip
facts.comparison: Retentive anchors with gold matrices
facts.main_result: At 1 year implant survival was 100% and peri-implant bone level change did not differ (p=.754); bite force, OHIP-EDENT and satisfaction index were equal, with subjective chewing better in the milled-bar group (p=.022).
facts.funding_coi: ITI research grant 767_2011; authors declare no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: No sample size calculation was possible because of lack of reference data.

facts.journal: Compendium of Continuing Education in Dentistry
facts.population: 67-year-old edentulous woman (single case)
facts.intervention: Two freestanding mandibular implants with a metal-reinforced overdenture on stock abutments and hinge-type resilient attachments, attachments incorporated in the laboratory

facts.population: Edentulous participants with maxillary denture complaints and insufficient bone volume, treated with sinus augmentation
facts.intervention: Maxillary bar overdenture on four posterior implants
facts.comparison: Maxillary bar overdenture on six posterior implants
facts.main_result: Implant survival was 100% (4 implants) vs 96.7% (6 implants); marginal bone loss 0.41 vs 0.70 mm; no significant group differences
facts.funding_coi: Unrestricted grant from Institut Straumann AG for the 1-year trial; no conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Loss of power for marginal bone change after 10 years, and university-based setting with selected participants
materials_brands: Straumann Standard SLA implants, 2.8 mm polished collar, 4.1 x 12 mm RN

facts.population: Edentulous maxilla participants with opposing mandibular two-implant overdentures (mean age 68.3 years)
facts.intervention: Four maxillary implants loaded asynchronously: two unsplinted cylindrical attachments, then the other two
facts.comparison: Two anterior (canine) versus two posterior (molar) implants carrying the overdenture, in a cross-over
facts.main_result: Implant survival after loading was 93.8% at a mean 3.1 years; denture survival 100%, denture success 95.8%; 23 of 24 preferred four implants
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the ITI; no conflict of interest

facts.population: In vitro studies of 3D-printed dental prosthetic materials (ceramics, polymers, metals)
facts.intervention: 3D additive manufacturing (AM) of prosthetic materials
facts.comparison: Subtractive milling and conventional processing
facts.main_result: Milling showed higher flexural strength than AM (Hedge g -3.88, 95% CI -7.20 to -0.58, P=.02); marginal discrepancy was similar

facts.intervention: Milled bar implant overdenture with OT Equator attachments and an internal cast metal framework
materials_brands: Vitapan Plus anterior and Lingoform posterior teeth

facts.main_result: Post selection depends on many factors including root length, tooth anatomy, remaining tooth structure and function; post length improves retention and stress distribution

facts.population: Wearers of mandibular free-end removable partial dentures
facts.intervention: Two 6 mm short implants bilaterally in mandibular molar sites with retentive ball abutments
facts.comparison: Non-retentive dome abutments (crossover)
facts.main_result: Implant survival 100% and success 90.9% at 12 months; mean bone loss 1.2 mm; 82% finally chose the ball abutment
facts.funding_coi: Innosuisse and SIC invent AG funding; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Small number of participants and short follow-up

materials_brands: Straumann LOCATOR FIXED housing and inserts
facts.key_finding: Manufacturer brochure for Straumann LOCATOR FIXED, which turns existing LOCATOR abutments into a fixed full-arch solution using a housing and PEEK inserts that correct up to 40 degrees of implant divergence.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Product marketing without study data; it gives insert selection by implant number and limits cantilevers to 1X A/P spread (0.5X for bruxers) but offers no outcome evidence.

materials_brands: ZEST Anchors LOCATOR implant, bar and root attachments
facts.key_finding: ZEST Anchors brochure presenting LOCATOR self-aligning pivoting overdenture attachments for implants, bars and roots, with customizable retention and a total height of 3.17 mm.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Marketing material without study data, so it gives no evidence of clinical outcomes.

facts.population: Five male cynomolgus monkeys with 4 implants per mandibular side
facts.intervention: Repetitive mechanical trauma on implants, with or without ligature-induced peri-implantitis
facts.comparison: Healthy implants without repetitive mechanical trauma
facts.main_result: Repetitive mechanical trauma showed no histologic effect on peri-implant bone loss in healthy or diseased implant sites
facts.funding_coi: Supported in part by Nobel Biocare

facts.population: Five adult Finnish sheep, 20 titanium implants placed in the forehead
facts.intervention: Horizontal loading of implants with orthodontic elastics (250 to 350 g) for 3 months
facts.main_result: No infection or bone loss around implants; histology showed firm bone-titanium interfaces under constant lateral force.
materials_brands: Straumann plasma-sprayed pure titanium implants, 4.5 mm long, 3.5 mm diameter
facts.funding_coi: Institut Straumann, Waldenburg, Switzerland

facts.main_result: Fracture healing depends on both host biology and the mechanical environment; NSAIDs, bisphosphonates, smoking, diabetes and age can impair it.
facts.funding_coi: No financial disclosures

facts.main_result: Mucositis can progress to peri-implantitis with circumferential bone loss while the implant stays osseointegrated; BOP, probing depth and radiographs are the sensitive diagnostic parameters and CIST is proposed for maintenance.

When strain falls below the resorption threshold osteocytes undergo apoptosis followed by bone resorption; loading maintains osteocyte viability and strains above the formation threshold release anabolic factors and drive bone formation.

facts.population: Periodontally treated, partially dentate patients with free-standing implant-supported FPDs
facts.intervention: Implant-supported FPDs with distal cantilever extensions (Astra Tech implants)
facts.comparison: FPDs without cantilever extensions
outcomes: Change in peri-implant bone level from FPD placement to 5 years
facts.main_result: Mean marginal bone loss was 0.4 mm over 5 years with no significant difference between FPDs with and without cantilevers; maxillary FPDs lost more bone than mandibular (0.6 vs 0.2 mm).
facts.sample_size: 50 FPDs in 45 patients (24 with, 26 without cantilever)

facts.population: Animal studies (dogs) of non-splinted titanium dental implants
facts.intervention: Occlusal overload on osseointegrated implants
facts.comparison: Implants without overload, with or without plaque control
outcomes: Radiographic and histologic distance from implant base to first bone-to-implant contact
facts.main_result: Two high-risk-of-bias trials: overload caused no tissue breakdown without plaque but, with plaque, increased peri-implant breakdown (PD change 5.3 mm; DIB 6.0 mm); overload tended to increase bone density.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Few studies, no RCTs, high risk of bias, heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis

facts.population: Human and animal studies on occlusal trauma, excessive occlusal forces, abfraction and gingival recession
facts.main_result: Occlusal trauma does not initiate periodontitis and only weakly, if at all, alters its progression; there is no credible evidence for abfraction as a cause of gingival recession.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Occlusal trauma can only be confirmed histologically, so clinical trials rely on surrogate indicators; heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis

facts.population: Six Labrador dogs with 45 titanium implants (TPS and SLA) in the mandible
facts.intervention: Gold crowns in supra-occlusal contact on implants for 8 months (excessive occlusal load) with plaque control
facts.comparison: Unloaded implants on the control side
facts.main_result: After 8 months of excessive occlusal load all implants stayed osseointegrated with no marginal bone loss versus unloaded implants (BIC 74% test vs 73% control).
materials_brands: ITI Dental Implant System (TPS and SLA implants), gold crowns

facts.population: 4 monkeys (Macaca fascicularis) with 5 Astra Tech titanium screw implants each in the mandible
facts.intervention: Fixed partial prosthesis in supra-occlusal contact causing lateral occlusal overload on 2 implants (18 months)
facts.comparison: Non-cleaned implants with cotton cord to promote plaque accumulation
facts.main_result: Plaque-accumulation implants stayed osseointegrated with 2.4 mm mean histologic bone loss; overloaded implants mostly became loose, with 2 losing osseointegration completely and 2 only apically.
facts.sample_size: 4 monkeys; 8 overloaded implants (6 histologically analysed) and plaque-accumulation implants
materials_brands: Astra Tech titanium screw implants (TiO2-blasted and machined)
Pallorag silver-palladium alloy fixed partial prosthesis
facts.limitations: Statistical analysis not performed because few overloaded implants were available

facts.population: Ten 18-month-old male Gottingen minipigs, 80 implants in maxilla and mandible
facts.intervention: Experimental implant design with high insertion torque (wide thread, limited marginal bone contact)
facts.comparison: Astra Tech OsseoSpeed 3.5S control implant
outcomes: Distance from shoulder to first bone-to-implant contact
facts.main_result: The experimental high-torque implant caused significantly more marginal bone loss than the control (first BIC 2.94 vs 1.7 mm), with excessive marginal strains suggesting osseocompression.

facts.journal: Journal of Investigative and Clinical Dentistry
facts.population: Peri-implant bone of osseointegrated dental implants under excessive occlusal load (14 animal and clinical studies)
facts.main_result: Evidence on excessive load on osseointegrated implants is limited and conflicting; overload may rarely cause loss of osseointegration, while functional load increases remodeling, BIC and bone density.
facts.limitations: No RCTs or meta-analyses available; evidence limited and conflicting

facts.population: Four beagle dogs with 32 machined titanium implants in the mandible
facts.intervention: Supra-occlusal contact (overloaded) versus infra-occlusal (unloaded) abutments, with or without ligature-induced peri-implant inflammation
facts.comparison: Unloaded implants and uninflamed (brushed) sides
facts.main_result: Overloading in healthy mucosa increased BIC% and slightly increased crestal bone resorption, while with inflammation overloading significantly increased thread exposure from bone loss.
materials_brands: Hi-Tec Implant machined titanium implants (3.75 x 10 mm)
facts.funding_coi: Funded by a Shauder grant
facts.limitations: Limited sample size; load was not quantified directly

facts.population: 38 partially edentulous patients (21-71 years) with 49 partial cantilever fixed prostheses on 100 implants
facts.intervention: Implant-supported partial fixed cantilever prostheses (mesial or distal cantilever) on ITI and Branemark implants
facts.comparison: Opposing dentition (natural teeth or tooth-supported fixed prostheses versus implant-supported fixed prostheses); mesial versus distal cantilever
facts.main_result: Seven years after loading, overall cumulative implant survival was 97% and prosthesis success 98%, with mesial cantilevers 97.1% versus distal 100%.

facts.journal: Medicina Oral, Patología Oral y Cirugía Bucal
facts.population: 75 potential implant sites in the posterior mandible from CT scans of 34 patients; used to build finite-element models
facts.intervention: Finite-element models with low/high cancellous-bone density, crestal cortical-bone density and thickness, loaded with 200 N oblique load on a Straumann implant
facts.comparison: Low vs high bone-density and thin vs thick cortical-bone models
outcomes: maximum von Mises equivalent strain in crestal cortical bone
maximum von Mises equivalent strain in cancellous bone
facts.main_result: Maximum strains in low-density cancellous-bone models were 1.56-2.62-fold (cortical) and 3.49-5.31-fold (cancellous) higher than in high-density models.
facts.sample_size: 75 implant sites in 34 patients (CT); finite-element models
materials_brands: Straumann threaded implant, 4.1 mm x 10 mm

facts.population: Literature on forces on oral implants and surrounding bone (animal experimental and clinical studies)
facts.main_result: Animal studies show occlusal load may increase marginal bone loss, but in clinical studies a causative relationship with overload has not been established.
facts.sample_size: 607 papers found in initial PubMed search
facts.limitations: No randomized controlled or prospective cohort studies were found; a small number of experimental animal studies underlies much of the knowledge.

facts.population: Five beagle dogs with 30 tissue-level implants (SLA and SLActive) in the mandible
facts.intervention: Excessive occlusal load on implants restored with a crown plus cantilever unit
facts.comparison: Single crown with stable occlusal contacts and non-loaded implants
outcomes: clinical parameters (BoP, attachment level, mucosal margin)
facts.main_result: Excessive load did not cause loss of osseointegration or significant clinical or radiographic changes, but SLA implants gained peri-implant bone density and technical complications were more frequent.
materials_brands: Straumann SLA and SLActive tissue-level implants (8 x 3.3 mm)
facts.funding_coi: Supported by ITI Foundation and Clinical Research Foundation; authors declare no conflict of interest

facts.population: Literature on early crestal bone loss around endosteal dental implants
facts.main_result: Reformation of biologic width, microgap at or below the crest, occlusal overload and implant crest module are the most likely causes of early implant bone loss; surgical trauma and peri-implantitis may also contribute.
facts.funding_coi: Partially supported by the University of Michigan Periodontal Graduate Student Research Fund
facts.limitations: Little evidence on the mechanism; no studies compare the possible causative factors, so randomized controlled trials are needed.

facts.population: Clinical and animal studies on osseointegrated oral implants subjected to overload
facts.intervention: Overload (e.g. supra-occlusal contacts)
facts.comparison: No overload
facts.main_result: Overload in uninflamed peri-implant tissue did not negatively affect osseointegration in animals, while with inflammation it increased plaque-induced bone resorption; clinical evidence was too biased to answer the question.
facts.sample_size: 726 titles screened; 41 full texts (16 clinical, 25 animal)
facts.funding_coi: Authors report no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: High risk of bias in many papers and lack of quantification of overload at the implant level

facts.population: Preclinical and clinical literature on occlusal overload and peri-implant bone loss
facts.main_result: Evidence does not support avoiding higher crown-to-implant ratios, cantilevers and non-splinted designs for fear of overload, and the impact of overload on peri-implantitis remains unknown.
facts.funding_coi: No funding; author declares no competing interests
facts.limitations: Non-systematic review; no randomized or prospective human trials exist on overload for ethical reasons

facts.population: Edentulous jaws of all stages of atrophy; series of 100 consecutive arches
facts.intervention: Complete arch immediate function with 4 implants (all-on-4) planned by a proposed site and jaw bone classification
outcomes: classification of edentulous jaw bone sites for immediate function
facts.main_result: A functional-descriptive classification (Class A to D mandible and maxilla) based on cortical bone fixation sites guides angled implant placement for immediate function and mostly avoids grafting.
facts.limitations: The minimum A/P spread acceptable for immediate loading has not been established

facts.population: Implant-supported fixed prostheses in edentulous maxilla or mandible (29 studies, 26 datasets)
facts.intervention: Different numbers of implants supporting a fixed prosthesis
facts.main_result: The majority of studies plan 4 to 6 implants per prosthesis, with average survival rates between 90% and 100% and similar outcomes regardless of implant number.
facts.funding_coi: Authors declare no conflict of interest

facts.population: Twenty adult male Japanese white rabbits with 80 implants in the femurs
facts.intervention: Abutment screw preload with recommended (35 Ncm) or high (70 Ncm) tightening torque
facts.comparison: Control implants without abutment, and temporary tightening group without preload
facts.main_result: Bone-to-implant contact, bone volume and bone area were significantly lower in recommended- and high-torque preload groups than in control and temporary-tightening groups.
materials_brands: Straumann Roxolid SLActive Bone Level implants (8 x 3.3 mm) and Narrow Connection Anatomic Straight abutments
facts.funding_coi: Partially supported by Straumann Japan; authors affirm no conflicts of interest

facts.population: Patients with osseointegrated dental implants (clinical human studies)
facts.intervention: Implant occlusal overload assessed by digital occlusal analysis and/or occlusal wear
facts.comparison: Absence of implant occlusal overloading
facts.main_result: Of 7 included studies, only one used a digital device to assess occlusal forces; four of seven reported a positive correlation between overload and crestal bone loss, and all had moderate to serious risk of bias.
facts.follow_up: At least 1 year after prosthetic loading in included studies
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: All included studies had moderate to serious overall risk of bias and methods for assessing overload were not standardized.

facts.main_result: Peri-implant mucositis is a host response like gingivitis, whereas peri-implantitis may differ from periodontitis in lesion extent, cell composition and progression rate.
facts.funding_coi: Unrestricted educational grant from Colgate; participants declared no conflicts of interest.

facts.main_result: Fracture healing is a complex physiological process involving a well-orchestrated series of biological events.

facts.population: 467 consecutive patients (500 jaws) treated with Branemark fixtures
facts.intervention: Standard, self-tapping and conical Branemark fixtures; effect of occlusal overload examined in fixed full prostheses and overdentures
facts.comparison: Standard versus self-tapping fixtures; with versus without overload factors
facts.main_result: Standard fixtures failed more often than self-tapping fixtures with no difference in bone loss; excessive bone loss or fixture loss correlated with lack of anterior contact, parafunction and opposing osseointegrated full prostheses.

facts.population: 130 patients with 193 edentulous arches restored with 4 (or 5) implants
facts.intervention: Immediately loaded full-arch implants (posterior tilted) with interim acrylic prostheses, then definitive CAD/CAM titanium-framework hybrid prostheses; cantilever length and AP spread measured
facts.comparison: CL/AP ratios of definitive versus interim prostheses
facts.main_result: Implant survival was 99.5% (770/774), mean CL/AP ratios were 0.84-0.90, and CL/AP ratio was not significantly associated with prosthetic repairs.
facts.funding_coi: Author denies any conflicts of interest; no funding stated
facts.limitations: Lack of recording of other clinical issues; AP-spread measurement accurate only to about 0.5 mm.

facts.population: 514 Japanese patients with 1535 implants in function for at least 4 years
facts.intervention: Analysis of systemic, intraoral and implant-related factors as risk indicators for marginal bone level change
outcomes: marginal bone level change (MBLC) on intraoral radiographs
facts.main_result: Mean annual MBLC was 0.048 mm; functional time, plaque control record >20%, Eichner C1-3, maxilla, cement-retained superstructure and keratinized mucosa width <2 mm significantly affected MBLC.
facts.funding_coi: Authors declare no conflicts of interest

facts.main_result: The evidence is weak and does not indicate that overload causes peri-implant bone loss except with inflammation; micromotion compromises osseointegration whereas efficient force transfer may stimulate bone formation.
facts.funding_coi: No additional funding; authors declare no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Overload has not been quantified at the implant level in the intra-oral setting.

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Osseointegrated dental implants in animal and human studies
facts.intervention: Static loading of implants (prosthesis misfit/passive fit, overload, orthodontic forces)
facts.comparison: Controls (human trials with or without controls; animal studies with controls)
facts.main_result: No apparent detrimental effect of static loading on osseointegrated implants across 36 studies (28 animal, 8 human).
facts.funding_coi: Authors reported no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: No randomized controlled trials in humans were found; only eight human case series or retrospective reviews.

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Four monkeys (Macaca fascicularis) with experimental implants
facts.intervention: Supraocclusal superstructures with excess occlusal height of 100, 180 and 250 µm on inflammation-free implants
outcomes: peri-implant bone level change on histology
facts.main_result: Bone resorption around implants tended to increase at 180 µm or more excess height, suggesting a threshold of about 180 µm.

facts.population: 10 adult New Zealand black rabbits (tibiae)
facts.intervention: Static (29.4 N transverse) or dynamic (14.7 N, 1 Hz, 2,520 cycles) loading of Brånemark implants for 14 days
facts.comparison: Unloaded control implant
outcomes: bone density lateral to the implant
facts.main_result: Dynamic loading produced crater-shaped marginal bone defects and significantly less peri-implant bone density (P<0.007), while static loading resembled unloaded controls.
facts.funding_coi: Nobel Biocare Scholarship Grant 1996 and a Flanders scientific-research grant

off_topic_reason: An orthopaedic review of long-bone fracture fixation and strain with no dental or maxillofacial content.

facts.journal: Acta Chirurgiae Orthopaedicae et Traumatologiae Cechoslovaca
facts.main_result: Fracture healing should be understood through tissue deformation (strain, gap movement divided by gap width) rather than fracture mobility alone.

facts.population: 98 bruxers identified among 2670 implant patients, plus a matched group of non-bruxers
facts.intervention: Bruxism (graded possible/probable/definite) in patients with implant-supported prostheses
facts.comparison: Matched group of non-bruxers
facts.main_result: The odds ratio of implant failure in bruxers versus non-bruxers was 2.71 (95% CI 1.25-5.88), with more mechanical complications in bruxers.
facts.sample_size: 98 bruxers of 2670 patients, matched with non-bruxers
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interests declared
facts.limitations: Other risk factors may also have influenced the results.

facts.population: Patients treated with dental implants at one specialist clinic in Malmo, Sweden; bruxers vs non-bruxers
facts.intervention: Dental implant placement; exposure variable was bruxism
facts.comparison: Bruxers versus non-bruxers
facts.main_result: Bruxism was a significant risk factor for implant failure (HR about 3.4; failure 13.0% in bruxers vs 4.6% in non-bruxers).
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Region Skane research funds, Swedish Research Council, Folktandvarden AB and CNPq; no conflicts declared

facts.population: 1,052 students at Wayne State University (544 men, 508 women, mean age 19 years)
facts.intervention: Questionnaire on present and past clenching or grinding, diurnal and nocturnal
outcomes: incidence of diurnal, nocturnal and combined bruxism
facts.main_result: 30.7% of the sample reported present or past bruxism; diurnal bruxism was more common than nocturnal, men reported more diurnal and women more nocturnal bruxism
facts.funding_coi: National Institute of Dental Research grant DE04536

facts.population: Patients with implant-supported cantilever fixed dental prostheses (ICFDPs) in five cohort studies
facts.intervention: Implant-supported cantilever fixed dental prostheses followed at least 5 years
facts.comparison: Short-span implant-supported end-abutment fixed dental prostheses (for bone level changes)
facts.main_result: Estimated 5- and 10-year ICFDP survival was 94.3% and 88.9%; veneer fracture and screw loosening were the most common complications
facts.sample_size: 5 studies; 420 implants and 180 ICFDPs (354 and 155 available for analysis)

facts.population: 14 participants missing 2 maxillary central incisors and 1 lateral incisor (6 men, 8 women, mean age 40 years)
facts.intervention: Implant-supported cantilever fixed partial denture (ICFPD), 2 implants per participant
facts.comparison: Implant-supported conventional fixed partial denture
facts.main_result: Marginal bone loss was significantly higher for the implant near the cantilever (1.8 mm at 2 years); stability, gingival and plaque indices did not differ
facts.funding_coi: Not funded by any institution
facts.limitations: Small sample size

facts.population: 30 patients with 34 FDPCs (31 SUCs and 3 FDPs) on 37 implants in posterior areas
facts.intervention: Screw-retained full-zirconia implant-supported FDPs with cantilever extension
facts.main_result: No implants lost; marginal bone levels (0.92 to 0.96 mm) and PPD (2.99 to 3.27 mm) did not change significantly; peri-implant mucositis in 22 cases
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the authors' own institution; no conflict of interest declared

facts.population: 21 participants missing a single tooth (except canine), abutment teeth
facts.intervention: Zirconia (Y-TZP) ceramic cantilever FDP retained by 2 complete crown abutments
facts.comparison: Metal ceramic cantilever FDP
facts.main_result: Survival was 100% in both groups; 6 complications in 5 participants (4 ZC, 2 MC); periodontal indices similar
facts.limitations: Exploratory pilot with small sample; P values exploratory

facts.population: 55 clinical cases of fixed complete implant-supported arch prostheses (3 to 8 implants)
facts.intervention: Calculation of maximum permissible cantilever length with the Skalak model under a 143 N vertical load
facts.comparison: Clinicians' optimal cantilever lengths
facts.main_result: Predicted satisfaction was 100%, 56%, 33%, 8% and 0% for 8 and 7, 6, 5, 4 and 3 implants; 98% of cases with AP spread above 11.1 mm were satisfied

facts.population: 192 partially edentulous patients with 454 implants in 2 included prospective cohort studies
facts.intervention: Implant-supported reconstructions at different crown-implant (C/I) ratios
facts.main_result: Survival was 94.1% for C/I ratio above 2; crestal bone loss seemed not influenced by C/I ratio except in one study
facts.limitations: Diversity among studies in data collection and study design

facts.population: Single-tooth, nonsplinted implant restorations in the posterior maxilla or mandible (8 studies)
facts.intervention: Restoration with high crown-to-implant ratio
facts.comparison: Similar restorations with a normal ratio
facts.main_result: Implant survival above 99% per year and peri-implant bone change below 0.1 mm per year; few complications

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Partially edentulous patients receiving at least 1 dental implant (15 studies)
facts.intervention: Higher crown-to-implant ratio (>1.5)
facts.comparison: Lower crown-to-implant ratio (<=1.5)
facts.main_result: No significant correlation between anatomical C/I ratio and survival (P = .905), marginal bone loss (P = .33) or prosthetic complications (P = .67)

facts.population: Four Macaca fascicularis monkeys with 5 screw-type titanium implants each in the mandible (20 implants)
facts.intervention: Excessive lateral occlusal load via supra-occlusal fixed partial prosthesis, or plaque accumulation via cotton cord
facts.comparison: Implants with plaque accumulation versus implants with excessive occlusal load
facts.main_result: 5 of 8 implants with excessive occlusal load lost osseointegration, whereas none with plaque accumulation did, although they lost 1.8 mm of bone on average after 18 months.
materials_brands: Astra Tech screw-type commercially pure titanium implants (TiO2-blasted and machined)
facts.funding_coi: Danish Medical Research Council and Astra Tech AB, Sweden

facts.population: Adjacent dental implants (literature on splinted vs nonsplinted restorations)
facts.intervention: Splinted restorations of adjacent implants
facts.comparison: Nonsplinted (single-unit) restorations
facts.main_result: No evidence that either splinted or nonsplinted design gives higher implant survival; splinted restorations have fewer technical complications
facts.limitations: Very weak evidence available to support either choice

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Patients with three adjacent external-hex implants in the posterior maxilla
facts.intervention: Implants splinted with cemented metal-ceramic restorations (left maxilla)
facts.comparison: Nonsplinted cemented single crowns (right maxilla)
facts.main_result: At 10 years median bone loss was 1.2 mm splinted vs 1.3 mm nonsplinted (P = .0042); the 0.1 mm difference was judged not clinically meaningful.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.journal: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.population: Photoelastic block model with three implants
facts.intervention: Splinted cement-retained restorations at increasing crown-to-implant ratios and crown height spaces, loaded at 30 degrees
facts.comparison: 1:1 crown-to-implant ratio group
facts.main_result: Buccal microstrain rose from 1,911.65 to 3,252.06 as C/I went from 1:1 to 1:1.5 (P<.001); at 1:1.75 and 1:2 the abutment screw fractured and crowns dislodged.
facts.limitations: Conclusions are limited to this biomechanical model
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare external hex implants 3.8 x 12 mm

facts.population: 660 partially edentulous patients with 1655 Brånemark implants loaded with fixed prostheses
facts.intervention: Implants supporting single crowns, implant-tooth connected or free-standing fixed partial prostheses
facts.comparison: Single crowns vs implant-tooth connected vs free-standing fixed partial prostheses
facts.main_result: No significant difference in bone level change among the three restoration types; estimated loss was 1.23 mm/year in the first 6 months then 0.025 mm/year.
outcomes: effect of jaw, site, membrane or graft, dehiscence, prosthesis material

facts.population: 660 partially edentulous patients with 1956 Brånemark system implants
facts.intervention: Single crowns, implant-tooth connected and free-standing fixed partial prostheses
facts.comparison: Implant-tooth connected vs free-standing prostheses
facts.main_result: Cumulative 16-year survival was 91.4% for implants and 95.8% for restorations; implant-tooth connected 93.6% vs free-standing 97.2% from loading.
facts.limitations: Exploratory study without multiple-testing correction; non-splinting finding needs replication

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: One 25-year-old woman with a failed implant at the maxillary left lateral incisor and lost papilla
facts.intervention: Vertical ridge augmentation, implant, papilla CTG with EMD, zirconia abutment with convex subgingival contour

facts.key_finding: Peri-implant pink esthetics depends on gingival biotype, papilla height, three-dimensional implant position, buccal bone support and gentle flap handling. Prevention (correct position, GBR contour augmentation, soft-tissue grafts for thin biotype) is favoured because papilla reconstruction and recession coverage at implants are unpredictable.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Plan implant position, bone contour augmentation and soft-tissue thickness in the esthetic zone up front, since repairing papilla or recession around implants later is unreliable.

facts.main_result: Rebuilding the interimplant papilla remains unpredictable; no technique is recommended over another because no long-term studies exist.

facts.journal: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.population: Patients with single tooth implants, immediate provisionalization or delayed 2-stage
facts.intervention: Immediate provisionalization of single implants
facts.comparison: Delayed 2-stage approach
facts.main_result: No difference in papilla or bone levels between immediate and delayed protocols; vertical distance from contact point to bone, especially to adjacent tooth bone, predicted papilla score.
facts.funding_coi: Grants from Nobel Biocare, Zimmer Dental, a university chair and the AAOMS Foundation

facts.population: 26 patients with nonadjacent missing teeth in the esthetic zone
facts.intervention: Curved (grooved) abutment
facts.comparison: Conventional divergent abutment
facts.main_result: No significant PES or VAS differences between curved and divergent abutments at baseline or 1 year; PES and VAS correlated significantly.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest; Nobel Biocare supplied implants and abutments free

facts.population: 48 patients with implant-supported fixed prostheses; 96 implant-implant and 80 tooth-implant interproximal sites
facts.intervention: Measurement of vertical (contact point to bone crest) and horizontal (inter-implant or tooth-implant) distances against papilla presence
facts.main_result: Papilla was absent 100% of the time at 2-2.5 mm lateral spacing and mostly present at 3-4 mm; ideal contact-point-to-bone distance was 3 mm between implants and 3-5 mm tooth-implant.
facts.follow_up: fixed prostheses in function 18 months to 6 years

facts.population: Patients with deficient interdental papillae (213 participants, 696 sites) in clinical studies
facts.intervention: Injection of hyaluronic acid gel into the deficient interdental papilla
facts.comparison: Mostly before-after (uncontrolled); some RCTs used saline, HA plus chitosan or a calcium hydroxide filler
facts.main_result: Single-arm meta-analysis found complete papilla reconstruction in 47% (CI 35-59%) and partial reconstruction in 49% (CI 40-59%) of sites after HA injection.
facts.funding_coi: No competing interests; MSc scholarship for one reviewer from CAPES
facts.limitations: Short-term evidence, mostly uncontrolled studies; further long-term controlled studies needed

facts.population: Three patients (cases 1-3) with maxillary single-tooth implant sites and soft tissue deficiency
facts.intervention: Modified roll technique: papilla-sparing incisions and a pedicle connective tissue graft rolled facially without sutures on the graft, with implant placement
facts.main_result: Combined PES and WES ranged from 16 to 20 at 24 months versus 14 to 18 at restoration delivery, with mean PES 9.33 and WES 8.33.
facts.limitations: The technique may initially be technique-sensitive.

facts.population: One 23-year-old woman missing maxillary right central and lateral incisors, restored with two adjacent implants
facts.intervention: Interimplant papilla reconstruction at second-stage surgery by joining two elevated connective tissue pedicle flaps
facts.main_result: The reconstructed papilla was still shorter than on the contralateral side, but the area refilled with papilla at 1 year after proximal modification of the crowns.
materials_brands: NobelProcera angulated screw channel zirconia crowns
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the Science and Technology Department of Sichuan Province
facts.limitations: The technique does not address vertical bone resorption and needs adequate keratinized tissue.

facts.journal: The Journal of Practical Periodontics and Aesthetic Dentistry (submitted manuscript)
facts.population: Maxillary anterior interproximal sites bordered by teeth, implants and pontics (clinical data over five years plus the 1998 data)
facts.intervention: Re-analysis of the height of bone to papilla tip at interproximal sites for each tooth/implant/pontic combination
facts.comparison: Six restorative classes (tooth-tooth, tooth-pontic, pontic-pontic, tooth-implant, implant-pontic, implant-implant)
outcomes: predictably achievable papilla height from the most coronal interproximal bone
facts.main_result: Achievable soft tissue height above the interproximal bone differs by class, from 3.5 mm between two implants to 6.5 mm between tooth and pontic.
facts.follow_up: five years of added clinical data

facts.population: Literature on interdental and interimplant papillae from the last 30 years
facts.intervention: Review of techniques to create or maintain interdental/interimplant papillae, plus the authors' esthetic triangle approach
facts.main_result: Bone support is the foundation for papilla; bone augmentation, soft tissue grafts and esthetic restorations are used, and an esthetic triangle of bone volume, soft tissue thickness and restorations is proposed.
facts.funding_coi: Partially supported by the University of Michigan Periodontal Graduate Student Research Fund; no financial interests declared

facts.journal: Journal of Health and Allied Sciences NU
facts.population: Literature on peri-implant and interdental papilla (review, articles and case reports)
facts.intervention: Narrative review of limitations of papilla preservation, affecting factors and methods to maintain or augment inter-implant papilla
facts.main_result: Among contributing factors, crestal bone levels play a major role in the presence of peri-implant papilla; surgical techniques and implant design changes such as platform switching are used to preserve it.

facts.population: 9 partially edentulous patients (mean age 65) with 23 immediately restored implants
facts.intervention: Computer-assisted flapless guided implant surgery with premade immediate screw-retained provisional restorations
outcomes: distance from contact point to bone
facts.main_result: Papilla fill was 91% between implants and 71% between implant and tooth, with bone mostly above the platform at about 545 days.

facts.population: Anterior implant sites needing peri-implant soft tissue augmentation (literature review)
facts.intervention: Soft tissue grafting (free gingival graft, subepithelial connective tissue graft, roll flap, envelope flap) around anterior implants
outcomes: peri-implant soft tissue thickness and contour
facts.main_result: Soft tissue augmentation techniques can optimize anterior implant esthetics, but the need for them remains controversial and lacks literature support; envelope technique gave a mean 0.8 mm mucosal thickness gain.
facts.funding_coi: Authors declare no conflict of interests
facts.limitations: Need for soft tissue augmentation lacks literature support; long-term clinical trials needed

facts.population: 30 patients, 288 interproximal sites (anterior, premolar and molar)
facts.intervention: Probing the distance from the base of the contact point to the crest of bone and recording papilla presence or absence
outcomes: presence or absence of the interproximal papilla
facts.main_result: Papilla was present almost 100% of the time at 5 mm or less from contact point to bone crest, 56% at 6 mm and 27% at 7 mm or more.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 17 nonsmoking periodontitis patients with one deep intrabony defect and a narrow interproximal space
facts.intervention: Papilla amplification flap combined with titanium-reinforced e-PTFE membranes for guided tissue regeneration
facts.main_result: Clinical attachment gain was 4.7 mm and probing depth reduction 6.3 mm at 1 year; primary closure was obtained in 100% of cases and maintained in 65% at 6 weeks.

facts.population: Illustrative clinical cases needing implant placement or augmentation in the esthetic zone
facts.intervention: Papillae-sparing incisions with a pedicle flap for implant placement and soft- or hard-tissue augmentation
facts.main_result: Papillae-sparing incisions give access to bone for implants and grafting without inducing recession of adjacent papillae.

facts.population: Adjacent implants in 33 patients from five private offices
facts.intervention: Probing of papilla height from crest of bone between two adjacent implants
facts.main_result: Mean papilla height between two adjacent implants was 3.4 mm (range 1-7 mm).

facts.population: Published in vitro and in vivo studies on PEEK CAD-CAM dental prostheses
facts.intervention: Literature review of PEEK for CAD-CAM fabricated dental prostheses
facts.main_result: PEEK is a viable alternative for CAD-CAM fixed and removable prostheses, but clinical data are scarce.
facts.funding_coi: Not funded; no competing interests
facts.limitations: Only a few clinical studies were identified, so long-term performance is unknown.

facts.population: Patients with peri-implantitis-affected implants
facts.intervention: Flap reflection, surface decontamination, EMD or PDGF, and GBR with bone graft and absorbable membrane and/or connective tissue graft
facts.main_result: 98.8% survival; BoP eliminated in 91%; probing depth reduced 5.10 mm and bone gain 1.77 mm on average.
facts.limitations: Randomized controlled trials and histological studies are still needed.

facts.intervention: Antibiotics and surgical debridement with autogenous bone and a collagen membrane
facts.comparison: Bovine-derived xenograft with collagen membrane
facts.main_result: Bovine xenograft gave more radiographic bone fill than autogenous bone at 12 months, though success of both was limited.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by BIOMET 3i; authors declare no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Success of both regenerative procedures was limited.

facts.population: 24 partially dentate patients with moderate to advanced peri-implantitis
facts.intervention: Anti-infective surgical protocol: open flap debridement, implant surface decontamination, systemic amoxicillin and metronidazole
facts.main_result: 100% implant survival at 12 months; all implants had mean PD below 5 mm, 47% were BoP negative, 92% had stable or gained bone.

facts.population: 29 patients with one implant with peri-implant mucositis
facts.intervention: Non-surgical debridement plus 0.5% chlorhexidine gel for 4 weeks
facts.comparison: Non-surgical debridement plus placebo gel
facts.main_result: Adjunctive chlorhexidine gel gave no added benefit over mechanical cleansing; 38% of implants had complete BOP resolution at 3 months.
facts.funding_coi: ITI research grant and Clinical Research Foundation; no conflict of interest

facts.population: Titanium and zirconium disks contaminated with a six-species high-adherence biofilm; human gingival fibroblasts
facts.intervention: Decontamination with titanium curette, ultrasonic scaler, glycine and erythritol air-polishing, Er:YAG laser, CHX, PVI, doxycycline, NaOCl
facts.comparison: Untreated control disks
facts.main_result: Air-polishing, ultrasonic scaler and Er:YAG laser reduced biofilm activity with favorable cytocompatibility, while chemical agents were cytotoxic.
facts.funding_coi: Oral Reconstruction Foundation grant; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: In vitro design only

facts.population: 117 patients with implant-supported restorations (450 implants) treated 2001-2013 at a university clinic
facts.intervention: Association of smoking history and patient/implant variables with peri-implant status
facts.comparison: Never-smokers versus former and current smokers
facts.main_result: Smoke intensity (>23 pack-years) was associated with higher peri-implantitis risk; quitting more than 21 years earlier gave lower risk.
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflict of interest

facts.population: 192 implants explanted due to peri-implantitis from 161 patients in 12 dental offices
facts.intervention: Measurement of bone loss at explantation using explants and radiographs
facts.main_result: Mean relative bone loss at explantation was 66.2%, higher in the mandible and for shorter implants.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared; Nobel offices received replacement implants
facts.limitations: Highly selective sample.

facts.population: 18 healthy volunteers wearing intraoral maxillary splints with material discs; human gingival fibroblasts in vitro
facts.intervention: 24 h intraoral wear of splints carrying discs of eight implant materials (zirconia, noble alloy coatings, Pagalinor, hydroxyapatite, TiZr, TAN, TiGr4)
facts.comparison: Titanium zirconium as the reference material against the other seven materials
facts.main_result: Noble metal alloys (AgPt, AgAuPd, Pagalinor) had less biofilm mass and CFU than titanium or zirconia, with zirconia highest (9.1-fold biofilm mass and 18.5-fold CFU versus AgPt).
facts.sample_size: 18 volunteers, two runs, two discs of each of 8 materials per run
facts.funding_coi: Discs provided by Straumann AG; authors declare no competing interests

facts.population: Patients with at least one dental implant with peri-implantitis (26 articles reporting 20 investigations)
facts.intervention: Surgical treatment of peri-implantitis: access flap, resective, reconstructive and combined approaches
facts.comparison: Reconstructive versus access flap versus resective surgery; with versus without barrier membrane
facts.main_result: Reconstructive surgery gave significantly less mucosal recession than access flaps (WMD -1.35 mm), while resective surgery led to about 1.2 mm of recession and combined approaches the most (1.97 mm).
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded for the EAO consensus conference; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: None of the included studies had low risk of bias, few comparisons were available for WMD, and heterogeneity was significant.

facts.population: Patients with implant-supported reconstructions placed in 2003 in Sweden, examined 9 years later
facts.intervention: Clinical examination (probing pocket depth, bleeding on probing) at 9 years tested as a screening test for history of bone loss
facts.main_result: Each additional mm of PPD corresponded to 0.30 mm more bone loss; BoP sensitivity for bone loss >2 mm was 80.9% with 42.2% specificity, whereas PPD sensitivity was low.
facts.sample_size: 1,578 implants in 427 patients with baseline radiographs
facts.funding_coi: Grants from the Swedish Social Insurance Agency, Swedish Research Council, TUA and the Swedish Dental Society; some authors report personal fees or grants from implant companies outside the submitted work

facts.population: Patients with peri-implantitis (7 human clinical trials) and 2 animal studies in beagle dogs
facts.intervention: Lasers (CO2 or Er:YAG) for peri-implantitis implant surface detoxification, surgical or non-surgical
facts.main_result: Lasers gave the same probing depth reduction as conventional decontamination for non-surgical therapy (WMD 0.00 mm, 95% CI -0.18 to 0.19).
facts.sample_size: 9 studies (7 human clinical trials, 2 animal studies)
facts.funding_coi: Partially supported by the University of Michigan Periodontal Graduate Student Research Fund; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Research on lasers for peri-implantitis is inadequate and the evidence is short-term.

facts.population: Thirty subjects with peri-implantitis treated by access flap surgery
facts.intervention: Supportive peri-implant care with ultrasonic PEEK tip plus glycine powder air polishing every 3 months
facts.comparison: Same ultrasonic instrumentation with rubber cup and polishing paste
facts.main_result: After 12 months PD changed -0.84 mm in the air-polishing test group versus +0.18 mm in controls (p<.001); healthy tissues were present at 83% of implants overall (87% vs 80%, p=.255).
materials_brands: EMS Instrument PI PEEK tip; Perio AIR-flow and Airflow Master Piezon (EMS)
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded by the ETEP Research Group; no conflict of interest

facts.population: Patients with advanced peri-implantitis combined supra- and intrabony defects (24 patients, 26 defects at 24 months)
facts.intervention: Access flap, granulation tissue removal and implantoplasty, then surface decontamination with Er:YAG laser, plus natural bone mineral and collagen membrane
facts.comparison: Plastic curets + cotton pellets + sterile saline for surface debridement/decontamination
facts.main_result: At 24 months Er:YAG laser did not give significantly higher BOP reduction (75.0% vs 54.9%) or CAL gain (1.0 vs 1.2 mm) than plastic curets, and CAL was not significantly different from baseline in either group.
facts.funding_coi: In part funded by Geistlich Biomaterials; materials provided by Elexxion AG and Geistlich; first author received lecture fees from Geistlich

facts.population: Published systematic reviews on dental implant failure and survival (748 found, 149 analyzed)
facts.intervention: Narrative synthesis of reviews on implant design, surface, augmentation, abutment connection and material
facts.main_result: True dental implant failure rates are likely higher than published, and roughened collars, microthreads and platform switching maintain bone while augmentation does not raise success rates.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest

facts.population: Nine cynomolgus monkeys with ligature-induced peri-implant mucositis around ITI titanium implants
facts.intervention: Mechanical cleansing alone, or mechanical cleansing with 0.12% chlorhexidine irrigation and 0.2% CHX gel, for two months
facts.comparison: Untreated control group
facts.main_result: Mechanical therapy alone or with chlorhexidine resolved mucositis clinically and histologically, with no difference in PD reduction between them (group A had more recession and less CAL gain than B).

facts.population: Dogs with implants having exchangeable intraosseous cylinders in the mandible and ligature-induced peri-implantitis
facts.intervention: Three decontamination modalities (cylinder exchanged, sprayed in situ with saline, removed, cleansed and steam-sterilized) on machined, SLA or TPS surfaces
facts.comparison: Pristine exchanged cylinder (T1) and surface types compared with each other
facts.main_result: In situ saline cleansing (T2) gave the highest BIC and SLA surfaces the highest BIC (better than machined); bone crest height did not differ by implant type.

facts.population: Titanium dental implants inoculated with a six-species subgingival biofilm
facts.intervention: Direct current of 0.75, 1.5 and 3 V (anodic) and -0.75, -1.5 and -3 V (cathodic) for 5 min in a three-electrode system
facts.comparison: Untreated biofilm and the different voltages and polarities against each other
facts.main_result: 3 V and -3 V significantly reduced total live bacteria from 3.15x10^6 to 1.85x10^5 and 2.92x10^4 per mL; F. nucleatum was most affected; 0.75 V and -0.75 V had no effect.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by an ITI grant; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Effects inside the abutment chamber were not examined, qPCR gives only an estimate of live bacteria, and only direct current was tested.

facts.population: 79 treated-periodontitis patients (moderate or high IDRA risk) with implant-supported single crowns or FDPs, at least 5 years in function
facts.intervention: Retrospective calculation of Implant Disease Risk Assessment (IDRA) risk at restoration delivery, related to peri-implantitis at most recent follow-up
facts.comparison: moderate versus high IDRA-risk patients
outcomes: odds ratio high vs moderate risk
facts.main_result: AUC of IDRA risk category for peri-implantitis was 0.613; peri-implantitis occurred in 12% at moderate and 27% at high risk (OR 2.727, not significant).
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the authors' own institution; no conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Retrospective design, low patient number and no low-risk IDRA group (selection bias).

facts.main_result: Peri-implantitis is best diagnosed with 2017 World Workshop case definitions; smoking, diabetes, periodontitis history and poor maintenance are key risk factors; mucositis responds to non-surgical therapy while peri-implantitis generally needs surgery (OFD, APF, GBR).
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; authors declare no conflict of interest

facts.population: 21 patients with 21 implants with advanced peri-implantitis (combined supra- and intrabony defects) at 4 years
facts.comparison: Plastic curets + cotton pellets + sterile saline decontamination
facts.main_result: At 48 months CPS sites tended to show larger BOP (85.2% vs 71.6%) and CAL (1.5 vs 1.2 mm) reductions than ERL, but outcomes were not influenced by decontamination method.
facts.sample_size: 21 patients (21 implants) at 4 years; 32 patients at baseline
facts.funding_coi: Long-term follow-up funded by authors' own department; materials supplied by Elexxion and Geistlich; F. Schwarz received lecture fees from Geistlich
facts.limitations: Small number of patients, only descriptive statistics.

outcomes: diagnostic value of BOP for peri-implantitis
long-term biologic complications at augmented sites
implant survival in geriatric/systemically compromised patients

facts.population: 32 partially edentulous patients with advanced peri-implantitis (38 combined supra- and intra-bony defects)
facts.intervention: Flap surgery, granulation tissue removal and implantoplasty, then Er:YAG laser surface decontamination, with natural bone mineral and collagen membrane
facts.comparison: Plastic curets + cotton pellets + sterile saline decontamination
facts.funding_coi: Partly funded by Geistlich Biomaterials; materials provided by Elexxion and Geistlich; no conflict of interest declared

facts.intervention: Introduction of the Implant Disease Risk Assessment (IDRA), an eight-vector functional diagram estimating a patient's risk of peri-implantitis
facts.main_result: The IDRA combines eight evidence-based parameters and may be useful for identifying individuals at risk of developing peri-implantitis; it requires validation.
facts.limitations: The tool requires validation through retrospective or prospective studies in multiple settings.

facts.population: Partially dentate patients with a history of treated periodontitis receiving dental implants
facts.intervention: Dental implants placed in patients treated for periodontitis
facts.comparison: Periodontally healthy patients
facts.main_result: Implants in treated periodontitis patients had more biological complications and lower success and survival (79.22-100% vs 91.67-100%) than in periodontally healthy patients.
facts.limitations: High heterogeneity prevented meta-analysis; conclusions limited by strength of evidence.

facts.population: 18 cpTi cylindrical screw implants (4 x 13 mm, external hex, Zimmer Biomet)
facts.intervention: Implantoplasty of the coronal 6 mm with tungsten carbide burs or diamond sonic tips, each followed by Arkansas finishing
facts.comparison: Untreated control implants; burs versus sonic tips
facts.main_result: Sonic diamond tips caused less material loss than burs but took longer (860 vs 453 s with finishing); fracture resistance did not differ from burs or controls (1.65 vs 1.51 vs 1.66 kN).
materials_brands: Komet tungsten carbide burs H379.310.023 and diamond sonic tips SF878K
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

facts.population: 180 stained implants (Replace Select Straight 4.3 x 13 mm) in resin peri-implant defect models of 30, 60 and 90 degrees
facts.intervention: Surface decontamination for 2 min with air powder abrasion (glycine powder), sonic scaler with steel tip, or curette
facts.comparison: Curette versus sonic scaler versus air powder abrasion across three defect angulations
outcomes: percent residual stain on implant surface
facts.main_result: Air powder abrasion cleaned best (residual color 0.13-8.03%) versus sonic scaler (11.4-19.69%) and curette (48.1-57.13%) in all defect angles, with no SEM surface damage.
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare Replace Select Straight implants
Perio-Mate air powder unit with glycine powder (NSK)

facts.journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
facts.population: 28 patients with 32 implants with peri-implantitis infrabony defects suitable for regenerative surgery
facts.intervention: Regenerative surgery with Bio-Oss xenograft, resorbable collagen membrane and hydrogen peroxide surface detoxification, prosthesis removed or maintained
facts.comparison: Prosthesis maintained versus removed after regenerative surgery
facts.main_result: Regenerative treatment gave similar bone gain in both groups; success did not depend on removing the prosthesis.
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest

facts.population: Partially edentulous subjects previously treated with implant-supported fixed dental prostheses
facts.intervention: Recall examination of existing implant-supported fixed prostheses (clinical, radiographic, questionnaires)
facts.comparison: Cement-retained vs screw-retained and short-span vs long-span prostheses
facts.main_result: Cumulative implant survival was 99.1%, peri-implantitis affected 5% and mucositis 84.1% of implants; mucositis was more likely with cement-retained (OR 6.8) and short-span prostheses (OR 2.3).
facts.funding_coi: Authors declare no financial interest in companies whose materials are included

facts.population: Patients with implants placed in a university setting, 83 patients with 168 implants analysed
facts.intervention: Radiographic measurement of restoration emergence angle and profile in bone-level and tissue-level implants
facts.comparison: Emergence angle >30 vs <=30 degrees; convex vs concave profile
facts.main_result: In bone-level implants peri-implantitis prevalence was 31.3% with emergence angle >30 degrees versus 15.1% with <=30 degrees (p = .04); no such correlation in tissue-level implants.
facts.sample_size: 96 patients with 225 implants (83 patients, 168 implants analysed)
facts.funding_coi: University of Washington School of Dentistry research fund; no conflicts of interest

facts.population: Patients with peri-implantitis treated surgically, from 17 long-term studies
facts.intervention: Surgical therapy of peri-implantitis with at least 5 years follow-up
facts.main_result: Mean long-term disease resolution after surgical peri-implantitis therapy was 58.6%, bone loss arrest 69.6%, retreatment need 27.2% and implant survival 88.6%.
facts.funding_coi: Conflict of interest statement: none

facts.population: 85 patients with peri-implantitis (cases) and 69 patients with healthy implants (controls)
facts.intervention: Submucosal peri-implant microbial sampling analysed by culturing techniques
facts.comparison: Patients with only healthy peri-implant conditions
facts.main_result: Peri-implantitis was associated with P. gingivalis, P. intermedia, T. forsythia and F. nucleatum, most strongly P. intermedia (OR 15.1) and T. forsythia (OR 13.3).
facts.funding_coi: Two authors declare stock ownership of LabOral International B.V. and LabOral Diagnostics; others none

facts.population: Observational studies on peri-implantitis, healthy implants and periodontitis (26 included)
facts.intervention: Systematic review of microbial biofilm profiles and microbiomes
facts.comparison: Healthy implants or periodontitis
facts.main_result: Peri-implantitis is a heterogeneous mixed infection with periodontopathic microorganisms and uncultivable anaerobic rods; sequencing of the entire microbiome improves identification.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the authors' institution (El Bosque University); no conflicts of interest

facts.population: Ten systemically healthy non-smokers with a history of periodontitis
facts.intervention: 16S rRNA high-throughput sequencing of plaque samples from a peri-implantitis implant and periodontally healthy dental sites
facts.comparison: Healthy dental sites in the same individuals
facts.main_result: Diseased peri-implant sites were less diverse than healthy sites; Prevotella and Porphyromonas discriminated disease, Actinobacillus and Streptococcus health.

facts.population: Systemically healthy human subjects with at least one osseointegrated dental implant
facts.intervention: Peri-implantitis (exposure), bacterial presence/count in submarginal biofilm
facts.comparison: Peri-implant health or mucositis
facts.main_result: Peri-implantitis was associated with S. epidermidis (OR 10.28), F. nucleatum (OR 7.83), T. denticola (OR 6.11), T. forsythia (OR 4.25), P. intermedia (OR 3.79) and P. gingivalis (OR 2.46).
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest and no specific funding
facts.limitations: Only 12 studies, all at moderate/high risk of bias, limiting external validity

facts.population: Clinical studies of reconstructive therapy of peri-implantitis defects
facts.intervention: Factors and techniques contributing to minimal invasiveness in reconstructive peri-implantitis treatment
facts.main_result: Most minimally invasive flap techniques were case reports, with no controlled or randomized trials showing superiority over conventional access.
facts.funding_coi: Open access funding by Universitat Bern; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Controlled or randomized trials are difficult to conduct because defects are not comparable

facts.population: 47 peri-implantitis patients, 158 eligible peri-implantitis implants
facts.intervention: CBCT classification of peri-implantitis defect morphology and severity
outcomes: associated patient, implant and site variables
facts.main_result: Class Ib was the most prevalent defect (55%) and moderate the most frequent severity (50.6%); smoking, prosthesis type and distance to adjacent implant related to severity.
facts.funding_coi: FEDICOM Foundation

facts.population: Expert consensus meeting of 96 clinicians and researchers, based on two systematic reviews
facts.intervention: Implant neck (collar design/surface) and abutment material characteristics
facts.comparison: Rough vs machined collar; titanium vs zirconia abutments
facts.main_result: Marginal bone levels were mainly influenced by the rough microstructure of the implant neck, not by abutment material; titanium abutments had higher bleeding on probing than zirconia.
facts.sample_size: 96 experts; two systematic reviews (13 publications, 608 implants for abutment material)
facts.funding_coi: Organized and supported by the Oral Reconstruction Foundation, Basel

facts.population: 37 systemically healthy adults with peri-implantitis (one target implant/site per patient)
facts.intervention: Non-surgical treatment plus systemic amoxicillin and metronidazole
facts.comparison: Non-surgical treatment alone
facts.main_result: Antibiotics group had a higher mean PIPD reduction at 12 weeks (2.28 vs 1.47 mm), not statistically significant; only 2 implants had a successful outcome.
materials_brands: EMS ultrasonic devices with PEEK fiber tip (PI instrument)
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest; funded by the authors' university departments (ACTA)
facts.limitations: Local etiological factors such as implant positioning, excess cement and keratinized gingiva were not evaluated.

facts.population: 39 patients with one implant with mild to moderate peri-implantitis in five specialist clinics
facts.intervention: Debridement with an oscillating chitosan brush
facts.comparison: Debridement with titanium curettes
facts.main_result: No significant difference in PPD and BI changes between brush and curette at 6 months; disease eradication in 9.5% (brush) vs 5.9% (curette).
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the Research Council of Norway and university grants; brush inventor holds the patent and two authors are shareholders in Labrida AS

facts.population: 60 dyed implants (30 apically tapered, 30 fully tapered) in plastic models with porcine soft tissue
facts.intervention: Cleaning for 150 s with curette, ultrasonic scaler or air powder waterjet with erythritol powder
facts.comparison: Curette as control therapy; two implant designs compared
facts.main_result: Cleaned surface ranged from 17.1% (FTAP, curette) to 45.5% (ATAP, air powder waterjet); titanium residues were highest with curette and near zero with waterjet.
materials_brands: Airflow One with Airflow Powder Plus (erythritol), EMS
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the researchers' institution; implants provided by Straumann; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: No treatment modality removed more than 50% of the surface in either design; model lacks naturally matured deposits and vital soft tissue.

facts.population: 43 patients diagnosed with peri-implantitis who underwent peri-implant surgery
facts.intervention: Surgical treatment of peri-implantitis, with OHIP-14 recorded before and after
facts.main_result: OHIP-14 scores were low and unchanged from baseline (7.2) to 36 months (7.0), with no significant changes.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the Faculty of Dentistry, University of Oslo; no conflicts of interest

facts.intervention: Proposed three-type treatment-driven classification of facial peri-implant marginal mucosa defects with prosthetic and surgical management recommendations
facts.main_result: Facial PMMDs are classified into three types by interproximal bone and papillary height loss; a bilaminar coronally advanced flap with connective tissue graft is advised as primary surgical modality, with prosthetic correction when needed.
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Literature on surgical management of single-tooth PMMDs is scant and dominated by case reports and case series.

facts.population: Published literature on peri-implantitis prevention, histopathology and therapeutics (214 studies retrieved)
facts.main_result: Peri-implantitis incidence is sustained and concerning, with no predictable treatment protocol; risk assessment, surgical/restorative expertise and strict maintenance are key.
facts.sample_size: 214 studies retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science and Science Direct
facts.funding_coi: No specific grant funding

facts.population: Published literature on regenerative surgical treatment of peri-implantitis bone defects (857 PubMed records screened)
facts.main_result: Regenerative techniques improve clinical and radiographic parameters, but no grafting material, membrane or decontamination method is shown superior; defect morphology is a key outcome factor.
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Not a systematic review; PubMed only and English only.

facts.population: 99 patients with 458 dental implants, randomly selected from a university clinic database
outcomes: prevalence of peri-implant health and diseases
risk and protective indicators of peri-implantitis
facts.main_result: Prevalence of peri-implantitis was 56.6% at patient level and 27.9% at implant level; smoking (OR 3.59) and moderate/severe periodontitis (OR 2.77) were among the risk indicators.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts; partly funded by an Osteology Foundation Young Research Grant
facts.limitations: Cross-sectional design; baseline data on bone loss from 0-1 years after loading were unavailable, so case definitions relied on single-time bone levels.

facts.population: 134 patients with 478 implants supporting fixed prostheses, without a regular maintenance program
facts.comparison: Tissue-level versus bone-level implants
facts.main_result: Peri-implantitis affected 20% of patients and 8.8% of implants; smoking and lack of keratinized mucosa were associated with it (OR 2.57 and 3.89).
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare Replace Select and Branemark MKIII

facts.population: 159 longitudinal clinical studies on prevention or management of peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis
facts.main_result: PPD and BOP were reported in 89% and 87% of 159 studies; patient-reported outcomes (6%) and adverse events (8%) were rarely reported and a primary outcome was defined in only 36%.
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflicts of interest

facts.population: 30 edentulous patients with two mandibular implants each, 2 years in function
facts.intervention: Internal implant decontamination (10% H2O2 + brush) plus sealant, CHX varnish or CHX gel
facts.comparison: Decontamination alone (control)
outcomes: total bacterial counts (real-time PCR) in internal implant cavity
facts.main_result: Internal bacterial counts fell about 4-fold after 12 months overall, with no difference between decontamination alone and added sealant or chlorhexidine (p = .348)
facts.funding_coi: Own institutions; materials supplied by Ivoclar Vivadent, Hager und Werken and GSK; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Possibly underpowered to detect minor differences; homogeneous implant sample; PCR cannot distinguish live from dead bacteria

facts.population: Patients with dental implants and peri-implant mucositis/peri-implantitis
facts.intervention: Consensus evaluation of measures for managing peri-implant mucositis (patient and professional plaque control, adjuncts)
outcomes: clinical signs of inflammation after management
facts.main_result: Meta-analysis estimated weighted mean prevalence of peri-implant mucositis 43% and peri-implantitis 22%; mechanical plaque control is effective, adjuncts add no benefit
facts.sample_size: Prevalence meta-analysis of 1196 patients and 4209 implants (mucositis)
facts.funding_coi: European Federation of Periodontology workshop, partly unrestricted grants from Johnson & Johnson and Procter & Gamble
facts.limitations: Included prevalence studies used convenience samples of limited size with varying follow-up

facts.population: 63 patients with one circumferential peri-implant intraosseous defect each
facts.intervention: Open flap debridement plus porous titanium granules
facts.comparison: Open flap debridement alone
facts.main_result: At 12 months radiographic defect fill was 3.6/3.6 mm with PTG versus 1.1/1.0 mm with OFD alone (P < 0.0001), with similar clinical improvements
facts.funding_coi: Research grant from Tigran Technologies AB; several authors report industry grants and Tigran advisory roles
facts.limitations: Biomaterial could not be distinguished from osseous tissue on radiographs, so new bone formation could not be verified

facts.population: Implants treated for peri-implantitis in 12 included studies (390 implants)
facts.intervention: Reconstructive surgical procedures for peri-implantitis
facts.comparison: Open flap debridement (only one RCT available)
facts.main_result: Weighted mean radiographic defect fill 2.17 mm (95% CI 1.46-2.87), PD reduction 2.97 mm, CAL gain 1.65 mm, BOP reduction 45.8%; no evidence versus nonreconstructive procedures
facts.funding_coi: Partly supported by University of Michigan Periodontal Graduate Student Research Fund; no conflicts declared
facts.limitations: Mostly small case series with short follow-up and inconsistent methodologies

facts.population: 138 patients (147 implants) with peri-implantitis
facts.intervention: Reconstructive surgery using bone substitute material
facts.comparison: Access flap surgery (control)
outcomes: composite outcome (implant not lost, no BOP/SOP, PPD <=5 mm, <=1 mm recession)
PPD, BOP, buccal keratinized mucosa, buccal recession
facts.main_result: Composite success was 16.4% (test) vs 13.5% (control), not significant; buccal recession was lower in the test group (0.7 vs 1.1 mm).
facts.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation Large Clinical Grant; several authors report honoraria/grants from Dentsply Sirona, Straumann, Geistlich etc.
facts.limitations: No blinding to group allocation was performed.

facts.population: 45 patients with peri-implantitis intraosseous defects
facts.intervention: Bovine-derived xenograft (BDX) with collagen membrane
facts.comparison: Autogenous bone graft with collagen membrane
facts.main_result: Successful treatment at year five in 36% of implants with autogenous bone versus 78.3% with BDX; bone level change -0.7 mm versus +1.6 mm
facts.sample_size: 45 patients enrolled; at year 5, 16 patients/25 implants (AB) and 23 patients/38 implants (BDX)
facts.funding_coi: Biomet 3i funded the initial 12-month study; long-term follow-up self-funded; Renvert reports grants from Biomet 3i and Geistlich

facts.population: 75 patients with one crater-like peri-implantitis defect around SLA tissue-level implants
facts.intervention: Reconstructive surgery with deproteinized bovine bone mineral with 10% collagen (DBBMC)
outcomes: treatment success (PD, BOP, pus, bone loss)
facts.main_result: At 5 years 51 of 75 patients remained, implant survival 80%, success in 29 patients (45.3%); outcome not related to defect configuration but to adherence to supportive therapy
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded, no external funding

facts.population: Six female Labrador dogs with experimental peri-implantitis
facts.intervention: Reconstructive surgical therapy with bone substitute materials (DBBM, biphasic graft, DBBM with collagen membrane)
facts.comparison: No augmentation (Group C)
facts.main_result: Healing was superior around smooth-surface implants than moderately rough ones; benefit of bone substitutes was overall small
facts.funding_coi: Swedish Research Council and TUA research funding; materials provided by Geistlich and Dentsply

facts.population: Consecutive partially edentulous patients with at least one peri-implantitis implant
facts.intervention: Local factors (surgical, implant, prosthesis-related) assessed as exposures
facts.comparison: Peri-implantitis versus non-peri-implantitis implants
facts.main_result: Implant malpositioning (tilt 10-30 degrees OR 5.84, 30 degrees or more OR 7.43) and medial position (OR 3.9) raised peri-implantitis odds; inside bony housing OR 0.13; Morse taper OR 0.43
facts.funding_coi: Statistics covered by the university department; otherwise self-funded; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Cross-sectional design cannot establish a direct link between local factors and peri-implantitis

facts.population: Granulation tissue biopsies from 39 peri-implantitis cases and 35 periodontitis controls
facts.intervention: Identification of titanium particles in peri-implantitis granulation tissue (SEM/EDS) and immunohistochemistry
facts.comparison: Periodontitis granulation tissue
outcomes: CD68, IL-6, Nf-kB and VEGF expression
facts.main_result: Titanium particles were found in all peri-implantitis specimens without foreign body reaction; peri-implantitis showed higher CD68 and VEGF expression than periodontitis
facts.funding_coi: Serbian Ministry of Education and Science, Medical Military Academy and Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts
facts.limitations: No SEM/EDS analysis of periodontitis specimens, which were assumed particle-free

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 51 peri-implantitis implants in 38 patients (BOP, PD ≥ 6 mm, bone loss ≥ 4 mm)
facts.intervention: Regenerative approach: surface decontamination, enamel matrix derivative, PDGF with bovine or freeze-dried bone, collagen membrane or connective tissue graft
facts.main_result: Probing depth fell 5.4 and 5.1 mm and bone level gain was 3.75 mm (group 1) and 3.0 mm (group 2); no implant lost bone
facts.limitations: Lack of histology to determine nature of newly formed tissue

facts.population: Patients in good general health requiring surgical treatment of peri-implantitis (16 RCTs)
facts.intervention: Implant surface decontamination protocols (mechanical, chemical, physical, systemic antimicrobials) during surgical treatment
facts.comparison: Other decontamination protocols, including placebo
facts.main_result: No single decontamination method showed clear superiority; systemic antibiotics improved treatment success (RR 1.84) but Er:Yag laser added no PPD benefit.
facts.funding_coi: Funded solely by the authors' institutions; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Most evidence rests on single RCTs and half of the trials were not at low risk of bias.

facts.population: Human clinical trials of surgically treated peri-implantitis (21 articles, 12 case series)
facts.intervention: Surgical treatment of peri-implantitis: access flap and debridement, resection, bone grafting, guided bone regeneration
facts.main_result: Surgical procedures gave weighted mean PD reduction of 2.04 to 3.16 mm, and grafting with membranes gave greater PD reduction and 2.1 mm bone fill.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Lack of high-quality comparative studies to support the findings.

facts.population: 40 participants with peri-implantitis and a contained intraosseous defect (one implant each)
facts.intervention: Access flap with xenograft (DBBM) and collagen membrane (GBR), plus systemic antimicrobials
facts.comparison: Access flap surgery alone (control), also with systemic antimicrobials
facts.main_result: No significant clinical or radiographic differences between access flap and GBR at 12 months; PD reduction 4.2 vs 3.7 mm, MBL gain 1.7 vs 2.4 mm.
materials_brands: Amoxicillin 500 mg + metronidazole 400 mg for 7 days
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the Osteology Foundation; first author reports speaking honoraria from Geistlich and Straumann among others
