facts.limitations: Sample of 40 participants is relatively small for a single-centre trial.

facts.population: 75 patients with one peri-implantitis crater-like lesion, PD >= 6 mm
facts.intervention: Implant decontamination then filling of the defect with deproteinized bovine bone mineral with 10% collagen
facts.main_result: Treatment success was obtained in 37 (52.1%) of 71 implants examined at 1 year; PD fell by 2.92 mm and BOP from 71.5% to 18.3%.
facts.sample_size: 75 patients, one implant each; 71 examined at 1 year
materials_brands: Bio-Oss Collagen (deproteinized bovine bone mineral with 10% collagen), Geistlich
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded, no external funding; first author received grants from Straumann, Dentsply, Geistlich and Sunstar outside the work

facts.population: 376 patients with 1095 dental implants treated 1999-2005 at a specialist clinic in Stockholm
facts.intervention: Dental implant therapy (Astra Tech 65%, Nobel Biocare 35%)
facts.main_result: Cumulative implant survival to 15 years was 82.6%; 65% of patients had at least one complication; implant loss was more frequent after treated severe periodontitis.
facts.funding_coi: Grants from Stockholm County Council and Folktandvården Stockholms Läns Landsting AB; no conflict of interest

facts.population: 27 patients with one peri-implantitis intrabony defect each (Class Ib, Ic or Ie)
facts.intervention: Access flap surgery with natural bone mineral plus collagen membrane
facts.comparison: Class Ib vs Class Ic vs Class Ie defect configurations (9 each)
facts.main_result: Class Ie defects tended to show higher PD and CAL changes than Class Ib and Ic, with significant differences only at 6 months.
materials_brands: Natural bone mineral with collagen membrane (Geistlich Biomaterials)
facts.funding_coi: Study materials provided by Geistlich Biomaterials; no conflict of interest declared

facts.population: 72 titanium SLA implants placed 5 mm supracrestally in porcine ribs
facts.intervention: Instrumentation with five decontamination protocols: metal scaler, PEEK scaler, round titanium brush, tufted titanium brush, glycine air-powder
facts.comparison: Untreated control implants
facts.main_result: Metal scaler damaged the surface, PEEK left plastic remnants, titanium brushes flattened threads and glycine air-powder caused minimal change.
facts.funding_coi: Korean government research grants (KHIDI); no conflict of interest

facts.population: 96 implants coated with ink in 3D-printed resin blocks simulating Ib, Ic and Ie peri-implant defects
facts.intervention: Mechanical decontamination with air-polishing (glycine), rotating titanium brush, PEEK ultrasonic tip, stainless steel ultrasonic tip
facts.comparison: Devices compared with each other (no untreated control)
outcomes: area of remnant ink on implant surface
facts.main_result: Air-polishing with glycine and titanium brushes cleaned better than ultrasonic devices in all three defect configurations, though none removed all ink.
materials_brands: Air-Flow system with Perio Prophylaxis Powder (EMS)
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded by the ETEP Research Group; no conflict of interest

facts.population: Animals (ligature-induced peri-implantitis) and patients with dental implants; 7605 patients with 26,188 implants in clinical studies
facts.intervention: Implants with different surface characteristics and/or materials
facts.comparison: Modified versus non-modified implant surfaces
facts.main_result: Modified surfaces showed greater bone loss in preclinical dog models, but clinical studies showed no difference in peri-implantitis incidence among implant surfaces.
facts.sample_size: 18 preclinical experiments (25 publications) and 31 clinical publications with 7605 patients
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no relevant conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Little information available on the impact of implant material.

facts.journal: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
facts.population: Ten long-term clinical studies of three modern implant brands with moderately rough surfaces
facts.intervention: Modern moderately rough oral implants
facts.comparison: Older machined implants
facts.main_result: Implants with peri-implant infection and bone loss leading to removal or surgery averaged 2.7% over 7 to 16 years; peri-implantitis plus failure is commonly below 5% over 10 years.
facts.funding_coi: Consensus meeting sponsored by five major implant suppliers

facts.main_result: CP titanium acts as a foreign body in live tissue, marginal bone loss may have immunological causes, and titanium allergy may exist only in rare cases.
facts.limitations: Lack of universally accepted, tested patch tests makes titanium allergy diagnosis difficult; no universal definition of marginal bone loss prevented a systematic review.

facts.main_result: Peri-implantitis-type marginal bone loss occurs in 1-2% of implants at 10+ years with trained clinicians and controlled systems; later bone loss mostly reflects treatment complications and foreign-body/immunological reactions, not infection.
Marginal bone loss around oral implants is attributed to a dis-balanced foreign body response, not a periodontitis-like infectious disease.
facts.funding_coi: Supported economically by the Sylván Foundation

facts.main_result: Osseointegration is redefined as a foreign body reaction in which interfacial bone forms as a defense reaction to shield the implant from the tissues.

A step-by-step decision process chooses among coronally advanced flap, CAF plus connective tissue graft and modified coronally advanced tunnel, based on non-carious cervical lesions, interdental attachment loss, buccal root displacement, then keratinized tissue and gingival thickness.
facts.limitations: Few studies assess esthetic outcome beyond complete root coverage or compare techniques on esthetic outcome.

facts.main_result: Saliva has roles in lubrication, buffering, mineralization, wound healing, taste and immune responses, and is a developing diagnostic fluid including for SARS-CoV-2.
facts.funding_coi: NIDCR/NIH training program and grants

facts.main_result: Intracrevicular margins do not cause periodontal disease; inflammation and bone loss occur only with large overhangs, and finish line design does not change periodontal response.

facts.population: 7 adult monkeys with retained mandibular root tips
facts.intervention: Self-tapping screw-type titanium implants placed in contact with retained root tips
facts.comparison: Control implants placed in bone free of retained roots
facts.main_result: Where implants contacted retained root tips, newly formed cementum covered the implant surface and a ligament-like space formed (8 of 14 test implants had root contact); controls were osseointegrated.
facts.funding_coi: Astra Meditec and a Danish research foundation grant

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 3 mongrel dogs, edentulous mandibular premolar regions
facts.intervention: Titanium implants coated with cultured autologous periodontal ligament cells, placed with a void and covered by a membrane
facts.main_result: Cementum-like tissue with a periodontal ligament-like layer and inserting collagen fibers formed on 37% of evaluated implant surfaces; no direct bone-to-implant contact.
materials_brands: Straumann commercially pure titanium screw implant, 8 mm x 4.1 mm
facts.funding_coi: Korea Science and Engineering Foundation grant

facts.population: Monkey mandibles with retained apical root portions
facts.intervention: Plasma-sprayed titanium hollow-cylinder implants placed in close contact with retained roots

facts.intervention: Inlay augmentation with allograft block (left side)
facts.comparison: Inlay augmentation with allograft particulate (right side)
facts.main_result: Mean vertical bone gain was 3.9 mm (right, particulate) and 4.4 mm (left, block); histology showed newly formed bone without inflammation and a tight block-to-basal bone connection.

materials_brands: OraGraft allograft block and particulate (LifeNet Health)
Mectron Piezosurgery inserts OT8R, OT8L, OT7
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: 10 partially edentulous patients needing bilateral vertical augmentation of the posterior mandible (5-7 mm residual height)

facts.comparison: Interpositional anorganic bovine bone block (Bio-Oss)
outcomes: time to recover mental nerve sensitivity
facts.main_result: Both procedures gave significant bone gain without significant difference; Bio-Oss sides recovered nerve sensitivity faster (4 vs 6.3 days) and patients preferred Bio-Oss.

materials_brands: Gebrüder Martin titanium miniplates and miniscrews
facts.funding_coi: Geistlich (Italy) donated Bio-Oss blocks and barriers
facts.limitations: Small number of patients

facts.population: 62-year-old man with Seibert class II atrophy of the right posterior mandible, over 10 mm thick, 5.6 mm residual height above the canal

facts.funding_coi: No financial interest declared

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 5 patients (3 partially, 2 totally edentulous) with vertical bone over 10 mm but ridge width of 3 mm or less

facts.main_result: Ridge width gain of 1-4 mm, larger in maxillary (3-4 mm) than mandibular (1.0-1.5 mm) sites; histology showed bone regeneration between the split crest portions.

facts.intervention: Surgical and combined prosthetic-surgical approaches to cover peri-implant soft-tissue dehiscence
outcomes: factors affecting peri-implant soft-tissue margin stability
facts.main_result: Incorrect implant placement, thin buccal soft tissue and bone and reduced buccal bone height are most associated with dehiscence; coronally advanced flap with connective tissue graft is the recommended surgical technique.

facts.population: Two stone master casts (mandibular and maxillary), eight stone replicas each, with simulated gingival recession marks

facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: In vitro on stone replicas; clinical trials are needed to confirm

facts.population: Three patients: two with multiple Miller class I recessions, one needing extraction of a root-fractured upper lateral incisor with immediate implant

facts.funding_coi: No sources of funding declared

facts.main_result: 7 of 9 EMD+CAF teeth showed histologic periodontal regeneration (corroborated by micro-CT) versus none of 3 CTG+CAF teeth; clinical measurements were comparable.

facts.journal: Medicina Oral Patología Oral y Cirugía Bucal
facts.population: 24 patients with atrophic edentulous free ends of a partially edentulous jaw
facts.intervention: 7 mm short implants, alone or splinted to longer implants, loaded immediately or delayed
facts.comparison: Delayed vs immediate loading; short-only vs mixed short and long implant bridges
facts.main_result: Cumulative survival of short implants was 87% at a mean 47.72 months; immediately loaded 96.4% vs delayed 76.9% (p=0.047).
facts.sample_size: 24 patients, 54 short (7 mm) and 15 longer implants
materials_brands: Brånemark System Mk III Shorty TiUnite (Nobel Biocare)
facts.funding_coi: NobelBiocare provided free implants and abutments (Grant 2005-355)

facts.population: Human studies of short dental implants (<10 mm) supporting fixed prostheses
facts.intervention: Short dental implants (<10 mm) supporting fixed prostheses
facts.comparison: Standard implants (>=10 mm)
facts.main_result: Implant length had no significant effect on marginal bone loss (meta-regression P = 0.633); short and standard implants did not differ (P = 0.222).
facts.funding_coi: Partly funded by the University of Michigan Graduate Periodontics Student Research Fund; no financial interests declared
facts.limitations: Scarcity of long-term follow-up prospective studies.

facts.population: Patients with single tooth gaps in the posterior area
facts.intervention: 6 mm Standard Plus Tissue Level SLActive implant with screw-retained single crown
facts.comparison: 10 mm Standard Plus Tissue Level SLActive implant
facts.main_result: 5-year implant survival was 91% for 6 mm vs 100% for 10 mm implants (p=0.036); marginal bone levels did not differ.
materials_brands: Straumann Standard Plus Tissue Level SLActive implants
facts.funding_coi: ITI grant (ITI Nr 517-2007); authors report no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Long-term data on short (<=8 mm) implants still lacking.

facts.population: 45 patients with single-tooth sites in posterior regions
facts.intervention: 6 mm long, 4.1 mm diameter moderately rough (SLA) implants loaded within 7 weeks with single crowns
facts.comparison: 10 mm long, 4.1 mm diameter implants
facts.main_result: After 5 years survival was 86.7% for 6 mm and 96.7% for 10 mm implants; marginal bone loss was small and similar.
materials_brands: Gold-palladium alloy and porcelain single fixed prosthesis
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the ITI Research Committee; authors declare no conflict of interest

facts.population: Patients needing implants in fresh extraction sockets, or in the posterior maxilla or mandible with limited bone height
facts.intervention: Alveolar ridge preservation; sinus elevation with grafting or vertical augmentation vs short implants
facts.comparison: Unassisted socket healing; longer implants after sinus elevation or vertical augmentation
facts.main_result: Short implants and implants after sinus elevation or vertical augmentation gave comparable outcomes, with fewer complications for short implants; ridge preservation reduced need for further augmentation.
facts.funding_coi: Workshop funded by the European Association for Osseointegration; participant disclosures kept on file
facts.limitations: Evidence derived from short-term RCTs, some from the same research group.

facts.population: Patients with atrophic maxillae or mandibles
facts.intervention: Short implants (<10 mm) for single or multiple units, fixed prostheses or overdentures
facts.main_result: Short implants (<10 mm) can be used effectively in atrophic jaws, even with crown/implant ratios once considered excessive.
facts.funding_coi: No disclosures

facts.population: Human studies of 6-mm Straumann micro-rough implants
facts.intervention: 6 mm micro-rough surface Straumann implants
facts.main_result: Pooled early cumulative survival of 6-mm implants was 93.7% (maxilla 94.7%, mandible 98.6%); 76% of failures were early.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest; no external funding

facts.population: 20 adult patients with 46 posterior single-crown implants (23 maxillary, 23 mandibular)
facts.intervention: 6-mm long, 4.1-mm wide implants supporting single metalloceramic crowns in the posterior region
facts.main_result: 6-mm single-crown implants showed 91.3% survival, 28.3% screw loosening and 0.3 mm cumulative bone loss at 48 months; clinical C/I ratio and time predicted bone loss, and the mandible carried higher failure risk
facts.funding_coi: ITI, CNPq and CAPES funding; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Authors call for studies with larger sample size and longer follow-up
outcomes: risk factors (arch, bruxism, bite force, C/I ratio, occlusal table area)

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 33 studies of short implants (<=8.5 mm) in posterior partially edentulous jaws, 3,573 implants
facts.intervention: Short implants (<=8.5 mm) placed in the posterior maxilla/mandible to support fixed restorations
facts.comparison: Longer implants (>8.5 mm)
facts.main_result: No significant difference in survival of short vs long implants; 5-year cumulative survival 98% (98.3% vs 97.7%)
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: 95 patients with posterior partially edentulous maxilla or mandible sites
facts.intervention: 6 mm (4.0 x 6) implants
facts.comparison: 11 mm (4.0 x 11) standard-length implants
facts.main_result: At 3 years MBL was 0.27 mm (6 mm) vs 0.44 mm (11 mm) apical to platform, favoring short implants; survival 96% vs 99%, not significant.
facts.funding_coi: Fully sponsored by Dentsply Sirona Implants; two authors received lecture honoraria

facts.population: Patients undergoing implant-prosthetic rehabilitation in 22 RCTs/prospective controlled studies
facts.intervention: Platform-switching implant-abutment configuration
facts.comparison: Platform-matching implant-abutment configuration
facts.main_result: Meta-analysis of 13 RCTs: mean marginal bone loss 0.49 mm with platform switching vs 1.01 mm with platform matching (P<0.0001)
facts.sample_size: 13 RCTs, 549 patients, 1035 implants in the meta-analysis
facts.funding_coi: Unrestricted grant from the Camlog Foundation
facts.limitations: Heterogeneous methodology, unclear or high risk of bias, short follow-up

facts.key_finding: Journal issue (Clinical Oral Implants Research, October 2014, pages 1105-1211) with original articles and reviews on implants in periodontally compromised patients, intraoral scanning impressions, short implants, socket preservation and implant surface cleaning.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Issue contents page only; individual articles must be consulted for clinical conclusions.

facts.population: Nine systematic reviews on the shortened dental arch in adults, covering 228 articles
facts.intervention: Overview of systematic reviews with AMSTAR methodologic appraisal
facts.main_result: Seven of nine SRs concluded the SDA concept is functionally sound; five were of high and four of medium AMSTAR quality
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: None of the included SRs assessed publication bias

facts.population: Swedish general dental practitioners (private and public)
facts.intervention: Questionnaire on attitudes toward the shortened dental arch concept
facts.comparison: Private practitioners vs Public Dental Health Service; male vs female
facts.main_result: Swedish GPs were generally positive toward the SDA concept (response rate 54%), with female clinicians more risk conscious and private practitioners seeing fewer advantages
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the Public Dental Health Service, Skane County Council

facts.journal: Journal of Medical and Dental Sciences
facts.population: 15 adults and 10 adolescents without stomatognathic disorder
facts.intervention: Biting on Temporary Stopping to locate the main occluding area, with occlusal contact analysis
facts.comparison: Adults vs adolescents
facts.main_result: Main occluding areas of adolescents were significantly anterior to and less stable than those of adults, and adults had larger occlusal contact area
outcomes: antero-posterior position of main occluding area

facts.population: Malaysian government dentists in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur
facts.intervention: Self-administered questionnaire on SDA knowledge, perceptions and application
facts.main_result: Dentists had good knowledge and perceptions of the SDA concept (response 84.0%) but only 20.4% had applied it clinically
facts.funding_coi: University of Malaya funded the study; no conflicts of interest
outcomes: clinical application of the SDA concept

facts.population: Tanzanian adults with shortened dental arches (725) and complete arches (125)
facts.intervention: Shortened dental arches with zero to eight posterior occluding pairs
facts.comparison: Subjects with complete dental arches
facts.main_result: No evidence that shortened dental arches provoke TMD signs and symptoms; joint sounds were more frequent with unilateral (17%) or no (10%) posterior support
facts.funding_coi: Supported by University of Nijmegen, Muhimbili University College and other bodies

facts.population: Partially dentate patients treated with the shortened dental arch concept (literature review)
facts.intervention: Shortened dental arch treatment approach
facts.main_result: Dental arches comprising anterior and premolar regions meet the requirements of a functional dentition, with improved hygiene, comfort and possibly lower cost

facts.population: General dentists in Victoria, Australia (175 respondents; 70% male, 44% rural)
facts.intervention: Mailed self-administered anonymous questionnaire on awareness and opinion of the shortened dental arch (SDA) concept
outcomes: patient acceptance as judged by dentists
facts.main_result: 61% of responding dentists were aware of the SDA concept and 78.4% considered it useful in clinical practice.
facts.sample_size: 175 respondents from 434 dentists surveyed (40.3% response rate)
facts.funding_coi: Financial assistance from the Australian Dental Research Foundation

facts.population: Human studies on the relationship between dentition and oral function (83 included articles)
facts.intervention: Systematic literature search (PubMed) on which dentition assures oral function
facts.main_result: A minimum of 20 teeth with nine to 10 pairs of contacting units is associated with adequate masticatory efficiency and ability.
facts.sample_size: 83 articles from an initial pool of 1460 citations
facts.limitations: Few studies with high levels of evidence were found

facts.population: Patients with residual bone height <5 mm needing unilateral sinus floor elevation for two nonadjacent implants (20 treated, 18 analysed)
facts.intervention: Lateral sinus augmentation with a composite graft and bone-core biopsies at mesial and distal implant sites after 6 months
facts.comparison: Mesial versus distal sites within the same sinus
outcomes: sinus width and residual bone height as predictors
facts.main_result: %NFMT was higher in mesial (17.5) than distal (11.6) sites (p = .0004) and correlated negatively with sinus width but not with residual bone height.
facts.follow_up: 6 months to biopsy; implants followed 7 to 31 months after loading
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded
facts.limitations: Single biopsy time point (6 months) and a single composite graft, so results do not extend to other bone substitutes

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Patients with atrophic posterior maxilla undergoing lateral window sinus augmentation (37 included studies with histomorphometric data)
facts.intervention: Barrier membrane placed over the lateral window
facts.comparison: No membrane over the lateral window
facts.main_result: Vital bone formation was similar with and without a membrane (32.36% vs 33.07%); graft material and healing time also did not influence it.
facts.follow_up: Included studies observed 6 months to 3 years
facts.funding_coi: Partly supported by University of Michigan Periodontal Graduate Student Research Fund; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Only four RCTs were identified, so lower levels of evidence were included and some nonrandomized studies were of non-acceptable quality

facts.population: Ten edentulous patients with marked bilateral maxillary atrophy
facts.intervention: Graftless sinus augmentation: sinus membrane lifted and held by a resorbable PDLLA membrane, space filled with blood clot
facts.comparison: Conventional sinus augmentation with autograft and xenograft mixture on the contralateral side
facts.main_result: Implant survival was higher on the conventional side (96.7% vs 86.2%, p<0.001) and bone gain was greater (9.69 vs 6.20 mm).
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 21 patients (mean age 57.6) needing maxillary sinus augmentation by lateral window with remaining bone height of 6 mm or less
facts.intervention: Lateral window sinus augmentation with a cortical/cancellous allograft mixture (MinerOss) as sole graft, with window area (AWD) measured
facts.main_result: Mean vital bone was 21.69%; larger window area correlated with less vital bone (r = -0.621, P = .0007) and more remaining allograft (r = 0.565).
facts.funding_coi: Partly supported by BioHorizons, ICOI research grant and University of Michigan fund; three authors declared industry research/lecture support

facts.population: 430 patients with transcrestal sinus floor elevation and single-implant insertion in sites with RBH ≤5 mm, seven Italian centers
facts.intervention: Transcrestal sinus floor elevation with simultaneous or staged single-implant placement
facts.main_result: Early implant failure occurred in 12 of 430 implants (2.8%) and was associated with large sinus width and membrane perforation.
facts.follow_up: Minimum 12 months after prosthetic crown delivery
facts.limitations: Retrospective design with records not designed for the study; membrane perforations may have been underestimated

facts.journal: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.population: 161 patients with oroantral communications treated at the University Hospital in Vienna, 2000 to 2005
facts.intervention: Closure of the oroantral communication with a pedicled buccal fat pad
facts.main_result: Closure was insufficient in 12 of 161 patients (7.5%); success was nearly 98% excluding severe and complicating cases.

facts.population: 86 patients (92 sinus lifts, 209 implants) with residual ridge height 0.1 to 7 mm in the posterior maxilla
facts.intervention: Lateral window sinus augmentation with sagittal sandwich technique (autogenous bone and ABBM, 3:7) and delayed implant placement
facts.comparison: Implants in native bone (group C) versus severe (group S) and moderate (group M) residual height
facts.main_result: 3 of 209 implants (1.4%) failed over 10 years and marginal bone loss did not differ between groups at 1, 2 and 5 years.
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare Branemark Mk III / Mk IV implants
facts.funding_coi: Dr. Urban received honoraria for speaking for Nobel BioCare and Geistlich Pharma

facts.population: 25 patients (34 Astra implants) in the posterior maxilla at 10-year follow-up
facts.intervention: Osteotome sinus floor elevation with simultaneous implant placement without bone grafts
outcomes: height of residual peri-implant alveolar bone
facts.main_result: Single-tooth and partially edentulous cases had 100% survival; mean marginal bone loss was 0.6 mm at 10 years.
facts.sample_size: 34 implants in 25 patients (from 53 implants in 36 patients originally)
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.population: Ten patients needing bilateral two-staged maxillary sinus floor augmentation
facts.intervention: Sinus augmentation with porcine bone mineral (Symbios) mixed 20:80 with autogenous bone
facts.comparison: Anorganic bovine bone (Bio-Oss) mixed 20:80 with autogenous bone on the contralateral side
facts.main_result: Graft resorption and histologic, histomorphometric and immunohistochemical results did not differ between bovine and porcine xenografts after 6 months.
facts.funding_coi: Partially funded by Dentsply Sirona Implants; senior author is a frequent Dentsply Sirona speaker
facts.limitations: Small sample size (10 cases per group) and possibly excessive graft maturation time

facts.journal: International Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.population: Patients with maxillary atrophy undergoing sinus lift (12 randomized split-mouth trials)
facts.intervention: Sinus lift with autogenous bone plus growth factors or bone substitutes, or bone substitutes alone
facts.comparison: Sinus lift with autogenous bone alone
facts.main_result: Bone fraction was significantly higher with autogenous bone than with beta-TCP alone (P = 0.036); other substitutes and PRP showed no difference.
facts.follow_up: Bone fraction at 5 months; implant survival at 1 year

facts.population: 152 elevated maxillary sinuses in 76 New Zealand white rabbits
facts.intervention: Bilateral maxillary sinus floor elevation with xenograft granules (Bio-Oss or Cerabone), analysed histologically for mucosal adhesion stages
outcomes: distance between elevated and undetached mucosae
facts.main_result: 31 of 152 sinuses showed adhesions: 12 proximity, 15 fusion and 4 synechia stages, with epithelial hyperplasia.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by ARDEC Academy; no conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Rabbit model has thinner sinus mucosa and faster healing than humans, and adhesions were infrequent (about 10%).

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Patients undergoing lateral-window sinus augmentation with large schneiderian membrane perforations
facts.intervention: Repair of large perforations with a bioabsorbable collagen membrane stabilized outside the antrostomy and folded inward to form a new roof or a pouch
outcomes: sinus health on radiographs and CT
facts.main_result: No procedural failures in 20 consecutive patients; histology at 6 to 9 months showed vital bone formation (26% in one case).

facts.population: Patients with a single missing tooth in the posterior maxilla
facts.intervention: One 6-mm implant without grafting for a single crown
facts.comparison: One 11-mm implant combined with maxillary sinus floor augmentation
facts.main_result: At 10 years implant survival was 89.5% (6 mm) vs 90.9% (11 mm) and marginal bone loss 0.18 vs 0.26 mm, with no significant difference (p = .650).
facts.sample_size: 21 implants in 20 patients (6 mm) and 20 implants in 18 patients (11 mm)
facts.funding_coi: 1-year study partly sponsored by Dentsply Implants (materials supplied); authors declare no economic interest
facts.limitations: Loss to follow-up of a number of initial participants.

facts.intervention: Lateral window technique for maxillary sinus augmentation
facts.main_result: The authors conclude that lateral-window sinus augmentation is a safe, reliable and predictable surgery whose risk factors can be managed with minimal trauma.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.intervention: Classification of sinus membrane perforations into 5 classes, each with a repair technique, during crestal-approach sinus augmentation
facts.main_result: The authors propose a 5-class classification and treatment planning guide for sinus membrane perforations.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: Patients with implants placed at maxillary posterior sites with 3-6 mm residual bone height
facts.intervention: Implant placement with simultaneous transcrestal sinus floor elevation (tSFE)
facts.comparison: Implant placement with simultaneous lateral sinus floor elevation (lSFE)
facts.main_result: At 6 years implant survival was 100%; totCON% was 96% (tSFE) vs 100% (lSFE) (p = .036) and median dMBL 0.3 vs 0 mm (p = .024), with similar peri-implant health.
facts.sample_size: 43 patients at the 6-year visit (21 tSFE, 22 lSFE)
facts.funding_coi: Supported by University of Ferrara research centre, Regione Emilia-Romagna, Osteology Foundation grants and a Geistlich Biomaterials donation; no conflicts declared
facts.limitations: Parallel-arm rather than split-mouth design did not control individual healing response.

facts.intervention: Snap-On Smile removable appliance made of crystallized acetyl resin
facts.key_finding: This is a manufacturer training manual describing the Snap-On Smile appliance, a removable tooth-borne cosmetic appliance made of crystallized acetyl resin that needs no tooth preparation, plus its uses, case selection, delivery and practice-building. The manual states it is expected to last about 3 to 5 years.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: It is promotional training material that presents the appliance as a reversible option for vertical dimension, implant provisionals, cosmetic partials and smile enhancement, with no independent clinical data.

facts.journal: Journal of Stomatology, Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.population: Postextraction sockets in patients, from five included RCTs/controlled clinical trials
facts.intervention: Socket preservation with deproteinized bovine bone mineral (DBBM)
facts.comparison: Natural healing
facts.main_result: DBBM socket preservation gave a significantly lower new bone percentage than natural healing (MD -24.75, p = 0.001), with no difference in connective tissue (MD 0.60, p = 0.83).
facts.follow_up: 3 to 6 months biopsy time in included studies
facts.funding_coi: No competing interest declared
facts.limitations: Lack of high-quality research; further large-sample studies are needed.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Patients with large bone defects after tooth extraction (31 teeth)
facts.intervention: Reactive soft tissue left in the defect and filled with collagen sheets, wound left open
outcomes: vital bone and connective tissue percentage on histomorphometry
facts.main_result: Mean vertical bone gain was 12.13 mm at 3 months (P < .05), with vital bone 41.59% and connective tissue 50.37%.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Results are not supported by a biologic explanation and need further laboratory and clinical research.

facts.population: Adult patients needing extraction of at least one single- or multi-rooted tooth (third molars excluded), from 22 RCTs
facts.intervention: Alveolar ridge preservation modalities (socket grafting with bone substitutes, socket sealing, blood-derived products, cell therapy, rhBMP-2)
facts.comparison: Tooth extraction alone (spontaneous socket healing)
outcomes: horizontal and vertical ridge dimensional change
facts.main_result: ARP by socket grafting prevented horizontal (1.99 mm) and vertical mid-buccal (1.72 mm) and mid-lingual (1.16 mm) bone resorption compared with extraction alone.
facts.funding_coi: Two authors declare research support or lecture fees from several implant and biomaterial companies (Geistlich, Osteogenics, Dentsply Implants and others); Chambrone declares none
facts.limitations: The effect of other local and systemic factors could not be assessed quantitatively, and a superior ARP approach could not be determined.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Human subjects who required single or multiple tooth extraction
facts.intervention: Alveolar ridge preservation procedures after tooth extraction
facts.comparison: Tooth extraction alone without further intervention
outcomes: vertical bone height changes (buccal, lingual, mesial, distal)
facts.main_result: Horizontal bone loss was reduced by 1.86 mm with ridge preservation versus extraction alone.
facts.funding_coi: No financial support, no conflicts of interest

facts.population: Patients needing single-rooted tooth extraction in the anterior maxilla
facts.intervention: Ridge preservation with guided bone regeneration (Bio-Oss + Bio-Gide) or socket seal (Bio-Oss + Mucograft Seal)
facts.comparison: Unassisted socket healing
outcomes: radiographic buccal and palatal ridge height
socket and alveolar process cross-sectional area
bone augmentation need at implant placement
facts.main_result: Buccal ridge height rose 0.65 mm with socket seal, stayed stable with GBR (0.07 mm) and fell 0.52 mm in controls.
facts.funding_coi: Military of Defence research support; no conflicts declared
facts.limitations: Low statistical power for ridge width changes

facts.population: Twenty patients with non-molar teeth indicated for extraction
facts.intervention: Ridge preservation with autogenous whole-tooth graft, covered by collagen membrane
facts.comparison: Autogenous demineralized dentin graft (0.6N HCl, 30 min)
outcomes: buccal and lingual ridge height change (CBCT)
histomorphometric new bone, graft remnant and soft tissue area
facts.main_result: Ridge width fell 0.85 mm with whole-tooth graft and 1.02 mm with demineralized dentin graft, with no significant difference.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Cairo University; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Only non-molar sites and few histological samples (n = 4 per group); soft tissue and patient-reported outcomes not assessed

facts.population: 75 patients needing single tooth extraction in the anterior maxilla
facts.intervention: Early implant placement 8 weeks after extraction with ARP using DBBM-C covered by collagen matrix or palatal graft
facts.comparison: Early implant placement after spontaneous healing, no ARP
outcomes: plaque, bleeding on probing, probing depth
facts.main_result: Median mid-facial mucosal margin change was -0.02, -0.13 and -0.14 mm in collagen matrix, palatal graft and control groups, with no significant differences.
facts.sample_size: 75 patients randomized, 70 re-examined at one year
facts.funding_coi: Implants provided by Straumann AG and biomaterials by Geistlich Pharma AG; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: 8-week healing may be too short for graft consolidation; keratinized mucosa width not measured

facts.population: 75 patients with single tooth extraction in the maxillary incisor/premolar area
facts.intervention: Ridge preservation with xenogeneic bone substitute (DBBM-C) covered with collagen matrix or free palatal graft, then implant at 8 weeks
facts.comparison: Spontaneous healing
outcomes: need for GBR at implant placement
facts.main_result: Horizontal bone resorption was -0.9 mm (collagen matrix) and -1.0 mm (palatal graft) versus -3.2 mm in controls, and GBR was needed in 32%, 24% and 72%.
facts.funding_coi: Implants by Straumann AG and biomaterials by Geistlich Pharma AG; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Buccal bone thickness and integrity were not calculated

facts.population: Adult patients with extraction sites or edentulous areas needing implant rehabilitation
facts.intervention: Biologics (autologous blood-derived products, EMD, rhBMP-2, rhPDGF-BB) in ridge preservation/reconstruction, ridge augmentation or sinus floor augmentation
facts.comparison: Conventional modalities without biologics
facts.main_result: Biologics did not give superior clinical or radiographic outcomes than conventional therapy, but histomorphometric results improved.
facts.follow_up: Minimum 2 months for ridge preservation, 4 months for sinus and ridge augmentation
facts.funding_coi: Consensus meeting sponsored by BioHorizons, Geistlich, Lynch Biologics and Straumann; authors declare no conflicts
facts.limitations: High heterogeneity prevented quantitative analysis

facts.main_result: Alveolar ridge preservation is not indicated when an implant can be placed within 0-2 months of extraction; otherwise it should be considered.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the Clinic of Fixed and Removable Prosthodontics, University of Zurich

facts.population: 36 patients with 40 extraction sockets
facts.intervention: Socket grafting with a 1:1 mixture of biphasic calcium phosphate (4BONE) and calcium sulphate (BOND BONE)
facts.comparison: Ungrafted sockets left to heal naturally
outcomes: horizontal ridge width at 0, 3 and 6 mm
facts.main_result: At 3 mm below the crest, control sites lost 2.28 mm of ridge width versus 0.03 mm gained in the test group (p=.007).
facts.funding_coi: Partly supported by an educational grant from MIS implants technology

facts.population: Patients who have received a ridge preservation procedure
facts.intervention: Minimally invasive ridge preservation approaches, with or without immediate implant placement
facts.comparison: Other ridge preservation procedures
facts.main_result: Limited studies and methodological discrepancies made it impossible to confirm a significant benefit of minimally invasive approaches in ridge preservation.
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Very few RCTs reported the same outcomes and pre-extraction site dimensions were not reported

facts.population: Lower incisor sockets of 120-day-old male rabbits
facts.intervention: Standardized 5 mm buccal plate defect created in one socket
facts.comparison: Contralateral socket with intact buccal bone wall
facts.main_result: Sockets with buccal plate loss had reduced width compared with intact sockets, and the difference decreased with time.

facts.population: Patients planned for tooth extraction with subsequent grafting and/or membrane procedure
facts.intervention: Graft and/or membrane placement after tooth extraction
facts.comparison: Control sites with no intervention
facts.main_result: Socket interventions reduced ridge dimensional change but could not prevent resorption (control width loss 2.46-4.56 mm vs 1.14-2.5 mm in test sites)
facts.limitations: Limited data on effectiveness of ridge preservation compared with control
outcomes: clinical ridge width and height change

facts.population: Patients scheduled for single tooth extraction and implant restoration (27 subjects, 28 extraction sites)
facts.intervention: Socket filled with collagen-enriched deproteinized bovine bone mineral and covered with collagen membrane
facts.comparison: Blood clot with collagen membrane only
facts.main_result: Total volume reduction after 6 months was 21.3% with grafting vs 20.0% without (NS); grafting helped only at sites with thin (≤1 mm) buccal bone wall
facts.funding_coi: Materials provided by Geistlich Pharma and Dentsply Sirona
facts.limitations: Hard and soft tissue changes were not evaluated separately

facts.population: Healthy humans with fresh extraction sockets
facts.intervention: Alveolar ridge preservation: socket grafting with bone substitute, GBR with membranes or soft tissue graft, or bioactive materials
facts.comparison: Unassisted socket healing
facts.main_result: ARP reduced resorption versus unassisted healing by about 1.31-1.54 mm in width and 0.91-1.12 mm in height
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts declared by authors
facts.limitations: Limited data prevented reliable histological conclusions or a recommendation of a specific technique

facts.intervention: Pontic-shield: modified socket-shield (partial extraction) to develop pontic sites
facts.main_result: The pontic-shield technique can successfully develop pontic sites and preserve the ridge (14 sites, 10 patients)
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: Two patients with late failure of implants near retained root fragments
facts.main_result: Both late implant failures (4 and 10 years) were associated with retained root fragments in close contact with the implant and bacterial infiltration
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Limited case reports and no prospective analyses exist

facts.journal: The International Journal of Esthetic Dentistry
facts.population: Single-rooted teeth
facts.intervention: Socket-shield technique at immediate implant placement with provisionalization
facts.main_result: Outlines an up-to-date step-by-step partial extraction therapy protocol for socket-shield with immediate implant placement

facts.population: 10 consecutive patients with a single maxillary anterior implant replacement (first premolar to first premolar)
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement with the socket shield technique (buccal root portion retained)
facts.main_result: Volumetric analysis showed low facial contour change (mean oro-facial tissue loss 0.33 mm), mean marginal bone loss 0.33/0.17 mm and mean PES 12 at about 5 years
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Descriptive retrospective study; technique should not be used routinely until prospective trials are available

facts.population: One 68-year-old patient with an immediate implant in the anterior maxilla, retrieved after five years
facts.intervention: Immediate implant placement with the root membrane technique
facts.main_result: Buccal bone plate was maintained without resorption with a healthy PDL; bone-to-implant contact 76.2% after five years
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Further studies needed to confirm; role of graft in gap unclear
outcomes: tissue in gap between root membrane and implant

facts.population: Three beagle dogs (premolar sites) plus one clinical case
facts.intervention: Socket shield with buccal root segment separated vertically into two pieces, implant placed lingually
facts.main_result: Shield segments showed healthy PDL and new bone between implant and shield; the clinical case lost 0.88 mm mean labial volume
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Thommen Medical research grant; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Only three dogs, no control, no histomorphometry, short follow-up

facts.population: Patients with anterior immediate implants placed with the root membrane technique in 3 private practices
facts.intervention: Root membrane technique: periodontal ligament-mediated immediate implant placement
facts.main_result: 5 failures in 250 implants; 10-year cumulative implant survival 96.5% and success 87.9%

facts.population: 40 patients each needing one anterior tooth replaced after extraction
facts.intervention: Socket shield technique with immediate post-extraction implant and immediate provisional crown

facts.funding_coi: Funded by the authors' own institutions; no conflicts of interest

facts.population: 23 published studies on the socket-shield technique (1 case-control, 4 animal histological, 1 abstract, 17+2 case reports)
facts.intervention: Socket-shield technique (intentional retention of a root section at immediate implant placement)
facts.main_result: Complications in 58/70 (82.86%) animal-study implants and 33/136 (24.26%) clinical-study implants; buccal/crestal bone loss most common
facts.sample_size: 23 studies; 70 animal implants and 136 clinical implants
facts.follow_up: 18 of 23 studies lasted 12 months or less
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: No meta-analysis possible (heterogeneity, no RCTs); 4 of 5 quality-assessed studies scored low

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Postextraction ridge sites (review; no study subjects)
facts.intervention: Partial extraction therapies: root submergence, socket-shield, pontic shield, proximal socket-shield
facts.main_result: Proposes PET as a collective term with a classification and indications; supporting literature is limited to case reports, case series and two animal histology reports
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Literature very poor (case reports, case series, animal histology); randomized and long-term data needed

facts.population: 30 adults with nonrestorable single anterior teeth with intact buccal periodontal tissues
facts.intervention: Modified socket shield technique (1.5 mm buccal root shield) with immediate implant and immediate single-crown restoration
facts.main_result: 100% implant survival at 1 year, ISQ 72.9 at placement and 74.6 at 1 year, no biologic complications, prosthetic complications 2.5%
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported (text truncated); funding not stated
facts.limitations: Limited follow-up time and no volumetric analysis

facts.main_result: Letter argues the systematic review misapplied its own eligibility criteria: 4 of 23 studies were not socket-shield, 3 were misrepresented as adverse effects, so bone loss was overstated
facts.funding_coi: No funding; three authors are paid to lecture on the socket-shield technique

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: One 45-year-old patient with a failing maxillary right central incisor adjacent to an implant crown

facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Single case, short-term (1 year) follow-up, technique-sensitive, limited long-term evidence

facts.population: Evidence from three systematic reviews on biologics in periodontal plastic surgery, infrabony defects and ridge preservation/implant site development
facts.intervention: Biologics: autologous blood-derived products, EMD, rhPDGF-BB, rhBMP-2
facts.comparison: Conventional treatment approaches
outcomes: ridge preservation/reconstruction and implant site development
facts.main_result: Appropriate use of biologics is generally safe and adds benefit to conventional treatment; benefit and risk vary by biologic and patient factors; evidence limited for gingival augmentation, ARP/ARR and ISD

facts.limitations: Limited clinical evidence for some indications (gingival augmentation, ARP/ARR, ISD)

facts.population: 65 patients with a single implant site in a healed alveolar ridge with lingual-buccal sloped configuration

facts.funding_coi: Supported by grants from Dentsply Sirona Implants/Astra Tech; some authors report honoraria and grants from industry
facts.limitations: Observational multicenter design without a well-defined control group

facts.population: Patients with dental implants and keratinized peri-implant mucosa
facts.intervention: Soft-tissue substitutes versus autogenous grafts to augment keratinized peri-implant mucosa; exposure KT <2 mm
facts.comparison: KT >= 2 mm; autogenous grafts
facts.main_result: Reduced KT width associated with biofilm, inflammation, discomfort, recession, bone loss and peri-implantitis; autogenous grafts are standard of care, xenogeneic substitutes similar to CTG
facts.sample_size: Systematic review 1: 22 articles (21 studies); review 2: 11 articles (10 investigations)
facts.funding_coi: Participants filed COI disclosures; industry funding, consultant and speaker fees declared
facts.limitations: Grafting review studies had unclear or high risk of bias

facts.population: 96 patients with 195 implants placed with simultaneous lateral GBR, at least 5 years after loading in a supportive periodontal therapy program

facts.follow_up: At least 5 years after loading; mean SPT 8.3 years
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Geistlich Pharma AG
facts.limitations: Retrospective analysis without formal sample size calculation

facts.population: Adult (over 18 years) subjects needing one or more dental implants, in prospective controlled trials of transcrestal sinus floor elevation
facts.intervention: Transcrestal sinus floor elevation, irrespective of technique, technology and timing
facts.comparison: Any other transcrestal sinus floor elevation procedure differing in at least one technical element (e.g. grafting protocol)
facts.main_result: Transcrestal sinus floor elevation is minimally invasive and effective; invasiveness can be reduced further without losing effectiveness by using powered instruments (drills, piezoelectric inserts, electrical mallet) instead of manual osteotome and hand mallet.
facts.funding_coi: Supported entirely by the Research Centre for the Study of Periodontal and Peri-implant Diseases, University of Ferrara

outcomes: number of surgical sessions and chair time

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Four illustrative patients with anterior (esthetic zone) implant sites, including a congenitally missing lateral incisor, a fractured central incisor, a resorbed incisor and an underdeveloped ridge
facts.intervention: Site preservation and overbuilding (orthodontic eruption, bone and connective tissue grafting, punch uncovering) before implant restoration

facts.population: Systemically healthy adults with at least one implant-supported fixed restoration
facts.intervention: Thin peri-implant soft tissue (buccal thickness <2 mm or probe shimmering)
facts.comparison: Thick peri-implant soft tissue (buccal thickness 2 mm or more)
facts.main_result: Post-follow-up PES did not differ between thin and thick tissue (MD 0.15, p=.46), but PES change favoured thick tissue (p=.05) and thin tissue showed more recession (-0.62 mm); evidence quality was very low.
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded by two University of Zurich clinics; authors declared no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Evidence quality was very low because of non-randomized studies, high risk of bias and residual confounding.

facts.population: Peri-implant soft tissues around osseointegrated implants (literature review)
facts.main_result: Supracrestal soft tissues around implants show structures analogous to non-inflamed gingiva, but the connective tissue has a different, scar-like spatial orientation; keratinized mucosa is not a prerequisite for long-term implant maintenance.
facts.limitations: Most studies have described structure only, with little data on the true biologic function of peri-implant soft tissues.

facts.population: One patient with multiple retained maxillary roots and periodontally compromised mandibular teeth, treated with interim complete dentures
facts.intervention: Cross-mounting buccal index (CMBI) made from the interim restoration for abutment selection and framework fabrication

facts.limitations: The method depends on a well-established provisional prosthesis and is contraindicated if the provisional has poor esthetics or function.

facts.journal: Journal of the International Academy of Periodontology
facts.population: Periodontally compromised teeth with increased mobility
facts.intervention: Splinting of mobile teeth to stronger adjacent teeth
facts.main_result: Splinting is an essential adjunct to cause-related therapy that can prolong the life of periodontally compromised mobile teeth, but it does not remove the cause of mobility and mobility may return after splint removal.
facts.limitations: Further research is required on the exact role of splints and on patient selection criteria.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 45 completely edentulous patients with poorly retained mandibular dentures (plus 2D finite element models)
facts.intervention: Two mini-implants splinted with a prefabricated bar retaining a mandibular overdenture

facts.main_result: At 24 months marginal bone loss was 1.43 mm (ball) vs 0.92 mm (bar), not significant (P=.116); FEA minimum principal stress was -118 MPa unsplinted vs -56.8 MPa splinted, and vertical bone loss was more prevalent in the ball group (51% vs 29%, P=.04).
facts.funding_coi: Grant from CONICYT (Chile), FONDEF Project Di1109
outcomes: bone stress by finite element analysis

facts.population: 198 patients with posterior partially edentulous jaws (Kennedy Class I/II) and 453 short implants (10 mm or shorter)

facts.funding_coi: Authors report no conflicts of interest

facts.population: 30 completely edentulous participants with problems retaining mandibular dentures

facts.comparison: Two nonsplinted immediately loaded implants with ball attachments

outcomes: vertical and horizontal circumferential bone loss on CBCT

facts.population: 18 patients (9 men, 9 women, aged 49-76) with at least two consecutive posterior implants bilaterally
facts.intervention: Splinted prostheses on short internal-connection implants (one side)

facts.funding_coi: Authors reported no conflicts of interest

facts.key_finding: Industry-sponsored special issue of Quintessence presenting Straumann BLX implants, including a case collection of immediate single molar crowns placed with a digital workflow.

facts.key_finding: Flyer for a one-day Straumann Academy course in Vienna in 2019 on BLX immediate implantation and immediate loading, with live surgeries.

facts.key_finding: Product catalog listing article numbers for Straumann BLX implants, instruments, abutments and prosthetic parts, plus bone substitutes and collagen products.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Reference list for ordering only; contains no clinical evidence.

facts.key_finding: Manufacturer technical guide to the Straumann BLX Implant System covering implant design, the TorcFit connection, drilling and placement steps, prosthetic components, impressions and instrument cleaning.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Procedural manual for the system; it is not clinical research.

facts.population: Bone level and tissue level implants in 14 included controlled clinical trials
facts.intervention: Apico-coronal implant position (supracrestal, equicrestal, subcrestal)
facts.comparison: Equicrestal versus subcrestal versus supracrestal placement
facts.main_result: For bone level implants, early CBL differed by 0.15 mm (P=.18) and late CBL by 0.03 mm between equi- and subcrestal placement; authors recommend tissue level implants equicrestally and bone level implants subcrestally.
facts.sample_size: 14 articles included, 12 in the quantitative synthesis
facts.funding_coi: University of Michigan Periodontal Graduate Student Research Fund

facts.population: 200 partially or fully edentulous patients with 657 Ankylos implants placed 1-3 mm subcrestally

facts.main_result: Prevalence of peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis was 66.5% and 15.0% at patient level (62.6% and 7.5% at implant level); peri-implantitis was associated with history of periodontitis (OR 5.33).
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Four patients; implants harvested en bloc with surrounding tissues

facts.funding_coi: Sponsored by a grant from BioHorizons

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry

facts.intervention: Healing abutments with a 0.7-mm Laser-Lok microgrooved band

facts.funding_coi: Supported by a grant from BioHorizons

facts.population: Six dogs

facts.main_result: Epithelial and connective tissue dimensions and connective tissue composition were similar at collagen-coated and uncoated implants after 4 and 8 weeks, with no adverse reactions.

facts.funding_coi: Grants from Implant Innovations Inc.; no conflicts declared

facts.population: Patients with treated periodontal disease receiving implants in partially edentulous premolar and molar areas

outcomes: marginal bone loss after 1 year of loading

facts.journal: Annals of Clinical and Analytical Medicine
facts.population: 2005 patients receiving cylindrical implants of the same trademark and type
facts.intervention: RBM surface implants
facts.comparison: SLA surface implants
facts.main_result: RBM implants had 96.06% success (74 of 1877 failed) and SLA 96.53% (93 of 2675 failed); no significant difference in osseointegration success.
facts.sample_size: 4793 implants in 2005 patients (abstract); 4552 implants in the results
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no conflict of interest

facts.journal: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
facts.main_result: Osseointegration is redefined as a foreign body reaction; moderately rough isotropic surfaces such as TiUnite show improved clinical results, while clinical evidence for nanoroughness, chemistry and hydrophilicity is lacking.
facts.funding_coi: Both authors are scientific advisors to Nobel Biocare

off_topic_reason: An automotive engineering paper on cylinder bore surface finish and oil consumption with no dental content.

facts.funding_coi: Phase II SBIR contract from the U.S. Army TACOM
facts.key_finding: The paper reviews the history of 2-D surface finish measurement and shows that 3-D measurement of surface replicas can characterize engine cylinder bore finish without destroying the part.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: It is an engineering paper on cylinder bores with no clinical dental content.

facts.population: Six commercial implant surfaces (7 surface areas) from different manufacturers
facts.intervention: Topographical characterization with FESEM, SEM and light interferometry
facts.main_result: Modern implant surfaces are highly complex with multiple scales of topography; Sa was lowest for the machined surface and about 1.5 micron for the BIOMET 3i blasted/dual-acid-etched/DCD, OsseoSpeed and SLActive surfaces.
facts.funding_coi: Authors are employees of BIOMET 3i
facts.key_finding: Six commercial implant surfaces were compared by FESEM, SEM and interferometry; they differ in sub-micron, micron and coarse topography, with Sa values from 0.18 micron (turned) to about 1.5 micron.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Implant surfaces differ in topography at several scales, but this manufacturer-authored poster gives no clinical outcome data.

facts.population: Animal studies (in vivo) of implants with measured surface roughness and 3-month bone healing
facts.intervention: Implants with increasing surface roughness (Ra/Sa)
facts.main_result: 15 of 16 comparisons showed higher bone-to-implant contact with higher roughness (6 significant); studies were too heterogeneous to pool.
facts.limitations: Selected studies were too heterogeneous for inference of data.

facts.population: 12 adult mini-pigs, implants placed in mandibles after premolar extraction
facts.intervention: Anodized (TiUnite) and HA-coated implants
facts.comparison: Machined surface implants
facts.main_result: Overall BIC was 19.39% for machined, 39.05% for HA-coated (P=0.0092) and 42.72% for anodized implants (P=0.0011), so anodized matched HA-coated.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 5 young adult mongrel male dogs, implants placed in healed premolar sites of the mandible
facts.intervention: Implants with TPS, HA-coated and sandblasted (SBM) surfaces
facts.comparison: Smooth machined implants
facts.main_result: Mean BIC was 41.7% machined, 48.9% TPS, 57.9% HA and 68.5% SBM; only SBM differed significantly from machined.
facts.funding_coi: Study supported by Paragon Implant Company

facts.population: 10 totally edentulous patients receiving transitional implants in the posterior maxilla

facts.comparison: Cylindrical EZPlus implant with self-tapping threads and sandblasted surface
facts.main_result: Mean BIC was 35.9% with test and 29.9% with control implants (p = 0.16, not significant); BD was similar (31.8% vs 32.5%, p = 0.9).

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.main_result: The authors argue marginal bone loss around implants reflects an immune imbalance rather than primary bacterial disease; massive immune overreaction affects only about 1-2% of implants at 10 years.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by grants from the Swedish Research Council, King Gustaf V and Queen Victoria Freemason Foundation and the Osteology Foundation; no conflicts of interest reported

facts.intervention: Surface topography (micro- and nanometer level) and surface chemistry modifications of oral implants, with reference to OsseoSpeed
facts.main_result: Moderately rough surfaces give the strongest bone response experimentally, but randomised clinical studies found no significant difference versus minimally rough implants; the benefit of nanosurfaces and hydrophilic/bioactive surfaces remains unproven.
facts.limitations: Evidence for nanotopography and surface chemistry effects is lacking in vivo and clinically.

facts.population: Twenty Labrador dogs with mandibular premolars extracted; implant sites in the mandible
facts.intervention: Screw implants with SLA surface and a circumferential trough creating a wound chamber, to model early healing/osseointegration
outcomes: histology of soft and hard tissue formation
bone formation and remodeling over time
facts.main_result: The wound chamber model allowed study of early bone formation: bone formation started within the first week, woven bone was replaced by parallel-fibered/lamellar bone, and implants stayed clinically stable despite temporary loss of hard tissue contact at 1-2 weeks.
materials_brands: ITI Dental Implant System solid screw implant, SLA surface (Institut Straumann AG)

facts.population: Göttingen minipigs with a buccal acute-type dehiscence model in the mandible
facts.intervention: Gradient anodized implant (NobelActive TiUltra) placed in buccal dehiscence defects
facts.comparison: Custom-made geometric replica with superhydrophilic sandblasted acid-etched (SLActive) surface, and a commercial BLX implant with the same surface
facts.main_result: At 8 weeks, de novo crestal bone and osseointegration were significantly greater around the SLActive control implants than around the gradient anodized test implant.
facts.sample_size: 15 minipigs; n = 6 per group at 2 weeks and n = 8 at 8 weeks
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Institut Straumann AG; two authors receive speaker honorariums from Straumann

facts.population: Patients treated with endosseous dental implants in published longitudinal human studies (edentulous, overdenture, partially edentulous, single tooth)
facts.intervention: Implants with roughened titanium surfaces
facts.comparison: Relatively smooth (machined) titanium implants; also hydroxyapatite-coated implants
outcomes: implant success rate (odds ratio, Peto meta-analysis)
facts.main_result: Predictably high success was achieved with rough and smooth titanium and HA-coated implants; rough surfaces had higher success in most indications except single-tooth replacements, and mandibular implants outperformed maxillary ones.
facts.limitations: The success criteria used in each study were not critically analyzed and different studies used different criteria.

facts.population: 50 edentulous or to-be-edentulous patients needing an implant-supported cross-arch prosthesis
facts.intervention: Immediately loaded cross-arch prostheses on four to eight roughened-surface implants (iRES Shape 1BC)
facts.comparison: Machined/turned surface implants (iRES iPerio), 25 patients
facts.main_result: At 1 year no prosthesis failed; two machined implants failed in one patient; marginal bone loss -0.64 mm (rough) vs -0.68 mm (turned), no significant difference.
facts.funding_coi: I-RES, the implant manufacturer, donated implants and components; no interference declared
facts.limitations: Small sample size (pilot) and baseline imbalance in implant length and number of implants per patient.

facts.population: 36 patients receiving ITI SLA implants in maxilla and mandible
facts.intervention: Immediately loaded implants with ISQ measured by resonance-frequency analysis
facts.comparison: Implants loaded after 3 months (delayed loading)
outcomes: ISQ at placement and over 12 weeks
facts.main_result: All implants passed the 1-year loading control; two implants failed (ISQ at placement 48 DL and 53 IL), and RFA was not a reliable tool to identify mobile implants.
materials_brands: ITI SLA implants (Straumann); Osstell RFA device

facts.intervention: Surface roughness, wettability and cleanliness modifications of dental implant surfaces
facts.main_result: Hydrophilic implants improve initial blood contact, support wound healing and accelerate osseointegration, and roughness and wetting parameters can help predict bioresponse.
facts.limitations: Knowledge of surface-related reactions is fragmentary and complex multi-scale surfaces are hard to manufacture reproducibly.

facts.intervention: RBM (hydroxyapatite/calcium phosphate blasting with soft etching) implant surface compared to SLA
facts.comparison: SLA (alumina large-grit blasted and acid-etched) surface
facts.main_result: Manufacturer states RBM avoids alumina contamination but yields a less porous surface; reported survival is 97.2% at 4 years for RBM and 95% at 5 years for SLA.
materials_brands: DSI implants of Ti6Al-4V ELI alloy
facts.key_finding: The brochure compares RBM and SLA implant surfaces: RBM uses resorbable calcium phosphate blasting with soft etching and avoids alumina residues, while SLA gives a more porous two-level topography. It quotes 97.2% survival at 4 years for RBM and 95% at 5 years for SLA.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: This is a manufacturer's comparison without independent data, so surface claims should not guide implant selection by themselves.

facts.intervention: Implant surface modifications (micro/nano topography, biomimetic coatings) and their effect on osseointegration
facts.main_result: Most in vitro and in vivo studies indicate micro and submicro (nano) topographies benefit bone cell interaction, accelerating and increasing the quality of bone-to-implant contact.

facts.intervention: Periodontal microsurgery with the surgical microscope, instruments and microsuturing
facts.main_result: Microsurgery offers enhanced outcomes over macrosurgery, especially passive wound closure and reduced tissue trauma, with more rapid healing.
facts.limitations: Microsurgery is technique-sensitive and more demanding than periodontal macrosurgery.

facts.journal: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
facts.intervention: Selective pressure method with concave transmucosal profile of implant provisional restorations
facts.main_result: The selective pressure method and concave transmucosal profile delivered esthetically and functionally successful implant restorations in the presented cases.

facts.population: A prepared extracted mandibular molar with a thermal probe in the pulp chamber, in a water bath
facts.intervention: Direct fabrication and relining of provisional crowns with five resins (PMMA, PEMA, PVEMA, Bis-acrylic, VLP urethane dimethacrylate)

facts.journal: The European Journal of Esthetic Dentistry

outcomes: accuracy of soft tissue profile transfer

facts.population: One 27-year-old woman with peri-implant recession at a maxillary right lateral incisor implant

facts.population: Partially edentulous patients with fixed implant-supported single crowns and FDPs

facts.population: Three adult female Göttingen minipigs, mandibular premolar extraction sockets
