facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: One 62-year-old woman with a peri-implant osseous defect at an IMZ implant (right central incisor)
facts.intervention: Open flap debridement, surface decontamination with 24% EDTA gel, grafting with porous titanium granules (PTG) and resubmersion
facts.main_result: After 12 months PTG was in close contact with new bone growing into the granule porosities and onto the implant surface; radiographic defect heights fell from 9.24/5.70 mm to 0.97/0.74 mm (mesial/distal)
facts.limitations: Only one case; further evaluation in patients with thinner mucosa is necessary; buccal graft height was lost
outcomes: histology and element analysis of the graft

off_topic_reason: A general surgical SmPC for a fibrin sealant with no dental or oral surgical content.

materials_brands: TISSEEL fibrin sealant (human fibrinogen, synthetic aprotinin, human thrombin)

facts.population: Five New Zealand white rabbits, both maxillary sinuses
facts.intervention: Sinus floor elevation grafted with Bio-Oss mixed with Tisseel fibrin sealant
facts.comparison: Bio-Oss mixed with normal saline
facts.main_result: New bone formation 14.8% (Bio-Oss+saline) vs 18.5% (Bio-Oss+Tisseel); residual grafted bone 70.5% vs 60.4%; difference in bone formation insignificant
facts.funding_coi: Funded by a research grant of Pusan National University; no competing interests
facts.limitations: Pilot experiment with only five animals

facts.population: Two patients (30-year-old and 59-year-old women) with extraction sites and bone defects needing implant site reconstruction
facts.intervention: Bone grafting with human fibrin sealant mixed with deproteinized bovine bone, covered with a collagen resorbable membrane, then delayed implant placement
outcomes: clinical bone regeneration for implant placement
facts.main_result: The protocol gave good clinical results for bone regeneration in implant surgery with a relatively simple, non-invasive procedure.
facts.follow_up: 20 months and 36 months post-op in the two cases
facts.limitations: Literature on xenograft plus fibrin sealant is controversial; more cases and long-term clinical and histological studies are needed.

facts.population: Two patients with horizontal bony deficiency: a 64-year-old woman and a 40-year-old man, both with periodontitis
facts.intervention: F.I.R.S.T. technique: fibrin sealant mixed with collagenated porcine xenograft and used to glue a cortical lamina membrane over the defect
facts.main_result: Case 1 gained 4.05 mm of horizontal width, stable at 3 years, with newly formed trabecular bone on histology; case 2 widened a 1 mm ridge to 5 mm and implants were stable 3 years after loading.
facts.limitations: Only two cases; further studies are needed to confirm the modification.

facts.journal: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
facts.population: Two patients: a 57-year-old woman needing anterior maxillary ridge augmentation and a 65-year-old woman needing mandibular ridge augmentation
facts.intervention: Tisseel fibrin sealant as binder for particulate bone grafts (autogenous plus xenograft), no membrane
outcomes: graft form and bulk retention on CBCT
facts.main_result: Tisseel-bound composite grafts maintained ridge form and position, with excellent retention at the 10-year scan in patient 1.
facts.funding_coi: First author has stock with X-Nav; other author none.
facts.limitations: Small sample, no randomization, and no comparative volume measurements because of differing imaging.

facts.population: 2,858 patients each with a posterior tooth with at least one visible crack, enrolled by 209 US dentists
facts.intervention: Practitioner-chosen treatment or monitoring of cracked posterior teeth, followed annually
facts.comparison: Teeth recommended for treatment versus teeth recommended for monitoring at baseline; intracoronal versus full/partial coverage restorations
facts.main_result: Over 98% of cracked teeth survived 3 years (37 extractions); 14% of restored teeth failed; about 80% of monitored teeth stayed on monitoring.
facts.funding_coi: NIH/NIDCR grants; authors declare no competing interests

facts.population: Zirconia crowns on custom abutments fabricated on a master cast with an Astra Tech EV implant analog (maxillary right first premolar)
facts.comparison: Interrupted digital Atlantis workflow (abutment received and rescanned)
facts.main_result: All three workflows gave clinically acceptable marginal gaps (<120 um); full digital Atlantis had the smallest marginal gap (SEM 22 um, Geomagic 14 um) and split-file the smallest internal fit (59 um).
facts.sample_size: 7 specimens per group (5-7 analyzed in Geomagic)
facts.funding_coi: Stanley D. Tylman Research Grant (AAFP) and Texas A&M Restorative Dentistry; funders had no role

facts.population: 10 healthy young volunteers with thick gingival biotype, 40 maxillary premolars
facts.intervention: Expasyl retraction paste
facts.comparison: Single KnitTrax cord size 0 with aluminum chloride
facts.main_result: Paste produced a gap 0.041 mm smaller than cord (P=.014); both gaps were clinically acceptable (cord 0.282 mm, paste 0.241 mm) and height change did not differ.
facts.follow_up: 2 weeks between sessions, plus a further 2 weeks final assessment
materials_brands: KnitTrax cord size 0 (Pascal) with aluminum chloride
facts.limitations: Small sample, unprepared teeth in thick-biotype patients, and measurement points relying on researcher judgment.

facts.journal: Journal of IMAB - Annual Proceeding (Scientific Papers)
facts.intervention: Second retraction cord (double cord technique) before subgingival impression for fixed prosthesis
facts.comparison: Single cord retraction technique
outcomes: impression quality grade of the prepared supports (poor/good/excellent)
facts.main_result: Poor impressions were 41.7% with one cord versus 3.6% with two cords; excellent were 23% versus 82.4%.

facts.population: 75 STL datasets of left upper first molar preparations for zirconia crowns made by 75 general dentists
facts.intervention: Digital (CAD software and 3D inspection) evaluation of preparation geometry against clinical recommendations
facts.main_result: No preparation met all recommendations; mean convergence angle was 26.7 degrees, abutment height 4.1 mm, and over 30% had insufficient interocclusal reduction.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

facts.population: Zirconia crown copings on acrylic maxillary molar dies prepared at 4, 8 and 12 degrees
facts.intervention: Preparation angle of 4, 8 or 12 degrees total taper, with copings made by a laboratory or milling-center CAD/CAM system
facts.comparison: Laboratory versus milling-center CAD/CAM fabrication; 4 versus 8 versus 12 degrees
outcomes: cement gap at chamfer, axial wall, occlusal and marginal locations
facts.main_result: Preparation angle and measurement location significantly affected fit; 12 degrees gave best overall fit; marginal openings were 36.6 to 45.5 um in all groups and did not differ by fabrication site.
facts.sample_size: 10 copings per angle per CAD/CAM system (60 copings)
materials_brands: Cercon zirconia (Cercon Base, Cercon Brain, DeguDent)
KetacCem Aplicap glass ionomer cement (3M ESPE)

facts.population: Gingival tissues around vital and nonvital human teeth in adults (10 included studies, 400 teeth)
facts.intervention: Gingival retraction with cords, pastes, surgery, cautery or lasers
facts.comparison: The methods served as their own comparators
facts.main_result: Of 145 articles, 10 studies (400 teeth) were included; chemomechanical retraction was most common and no method was clearly superior; clinical parameters were not significantly affected.
facts.funding_coi: Authors deny any conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Heterogeneous results; English only and no grey literature search.

facts.intervention: Conventional and modern gingival retraction methods (mechanical, chemical, surgical) for tooth- and implant-supported fixed prostheses
facts.main_result: Gingival retraction techniques are classified as mechanical, chemical or surgical; the review discusses cords, cordless techniques, hemostatic agents, lasers, rotary curettage, electrosurgery, implants and digital impression.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

facts.population: 40 extracted sound human maxillary first premolars (from patients aged 18-22 years)
facts.intervention: Monolithic zirconia crowns (traditional IPS e.max ZirCAD LT vs translucent ZirCAD MT) on teeth prepared with shoulder or feather-edge margin
facts.comparison: Shoulder (1 mm) vs feather-edge margin design; traditional vs translucent zirconia
facts.main_result: Mean fracture resistance was highest for traditional zirconia with shoulder margin (A1 2.903 kN), then A2 2.3, B1 1.854 and B2 1.523 kN; shoulder beat feather-edge and traditional beat translucent zirconia.
materials_brands: IPS e.max ZirCAD MT Multi A3 (Ivoclar)
RelyX U200 self-adhesive resin cement (3M ESPE)

facts.intervention: Mechanical, chemicomechanical and surgical retraction of periodontal and peri-implant soft tissues
facts.main_result: In peri-implant tissues contemporary retraction means should be avoided; technique choice should consider medical history, working zone and soft-tissue biotype.

facts.population: 40 gingivally healthy adult probands (upper premolars), later with mild artificial gingivitis
facts.intervention: Gingival displacement before impression: double cord technique with aluminum chloride, or kaolin paste (Expasyl) containing aluminum chloride
facts.comparison: Contralateral quadrant without gingival displacement (split-mouth), and cord vs paste
outcomes: marginal gingiva height change / gingival recession
facts.main_result: Cord gave better sulcus representation than paste in healthy gingiva, but mild gingivitis worsened it for cord and not for paste; no permanent palatal recession up to six months.
facts.funding_coi: Investigator-initiated trial partly supported by 3M Oral Care; no conflict of interest declared

facts.intervention: Tissue displacement methods: mechanical, mechanico-chemical, rotary gingival curettage and electrosurgery
facts.main_result: Four families of gingival displacement are described with advantages and disadvantages; electrosurgery is safe and effective when variables are controlled.

facts.population: Seven studies (four RCTs) on patients needing indirect fixed restorations or with unprepared teeth, healthy gingiva
facts.intervention: Gingival retraction techniques without cord (cordless, e.g. paste)
facts.comparison: Cord technique
facts.main_result: Both cord and cordless techniques reliably retract gingiva; paste gives a drier field and is less injurious but displaces tissue less than cord.
facts.sample_size: 7 studies included (4 RCTs), 8 to 252 participants per study
facts.limitations: No meta-analysis because of heterogeneity of measurement variables across studies

facts.journal: The University of Adelaide, School of Dentistry (PhD thesis)
facts.population: 60 extracted third molars sectioned into enamel halves, worn against porcelain or gold discs
facts.intervention: Wear of enamel against four porcelain systems and a type III gold alloy in electro-mechanical wear machines at pH 6.1 and pH 1.2
facts.comparison: Enamel worn against enamel (control)
outcomes: wear volume loss of enamel and ceramic (3D scanning)
facts.main_result: At pH 6.1 only the leucite-reinforced pressable ceramic significantly increased enamel wear versus enamel controls; under acid conditions enamel wear rose sharply but gold did not exceed enamel controls.
materials_brands: Authentic (Ceramay) leucite-reinforced veneering and pressable ceramic
Vita Mark II (Vita Zahnfabrik) machinable ceramic
facts.limitations: Findings should be cautiously extrapolated to in vivo conditions
facts.key_finding: Enamel worn against leucite-reinforced pressable ceramic wore more than enamel worn against enamel at near-neutral pH, while the other porcelains and the gold alloy did not. Under simulated gastric acid, enamel wear rose sharply for all groups, but gold did not wear enamel more than enamel controls, and the machinable ceramic became porous.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: In this laboratory study, the choice of porcelain affects wear of opposing enamel and gold remained enamel-friendly even under acid; results need cautious extrapolation to patients.

facts.intervention: Ceramic laminate veneers: materials, applications and techniques
facts.main_result: Clinical success of laminate veneers depends on suitable patient indications and correct application of the materials and techniques.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.intervention: Less invasive adhesive and CAD/CAM-based restorative concepts: polymer pre-treatment, veneers, onlays and fixed dental prostheses
facts.main_result: Overview of advances in fixed prosthodontics with support in material selection for single-tooth restorations through fixed dental prostheses.

facts.population: 66-year-old man with bruxism and severe tooth wear
facts.intervention: Full-mouth rehabilitation at increased vertical dimension: lithium disilicate veneers (anterior), CAD/CAM lithium disilicate overlays (posterior) and monolithic zirconia crowns on canines and first molars for four-point stability
facts.main_result: After 4 years of function no complications were registered.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Longer-term randomized studies on ceramics in grinders are needed

facts.population: Clinical studies of patients with tooth wear restored with direct or indirect restorations
facts.intervention: Indirect restorations (ceramics, composites, metal) for tooth wear
facts.comparison: Direct restorations (resin composite)
outcomes: clinical performance by FDI or USPHS criteria
facts.main_result: No evidence was found for the superiority of any restoration technique for treating tooth wear.
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Most included studies were at high risk of bias and heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis.

facts.population: 7 patients with severe tooth wear
facts.intervention: Full-mouth adhesively bonded monolithic lithium disilicate occlusal onlays (IPS e.max Press)
facts.main_result: Monolithic lithium disilicate occlusal onlays showed 100% survival up to 11 years; 3.9% marginal discoloration and 1% marginal crack.

facts.population: Published treatment reports of generalized, complete-arch tooth wear
facts.intervention: Minimally invasive adhesive rehabilitation of generalized tooth wear, analyzed in five steps (waxing, occlusal position, VDI, restoration, follow-up)
facts.main_result: Eleven studies (16 publications) were included; diagnostic waxing was used in 9, VDI tested in 8, and composite resin and glass ceramic were each used in 6 for definitive treatment.
facts.sample_size: 11 studies (16 publications), each of 1 to 4 patients
facts.follow_up: 0 to 20 months after definitive treatment in included studies
facts.limitations: Included studies were case reports and small case series.

facts.population: Patients with severely worn occlusal surfaces (posterior teeth)
facts.intervention: Minimally invasive glass-ceramic (lithium disilicate) occlusal onlays with supragingival margins, adhesively cemented
facts.comparison: Traditional full crowns and direct composite restorations (discussed)
facts.main_result: Occlusal onlays of high-strength glass-ceramics with supragingival margins reduce loss of dental hard tissue and increase enamel available for bonding compared with full crowns, provided the protocol is followed.
facts.limitations: Highly technique-dependent; lack of long-term clinical data for CAD/CAM polymer restorations.

facts.population: Two patients in their mid-thirties with localised anterior tooth wear
facts.intervention: Gold palatal veneers on maxillary canines plus direct composite restorations, using the Dahl concept and canine-guided mutually protected occlusion
outcomes: posterior dento-alveolar compensation and occlusal contact
canine guidance and mutually protected occlusion
facts.main_result: In both cases posterior dento-alveolar compensation occurred within 18 weeks with full occlusal contact re-established and a canine-guided mutually protected occlusion.
facts.limitations: Any interventive restorative treatment is subject to maintenance, repairs or replacement.

facts.journal: The Kaohsiung Journal of Medical Sciences
facts.population: Published literature on the lithium disilicate glass-ceramic IPS e.max (mainly e.max CAD)
facts.intervention: IPS e.max CAD lithium disilicate glass-ceramic (materials science, properties, clinical use)
facts.main_result: IPS e.max CAD shows excellent mechanical properties and acceptable esthetics with promising short- and medium-term single-crown survival, but long-term survival data are insufficient.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: Clinical studies are limited in scope and time; lack of long-term data and of data on multi-unit FPDs.

facts.population: New mechanical torque-limiting devices (friction-style and spring-style) from 6 implant manufacturers
facts.intervention: Measurement of delivered torque of friction-style and spring-style devices with a digital torque gauge
facts.comparison: Friction-style versus spring-style devices
outcomes: absolute difference between delivered and target torque
facts.main_result: No difference in accuracy between friction-style and spring-style devices (P=.872); all devices were within ±10% of target torque.
facts.sample_size: 30 devices (5 per manufacturer), each tested 10 times
facts.limitations: In vitro study using only new devices; wear with use was not tested.

facts.population: Controlled human (4) and animal (6) studies of implants placed with high vs low insertion torque
facts.intervention: High insertion torque (>25 Ncm, up to 176 Ncm)
facts.comparison: Low insertion torque (<30-35 Ncm)
facts.main_result: No significant difference in marginal bone resorption (ES 0.13, 95% CI -0.12 to 0.38, human studies) or implant failure (RR 0.39, 95% CI 0.01-20.77) between high and low insertion torque.
facts.sample_size: 591 implants (348 high torque, 243 low torque) in 4 human and 6 animal studies
facts.funding_coi: Authors declare no financial interest
facts.limitations: High risk of bias in nearly all studies, few implants and large between-study heterogeneity; overall body of evidence is weak.

facts.population: Patients rehabilitated with dental implants (6 studies: 3 RCTs, 3 prospective)
facts.intervention: Implant placement with high insertion torque (50 Ncm or more)
facts.comparison: Regular or low insertion torque (less than 50 Ncm)
facts.main_result: No significant difference between high and regular/low torque in implant survival (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.06-4.06, P=.52) or marginal bone loss (MD 0.15 mm, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.44, P=.30).
facts.sample_size: 651 implants (437 high torque, 214 regular/low) in 389 participants from 6 studies
facts.follow_up: at least 6 months (inclusion criterion); 6 to 36 months in included studies
facts.limitations: Authors recommend further research; consensus on definition of high/low torque is lacking.

facts.population: 21 patients with edentulous mandibles (mean age 67.4 years)
facts.intervention: Implants placed with low (<20 Ncm) or high (>50 Ncm) insertion torque, with machined or anodized neck design
facts.comparison: Low versus high insertion torque; machined versus anodized neck (split-mouth)
outcomes: peri-implant bone level change on radiographs
probing depth and bleeding on probing
facts.main_result: No influence of insertion torque (p=.912) or implant neck design (p=.682) on peri-implant bone level at 1 year; bone loss was 0.69 and 0.68 mm for the two torque groups.
materials_brands: Osstell mentor with Smartpeg abutments (Integration Diagnostics)
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest; supported by the authors' department (Department of Oral Surgery, Medical University of Vienna)

facts.population: 48 patients (38 analysed) with 66 Tapered Screw-Vent implants, 4.5 mm diameter
facts.intervention: Implants placed with maximum insertion torque of 70 Ncm or more (mean 110.6 Ncm, up to 176 Ncm)
facts.comparison: Implants placed with insertion torque of 30-50 Ncm (9 implants, mean 37.1 Ncm)
outcomes: marginal bone resorption at loading and 1 year
facts.main_result: Mean marginal bone loss was 1.03 mm (low torque) vs 0.72 mm (high torque) at loading and 1.09 vs 1.24 mm at 1 year, with no significant difference between groups.
facts.sample_size: 66 implants in 48 patients in the abstract; 66 implants in 38 patients analysed
facts.limitations: Nonrandomized, non-blinded design with a small control group and limited access to posterior sites for torque measurement.

facts.main_result: Trauma from occlusion does not cause gingivitis or periodontal pockets but affects the supporting tissues; inflammation and occlusal trauma act as co-destructive factors in periodontitis.
facts.funding_coi: Research supported by NIDR, USPHS grant DE-00646-0 5

facts.population: 64 sets of human jaws from autopsy; 106 interdental spaces examined histologically
facts.intervention: Bite analysis, then histological mesio-distal sectioning and radiographs of jaw specimens
facts.main_result: Angular defects and attachment loss were related to subgingival plaque downgrowth and CEJ level, with no evidence that trauma from occlusion acts as a co-factor.
facts.sample_size: 106 interdental spaces from 31 persons' specimens analysed (of 64 collected)

facts.main_result: Periodontal staging and grading should start every implant case so that treatment planning maximizes conservation of teeth and preservation of alveolar bone ahead of restoratively driven plans.
facts.funding_coi: Authors report grants/honoraria from implant and biomaterial companies (e.g., Straumann, Geistlich, BioHorizons)

facts.main_result: A prosthodontically driven virtual plan combining CBCT, intraoral/facial scans and a diagnostic wax-up supports computer-guided implant surgery, with treatment difficulty assessed beforehand.
facts.funding_coi: No disclosures

facts.population: 20 adults with single implants replacing a second molar
facts.intervention: Single-implant prosthesis on a second molar, tested with peanut chewing test, questionnaire and VAS
facts.comparison: Same patients before insertion of the implant prosthesis
facts.main_result: Masticatory performance rose from 67.8% to 84.3% after the implant prosthesis (P<0.0001), and over 90% of patients were satisfied.
Prosthetic design in the edentulous jaw depends on number and location of implants, which in turn determine whether a fixed or removable (overdenture) prosthesis is chosen.

facts.population: 50 subjects with stage III or IV periodontitis and a tooth with attachment loss to or beyond the apex
facts.intervention: Periodontal regeneration (papilla preservation flaps with EMD, membranes, bone grafts)
facts.comparison: Extraction and replacement with implant- or tooth-supported fixed partial denture
facts.main_result: Survival was 88% for regeneration and 100% for extraction and replacement, with similar complication-free survival and lower cost for regeneration.
facts.funding_coi: Funded in part by the European Research Group on Periodontology
facts.limitations: Sample size was based on logistic considerations given the pilot nature of the study.

facts.main_result: Many patients prefer fixed prostheses for the edentulous jaw, but patient-centred studies do not confirm this, and overdentures may offer advantages in cost and hygiene.

Tooth maintenance is suitable when the tooth is not extensively diseased, has high strategic value, lies in an intact arch and gingival preservation is paramount; otherwise strategic use of implants and short-span FDPs is recommended.

facts.population: Adult General Dental Services patients in England and Wales, 1990-2006
facts.intervention: Restorations (amalgam, resin composite, glass ionomer, crowns, veneers) placed in permanent teeth
outcomes: time to extraction of the restored tooth
facts.main_result: At 15 years 32-42% of restorations survived to re-intervention and 77.8-84.2% of restored teeth were not extracted; larger restorations did worse and crowns beat direct restorations for re-intervention but not extraction.
facts.sample_size: 13,896,048 tooth restorations in more than 3 million patients

facts.population: Adult General Dental Services patients in England and Wales with restored incisor teeth, 1990-2006
facts.intervention: Direct restorations, crowns and veneers in incisor teeth
facts.comparison: Restoration types, patient and dentist factors compared
outcomes: time to extraction of the restored incisor
facts.main_result: 35% of incisor restorations survived without re-intervention at 15 years and 81% of restored incisors were not extracted; crowns did best for re-intervention (48%) but worst-but-one for extraction (75%) versus composite 84% and veneers 93%.

facts.population: Partially and totally edentulous patients with implant-supported fixed reconstructions (nine studies, 1,369 patients)
facts.intervention: Partial FDPs on 2-4 implants and full-arch FDPs on 4-6 implants
facts.main_result: Partial FDP survival was 98.9% at 5 and 97.8% at 10 years, full-arch FDP survival on 4-6 implants 97.5%/95.0% maxillary and 97.9%/95.9% mandibular, but evidence on the optimal number and distribution is lacking.
facts.sample_size: 9 studies, 5,642 implants and 1,448 reconstructions in 1,369 patients
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Substantial lack of evidence; no controlled trials comparing implant numbers and implant-to-replaced-unit ratios not reported

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 18 patients (14 partially, 4 fully edentulous), age 38-71, with insufficient vertical bone height
facts.intervention: Implants placed with exposed threads (2-7 mm), autogenous bone chips from a bone filter aspirator and a barrier membrane, flaps coronally displaced, 12-month healing
outcomes: regenerated tissue filling the space under the membrane
facts.main_result: 3 of 22 membranes became exposed; in the 19 covered cases the space beneath the membrane filled with regenerated tissue, shown histologically to be vital bone.
facts.limitations: Technique-sensitive, with risk of early membrane exposure; further research needed on load-bearing capacity and long-term results.

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 20 partially edentulous patients with vertical jawbone deficiencies, 58 implants
facts.intervention: Titanium-reinforced e-PTFE membrane with demineralized freeze-dried bone allograft (Group A) condensed under the membrane
facts.comparison: Autogenous bone chips under the membrane (Group B)
facts.main_result: Mean vertical bone gain was 3.1 mm (124%) with allograft and 5.02 mm (95%) with autogenous chips; new bone-titanium contact ranged 39.1-63.2% depending on pre-existing bone quality.
facts.sample_size: 20 patients, 58 implants (22 in Group A, 30 extending beyond bone crest in Group B)

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: Partially edentulous adults needing vertical bone augmentation with single or multiple implants

facts.main_result: Mean bone level at 6 years was 1.33 mm (resorbable) vs 1.00 mm (nonresorbable); adjusted difference 0.15 mm (95% CI -0.39 to 0.69, P = .5713), no failures or complications after loading.

facts.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflicts of interest

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: 19 patients with vertically deficient alveolar ridges (20 procedures)
facts.intervention: GBR with a 1:1 mixture of autogenous bone and ABBM covered by a titanium-reinforced high-density PTFE membrane

facts.follow_up: Mean 8.24 months of graft healing before biopsy
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 21 patients (29 mandibular surgical sites) needing vertical bone regeneration in the posterior mandible

facts.main_result: Cumulative implant survival was 93.6% with mean bone remodeling 0.34-1.04 mm over 6 years; success was higher with simultaneous (82.5%) than staged (66.8%) placement and with keratinized mucosa (82.1% vs 58.4%).
materials_brands: W. L. Gore titanium-reinforced e-PTFE membrane
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: 21 patients with edentulous, severely atrophic anterior maxillae needing horizontal and vertical augmentation
facts.intervention: Bilaminar cortical tenting graft from a split ramus block, filled with particulate autograft, covered with ABBM and collagen membrane

facts.funding_coi: No specific grant funding; no competing interests

facts.population: 49 partially edentulous patients with 123 Brånemark implants in 53 vertically augmented ridges

facts.journal: The International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry

materials_brands: ITI Dental Implant System (Straumann), TPS surface

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants

facts.population: Adult patients with anterior tooth wear, compensatory eruption and deep overbite needing restorative space
facts.intervention: Orthodontic intrusion of maxillary and/or mandibular incisors (or jaw surgery) to create restorative space, guided by four diagnostic principles
facts.comparison: Crown lengthening with endodontic and post-and-core treatment, or opening the vertical dimension by restoring posterior teeth
facts.main_result: Orthodontic intrusion of abraded incisors is a viable method for restoring them more conservatively, rather than increasing vertical dimension.
facts.key_finding: Anterior tooth wear with deep overbite is usually caused by compensatory eruption, not an overclosed bite, so increasing the vertical dimension is usually the wrong diagnosis. Orthodontic intrusion of the incisors, planned from the occlusal plane, upper lip position and gingival levels, creates restorative space without further tooth reduction.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Before opening the vertical dimension in a worn anterior dentition, assess the occlusal plane and consider orthodontic incisor intrusion with the restorative dentist.

facts.journal: International Journal of Applied Dental Sciences
facts.population: Seven completely edentulous complete-denture wearers aged 45-70 years
facts.intervention: Complete dentures with occlusal vertical dimension reduced by about 3 mm
facts.comparison: Complete dentures with an appropriate OVD
outcomes: masseter EMG amplitude during maximum clenching
facts.main_result: Mean masseter EMG during maximum clenching was 435.35 uV with appropriate OVD versus 299.25 uV with reduced OVD (significant).
facts.follow_up: EMG two months after first denture delivery, repeated two weeks after the second set

facts.intervention: Increasing or decreasing the vertical dimension of occlusion in treatment planning
facts.key_finding: The vertical dimension of occlusion is set by the contracted length of the elevator muscles, and the teeth adapt to it. Changes in VDO self-adapt back to the original dimension without harm if the occlusal contacts are in harmony with centric relation, so unnecessary increases are overtreatment.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Evaluate VDO changes on face-bow mounted casts in centric relation, and use the most conservative change that gives a stable anterior and posterior contact.

facts.population: 30 dental students (12 men, 18 women), aged 21-30
facts.intervention: Occlusal vertical dimension increased by 2, 4, 6 and 8 mm with polyvinyl siloxane occlusal registrations while posed smiles were photographed

outcomes: incisal edge to upper lip distance
incisal edge to lower lip distance
facts.main_result: Increasing OVD significantly increased interlabial gap height, incisal edge to lower lip distance and display zone area, and decreased smile index; smile width and upper lip length were unchanged.

Nikon D7000 camera with Micro-NIKKOR 105 mm lens

facts.journal: International Journal of Dentistry and Oral Science

facts.intervention: Phonetic (closest speaking space) method of locating the vertical dimension of occlusion
facts.key_finding: The phonetic method marks the closest speaking line on the lower incisors while the patient makes s sounds, then the centric bite record is made about 1 mm closed from that line. Patients with opposing natural teeth should keep their existing vertical dimension.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Use the closest speaking level to set the vertical dimension when no opposing teeth are in contact, and otherwise work as close to the existing vertical dimension as possible.

facts.journal: Journal of the American Ceramic Society (Communications)

facts.intervention: Lava / Lava Plus zirconia restorations: indications, preparation, shading, handling and cementation

facts.population: Forty disk-shaped yttria-stabilized zirconia specimens (15 x 1.2 mm) plus 10 controls
