outcomes: failures during thermal cycling and mechanical loading
facts.main_result: No FPD failed during chewing simulation and median fracture force (1173.5 to 1316.0 N) did not differ between groups or from the control.
facts.follow_up: chewing simulation of about five years of oral service

facts.population: Fifty zirconia plates (LavaMulti, 3M ESPE) with steatite ball antagonists
facts.intervention: Surface treatments: as fired, sandblasted, ground, ground and polished, ground and glazed, tested in a pin-on-disk wear apparatus
facts.comparison: The five surface-treatment groups against each other
facts.main_result: Polished zirconia caused the lowest antagonist wear (66 um) versus 81-85 um for other treatments; zirconia wear was measurable only for the glazed group (46 um).

facts.funding_coi: Published by the manufacturer, Ivoclar Vivadent AG Research & Development
facts.key_finding: Manufacturer scientific documentation for IPS e.max ZirCAD, a zirconia available as discs and blocks in several translucency levels for copings, frameworks, full-contour crowns and bridges. It summarizes zirconia material science, in-vitro tests, clinical studies and biocompatibility.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Useful as a source of material properties and indications from the manufacturer, but it is not independent evidence of clinical performance.

facts.population: Stereolithography additively manufactured zirconia bar specimens (25x4x3 mm)
facts.intervention: Printing zirconia bars with an SLA ceramic printer and sintering to 0%, 20% or 40% porosity
facts.comparison: 0% versus 20% versus 40% porosity groups
facts.main_result: The 40%-porosity group had the highest manufacturing accuracy and lowest volume change; volumetric changes ranged from -20.33% to +3.5% and were uneven across axes.
facts.limitations: None of the groups tested were able to perfectly match the virtual design of the specimens.

facts.intervention: Monolithic zirconia ceramics (conventional and ultra-translucent/multicolor)
facts.main_result: Monolithic zirconia causes minimal antagonist wear if polished and shows promising 5-7 year survival, but evidence on ultra-translucent types is limited.
facts.follow_up: up to 5 or 7 years (short-term studies reviewed)
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Due to limited studies evaluating the wear properties of ultra-translucent material, no sound conclusions can be made.

facts.population: 32 extracted human maxillary premolars in 4 groups of 8
facts.intervention: Monolithic 3Y zirconia full crown (control), MODF onlay, MODL onlay and MODBL overlay, bonded by air abrasion, MDP primer and composite resin cement, then 1.2 million thermomechanical cycles
facts.comparison: Full crown preparation (group 1, control) versus three partial coverage designs
facts.main_result: One MODF onlay debonded at 632,000 cycles, none fractured, and all seven intact MODF specimens showed marginal deterioration where the antagonist contacted.
facts.follow_up: 1.2 million loading cycles (about 5 years of function)
facts.funding_coi: Authors deny any conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Within the limitations of this in vitro study (no specific limitations listed).

facts.intervention: Resin-bonded, all-ceramic and metal-ceramic fixed dental prostheses
facts.main_result: Metal-ceramic FDPs show the highest survival; all-ceramic can be comparable but chip more; resin-bonded FDPs act as long-term provisionals.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest

facts.population: Pre-sintered zirconia (Y-TZP) disks, 15 mm diameter, 2.4 mm thick
facts.intervention: Sandblasting with 50 um aluminum oxide before sintering (Z-PRE) or after sintering (Z-POS)
facts.comparison: Z-CTR, no surface treatment
facts.main_result: Pre-sintering sandblasting gave rougher surfaces and more defects but did not raise shear bond strength over post-sintering sandblasting; both beat control.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by FAPESP grants
facts.limitations: Long-term consequence of pre-sintered treatment on the zirconia-veneer interface needs further investigation.

facts.population: 10 patients (5 women, 5 men; mean age 52.8) receiving 17 posterior four-unit zirconia FDPs
facts.intervention: Lava zirconia-based four-unit posterior FDPs veneered with Lava Ceram, cemented with RelyX Unicem
facts.comparison: Contralateral untreated control teeth for periodontal parameters
facts.main_result: After 4 years cumulative survival of the four-unit FDPs was 76.5%, with three framework fractures at the distal connector.
facts.funding_coi: University Complutense of Madrid grant no. 229-2006
facts.limitations: Within the limitations of this prospective clinical study; small sample and short follow-up, more long-term observation needed.

facts.intervention: Zirconia and alumina core materials for all-ceramic restorations
facts.funding_coi: Grant-in-Aid, Japan Society for the Promotion of Science No. 18390521

facts.intervention: Dental zirconia types, properties, applications and cementation
facts.main_result: Monolithic translucent zirconia has shown promising results and high survival rates, and cementation methods have improved.
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Data are scarce; well-designed clinical trials are needed.

facts.population: 160 disks of four 4Y/5Y translucent zirconia materials
facts.intervention: Surface treatments: as-machined, glass bead abraded, alumina abraded
facts.comparison: Hand-polished control with 2000-grit silicon carbide paper
facts.main_result: 4Y zirconia was stronger than all 5Y materials; alumina abrasion slightly strengthened 4Y but weakened 5Y materials and produced the roughest surfaces.
facts.funding_coi: No specific grant funding

facts.population: Prospective and retrospective cohort studies of all-ceramic and metal-ceramic FDPs
facts.intervention: All-ceramic fixed dental prostheses
facts.comparison: Metal-ceramic FDPs
facts.main_result: 5-year survival was 94.4% for metal-ceramic FDPs versus 88.6% for all-ceramic FDPs (P<0.0001).
facts.follow_up: mean follow-up of at least 3 years
facts.limitations: Assumption of a constant annual event rate; mean observation period was 3.8 years for all-ceramic versus 8 years for metal-ceramic FDPs.

facts.population: Studies of tooth-supported single crowns: 4663 metal-ceramic and 9434 all-ceramic
facts.intervention: All-ceramic tooth-supported single crowns
facts.comparison: Metal-ceramic single crowns
facts.main_result: Estimated 5-year survival of metal-ceramic SCs was 94.7%, similar to reinforced glass-ceramic (96.6%), alumina (96%) and zirconia (92.1%) crowns; zirconia had more veneer fractures and loss of retention.
facts.follow_up: mean follow-up of at least 3 years; 5-year estimates
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest

facts.population: Bar-shaped bilayered specimens: three zirconia core ceramics with their veneering ceramics plus a metal ceramic control
facts.intervention: Core-veneer shear bond strength of three zirconia core/veneering ceramic systems by the Schmitz-Schulmeyer method, with half of each group thermocycled
facts.comparison: Metal ceramic control (Degudent U94 / Vita VM13) and dry storage versus thermocycling
facts.main_result: All-ceramic groups reached about 9-12.5 MPa, unaffected by thermocycling, and all were significantly below the metal ceramic control (about 26-28 MPa).
facts.sample_size: 30 specimens per group, four groups (n = 15 thermocycled per group)
materials_brands: Vita In-Ceram YZ Cubes / Vita VM9
Degudent U94 / Vita VM13 (metal ceramic control)

facts.population: Bilayered ceramic core-veneer specimens of four all-ceramic systems and a metal ceramic control, all made from one master die
facts.intervention: Shear loading of the core-veneer interface of IPS-Empress2/Eris, Procera AllZircon/CZR, DC-Zircon/Vita D and Procera AllCeram/AllCeram until failure
facts.comparison: Metal ceramic (MC) control
facts.main_result: Shear strength of IE (30.86 MPa), PZ (28.03) and DC (27.90) did not differ significantly from the metal ceramic control (30.16), whereas PA (22.40) was lower.

facts.journal: The Journal of the American Dental Association
facts.population: Lithium disilicate glass-ceramic, Y-TZP and metal-ceramic molar crowns (in vitro) and patients with zirconium oxide-based or lithium disilicate restorations (in vivo)
facts.intervention: Step-stress fatigue testing of crowns, clinical recall of Lava zirconium oxide and IPS e.max Press restorations, and a wear trial of ceramic crowns against enamel
facts.comparison: Metal-ceramic and veneered Y-TZP crowns in vitro; enamel-to-enamel wear and veneer porcelains in vivo
outcomes: wear of ceramic and antagonist enamel
facts.main_result: LDGC crowns had the highest characteristic strength in vitro (eta 1,719 N vs 1,304 N for MCR and 631 N for Y-TZP), and 2.8% of zirconium oxide crowns at 7 years were replaced versus none of the LDGC restorations at 4 years.
facts.sample_size: n = 21 crowns per in vitro group; 574 zirconium oxide restorations and 236 LDGC restorations recalled; 31 patients with 36 teeth in the wear trial
facts.funding_coi: Two authors are co-owners of Dental Consultants (publisher of The Dental Advisor) and Apex Dental Milling

facts.population: Standardized zirconia crown frameworks (maxillary canine analog) cemented on CoCr abutments
facts.intervention: Veneering with overpressed porcelains (PressX Zr, GC Initial LF, VITA PM9, IPS e.max ZirPress)
facts.comparison: Layered veneering porcelains (Zirox, GC Initial ZR, VITA VM9, IPS e.max Ceram)
facts.main_result: Overpressed crowns had similar or higher fracture load than layered ones; IPS e.max ZirPress (1519 N) exceeded IPS e.max Ceram (894 N).

facts.population: Bar-shaped zirconia specimens (3 mol% Y2O3, Zirluna ACF), glazed or veneered with feldspathic ceramic
facts.intervention: Clinically simulated sequential grinding (NTI diamond burs 20, 10, 7.5 um) and polishing of glazed full-contour zirconia
facts.comparison: Zirconia veneered with feldspathic ceramic and glazed (group 2)
facts.main_result: Glazed full-contour zirconia had significantly lower roughness than veneered zirconia, and fine polishing gave roughness comparable to glazing, while veneered zirconia stayed rougher after polishing.
materials_brands: NTI diamond burs and polishing kit

facts.population: Tooth-supported monolithic ceramic single crowns and fixed partial dentures in human clinical studies
facts.intervention: Monolithic ceramic (lithium disilicate, zirconia, PICN) single crowns and FPDs
facts.comparison: Veneered ceramic restorations (5 studies with direct comparison)
facts.main_result: Pooled failure was 1% for monolithic single crowns and 3% for FPDs, with no significant difference from veneered restorations in survival (RR 0.68).
facts.sample_size: 18 studies: 1061 monolithic single crowns and 104 FPDs
facts.funding_coi: No specific grant from funding agencies

facts.population: Thirty zirconia disks in three thickness groups on nine backgrounds
facts.intervention: Spectrophotometric CIELab measurement of zirconia disks of 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 mm placed on nine backgrounds
facts.comparison: A2 composite resin background as the reference for color difference
facts.main_result: Mean delta E ranged 1.44 to 7.88 and was affected by thickness and background; 0.4 mm masked most backgrounds, 0.6 mm amalgam and 0.8 mm nickel-chromium alloy.
materials_brands: DD Bio ZX2 monolithic zero zirconia

facts.population: 46 patients (49 teeth) needing full-crown restoration of first and/or second molars
facts.intervention: Monolithic zirconia crowns for posterior teeth
facts.main_result: Marginal adaptation was excellent in 100% of crowns, color match acceptable in 6.1%, with no significant change in wear of antagonist teeth over 96 weeks.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Guangxi Province and Guilin City research plans; no conflicts of interest

facts.population: 35 zirconia specimens (ICE Zirkon) bonded with Variolink II resin cement
facts.intervention: Sandblasting alone or combined with Monobond S, Monobond Plus or Z-Prime Plus before cementation
facts.comparison: Untreated control (Group I)
facts.main_result: MDP-containing primers (Monobond Plus, Z-Prime Plus) with sandblasting gave the highest shear bond strength and the untreated control the lowest.

facts.journal: Journal of the Mechanical Behavior of Biomedical Materials
facts.population: Y-TZP ceramic specimens (in vitro studies)
facts.intervention: Grinding of Y-TZP
facts.comparison: As-sintered Y-TZP without grinding
facts.main_result: Grinding generally decreased flexural strength and increased roughness of Y-TZP; slow-speed handpiece, grit size under 50 um and plenty of coolant limited the damage.

facts.population: Disc-shaped specimens of partially stabilized (Prettau) and fully stabilized (Prettau Anterior) monolithic zirconia
facts.intervention: Staining (A2 liquid) and vacuum sintering
facts.comparison: Non-stained specimens sintered without vacuum
facts.main_result: Staining lowered translucency of fully stabilized zirconia and raised its flexural strength but lowered that of partially stabilized zirconia; vacuum sintering gave minimal benefit.
facts.sample_size: n=15 per subgroup, two zirconia types, three conditions

facts.journal: Journal of the European Ceramic Society
facts.population: Pressureless-sintered biomedical grade Y-TZP ceramic specimens
facts.intervention: Dental grinding and sandblasting
facts.comparison: Pristine as-sintered specimens
facts.main_result: Grinding at high rotation speed lowered mean strength and cyclic survival, whereas sandblasting strengthened the surface and raised cyclic survival; testing in artificial saliva lowered survival strength by about 10-15%.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the Slovenian Research Agency
outcomes: survival under cyclic loading (dry and artificial saliva)

facts.main_result: Zirconia can withstand posterior physiologic loads, but veneer chipping and the poorly understood zirconia-veneer bond are the main weaknesses.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.main_result: Zirconia materials can withstand posterior physiologic loads, yet zirconia cores are not problem free.
Third-generation zirconia has improved optical properties, while data on its mechanical properties are still scarce.
Newer zirconia generations are more translucent but generally weaker, and lower masking potential can be a drawback.
facts.funding_coi: Translucency measurements financed by pritidenta, which also supplied crowns; authors state they were not influenced

facts.population: 36 CAD/CAM monolithic translucent zirconia discs (10 mm x 0.8 mm)
facts.intervention: Classic, speed and super speed sintering cycles, with or without thermodynamic aging
facts.comparison: Classic sintering cycle (1510 C, 120 min hold)
facts.main_result: Rapid sintering reduced translucency and biaxial flexural strength (super speed 863.8 MPa vs classic 1169.4 MPa before aging); aging reduced translucency only.
facts.sample_size: 36 discs, n=12 per sintering group, n=6 per subgroup

facts.population: 80 milled monolithic molar crowns
facts.intervention: Cubic ultratranslucent (UT) and supertranslucent (ST) zirconia crowns at 1.0 and 1.5 mm
facts.comparison: Lithium disilicate (IPS e.max CAD LT) crowns, 1.5 mm
facts.main_result: Translucency ranked UT1.0 > ST1.0 > UT1.5 > lithium disilicate 1.5 by total transmission; UT and ST cubic zirconia were more translucent than lithium disilicate LT.
facts.funding_coi: Kuraray Europe Italia supplied materials and technical assistance; no funding statement

facts.population: Yttria-stabilized zirconia (8 mol% Y2O3) ceramic samples with and without TiO2
facts.intervention: Addition of 10 mol% TiO2, sintering and hot isostatic pressing
facts.comparison: TiO2-undoped ZrO2 (8 mol% Y2O3) sample
facts.main_result: 10 mol% TiO2 dissolved into cubic 8Y-ZrO2, promoted grain growth and pore migration, and gave transparent ceramics for 0.35 to 7 um wavelengths.

facts.population: 3Y-TZP zirconia specimens of different grain sizes and 3Y-TZP-MWCNT nanocomposites
facts.intervention: Sandblasting with two particle sizes (110 and 250 µm), two pressures (2 and 4 bars) and two impact angles (30 and 90 degrees)
facts.comparison: Non-sandblasted control material
facts.main_result: Mild sandblasting (110 µm, 2 bars) raised biaxial strength and left surface mechanical properties unchanged, while 250 µm particles at 90 degrees lowered strength; 10-15% monoclinic phase formed to a depth of about 10-13 µm.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation (MAEC-AECID)
facts.limitations: Conclusions apply within the limits of the sandblasting conditions studied.
facts.key_finding: In this PhD thesis, sandblasting 3Y-TZP zirconia under mild conditions did not harm and even raised biaxial strength, whereas severe conditions (large particles, high pressure) lowered it. Sandblasting induced about 10-15% monoclinic phase to a depth of about 10-13 micrometres, and nanometric-grain zirconia resisted hydrothermal degradation.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Sandblasting zirconia restorations is acceptable if particle size is 110 micrometres or less and pressure below 4 bars.

facts.population: In vitro studies (and a few clinical studies) of bonding to zirconia ceramics
facts.intervention: Surface treatments, primers/adhesive monomers and aging conditions used to improve adhesion to zirconia
facts.main_result: Airborne-particle abrasion and tribochemical silica coating are reference pretreatments, adhesive monomers are necessary for chemical bonding, and contamination and aging reduce adhesion; results across 134 publications were hard to compare.
facts.limitations: Results were difficult to compare because parameters varied between research protocols, and laboratory studies need clinical confirmation.

facts.journal: The International Journal of Oral & Maxillofacial Implants
facts.population: ZiReal Post (Biomet 3i) zirconia abutments, as-received and porcelain-coated
facts.intervention: Characterization by XRD, XRF, EDS, optical, scanning and transmission electron microscopy
facts.comparison: As-received versus fluoroapatite-porcelain-coated abutments
facts.main_result: The abutments are high-purity tetragonal zirconia with 3-4 mol% yttria and homogeneous equiaxed grains averaging 0.30 µm, with only 1 µm machining ring marks.
facts.funding_coi: Partial support from the Spanish Ministerio de Ciencia e Innovación; Biomet 3i supplied the abutments

facts.population: VITA YZ T, HT, ST and XT zirconia blanks and VITA VM 9 veneering material (laboratory testing)
facts.funding_coi: Manufacturer (VITA Zahnfabrik) document
facts.key_finding: Manufacturer documentation of the VITA YZ zirconia range (T, HT, ST, XT translucency levels) with its composition, mechanical properties, sintering and processing tests, and the VITA VM 9 veneering ceramic. Listed values include 3-point flexural strength of 1200 MPa and fracture toughness of 4.5 MPa m-0.5 for YZ T and HT, falling to above 600 MPa and 2.5 for XT.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Higher-translucency VITA YZ grades trade strength for esthetics, so grade choice should follow the indication, and the data are manufacturer-reported.

facts.population: Porcelain-fused-to-metal crowns on an Ankylos implant abutment analog (mandibular first molar form)
facts.intervention: Three metal substructure designs: minimum thickness (A), conventional 1.5 mm cutback (B), wrinkled design (C)
facts.comparison: Conventional design (Group B)
facts.main_result: Mean fracture resistance was 236.13 kg for the conventional design, 188.63 kg for the wrinkled design and 111.13 kg for the minimum-thickness design (P < 0.05).
facts.limitations: The authors state the theory that PFM can provide better support requires further corroboration.

facts.population: Zirconia bars (17 x 2 x 1 mm), ground-and-polished or milled with Cercon CAD/CAM
facts.intervention: Airborne-particle abrasion with 50 or 120 µm aluminum oxide, with or without a veneer-baking heat treatment
facts.comparison: Polished zirconia bars
outcomes: surface and subsurface damage on SEM
facts.main_result: Flexure strength ranged from 546 MPa (ground bars abraded with 120 µm) to 1166 MPa (polished), correlating strongly with surface roughness (R2 = 0.912); heat treatment had no significant influence.

facts.population: Sixty alumina-core all-ceramic crowns on brass dies
facts.intervention: Procera AllCeram crowns with 0.4 mm (Group 1) or 0.9 mm (Group 2) AllCeram veneer porcelain
facts.comparison: In-Ceram crowns with 0.9 mm Vitadur Alpha veneer (control)
facts.main_result: Mean load at fracture was 2197.6 N, 2401.4 N and 2581.0 N for the three groups, with no significant difference between them.
facts.limitations: Values are useful for comparative purposes only and cannot be extrapolated to the clinical situation.

facts.population: 182 zirconia frameworks with 305 abutment teeth prepared by general dentists in Germany
facts.intervention: 3D analysis of STL framework data for total occlusal convergence, abutment height and finish line design
facts.comparison: Literature-based criteria for adequate zirconia preparations
facts.main_result: Only 13 of 305 teeth (4.3%) met the adequacy criteria; mean total occlusal convergence was 17.9 degrees, higher in molars (23.2) than premolars (14.2), and 92.5% of finish lines were not ideal.
facts.funding_coi: BEGO Medical GmbH supplied the data sets

facts.population: 53 monolithic all-ceramic maxillary first molar crowns on a metal abutment analog
facts.intervention: Axial static loading to fracture of monolithic zirconia, lithium disilicate and feldspar ceramic crowns, adhesively luted or conventionally cemented
facts.comparison: Lithium disilicate and feldspar ceramic crowns; adhesive versus glass-ionomer cementation
facts.main_result: Zirconia crowns fractured at the highest loads (5,620 N luted, 4,340 N cemented) versus about 2,700 N for lithium disilicate and 1,340 N for feldspar ceramic.
facts.funding_coi: DeguDent provided material and financial support; no conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Limitations of the in vitro setting do not allow conclusions for clinical practice.

facts.population: Disk specimens (10 mm diameter, 1.3 mm thick) of 3 mol% yttria-stabilized zirconia with and without 0.3 mol% alumina dopant
facts.intervention: High-pressure spark plasma sintering (400 MPa) of alumina-doped 3Y-TZP powder (TZ-3Y-E)
facts.comparison: Undoped 3 mol% yttria zirconia powder (TZ-3Y)
facts.main_result: Alumina dopant lowered transparency despite similar 80 nm grains and porosity below 0.05%, because alumina along grain boundaries caused strong birefringent scattering.
facts.funding_coi: Grants-in-Aid from the Japanese Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology and JSPS

facts.journal: Journal of Biomedical Materials Research Part B: Applied Biomaterials
facts.population: Y-TZP and alumina ceramic plates bonded to polymer (polycarbonate) substrates, simulating crowns on dentin; no patients
facts.intervention: Sandblasting of the ceramic undersurface (50 um Al2O3, 5 s) before bonding, then dynamic and cyclic Hertzian loading to radial crack initiation
facts.comparison: As-polished (unblasted) specimens
outcomes: strength at radial crack initiation (dynamic and cyclic loading)
facts.main_result: Sandblasting lowered strength by under 10% in single-cycle loading but by 20-30% in 10 Hz cyclic loading; extrapolation still suggests sandblasted Y-TZP crowns can cope with masticatory forces up to 400 N.
facts.funding_coi: National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research (PO1 DE10976)
facts.limitations: The 10 Hz cyclic frequency is high relative to mastication (about 1 Hz), so the fatigue effect is probably overestimated.

facts.journal: Journal of the American Ceramic Society
facts.population: One transparent cubic 8 mol% yttria-stabilized zirconia (c-YSZ) disk (no patients)
facts.intervention: High-pressure spark plasma sintering (400 MPa) followed by annealing in air for 100 h
facts.comparison: As-sintered versus annealed disk
facts.main_result: The as-sintered zirconia strongly absorbed light because of oxygen vacancies; annealing in an oxidizing atmosphere improved transparency despite increased porosity, and fine residual pores scattered light.
facts.sample_size: one sintered disk, 10 mm diameter, about 1 mm thick after polishing
facts.funding_coi: World Premier International Research Center Initiative (MEXT, Japan) and a Japanese Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research

facts.population: Theoretical 3 mol% yttria-stabilized tetragonal zirconia (3Y-TZP) plates 0.3-2.0 mm thick (no specimens or patients)
facts.intervention: Rayleigh scattering model of in-line transmission versus grain size and thickness
facts.comparison: Threshold in-line transmission of a suite of dental porcelains (about 2.5% at 1 mm, 555 nm) and one published experimental data set
outcomes: critical grain size for porcelain-like translucency
facts.main_result: To match dental porcelain translucency, the mean 3Y-TZP grain size must be about 82 nm at 1.3 mm thickness, 77 nm at 1.5 mm and 70 nm at 2 mm.
facts.funding_coi: NIDCR grant R01 DE017925 and NSF grant CMMI-0758530; author declares no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Theoretical predictions were higher than the single available experimental data set across the visible spectrum.

facts.population: Dental zirconia ceramics (Y-TZP, 4Y/5Y-PSZ, graded and nanostructured variants); no patients
facts.intervention: Narrative review of generations of dental zirconia and routes to greater translucency
facts.comparison: Lithia-based glass-ceramics
facts.main_result: More translucent zirconia generations (more cubic phase) lose strength and toughness, so the most durable ceramics are the least translucent; grain size below about 100 nm is predicted to be needed for translucent Y-TZP.
facts.funding_coi: US NIH/NIDCR and NSF grants; no conflicts declared
facts.limitations: Nanostructured zirconia is still at an early stage, and standardized laboratory tests give only a cautionary glimpse of clinical performance.

facts.population: Modern zirconia materials grouped into four generations; no study population
facts.intervention: Classification of zirconia generations by composition, translucency and strength, with guidance on luting and finishing
facts.main_result: More cubic crystals (higher yttria content) raise translucency but lower flexural strength and fracture toughness, so each of the four zirconia generations has its own indications.
facts.limitations: Clinical long-term data on the newest zirconia generations are scarce and only in-vitro data exist.

facts.population: 30 patients (aged 27-75) needing a three- or four-unit posterior FPD replacing one or two missing teeth
facts.intervention: Three- and four-unit posterior FPDs with CAD/CAM yttria-stabilized zirconia frameworks, veneered and cemented with glass-ionomer cement
facts.comparison: No comparator restoration; periodontal parameters of abutment teeth compared with contralateral control teeth
outcomes: Gingival, Plaque and sulcus bleeding indices and pocket depth
facts.main_result: After a mean 34.2 months all 27 examined FPDs were intact (100% framework survival); one had a major veneer chip, giving a cumulative success rate of 96.3%.
facts.sample_size: 30 patients enrolled; 27 patients with 27 FPDs (19 three-unit, 8 four-unit) examined
facts.limitations: Only medium-term (3-year) follow-up; 3 of 30 patients were lost to recall.

facts.key_finding: فصل کتاب درسی که سرامیک‌های دندانی را بر پایهٔ ترکیب و میزان فاز بلوری دسته‌بندی می‌کند و زیرکونیا (Y-TZP و ZTA) را به‌دلیل استحکام خمشی و چقرمگی بالا، اما شفافیت کمتر و دشواری باندینگ (نبود فاز شیشه‌ای) معرفی می‌کند.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: زیرکونیا اجازهٔ ساخت ترمیم‌هایی با ضخامت کمتر و تراش محافظه‌کارانه‌تر از گلاس‌سرامیک‌ها را می‌دهد، اما چون اسید هیدروفلوریک روی آن اثر ندارد باندینگ به آماده‌سازی سطحی ویژه نیاز دارد.

off_topic_reason: Covers the chemistry, sources and industrial/nuclear uses of zirconium with no clinical dental content; dental use is deferred to later parts.

facts.key_finding: بخش اول از یک سری مقاله در مجلهٔ دندانسازان حرفه‌ای که عنصر زیرکونیوم، تاریخچهٔ کشف و استخراج آن، خواص فیزیکی و شیمیایی و کاربردهای صنعتی آن (مانند ریخته‌گری، رآکتورهای هسته‌ای و جواهرات) را معرفی می‌کند.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: این بخش مقدمه‌ای غیرکلینیکی است و توصیهٔ مستقیمی برای کار بالینی ندارد؛ کاربرد دندانپزشکی زیرکونیا در بخش‌های بعدی سری می‌آید.

facts.key_finding: بخش دهم سری مقالات، اباتمنت‌های زیرکونیا را معرفی می‌کند: مطالعه‌های ۳ تا ۶ ساله نتایج رضایت‌بخشی از نظر زیست‌سازگاری و زیبایی گزارش کرده‌اند و در آزمایشگاه این اباتمنت‌ها بار تا ۷۳۸ نیوتن را تحمل کرده‌اند.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: برای دندان‌های قدامی و پرمولرها نتایج امیدبخش است، اما برای مولرها و استفادهٔ گستردهٔ بدون ریسک شواهد کافی و بلندمدت وجود ندارد.

facts.key_finding: بخش دوم سری مقالات، مروری تاریخی بر ترمیم‌های تمام‌سرامیک و PFM، ورود CAD-CAM به دندانپزشکی و پژوهش گاروی در ۱۹۷۵ دربارهٔ پایدارسازی زیرکونیا با حدود ۵٫۵٪ ایتریا تا ظهور زیرکونیای قابل فرزکاری در دههٔ ۲۰۰۰.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: این بخش تاریخی است و توصیهٔ بالینی مستقیم ندارد؛ فقط توضیح می‌دهد چرا تمام‌سرامیک‌ها به‌دلیل زیبایی و سازگاری زیستی بر PFM ترجیح داده شدند.

facts.sample_size: 5102 articles retrieved by a Web of Science search for 'dental zirconia'
facts.funding_coi: CNPq (Brazil), US NIH/NIDCR and UFMG research funding acknowledged

facts.population: in vitro studies of fixed prosthetic restorations (intra-coronal, extra-coronal, FPDs, implant overdentures)
facts.intervention: translucent zirconia as the primary material for fixed prosthetic restorations
facts.comparison: traditional zirconia or other materials commonly used in fixed prosthodontics
facts.main_result: Translucent zirconia has complex esthetic properties with potential for high translucency and color adaptability, and is a versatile material in restorative and implant dentistry (70 studies included, mostly in vitro).
facts.funding_coi: Internal grant of Iuliu Hatieganu University; no conflict of interest declared

facts.main_result: Higher yttria content increases zirconia translucency but reduces strength; zirconia is classified into 3Y-, 4Y-, 5Y-TZP and combined multilayer types.
facts.funding_coi: No funding; one author is an academic editor of PeerJ

facts.population: Ultra-high translucent zirconia (Shofu Disk ZR Lucent Ultra)
facts.intervention: Ultra-high translucent zirconia made with Cyclic CIP and Plus Y Technology
facts.comparison: 5Y and 3Y zirconia, lithium disilicate
facts.main_result: UHTZ has translucency comparable to lithium disilicate while its flexural strength is comparable to 5Y zirconia.
facts.funding_coi: No funding stated; Shofu Inc. supplied specimens and technical help

facts.population: Translucent zirconia, 3Y-TZP and lithium disilicate specimens
facts.intervention: Two translucent zirconias (Katana UTML, Lava Esthetic)
facts.comparison: Conventional 3Y-TZP (Lava Plus) and lithium disilicate (IPS e.max Press)
facts.main_result: As translucency increased with increased cubic content, edge toughness decreased (Katana UTML 304 N/mm vs Lava Plus 717 N/mm).
facts.sample_size: n=20 per material for translucency and edge chipping, n=3 for XRD

facts.population: 60 monolithic zirconia molar crowns on prefabricated implant abutments
facts.intervention: Speed sintering (about 2 h) of 3Y-TZP and 4Y-TZP crowns
facts.comparison: Long-term sintering (about 7 h)
facts.main_result: Shortening sintering time increased marginal gaps only for 4Y-TZP crowns; all groups stayed under 120 µm.
facts.funding_coi: Hacettepe University research funds; no competing interests

off_topic_reason: A nuclear-materials study of zirconium alloy hydrides with no dental relevance.

facts.population: Zr and Zr–Y alloy samples
facts.intervention: Yttrium addition to zirconium followed by hydriding
facts.comparison: Pure Zr
facts.main_result: Yttrium oxide nanoparticles give thin intragranular hydrides, which mitigates hydride embrittlement.
facts.funding_coi: National Natural Science Foundation of China

facts.population: 108 zirconia FDPs (single-unit, three-unit, cantilever) on a mandibular model
facts.intervention: High-speed sintering (1,580°C, about 20 min) of multi-layer 4Y-TZP
facts.comparison: Conventional sintering (1,450°C, about 10 h)
facts.main_result: High-speed sintering reduced accuracy of three-unit FDPs but had no clinically relevant effect on fit.
facts.funding_coi: Amann Girrbach supplied materials; no conflicts of interest

facts.intervention: 90-minute sintering of KATANA Zirconia
facts.key_finding: Manufacturer brochure for the KATANA Zirconia YML, UTML, STML, HTML PLUS, HT and LT series, claiming about 90-minute sintering for single restorations without loss of translucency or strength.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Choose the series by translucency and strength needs; the 90-minute program applies to single restorations only and is the manufacturer's claim.

facts.intervention: 90-minute sintering of KATANA Zirconia HT/LT
facts.key_finding: Leaflet for mono-colored KATANA Zirconia HT and LT, which differ in translucency for porcelain layering and can be sintered in about 90 minutes up to a 3-unit bridge.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Use HT to reflect abutment color and LT to mask a metal or discolored abutment; the fast sintering applies up to 3-unit bridges.

facts.intervention: 54-minute high-speed sintering of KATANA Zirconia UTML/STML
facts.key_finding: Brochure for KATANA Zirconia UTML and STML, four-layer multilayered zirconia with translucency near natural enamel and optional 54-minute sintering for up to a 3-unit bridge.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: UTML suits anterior crowns and laminate veneers; STML balances translucency and strength; the 54-minute sintering is limited to 3-unit bridges.

facts.key_finding: Technical guide for KATANA Zirconia UTML, STML, ML and HT covering series, shade and disc thickness selection, framework design, milling, sintering and finishing.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Pick UTML for anterior crowns and veneers, STML for up to 3-unit posterior bridges and ML/HT for single frameworks and long spans; do not use UTML or STML for cantilever pontics.

facts.main_result: Higher yttria content gives higher translucency and lower strength; adequately selected zirconia suits implant superstructures and fixtures.
facts.funding_coi: No external funding

facts.population: Rectangular bar specimens of high-translucent and low-translucent Y-TZP zirconia
facts.intervention: High-translucent Y-TZP (Prettau Anterior), also tested after autoclave aging
facts.comparison: Low-translucent Y-TZP (Diazir) and aged high-translucent Y-TZP
facts.main_result: High-translucent zirconia had markedly lower flexural strength (427 vs 805 MPa) and fracture toughness (4.9 vs 8.9 MPa.m1/2) than low-translucent zirconia; aging did not significantly change flexural strength.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by authors' university funds; no conflict of interest declared

facts.population: Bar-shaped specimens cut from each of four layers of pre-sintered multilayer zirconia blocks
facts.intervention: Three Katana multi-layered zirconias (HTML, STML, UTML) tested at 0.4, 0.8 and 1.2 mm thickness
facts.comparison: Comparison among the three Katana grades (HTML vs STML vs UTML)
facts.main_result: Flexural strength and fracture toughness were significantly higher for Katana HTML (652.85-887.64 MPa; 4.25-5.01) than STML (280-436 MPa) and UTML (258-331 MPa), with no differences between layers.
facts.sample_size: 15 specimens per group per layer and thickness
facts.funding_coi: Supported by Kuraray Noritake; authors declare no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: Conclusions are limited to the in vitro design

facts.population: One 31-year-old female patient with an endodontically treated upper first molar
facts.intervention: Chairside fabrication of a monolithic crown from multilayer super-translucent zirconia (CEREC MTL Zirconia) with speed-sintering
facts.main_result: A monolithic multilayer zirconia crown could be fabricated chairside in about 75-90 minutes with a good color match.
facts.limitations: Clinical data for this type of restoration are still sparse.

facts.intervention: Air abrasion of cubic-containing high-translucent zirconias, with laboratory processing and an anterior monolithic case
facts.comparison: Original high-strength tetragonal zirconia without a cubic phase
facts.main_result: Cubic-containing zirconia responds differently to air abrasion than conventional tetragonal zirconia, so clinical decisions should not be based on tetragonal data.

facts.journal: Journal of Physics and Chemistry of Solids
facts.population: Sol-gel synthesized zirconia powders with progressively increasing yttrium content (5YZ to 100YZ)
facts.intervention: Progressive yttrium additions with heat treatment at 1300 and 1500 C, analysed by XRD, Raman and Rietveld refinement
facts.main_result: Tetragonal, mixed tetragonal-cubic and fully cubic phases formed depending on yttrium content; cubic compositions resisted tetragonal-to-monoclinic transformation at 1500 C.
facts.funding_coi: DST-SERB India financial assistance

facts.population: Zirconia specimens (32 specimens from 17 zirconia blanks) supplied by 9 dental laboratories for posterior and anterior indications
facts.intervention: Laboratory-fabricated zirconia specimens ordered for posterior (high strength) and anterior (high translucency) indications, tested for flexural strength, hardness, composition and transmittance
facts.comparison: Posterior (HS) versus anterior (HT) intended zirconia, and 3 mol% versus 5 mol% yttria grouping
facts.main_result: Strength scattered widely (posterior 490 MPa, anterior 581 MPa) because of mixed yttria use; grouped by yttria it was 584 MPa for 3 mol% and 373 MPa for 5 mol%.
facts.funding_coi: None of the authors reported any disclosures.
facts.limitations: Strength was highly dependent on laboratory processing and finishing; all fractures originated from machining flaws.

off_topic_reason: Zirconia microspheres for photonics/thermal barrier coatings with no dental application.

facts.journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
facts.population: Sol-gel synthesized zirconia and yttria-stabilized zirconia microspheres
facts.intervention: Heating particles to 1500 C with monitoring by SEM, ex situ XRD and in situ XRD
facts.comparison: Undoped zirconia versus yttria-doped zirconia particles
facts.main_result: Yttria-doping reduced grain growth, stabilized the tetragonal phase and significantly improved thermal stability of the zirconia microspheres.
facts.funding_coi: German Research Foundation (DFG) financial support

facts.population: In-vitro studies on translucent zirconia with yttria content higher than 3 mol%
facts.intervention: Changing yttria content and other material-related variables in zirconia
facts.comparison: 3 mol% yttria stabilized zirconia
facts.main_result: Fifty-three in-vitro studies showed that changing yttria content significantly affected translucency, and zirconia of the same generation varies in translucency.
facts.funding_coi: No funding to report; no competing interests

facts.journal: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
facts.intervention: Airborne particle abrasion of zirconia fixed dental prostheses before adhesive cementation
facts.main_result: Air-abrasion improves resin adhesion to zirconia but can raise monoclinic phase and lower strength, so it should be brief (about 20 seconds), below 2.8 bar, with 30-50 um silica-coated or silica particles.
facts.limitations: Whether air-abrasion contributes to long-term zirconia degradation is not clinically proven.

facts.intervention: Surface treatment methods for bonding resin cement to zirconia-based ceramics
facts.main_result: Silica coating with aluminum oxide particles is the surface treatment of choice for bonding Y-TZP with resin cements, and functional monomers add chemical bonding.
facts.limitations: Further clinical studies are necessary to establish the ideal technique and materials.

facts.population: Patients with bonded zirconia restorations (resin-bonded FPDs, inlay-retained FPDs, veneers) in 8 included clinical studies
facts.intervention: Bonded zirconia restorations: posterior inlay-retained FPDs and anterior cantilevered resin-bonded FPDs
facts.main_result: Anterior resin-bonded FPDs showed 100% survival at 3 to 10 years; posterior inlay-retained FPDs ranged from 12.1% at 10 years to 95.8% at 5 years; debonds occurred in all studies but prostheses could usually be rebonded.
facts.follow_up: 20 months to about 10 years across studies (12 months minimum for inclusion)
facts.limitations: Heterogeneity in study design hampered any meta-analysis, and the role of bonding efficacy in survival is unknown.

facts.population: Zirconia disks (7 mm diameter, 3 mm height) of two commercial systems, Cercon and Biodenta, veneered with their matching ceramics
facts.intervention: Veneering of each zirconia core with its manufacturer-recommended layering ceramic, then thermocycling and shear testing
facts.comparison: Cercon zirconia with Cercon ceram versus Biodenta zirconia with 2 in 1 ceramic
facts.main_result: Mean SBS was 27.19 MPa (Cercon) and 28.22 MPa (Biodenta) with no significant difference; Biodenta failed mostly adhesively, Cercon with mixed failures.
materials_brands: Biodenta zirconia with 2 in 1 ceramic (Biodenta Swiss AG)

facts.population: 4Y-TZP zirconia blocks (9.0x7.0x5.0 mm, n=72 per group assignment) contaminated with human saliva
facts.intervention: Precoating the zirconia bonding surface with ethyl cellulose before saliva contamination, then removal with ethanol in an ultrasonic bath
facts.comparison: Uncontaminated control; saliva then ultrasonic ethanol cleaning; saliva then zirconia cleaner; zirconia primer then saliva then water spray
facts.main_result: Shear bond strength was significantly higher in the ethyl cellulose group than in the other cleaning methods, and no saliva contaminants were found after removal of the coating.
facts.sample_size: 72 zirconia blocks in 5 groups, each divided into 3 aging subgroups (n=24)
facts.follow_up: Artificial aging equivalent to up to 2.2 years in an oral environment
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF) grant funded by the Korea government (MSIT)

facts.population: 100 cylindrical 3Y-TZP zirconia disks (Ceramill Zi)
facts.intervention: Etching with hydrofluoric acid at 40%, 9.5% and 5% concentration for 1, 5 or 15 minutes
facts.comparison: Control specimens polished with SiC abrasive paper (baseline surfaces)
facts.main_result: 40% HF significantly increased Ra and Rz at all times, 9.5% HF only after 15 minutes, and 5% HF produced no significant change.
facts.sample_size: 100 disks: 9 etching subgroups of 10 plus a control of 10

facts.intervention: Zirconia and other all-ceramic systems versus porcelain-fused-to-metal as framework materials for crowns and fixed partial dentures
facts.comparison: Conventional metal-ceramic restorations
facts.main_result: Zirconia shows favourable mechanical properties and suits single crowns and short-span FPDs, but clinical results are not yet comparable with metal-ceramic and long-term data are insufficient.
facts.limitations: Zirconia long-term clinical performance, bonding to veneering ceramic, cementation, aging and wear need further investigation.

facts.population: Fifty identical epoxy resin replicas of a prepared molar, each restored with an all-ceramic or PFM crown
facts.intervention: Monolithic CAD/CAM lithium disilicate crowns; zirconia core veneered by hand-layering, heat-pressing, or CAD/CAM lithium disilicate veneer (CAD-on)
facts.comparison: Porcelain-fused-to-metal crowns as control
facts.main_result: All LDG and CAD-on crowns survived 500,000 cycles, whereas all PFM, ZVP and ZVL crowns failed.

facts.journal: Indiana University School of Dentistry (MSD thesis)
facts.population: 48 cylindrical Y-TZP zirconia specimens (6 mm diameter, 4 mm height) veneered with porcelain cylinders
facts.intervention: Surface treatments before veneering (heat treatment, airborne-particle abrasion, or both), with or without cyclic loading
facts.comparison: Control group with no treatment after grinding
facts.main_result: Surface treatment had no significant effect on shear bond strength; air-particle abrasion without heat treatment gave significantly lower strength after cyclic loading (10.7 vs 34.1 MPa).
facts.sample_size: 48 specimens, 12 per group (6 with and 6 without cyclic loading)

facts.population: Ce-TZP/A (NANOZR) cubes, 10 mm edge, veneered with ceramic layers of 5 mm
facts.intervention: Six veneering ceramics layered on Ce-TZP/A with or without liner, polished or airborne-particle abraded, then sheared at the interface
facts.comparison: Polished hipped Y-TZP veneered with Cerabien ZR and Vintage ZR
facts.main_result: Airborne-particle abrasion did not improve bond strength to Ce-TZP/A, liners reduced it, and means ranged from 14.2 MPa (IPS e.max with liner) to 27.5 MPa (VITA VM 9).
facts.limitations: No power analysis was performed and the laboratory cube design differs from the clinical situation.

facts.journal: Journal canadien de dentisterie restauratrice et de prosthodontie
facts.intervention: Low-pressure alumina air abrasion plus MDP-containing zirconia primer (Z-PRIME PLUS) with dual-cure resin cement
facts.comparison: Self-adhesive resin cements (BisCem, RelyX Unicem, SmartCem2) on sandblasted zirconia
facts.main_result: Z-PRIME PLUS/DuoLink gave the highest shear bond strengths to zirconia (28.7 MPa initial light-cured) and kept them after aging, unlike the self-adhesive cements.
facts.sample_size: n = 8 per group in the Table 1 data
facts.funding_coi: Three authors are founder or employees of Bisco Dental, maker of the featured products

facts.population: 54 yttria-partially-stabilized zirconia beams with feldspathic porcelain buttons
facts.intervention: Porcelain firing with three heating rates (25, 50, 75 C/min) and three cooling regimens (fast, moderate, slow)
facts.comparison: Fast heating/fast cooling group versus slow heating/slow cooling group
outcomes: delamination (failure) force of porcelain from zirconia beam
facts.main_result: Slower cooling and slower heating gave higher failure loads (cooling effect P<.001, heating P=.002); slow/slow specimens were about twice as strong as fast/fast.
facts.sample_size: 54 beams, 6 specimens in each of 9 heating/cooling groups
materials_brands: Lava All-Ceramic System zirconia beams (3M ESPE)
facts.limitations: In vitro model results cannot be directly extrapolated to clinical outcomes; actual specimen heating and cooling rates were unknown.

facts.population: Specimens of zirconia ceramic and cobalt-chromium alloy (plus aluminum oxide in part 1)
facts.intervention: Sandblasting with 50-um aluminum oxide, with or without ultrasonic cleaning afterwards
facts.comparison: Ultrasonic cleaning versus no ultrasonic cleaning after sandblasting
facts.main_result: Specimens not ultrasonically cleaned after sandblasting had significantly higher shear bond strength than cleaned ones, for zirconia (13.11 vs 9.67 MPa, P<0.001) and Co-Cr (13.60 vs 9.80 MPa, P=0.006).
facts.funding_coi: JSPS KAKENHI grant; no competing interests
outcomes: shear bond strength of resin luting material

facts.population: Y-TZP plates (10 x 10 x 1 mm) veneered with porcelain
facts.intervention: Three porcelain application methods (wash-dentin firing, thicker moist layer, no liquid) on Y-TZP, analysed by XRD2 micro-diffraction
facts.comparison: Porcelain applied with versus without liquid medium; thin versus thick layer
outcomes: tetragonal/monoclinic phase content at the interface

facts.journal: Journal of Clinical and Experimental Dentistry
facts.population: In vivo and in vitro studies of zirconia-based fixed dental prostheses
facts.intervention: Literature review of zirconia-based fixed dental prostheses
facts.comparison: Ceramo-metallic restorations
facts.main_result: Porcelain-veneered zirconia restorations showed fracture rates of 6-15% over 3-5 years versus 4-10% over ten years for ceramo-metallic restorations.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.key_finding: A 3M ESPE brochure explains that zirconia's low thermal conductivity and its thermal-expansion match with the veneering porcelain make the porcelain prone to chipping unless it is fired and cooled slowly. It also covers framework design, furnace calibration, sandblasting and wash firing, citing preliminary in-house and UCLA bend-test data.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Following manufacturer advice for zirconia (slow heat rise and cooling, supported framework with even porcelain thickness, calibrated furnace, minimal sandblasting) is presented as the way to reduce porcelain chipping.

facts.population: Zirconia blocks (80 specimens, 8 groups) contaminated with human saliva
facts.intervention: Cleaning of saliva-contaminated zirconia with water, 35% phosphoric acid, Ivoclean or particle abrasion, before or after MDP primer
facts.comparison: Control group bonded without saliva contamination
facts.main_result: Water rinsing after MDP application (20.6 MPa) and particle abrasion or Ivoclean before MDP (23.1 and 22.7 MPa) preserved bond strength relative to control (25.8 MPa); phosphoric acid did not.
facts.funding_coi: Materials donated by manufacturers; authors deny conflicts of interest

facts.population: Fully sintered IPS e.max ZirCAD zirconia micro-specimens bonded in pairs
facts.intervention: Tribochemical silica sandblasting (CoJet) and/or silane/MDP primers (Clearfil Ceramic Primer, Monobond Plus) before bonding with two composite cements
facts.comparison: No sandblasting and/or no primer; BisGMA-based versus MDP-based cement; three ageing protocols
facts.main_result: Best bond durability came from CoJet sandblasting plus a silane/MDP primer (highest Weibull scale 54.04 MPa and shape 3.47 with Clearfil Ceramic Primer and Panavia F2.0 at 10 d); sandblasting was indispensable for Panavia F2.0.
facts.follow_up: 10 days, 10,000 thermocycles or 6 months water storage
outcomes: micro-tensile bond strength (Weibull scale and shape)

facts.population: Air-abraded Lava zirconia disks (20 mm x 1.5 mm) contaminated with fresh human saliva
facts.intervention: Cleaning of saliva-contaminated zirconia with Ivoclean, SDS, hydrogen peroxide or sodium hypochlorite solutions
facts.comparison: Additional air-abrasion, water-spray rinsing and a no-contamination control
facts.main_result: Ivoclean and 1% NaOCl restored shear bond strength (9.1 and 10.9 MPa) to the level of the uncontaminated control (10.4 MPa) and air-abrasion (9.5 MPa); SDS, H2O2 and water spray alone gave 4.4-6.7 MPa.
facts.sample_size: 28 zirconia disks, 12 resin cylinders per group
facts.limitations: Long-term clinical studies are still required to confirm efficacy of the cleaning solutions.
outcomes: failure mode and SEM of fractured surfaces

facts.population: Alumina-blasted yttria partially stabilized zirconia discs
facts.intervention: MDP-salt primer (experimental MDP-containing cleaner) applied to zirconia before resin cement
facts.comparison: Untreated control, 1% MDP, and MDP+silane (Clearfil Ceramic Primer Plus)
facts.main_result: MDP-salt gave the highest characteristic tensile bond strength before (51.6 MPa) and after 5,000 thermocycles (35.5 MPa) versus MDP and MDP+silane.
facts.funding_coi: Grant 17K11701 from the Japanese Ministry of Education; Kuraray Noritake provided experimental materials; no conflicts declared

facts.population: Published zirconia bond-strength studies (1,371 tests from 144 papers)
facts.intervention: Pooled analysis of luting techniques (mechanical and chemical pre-treatments, cements, test methods) for bonding to zirconia
facts.main_result: Combined mechanical and chemical pre-treatment was crucial for durable zirconia bonding; cement choice did not matter after aging if composite cement was used, and macro-shear tests gave lower, less discriminative values.
facts.funding_coi: Flemish scholarship, FWO-Flanders and KU Leuven projects; no conflicts declared
outcomes: bond strength by pre-treatment, cement, test method and aging

facts.population: Polished yttria-stabilized zirconia (LAVA) plates
facts.intervention: Gas-phase plasma fluorination of the zirconia surface
facts.comparison: Three commercial zirconia primers (Clearfil Ceramic Primer, Monobond Plus, Z-Prime) and an untreated control
facts.main_result: Fluorinated zirconia gave the lowest contact angle (7.8 deg) and highest shear bond strength (37.3 MPa), ahead of Z-Prime (24.3 MPa), control (9.2), Clearfil (10.0) and Monobond Plus (7.5).
facts.funding_coi: RTI Fellows Program, RTI International

facts.population: 30 participants needing a single maxillary implant-supported crown (14 to 24)
facts.intervention: Monolithic high-translucency multilayer zirconia crowns on implants
facts.comparison: Traditional veneered zirconia crowns (3Y zirconia core, feldspathic veneer)
facts.main_result: No significant difference in patient VAS satisfaction, but WES differed significantly between the two crown types (P<0.05).
facts.sample_size: 30 participants, each receiving both crown types
facts.funding_coi: Research Discipline fund from Ninth People's Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University

facts.population: 80 disk-shaped specimens (10 mm diameter; 0.8 and 1.5 mm thick) of 3Y, 4Y and 5Y zirconia and lithium disilicate
facts.intervention: Zirconia of 3, 4 and 5 mol% yttria (Katana HT, STML, UTML) measured for translucency parameter and masking ability
facts.comparison: Lithium disilicate (Rosetta SM)
facts.main_result: TP increased with yttria content (3 to 4 to 5 mol%), all zirconia less translucent than lithium disilicate; zirconia masked normal dentin but not severely discolored dentin at 0.8 or 1.5 mm.
facts.funding_coi: Grant from Korea Health Industry Development Institute (KHIDI); no conflict of interest declared

facts.population: 60 ceramic crowns (30 zirconia, 30 alumina) cemented on resin models
facts.intervention: Zirconia-core crowns tested for fracture load after water storage, heat treatment and cyclic preloading
facts.comparison: Alumina-core crowns
facts.main_result: Zirconia crowns were about 3 times stronger and tougher than alumina crowns (about 1200 vs 400 MPa); all fractures occurred in the alumina group (p<0.001).

facts.population: A1-shaded ceramic specimens of 5 indirect restorative systems cemented on three tooth-colored resin substrates (ND3, ND8, ND9)
facts.intervention: Five indirect restorative systems (lithium disilicate, translucent zirconia, PICN, bilayer zirconia, CAD-on) resin-cemented on different substrates
facts.main_result: The bilayer YLD-T (zirconia plus veneer) showed delta E values below the acceptability threshold on all substrate comparisons and the lowest translucency, i.e. the best masking ability.
facts.sample_size: n = 5 specimens per system, cemented on 3 substrates (n = 15)
facts.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq and CAPES (Brazil), Junta de Andalucia and Spanish Ministry of Economy

facts.population: 15 anterior zirconia crowns (n = 5 per group) placed on 11 substrates (ND1-ND9, zirconia, metal)
facts.intervention: Monolithic, bi-layer and tri-layer 3Y-TZP zirconia crowns
facts.comparison: Layered (bi-layer and tri-layer) crowns versus monolithic
facts.main_result: Monolithic crowns had better masking ability than bi-layer and tri-layer crowns, but color differences were below the acceptability threshold only for ND2, ND3 and ND7 substrates in cervical and middle areas.
facts.funding_coi: Grant of the Romanian Ministry of Education and Research, CCCDI-UEFISCDI

facts.population: 1 mm-thick specimens of five monolithic zirconia systems, two lithium disilicate glass-ceramics and bovine enamel/dentin
facts.intervention: Highly translucent 5Y-PSZ zirconias and 3Y-TZP zirconias tested for optical and mechanical properties
facts.comparison: e.max CAD HT and LT lithium disilicate, bovine enamel and dentin as references
facts.main_result: Higher yttria content (5 mol%) significantly improved zirconia translucency, but zirconia remained less translucent than lithium disilicate (p < 0.05).
facts.sample_size: n = 10 per zirconia group for optical tests; n = 10 flexural, n = 5 toughness

facts.population: Disc-shaped ceramic specimens (8 mm diameter, 1.8 mm thick), 11 ceramic groups, over resin composite and metal substrates
facts.intervention: Bilayer and monolithic ceramic systems, with and without an opaque resin-based luting agent (OLA), over discolored substrates
facts.comparison: Bilayer versus monolithic ceramics; with versus without OLA; control substrate A1
facts.main_result: Bilayer structures showed significantly lower delta E00 than monolithic ones; OLA reduced delta E00 for monolithic ceramics and CAD-on with OLA masked metal substrates at a non-perceptible level.

facts.population: Specimens (1.2 x 1.2 x 3.0 mm) of amalgam, dental ceramic, gold alloy, dental resin, zirconia and titanium alloy; enamel and dentin values from a prior study
