facts.intervention: Tribochemical silica sandblasting (CoJet) and/or silane/MDP ceramic primers before bonding with two composite cements
facts.comparison: No sandblasting and/or no primer; three ageing protocols (10 d water, 10,000 thermocycles, 6 months water)
facts.main_result: CoJet sandblasting plus a silane/MDP primer gave the most reliable durable bond (Weibull shape 3.47, scale 54.04 MPa for CoJet/Clearfil Ceramic Primer/Panavia F2.0 at 10 d); without a primer, bonding largely failed.
facts.follow_up: 10 days, 10,000 thermocycles, or 6 months water storage

facts.population: Airborne-particle-abraded IPS e.max ZirCAD zirconia plates, saliva contaminated
facts.intervention: Cleaning of saliva-contaminated zirconia with tap water, 37% phosphoric acid, Ivoclean or additional airborne particle abrasion, then Monobond Plus and resin cement
facts.comparison: Uncontaminated control group
facts.main_result: Additional airborne particle abrasion (and Ivoclean) restored bond strength and surface free energy of saliva-contaminated zirconia; tap-water rinse alone gave the lowest bond strength (5.7 MPa at 24 h vs 16.4 MPa control).
facts.funding_coi: Grants from the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, Sato Fund and Nihon University Dental Research Centre

facts.population: Sintered zirconia plates (Toso), alumina-blasted and saliva contaminated
facts.intervention: Cleaning of saliva-contaminated zirconia by water-rinsing, phosphoric acid gel, Ivoclean, AD Gel (NaOCl) or additional alumina-blasting before bonding with 2 resin cements
facts.comparison: Alumina-blasted zirconia without saliva contamination (control)
outcomes: shear bond strength at 24 h and after 10,000 thermal cycles
facts.main_result: Additional alumina-blasting or AD Gel cleaning preserved resin cement bond strength to saliva-contaminated zirconia; water-rinse, phosphoric acid and Ivoclean did not give durable bonding.
facts.sample_size: 16 specimens per group, 6 groups (8 per storage subgroup)

facts.population: Six mongrel dogs, mandibular extraction sites
facts.intervention: Zirconia implants (modified surface Z1, standard surface Z2) and titanium implants placed within bone or with a buccal bone dehiscence
facts.comparison: Titanium implants (CAMLOG Screw-Line) and implants within the bony housing vs with dehiscence
outcomes: height of peri-implant mucosa and margo mucosae
facts.main_result: With buccal dehiscence, titanium implants lost significant peri-implant mucosal height (-1.45 mm) unlike zirconia implants; the modified zirconia surface showed higher bone-to-implant contact.
facts.sample_size: 6 dogs, 5 implants per side (n = 6 per healing time point)
materials_brands: CAMLOG SCREW-LINE promote plus titanium implant (Camlog Biotechnologies)
facts.funding_coi: Funded by CAMLOG Biotechnologies AG and the Universities of Zurich and Yonsei; no conflict of interest reported

facts.intervention: BioWin! one- and two-piece zirconia (alumina-toughened) ceramic implants, 6 to 13 mm long, with a glass fiber post in the two-piece version
facts.main_result: Manufacturer states a 95.8% osseointegration success rate in a 2-year study, including patients with periodontal disease.
facts.funding_coi: Manufacturer brochure (Champions-Implants GmbH)
facts.key_finding: Manufacturer brochure for the Champions BioWin! one- and two-piece zirconia implants (0.25% alumina, 6 to 13 mm lengths, rough surface by a patented process, two-piece version with a glass fiber post and no micro-gap), citing a 95.8% osseointegration success rate since 2004.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: The claims are the manufacturer's own; the brochure cites a 2-year study (Prof. Becker) for the 95.8% figure.

facts.population: Patients with commercially available zirconia implants, at least 60 months follow-up
facts.intervention: Zirconia (1- and 2-piece) dental implants
facts.main_result: Pooled 5-year implant survival was 97.2% (95% CI 94.7-99.1), marginal bone loss 1.1 mm and probing depth 3.0 mm.
facts.sample_size: 6 cohort studies, 277 implants in 221 patients (survival analysis)
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
facts.limitations: Low number of zirconia implants evaluated and only observational studies, no RCTs.

facts.population: Sixty partially edentulous patients (46 recalled, 30 examined at 9 years)
facts.intervention: Two-piece zirconia implants with cemented fibreglass abutments and all-ceramic crowns in the posterior jaws
facts.main_result: At a mean 111.1 months one implant was lost among 30 patients; BOP and PD were unchanged, PI increased, and no additional peri-implantitis occurred after the first 2 years.
facts.sample_size: 30 patients (one target implant each) of 46 eligible at 9 years
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflict of interest
facts.limitations: High dropout rate, no control group and retrospective design.

facts.population: 30 patients with premolar agenesis and 63 single-tooth premolar implants
facts.intervention: All-ceramic crowns on zirconia abutments
facts.comparison: Metal-ceramic crowns on metal abutments
facts.main_result: At 5 years marginal bone loss was minor and not significantly different between all-ceramic (0.3 mm) and metal-ceramic (-0.1 mm) restorations (p = .056), while marginal adaptation was significantly better for metal-ceramic (p = .025).
facts.funding_coi: DENTSPLY Implants and Danish Dental Association; no conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: OHIP questionnaires were used although most participants had restorations of several materials.

facts.intervention: Champions BioWin! ceramic (zirconia) implant placement protocol: torque, drilling sequences, condenser use, immediate loading
facts.key_finding: Manufacturer's quick guide for placing Champions BioWin! ceramic implants: primary stability of about 20 Ncm and a maximum insertion torque of 30 Ncm, flapless (MIMI) or flap placement, bone-density-specific drilling and condenser sequences, and immediate restoration or loading when 30 Ncm stability is reached.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: A product-specific protocol from the manufacturer without clinical data, useful as a technique reference for this implant system only.

facts.main_result: Posterior lack of support should be treated with implants, with attention to restorative space, retrievable designs and splinting of multiple implants.
Aesthetic success depends on tissue loss at the start of treatment, not on a specific implant system or design.
Implant placement must be biologically and restoratively driven, follow comprehensive diagnosis, and deficient ridges must be reconstructed first.
Immediate implant placement at extraction is predictable when diagnosis, prognosis of the dentition and surgical guidelines are followed.
Choice of fixed versus removable implant prosthesis for the edentulous maxilla is the key decision; removable designs need more maintenance.
In the edentulous mandible function outweighs aesthetics; interarch space and long-term maintenance guide choice between overdenture and hybrid prosthesis.
Screw-retained implant restorations are more easily retrieved and maintained and easier with immediate loading; cemented restorations accommodate more implant positions.

facts.population: A mandibular typodont jaw model with three abutment tooth models
facts.intervention: Scanning with two intraoral scanners (Trios 3, Primescan) with water or artificial saliva on the tooth surface
facts.comparison: Dry versus wet versus blow-dried tooth surface
facts.main_result: Wet surfaces gave significantly higher RMS (lower trueness and precision) than dry or blow-dried surfaces, with no difference between water and artificial saliva.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

facts.main_result: Interproximal contact loss next to implant restorations is common (maxilla 18-66%, mandible 37-54%) and multifactorial, occurring as early as 3 months.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
facts.limitations: All reviewed prevalence papers were retrospective, so prospective studies are needed.

facts.population: Permanent posterior teeth in children and adults (primary analysis: 921 children)
facts.intervention: Direct composite resin fillings
facts.comparison: Amalgam fillings
facts.main_result: Low-certainty evidence: composite restorations had almost double the failure risk of amalgam (RR 1.89) and higher secondary caries (RR 2.14), with no higher fracture risk.
facts.limitations: All included studies were at high risk of bias (no blinding, unit-of-analysis problems) and mostly over 10 years old.

facts.population: 13 studies of amalgam and composite resin restorations in permanent premolars and molars
facts.intervention: Composite resin restorations
facts.comparison: Amalgam restorations
outcomes: restoration failure (replacement, fracture, secondary caries, sensitivity, toothache)
facts.main_result: No significant difference in failure risk between amalgam and composite resin restorations (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.68-1.34).
facts.sample_size: 13 studies (5 RCTs, 4 prospective and 4 retrospective cohorts)
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the Dasman Diabetes Institution, Kuwait; no competing interests declared
facts.limitations: Variation in failure definitions and insufficient reporting of influential factors produced heterogeneity.

facts.intervention: Updated international consensus on definitions and assessment of sleep and awake bruxism
outcomes: definitions of sleep and awake bruxism
facts.main_result: In otherwise healthy individuals bruxism is a behaviour (risk and/or protective factor), not a disorder; self-report and electromyography can both be used; no standard cut-off points should be used.
facts.funding_coi: Lobbezoo, Santiago and Lavigne declare grants or fees from industry or institutions, outside the submitted work
facts.limitations: Further research is needed to assess clinical use of the assessment approaches.

facts.intervention: Basic Erosive Wear Examination (BEWE): a four-level score of the worst surface in each sextant, summed and matched to risk levels guiding management
facts.main_result: A simple scoring system is proposed; cumulative sextant scores map to none, low, medium and high risk levels guiding management and recall intervals.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Cut-off values are based on experience of one author and have to be reconsidered; the system still needs validation.

facts.intervention: Practical guidance on scoring tooth wear with the BEWE index at routine examinations, alongside the BPE
facts.main_result: The BEWE should be recorded at every routine examination with the BPE, scoring the worst surface per sextant (0-3), with a lower score chosen in doubt.
facts.funding_coi: Open Access fee paid by Colgate Palmolive and the Latin American Oral Health Association
facts.limitations: The BEWE is not designed or accurate enough to assess progression over time.

facts.population: Patients with resin or ceramic inlays, onlays and overlays in 14 included clinical studies
facts.intervention: Ceramic (feldspathic porcelain, glass-ceramic) and resin inlays, onlays and overlays
outcomes: failure types (fracture, endodontic complications, secondary caries, debonding, marginal staining)
facts.main_result: Pooled survival of glass-ceramic and feldspathic porcelain inlays/onlays/overlays was 95% at 5 years (n = 5,811) and 91% at 10 years (n = 2,154); fractures were the most frequent failure cause.
facts.sample_size: 14 studies; 5,811 restorations at 5 years and 2,154 at 10 years
facts.funding_coi: Granted by Ibirapuera University, Brazil; no conflicts declared
facts.limitations: No resin inlay/onlay/overlay studies were available for meta-analysis and several outcomes lacked standardized data.

facts.journal: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Patients with extended posterior defects treated with partial coverage restorations
facts.intervention: Ceramic and ceramic-based partial coverage restorations (onlays, occlusal veneers, partial crowns)
facts.comparison: Different ceramic and ceramic-based materials (RMC, LDS, LRGC) head to head
facts.main_result: At 3 years survival was 89.3% for resin matrix ceramic and 93.7% for lithium disilicate; LDS slightly outperformed RMC on failure and loss of retention (low certainty), with no significant short-term differences.
facts.follow_up: 1-3 years in four studies, 4-6 years in one, 7 years or more in one
facts.funding_coi: No specific funding; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Most included studies had short follow-up and non-English studies were excluded; certainty of evidence was low to very low.

authors: Cleber Davi Del Rei Daltro Rosa
facts.population: Patients with single-unit posterior ceramic crowns opposing natural enamel
facts.intervention: Monolithic zirconia, monolithic lithium disilicate and metal-ceramic (feldspathic veneer) single crowns
facts.comparison: Natural antagonist enamel (enamel-to-enamel contact)
outcomes: vertical wear of antagonist natural enamel (µm)
facts.main_result: Zirconia (MD -1.32) and lithium disilicate (MD -0.45) caused significantly more antagonist enamel wear than natural enamel; feldspathic metal-ceramic did not differ significantly (p = 0.06).
facts.funding_coi: CNPq research fellowships for two authors; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Longer follow-up studies are needed to confirm long-term stability.

facts.population: Patients with monolithic zirconia tooth-supported fixed-prosthesis crowns and their natural antagonist teeth
facts.intervention: Monolithic zirconia crowns
outcomes: maximum wear of the antagonist tooth (µm)
wear of the zirconia crown itself
facts.main_result: Mean maximum antagonist wear against monolithic zirconia crowns was 95.45 µm (95% CI 79.57-111.33), rising about 6.13 µm per month, greater than wear of the crown itself (58.47 µm).
facts.sample_size: 8 studies in qualitative synthesis, 4 in meta-analysis; 10 to 60 crowns per study
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Further studies with larger samples, longer follow-up and adequate control groups are needed.

facts.population: Endodontically treated teeth (in vitro load-to-fracture studies)
facts.intervention: Endocrown restorations
facts.comparison: Post-and-crown restorations
outcomes: effect of luting material, ferrule, tooth type, restoration material, aging and load angle
facts.main_result: Load-to-fracture did not differ significantly between endocrowns and post-and-crown restorations; resin composite luting increased and oblique loading decreased load-to-fracture.
facts.sample_size: 25 in vitro studies, 90 experimental groups, 804 teeth

off_topic_reason: Medical informatics trial on LLM use by family, internal and emergency medicine physicians with no dental content.

facts.population: Fifty US-licensed physicians (family, internal or emergency medicine; 26 attendings, 24 residents)
facts.intervention: Access to a large language model in addition to conventional diagnostic resources
facts.comparison: Conventional resources only
facts.main_result: Median diagnostic reasoning score was 76% with the LLM versus 74% with conventional resources only, a non-significant adjusted difference of 2 percentage points (P = .60); the LLM alone scored 16 points higher than the control group.
facts.funding_coi: Funded by the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation

facts.population: Teeth prepared for indirect bonded restorations (inlays, onlays, veneers) with exposed dentin
facts.intervention: Immediate dentin sealing: applying and curing the dentin bonding agent on freshly cut dentin before impression taking
facts.main_result: Applying and polymerizing the dentin bonding agent on freshly cut dentin before impression taking is recommended; it appears to give improved bond strength, fewer gaps, less bacterial leakage and reduced sensitivity.

facts.population: Five implant disks: machined titanium, SLA titanium, titanium alloy grade 5 and two zirconia
facts.intervention: Exposure to tobacco smoke simulating occasional (5x/day for 3 days) and heavy (20x/day for 10 days) smoking
facts.comparison: The same disk surfaces before smoke exposure (control disks)
outcomes: contact angle (wettability) with saline, artificial blood and albumin
facts.main_result: Tobacco smoke improved wettability of titanium surfaces but made zirconia surfaces more hydrophobic with saline and artificial blood; roughness barely changed.
facts.sample_size: n = 15 per group; 180 contact angle measurements (occasional) and 450 (heavy smoking)
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest declared

facts.population: Implants placed in smokers and non-smokers across 292 publications
facts.intervention: Smoking (at least one cigarette per day) as exposure
facts.comparison: Non-smokers
facts.main_result: Implants in smokers had a higher failure risk than in non-smokers (OR 2.402, p < 0.001); marginal bone loss was 0.580 mm higher in smokers.
facts.sample_size: 292 publications; 35,511 implants in smokers and 114,597 in non-smokers
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest

facts.population: Implants (59,246) and patients (14,115) from 32 observational studies
facts.intervention: Smoking as exposure
facts.comparison: Non-smokers (also ex-smokers in subgroups)
facts.main_result: Smoking was associated with increased early implant failure risk at implant level (OR 2.59, 95% CI 2.08-3.23), higher in the maxilla (OR 5.90) than mandible (OR 3.76).
facts.funding_coi: Funded by Chinese hospital/municipal research grants; no conflict of interest declared

facts.journal: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: Studies from two systematic reviews: vertical vs horizontal finish lines (15 studies) and intraoral scanner accuracy for inlays, onlays and veneers (33 studies)
facts.intervention: Vertical versus horizontal finishing line designs, and intraoral scanner (IOS) digitization for inlays, onlays and veneers
facts.comparison: Horizontal versus vertical finishing lines; IOS versus conventional impressions
facts.main_result: Vertical and horizontal finish lines showed no significant differences in survival, success or periodontal outcomes over 3-7 years; IOSs were reliable for single-unit inlays and onlays but evidence for veneers was inconclusive.
facts.funding_coi: Authors received travel compensation from PROSEC Foundation, SEPES or SSRD; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Data on veneer restorations scanned with IOS were inconclusive because few studies exist.

facts.population: Clinical studies of patients with ceramic veneers (1429 veneers)
facts.intervention: Bonding ceramic veneers to different tooth substrates (enamel, dentin, existing composite restoration)
facts.comparison: Enamel versus dentin versus existing composite resin substrate
facts.main_result: Enamel-bonded veneers had survival 99% and success 99%; severe dentin exposure lowered survival to 91% and success to 74%.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by the Saudi Ministry of Education; no competing interests declared

facts.population: Adults with obesity or overweight with a weight-related comorbidity; adults with obesity and moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea
facts.intervention: Zepbound (tirzepatide) 2.5 mg subcutaneous once weekly, escalated to 5-15 mg maintenance
facts.key_finding: Prescribing information for Zepbound (tirzepatide), a once-weekly subcutaneous GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist for weight reduction in adults with obesity or overweight and for moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. It carries a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors and warns of severe gastrointestinal reactions, delayed gastric emptying and pulmonary aspiration during general anesthesia or deep sedation.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: For dental care under sedation or general anesthesia, patients on Zepbound should be identified, since the label reports pulmonary aspiration risk and asks patients to tell providers about planned procedures.

facts.population: Edentulous patients with atrophic maxilla treated with the all-on-four concept
facts.intervention: Four implants (two distal tilted) with immediate loading of a full-arch prosthesis (all-on-four)
facts.main_result: Implant survival of 99.8% beyond 24 months; frequent prosthetic complications (acrylic fracture) and few biological complications at about two years.
facts.follow_up: minimum 3 years required for inclusion; mean about 2 years for biological complications
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Evidence limited by scarce methodological quality information, inadequate follow-up and sample attrition.

facts.population: Etched and silanized bonding surfaces of glass ceramic restorations contaminated with saliva, blood or silicone
facts.intervention: Cleaning sequence: rinse, phosphoric acid or particulate cleaning paste, then re-etch with hydrofluoric acid for silicone, and re-silanize
outcomes: removal of saliva, blood and silicone contaminants
facts.main_result: Water spray, alcohol and acetone do not remove saliva residues from glass ceramics, whereas phosphoric acid gel or particulate cleaning paste do; silicone needs hydrofluoric acid etching.
facts.funding_coi: First author is head of the adhesive R&D section at Ivoclar Vivadent (maker of Ivoclean); no funding statement

facts.intervention: Proposed 'esthetic width' concept for metal-ceramic restorations: margin positioning, reduced metal framework with extended porcelain shoulder, pontic and interdental design
facts.main_result: Reduced frameworks with porcelain shoulders avoid the umbrella effect; ridge-lap pontics and interdental mini-wings are recommended for collapsed anterior ridges and flattened papillae.

facts.population: Sixty extracted human maxillary first molars, endodontically treated, six groups of 10
facts.intervention: ZLS endocrowns without ferrule with 2, 3 and 4 mm pulpal extensions
facts.comparison: ZLS endocrowns with 1 mm shoulder ferrule at the same pulpal extensions
outcomes: marginal, axial and internal adaptation (replica technique)
facts.main_result: Endocrowns without ferrule had higher fracture resistance (about 1371-1410 N) than with 1 mm ferrule (about 1162-1247 N) at all depths, while the ferrule and deeper pulpal extension increased gaps, all clinically acceptable.
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest

facts.population: 80 extracted human molars (mandibular and maxillary) embedded in acrylic
facts.intervention: Zirconia endocrowns with a 2 mm ferrule design and/or adhesive luting
facts.comparison: No-ferrule and conventional cementation groups (classic endocrown preparation)
facts.main_result: 88.8% of specimens passed the step-stress test up to 1500 N; no significant differences between ferrule/no-ferrule or cementation mode.

facts.population: Posterior teeth restored with endocrowns (in vitro studies)
facts.intervention: Endocrown preparation design (cavity depth, occlusal thickness, ferrule, divergence angle, finish line, vents)
facts.main_result: Marginal discrepancy increases with added preparation features, deeper cavity and greater divergence; fracture resistance rises with more occlusal reduction and cavity depth but is already beyond normal clinical force.
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
facts.limitations: Meta-analysis not possible because of heterogeneity of preparation designs and evaluation methods.

facts.population: Tooth impressions taken in vitro with intraoral scanners
facts.intervention: Intraoral scanners used with scanning strategies different from the manufacturer's instructions
facts.comparison: Scanners used following the manufacturers' requirements
facts.main_result: Humidity negatively affected the accuracy of intraoral scanners (P<.001); the review recommends dry conditions and artificial landmarks, especially in edentulous cases.
facts.sample_size: 15 in vitro studies in the meta-analysis (55 in the qualitative analysis)

facts.journal: Journal of the Canadian Dental Association
facts.population: Severely damaged endodontically treated molars
facts.intervention: Endocrown: monolithic one-piece ceramic bonded restoration with supragingival butt-joint margin and pulp-chamber retention
facts.main_result: No outcome data; the authors conclude endocrown preparation is rational, simple and quick, avoids the root canals and preserves the periodontium.
facts.funding_coi: No declared financial interests

facts.population: Two young male patients with grossly decayed mandibular molars (36 and 37)
facts.intervention: Split cast post and core: two-section multisection design (case 1) and single post and core with separate auxiliary post (case 2), followed by crown
facts.main_result: At 1-year follow-up of case 1 the prosthesis showed no failure and the patient was satisfied with function and esthetics.

facts.population: Patients rehabilitated with implant-supported or implant-retained fixed or removable dentures
facts.intervention: Implant-supported or retained dentures (fixed and removable)
facts.comparison: Conventional dentures
facts.main_result: Objective benefits in masticatory performance of implant-supported or retained dentures over conventional dentures are limited to mandibular implant overdentures in edentulous patients with a resorbed mandible and/or difficulty adapting to conventional dentures.

facts.population: Extensively damaged endodontically treated teeth (molars, premolars, incisors)
facts.intervention: Endocrowns
facts.comparison: Post-retained restorations and crowns
facts.main_result: Molar endocrowns had survival above 90% from 6 months to 10 years, similar to traditional crowns; premolar endocrowns 68-75%; loss of retention caused 53% of endocrown failures.
facts.limitations: High heterogeneity of methods, prostheses, materials and parameters across studies.

facts.population: 99 patients wearing maxillary complete dentures opposing mandibular anterior natural teeth only
facts.intervention: Single-examiner observational assessment of ridge form, denture quality and features of Combination Syndrome
facts.comparison: Patients with versus without a mandibular removable partial denture (64 vs 35)
outcomes: patient-rated denture fit and chewing ability
facts.main_result: Only 8 of 99 patients showed two features and 38 one feature (excessive anterior maxillary resorption); none showed three or more, so Combination Syndrome appeared rare or non-existent.
facts.sample_size: 99 patients (64 with mandibular partial denture, 35 without)
facts.limitations: No sample size calculation was possible; target of 100 chosen pragmatically; single examiner.

facts.population: 140 glass fiber posts (Whitepost DC #3), 10 groups of 14
facts.intervention: Post surface pretreatment with 30% hydrogen peroxide or 35% phosphoric acid for 1 or 5 minutes, with or without silanization
facts.comparison: No treatment or silanization alone
facts.main_result: Silanization significantly increased bond strength (silane alone 23.7 vs control 16.8 MPa) whereas hydrogen peroxide or phosphoric acid did not; the highest value was P5S (23.8 MPa).

facts.population: Dental patients requiring restorative treatment (mostly children)
facts.intervention: Rubber dam isolation
facts.comparison: Cotton rolls (and the Isolite system in one study)
facts.main_result: Rubber dam may increase survival of direct restorations at 6 months versus cotton rolls (OR 2.29, 95% CI 1.05 to 4.99; low certainty); little to no effect at 12 and 18 months (very low certainty).
facts.limitations: All included studies were at high risk of bias, few and small.

facts.journal: International Journal of Periodontics & Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 66 patients (aged 23 to 73 years) treated in one private office by one dentist with 580 porcelain laminate veneers
facts.intervention: Porcelain laminate veneers (mostly heat-pressed ceramic) bonded with preparations varying in depth and margin (enamel vs dentin)
facts.comparison: Veneers with preparations/margins confined to enamel versus those with dentin exposure or dentin margins
outcomes: veneer failure (fracture, debonding, microleakage, secondary caries, sensitivity, root canal treatment)
facts.main_result: 42 of 580 veneers (7.2%) failed with 86% cumulative survival at 12 years; dentin-exposed preparations and dentin margins carried about 10-fold higher failure risk and coronal crown lengthening 2.3-fold.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

facts.population: 637 posterior partial lithium disilicate restorations in 373 patients treated by undergraduate students (2009-2019)
facts.intervention: Posterior partial lithium disilicate restorations (inlays/onlays) placed by 4th, 5th and 6th year undergraduates
facts.comparison: Operator academic year (4th vs 5th vs 6th), plus patient-, tooth- and material-related factors
outcomes: risk factors by multilevel Cox regression
facts.main_result: 5- and 10-year survival were 89.1% and 77.6%; medium-to-high caries risk (HR 1.57) and an approximal outline within 3 mm of the bone (HR 1.52) increased failure, whereas operator academic year had no significant effect.
facts.funding_coi: No specific grant; no competing interests declared

facts.journal: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 60 sound extracted human third molars (dentin fragments) placed in intraoral acetate trays in one volunteer
facts.intervention: Bonding with two two-step etch-and-rinse adhesives (Adper Single Bond Plus, One Step Plus) performed at intraoral incisor and molar sites
facts.comparison: Room condition as control group
facts.main_result: Molar site had higher temperature (27.28 C) and RH (90.79%) than incisor site (26.18 C, 84.84%), both above room (21.10 C, 50.30%), but intraoral environment did not affect bond strength; One Step Plus gave the highest bond strength.
facts.follow_up: 48 hours storage before testing (immediate bond strength)
facts.funding_coi: Partially supported by CAPES, Brazil; no financial interest in the companies

facts.population: In vitro dentin specimens from human or bovine teeth
facts.intervention: Blood decontamination protocols applied to blood-contaminated dentin before bonding
facts.comparison: No decontamination or alternative decontamination protocols
facts.main_result: Blood contamination consistently reduced dentin bond strength across adhesive systems, worst when contamination followed polymerization; decontamination only partially recovered bonding.
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no competing interests
facts.limitations: Substantial heterogeneity in protocols prevented meta-analysis, so only a qualitative synthesis was done.

facts.population: Permanent human dentin (in vitro studies)
facts.intervention: Dentin contamination with blood, saliva or hemostatic agents, with or without decontamination (rinsing, re-etching, chlorhexidine, sodium hypochlorite, adhesive reapplication)
facts.comparison: Uncontaminated dentin
facts.main_result: Any blood or saliva contamination impaired resin bond strength to dentin; water spray and reapplication of the bonding system could reverse the impairment, and hemostatic agents are not recommended for decontamination.
facts.sample_size: 62 in vitro studies included from 3750 records
facts.funding_coi: No financial interest in the companies whose materials are included
facts.limitations: Limited to in-vitro studies, so findings cannot be extrapolated clinically, and high heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis.

facts.population: 60 fiberglass epoxy resin posts (White Post DC3), in vitro
facts.intervention: Surface treatment of fiber posts (silane, 24% hydrogen peroxide, aluminum oxide blasting, NH3 plasma, HMDSO plasma) before cementation with self-adhesive resin cement RelyX U200
facts.comparison: Control group with no surface treatment
facts.main_result: Surface treatments influenced adhesion; silane, blasting and the two plasma treatments raised push-out bond strength above control (about 13-16 vs 9.65 MPa), while 24% hydrogen peroxide (9.40 MPa) did not differ from control.
facts.sample_size: 60 posts in 6 groups (n = 10), 40 discs per group
facts.funding_coi: Supported by Faperj, Capes and CNPq

facts.population: Patients treated with dental implants (19 studies, 4215 implants in 2185 patients)
facts.intervention: Nonsplinted implant-supported restorations
facts.comparison: Splinted implant-supported restorations
facts.main_result: No significant difference in marginal bone loss or prosthetic complications; 75 implants failed (3.4%), 24 splinted (99.1% survival) versus 51 nonsplinted (96.5% survival), significantly favoring splinting.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by a Sao Paulo Research Foundation grant

facts.population: Partially or fully edentulous adults aged 18 or older with implant-supported prostheses
facts.intervention: Implant-supported prostheses with specific prosthetic designs (screw-retained, splinted, platform-switched, internal connection, large crown-to-implant ratio, abutment height of 2 mm or more, one abutment-one time, small emergence angle, concave/straight profile)

facts.key_finding: The review gives definitions, indications and step-by-step protocols for surgical extrusion, intentional replantation and tooth autotransplantation. Reported survival is about 90% for intentional replantation and 80-100% for autotransplanted teeth.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Teeth that would normally be extracted can often be saved by these procedures, provided the periodontal ligament is protected during atraumatic extraction, but the evidence base is still limited.

facts.clinical_bottom_line: After roughening, etching and silane application, squeeze the repair composite into the uncured thin adhesive layer and then light-cure.

facts.journal: Clinical Implant Dentistry and Related Research
facts.population: 60 patients needing implant therapy; 39 patients with 95 implants analyzed at 15-17 years

facts.comparison: Two-piece implants (Brånemark, Nobel Biocare, BRA)
facts.main_result: Cumulative survival was 95.0% (STM 91.8%, BRA 98.0%); the one-piece system had more stable marginal bone (0.08 vs 1.53 mm) but more technical complications (35.4% vs 5.8% of implants).
facts.sample_size: 60 patients randomized; 39 patients with 95 implants analyzed

facts.funding_coi: Self-funded by the university clinic; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Loss to follow-up of 21 patients (56 implants) may introduce attrition bias, and examiners could not be blinded.
facts.key_finding: At 15-17 years both one-piece and two-piece implants showed high survival (95% overall). The one-piece system kept marginal bone more stable but had a higher rate of technical complications, and peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis were frequent in both groups.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Both designs are reliable long term, but the one-piece system trades better bone stability for more prosthetic maintenance, so plan for regular maintenance either way.

facts.population: 65 patients with 153 adjacent posterior implants (2 or 3 adjacent implants, at least 1 year post loading)
facts.intervention: Vertical level discrepancy between the platforms of adjacent implants
facts.comparison: Coronal versus apical implant of each adjacent pair
facts.main_result: With horizontal inter-implant distance of 3 mm or less and VLD above 1 mm, marginal bone loss was -2.03 mm around coronal implants versus -1.01 mm around apical implants (p = 0.004).
facts.funding_coi: No interests declared
facts.key_finding: In a retrospective radiographic study of 153 adjacent posterior implants, a vertical level discrepancy between implant platforms was associated with more marginal bone loss around the coronal implant. The association was limited to implants with a horizontal inter-implant distance of 3 mm or less.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: When adjacent implants sit close together (3 mm or less), avoid placing them at different vertical levels, since the more coronal implant tends to lose more bone.

facts.population: 156 patients with 337 adjacent implants restored with two or three adjacent single or splinted crowns or three-unit bridges, treated at UCSF School of Dentistry
facts.intervention: Splinted adjacent implant restorations and vertical platform discrepancy between adjacent implants
facts.comparison: Non-splinted adjacent implant restorations; platform discrepancy < 0.5 mm
outcomes: Proximal radiographic marginal bone loss (RMBL), odds of at least 1 mm loss
facts.main_result: A vertical platform discrepancy of 0.5 mm or more was associated with at least 1 mm RMBL (OR 4.30, 95% CI 1.85 to 10.01), and splinted adjacent implants had higher odds than non-splinted ones (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.17 to 5.17).
facts.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared; funding not stated
facts.key_finding: In this retrospective chart review, adjacent implants whose platforms sat at different vertical levels (0.5 mm or more) had a clearly higher chance of at least 1 mm marginal bone loss, and splinting the crowns together increased that risk further compared with non-splinted restorations.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: When placing two or three adjacent implants, aim for platforms at the same vertical level, and be cautious about splinting implants that are at different heights.

facts.population: Three-dimensional finite element model of a posterior mandibular bone segment (cortical shell and trabecular core) with three splinted 3.5 x 13 mm implants
facts.intervention: Four vertical placement configurations of three splinted implants (crestal, mixed crestal/subcrestal, subcrestal), loaded with 400 N
facts.comparison: All-crestal placement versus mixed-height and all-subcrestal configurations
outcomes: Von Mises stress in cortical and trabecular bone
Von Mises stress in the implants and implant-abutment connection
facts.main_result: The configuration with a subcrestal central implant and crestal lateral implants produced localized cortical peak stresses exceeding physiological thresholds, while uniform vertical positioning gave lower, more even stresses.
facts.sample_size: 4 finite element models, each with 3 splinted implants
materials_brands: AoN Implants (3.5 mm x 13 mm, conometric connection)
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest declared
facts.key_finding: In a finite element model of three splinted implants in a posterior mandible, placing the central implant subcrestally while the outer two stayed crestal concentrated the highest stress in cortical bone, above the physiological limit under oblique load. Keeping all three implants at the same level, especially subcrestal, gave lower and more even stresses, and the peak implant stress was always at the implant-abutment connection.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: When splinting adjacent implants, keep their platforms at a uniform vertical level; avoid mixing crestal and subcrestal positions. This is a simulation, so clinical confirmation is needed.

facts.intervention: Conformative approach and the EDEC (Examine, Design, Execute, Check) sequence for providing direct and indirect restorations without altering the patient's occlusion
facts.main_result: The conformative approach is the safest way to ensure a restoration's occlusion has no harmful consequences, achieved by examining and recording the occlusion before treatment and checking it after (EDEC).
facts.limitations: Occlusal theories are largely empirical and untested, lacking scientific validity as rules
facts.key_finding: This review recommends providing routine restorations by the conformative approach, which keeps the patient's existing jaw relationship and occlusal contacts unchanged. It teaches a four-step EDEC sequence (Examine, Design, Execute, Check) for direct and indirect restorations, including recording the pre-existing occlusion for the laboratory and keeping it with a well-fitting temporary crown.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Record the patient's occlusion before preparing a tooth, design and execute the restoration to preserve it, and check that other teeth still contact as before.

facts.population: Partially edentulous patients restored with root-retained overdentures (11 RCTs published 1978 to 1999)
facts.intervention: Root-retained (root-supported) overdentures
outcomes: Periodontal condition and bone changes around abutment teeth
facts.main_result: Root-retained overdentures remain viable, with better stability, bone preservation around abutment teeth and high patient satisfaction; root caries is the main risk for abutment loss; only 2 of 11 RCTs had low risk of bias and no meta-analysis was possible.
facts.funding_coi: No financial support from companies; no conflicts of interest
facts.limitations: Heterogeneity of studies prevented meta-analysis, and few RCTs of mostly high risk of bias were available
facts.key_finding: This systematic review of 11 randomised trials found that root-retained overdentures remain a viable option, giving better denture stability, preservation of bone around the abutment teeth and high patient satisfaction. Caries on the abutment teeth was the most frequently reported complication and the main risk for losing them, but most of the trials had a high risk of bias and could not be pooled.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Keeping roots for an overdenture is reasonable, but it depends on meticulous oral hygiene, caries prevention and regular recall visits.

facts.population: 72 published articles on food impaction identified from PubMed
facts.intervention: Literature review of aetiology, classification and treatment of food impaction
facts.main_result: Food impaction has multifactorial causes (proximal contact loss, occlusal disharmony, morphological deformity, positional abnormality, interdental papilla loss) and treatment should follow the cause.
facts.funding_coi: Supported by Seoul National University Foundation 2022
facts.limitations: Heterogeneity and subjectivity of the studies make a standard treatment plan difficult
facts.key_finding: This review of 72 articles found that food impaction arises from proximal contact loss, occlusal disharmony, morphological deformity, positional abnormality and loss of the interdental papilla. Because causes differ, management ranges from restoration and occlusal adjustment to orthodontic, nonsurgical or surgical treatment.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Identify the cause of food impaction before treating it, then choose the management (restoring contact, adjusting occlusion, orthodontics or periodontal treatment) that fits that cause.

facts.intervention: Pre-prosthetic orthodontic intervention (multiple missing teeth, deep overbite, worn anterior teeth, tilted molars, orthodontic extrusion for crown lengthening)
facts.main_result: Orthodontic treatment can improve esthetic and functional outcomes of restorative care, and a diagnostic wax-up and clear orthodontist-restorative dentist communication are essential.
facts.limitations: Most literature on pre-prosthetic orthodontics consists of clinical reports or opinions, the lowest levels of evidence
facts.key_finding: This narrative review covers five situations where orthodontics before restorative treatment helps: multiple missing teeth, excessive deep overbite, worn anterior teeth, tilted molars, and orthodontic extrusion for crown lengthening. It stresses planning with a diagnostic wax-up and close communication between orthodontist and restorative dentist, and notes that the underlying literature is mostly clinical reports and opinion.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Consider an orthodontic referral before restoring patients with deep bites, worn anterior teeth, tilted molars or subgingival margins, and plan together from a diagnostic wax-up.

facts.journal: Journal of Korean Academy of Prosthodontics
facts.population: One 65-year-old man with skeletal Class III malocclusion, lost occlusal vertical dimension, bilateral mandibular posterior edentulism and severe tooth wear
facts.intervention: Full-mouth rehabilitation: CAD-CAM provisional denture to establish centric relation and OVD, mandibular posterior implant-supported prostheses, zirconia full-coverage crowns on remaining teeth
facts.main_result: The severe anterior crossbite was corrected to an edge-to-edge relationship and mutually protected occlusion was achieved in eccentric movements.
materials_brands: NextDent SG printing resin (3D printed overlay denture)
facts.funding_coi: Supported by a Pusan National University research grant
facts.key_finding: In a 65-year-old man with skeletal Class III malocclusion, lost vertical dimension and severe wear, a stable centric relation was first established with a CAD-CAM provisional denture, then implants restored the posterior support and zirconia crowns the remaining teeth. The anterior crossbite became edge-to-edge with mutually protected occlusion, with no fracture, loss or joint problems at one year.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: In skeletal Class III patients with collapsed posterior support, establish centric relation and the new vertical dimension with a trial provisional stage before committing to definitive implant and crown work.

facts.population: 31 published studies (non-randomized studies, case reports, technical articles) on completely edentulous arches in digital workflows
facts.intervention: Methods for recording functional impressions of edentulous arches within digital complete-denture workflows
outcomes: surface deviation of optical vs conventional impressions
facts.main_result: No fully digital functional impression technique exists; most studies used hybrid workflows, and optical impressions captured mucostatic detail but not mobile tissues.
facts.funding_coi: No external funding; no competing interests declared
facts.key_finding: This scoping review of 31 studies found that no fully digital technique exists for functional impressions of edentulous arches. Most used hybrid workflows with conventional border molding and a definitive impression, or skipped the step. Intraoral scans captured static tissue well but not mobile tissue.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Functional impressions for complete dentures still need a conventional step, so use a hybrid workflow rather than a fully digital one.

facts.population: RPD metal frameworks (30 studies; 815 frameworks or part specimens, mostly in vitro)
facts.intervention: 3D-printed RPD metal frameworks via SLS, SLM or DMLS
facts.comparison: Conventional casting and partial digital methods (CAD/CAM resin pattern followed by casting)
facts.main_result: 3D-printed RPD metal frameworks showed accuracy and mechanical-physical performance comparable or superior to conventional and partially digital methods.
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no competing interests declared
facts.limitations: Evidence limited by methodological variability, moderate risk of bias in many studies, and inconsistencies across designs and parameters.
facts.key_finding: Across 30 mostly in-vitro studies, 3D-printed (SLM/SLS/DMLS) metal RPD frameworks matched or exceeded casting and partially digital frameworks in fit, mechanical and physical properties. The few clinical studies reported improved retention and patient satisfaction.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Printed metal RPD frameworks appear a viable alternative to casting, though evidence is mostly laboratory-based and heterogeneous.

facts.intervention: AiDENTAL RPD Surveyor and Designer, a browser-based tool for digital surveying and automated RPD framework design from intraoral scan STL files
facts.main_result: The authors report the whole process takes 2 to 5 minutes; no formal outcome data are presented.
facts.limitations: May be limited in severely compromised or malposed teeth or complex occlusal relationships, needing manual adjustments; further studies are needed.
facts.key_finding: The paper describes a step-by-step technique using a web-based tool to digitally survey an intraoral scan, set the path of draw, mark undercuts, generate an RPD framework design and export it to the lab. No clinical or accuracy data are reported.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: A browser-based digital surveyor and designer could let clinicians survey and design RPDs from scans without a physical cast, but it is unvalidated and needs clinician judgment.

facts.population: 24 participants aged 50-65 with mandibular Kennedy class I partially edentulous arches
facts.intervention: Fully-digital workflow (intraoral scan) for SLM Co-Cr RPD frameworks
facts.comparison: Combined analog-digital workflow (physical impression, stone cast, lab scanner)
outcomes: gap at rest, proximal plate, lingual plate, I-bar clasp terminal
facts.main_result: Overall mean gap was 0.112 mm for combined vs 0.101 mm for fully-digital workflow (P=0.0125); fully-digital was superior in all areas.
facts.funding_coi: Self-funded; no competing interests
facts.key_finding: Fully-digital intraoral-scan workflow gave Co-Cr SLM RPD frameworks with smaller gaps than the analog-digital workflow (0.101 vs 0.112 mm overall), though both were clinically acceptable.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Intraoral scanning can be used for SLM RPD frameworks with equal or slightly better fit than conventional impressions.

facts.population: Edentulous arches with 4 or more implants, in vitro models and patients (22 in vitro, 1 clinical study)
facts.intervention: Five categories of complete arch implant intraoral scan techniques (IOS-O, IOS-SA, IOS-CHS, IOS-CISP, IOS-IPG)
facts.comparison: Conventional abutment-level splinted open tray impression
facts.main_result: IOS-O and IOS-SA were more accurate than conventional for short spans but conventional was more accurate for long spans; IOS-CISP appeared better in long spans (limited evidence).
facts.funding_coi: No competing interests declared; work of AAFP Research in Fixed Prosthodontics Committee A
facts.limitations: Evidence for IOS-CISP is limited and studies on IOS-CHS and IOS-IPG are insufficient; nearly all studies in vitro.
facts.key_finding: In this systematic review of 23 mostly in vitro studies, intraoral scans (with or without scan aids) were more accurate than splinted open-tray impressions for short implant spans but less accurate for long spans. Calibrated scan protocols (IOS-CISP) looked better in long spans, but evidence is scant.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: For long-span complete arch implant records, the conventional splinted open-tray technique remains more reliable than standard intraoral scanning.

facts.population: Partially edentulous patients with single implant crowns in 5 included RCTs
facts.intervention: Early loading of a single implant crown
facts.comparison: Immediate loading of a single implant crown
facts.sample_size: 5 RCTs (147 early vs 140 immediate implants at 1 year)
facts.key_finding: This meta-analysis of 5 randomized trials found no significant difference between early and immediate loading of single implant crowns in implant survival (about 97% in both groups) or marginal bone loss at 1 and 3 years.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Either immediate or early loading can be considered for single implant-supported crowns, especially when implants are placed with high insertion torque.

facts.intervention: Alteration of occlusal vertical dimension in restorative treatment
facts.main_result: OVD is a dynamic dimension within a zone of physiological tolerance and should be changed minimally, only when a clinical demand exists.
facts.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest and no financial support reported
facts.key_finding: The review concludes that occlusal vertical dimension is a flexible parameter within a zone of physiological tolerance, to be altered only when clinically needed and by the minimum necessary amount.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Confirm a clinical demand before changing OVD, keep the change minimal, and use provisionals to test esthetic and functional outcomes.
